speaker: Bayek
en: I am ready to speak of my dream.

speaker: Seer
en: Of course, Deliverer. But first you must help me.

speaker: Bayek
en: How?

speaker: Seer
en: I have visions of danger. A dark cloud looms over three heads. An adventurer, a philanderer, and a beggar are all at risk.

speaker: Bayek
en: What would I do for them?

speaker: Seer
en: Give each an amulet to guard against the darkness. One may be found near the Great Temple, one in its eastern district, and one in the tunnels that wind below it. I'll wait for you by the docks at the basin of the Great Temple.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 1
en: How much bread did he steal?

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 2
en: All that was meant for the palace. The baker wants him executed.

speaker: Beggar
en: Please, I did it to feed my family!

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 2
en: Shut up. This isn't his first time stealing, either. I've caught him at it myself.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 1
en: Should we just kill him now and be done with it?

speaker: Beggar
en: Oh, please, let me live!

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 2
en: I said shut up! I can't think straight with you jabbering at me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do you know the Seer?

speaker: Beggar
en: He sent help! Thank the gods! Ready for a fight, Medjay?

speaker: Bayek
en: Always.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is done.

speaker: Beggar
en: Freedom!

speaker: Bayek
en: You're quite the fighter.

speaker: Beggar
en: I do my best. They caught me off guard the first time.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Seer offers this amulet to keep you from further harm.

speaker: Beggar
en: My children cannot eat a stone.

speaker: Bayek
en: I cannot do more for you than this. May your luck change course.

speaker: Beggar
en: Pardon my rudeness. You have already risked yourself to save me. As long as I am alive, my family still has a chance.

speaker: Bayek
en: These are the tunnels the Seer mentioned. I'm on the right track.

speaker: Bayek
en: I've come too late to save this one.

speaker: Bayek
en: Divine ones circle around him. May this amulet preserve his .

speaker: Cleïs
en: I never touched her, you neket iadet!

speaker: Egyptian Soldier
en: And she says you did! Are you calling my wife a liar?

speaker: Cleïs
en: Are you calling me a liar?

speaker: Egyptian Soldier
en: Yes! A liar and adulterer!

speaker: Cleïs
en: Fine, then! If you're going to insult me like that, I did sleep with your wife!

speaker: Cleïs
en: Beautiful Valeria... I found her crescent-shaped mole on her right buttock particularly charming!

speaker: Egyptian Soldier
en: You reeking bog witch! You'll suffer for this.

speaker: Cleïs
en: How dare you put a tongue so foul on sweet Valeria?

speaker: Egyptian Soldier
en: I'm going to kill you!

speaker: Cleïs
en: Then do it now, coward! Open this door and cut me down in the street! Show everyone what kind of man you are!

speaker: Bayek
en: A friend asks me to free you.

speaker: Philanderer
en: Well then! What are you waiting for?

speaker: Philanderer
en: I'd like to say I'm capable of walking, but that would be a lie.

speaker: Bayek
en: Set aside your pride. I'll carry you.

speaker: Philanderer
en: I've nothing to reward you with, except my thanks.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will claim my reward elsewhere.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Seer sends this amulet. His visions show you are in need of protection.

speaker: Philanderer
en: Why would I want this piece of junk?

speaker: Bayek
en: Just take it so we can conclude our business.

speaker: Philanderer
en: Fine. I suppose wearing it will make my mother happy.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is all three amulets given out. Now to return to the Seer.

speaker: Seer
en: Have you delivered the amulets?

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes. One arrived too late to protect its bearer.

speaker: Seer
en: Which?

speaker: Bayek
en: The adventurer. He met a lonely end, bitten by a snake.

speaker: Seer
en: This is sad news. All the same, I consider your debt paid. A sacred island lies further in the embrace of Mother Nile. Bring me there, and I will tear aside the curtain that shrouds your nightmares.

speaker: Seer
en: Now, Deliverer, tell me what you saw.

speaker: Bayek
en: I saw... I saw what has lain behind my eyes every night for the past year. It begins with a sandstorm. I rise to my feet and walk a corridor of ruins, passing into the Hall of Judgement. There, a twin of myself places a black stone heart onto the scales of Ma'at. It is then that the god-snake strikes – Apep, larger than a mountain, larger than reason. A bow of light appears in my hands. I fight the snake and win, though, not without injury. Then I rise through dark, choking waters to surface among lotus flowers. I claim my heart from an altar and travel to the Field of Reeds. In the distance I see my son. When I reach for him, he turns to ashes. He...

speaker: Seer
en: Thus is your true seeing unbound.

speaker: Seer
en: Here. The sacred island awaits our coming. Hurry – the moment is now!

speaker: Seer
en: Deliverer, would you be free of the curse that plagues your sleep? There is a ritual that will banish it from your mind forever.

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes. Do it, then!

speaker: Seer
en: Go beneath the waters south of here, and bring up the statue of Khnum from the Sunken Temple of Ramses. With this likeness of the Great Potter to hand, the ritual can be performed.

speaker: Bayek
en: The statue. I will bring it back to the Seer.

speaker: Bayek
en: Here is the statue.

speaker: Seer
en: Khnum, sculptor of children. He will battle Apep in your place. This ritual needs your mind's strength. Sit by my side and meditate as I speak with the gods.

speaker: Seer
en: Grow, O light... Come forth, O light... Rise, O light ascend, O light... You who are without, come in. O darkness, remove yourself from his eyes. O God of seeing, bring in the light to him! O Apep who coils in the abyss, be turned aside! Devoid of moisture, come forth from the stream! As your sail bends to yesterday, accept him as a passenger on your divine ship! Khnum, stand beside him and be his champion!

speaker: Bayek
en: Eh? The Seer is gone! How did he leave the island?

speaker: Seer
en: How do you fare, Deliverer?

speaker: Bayek
en: My mind is more peaceful.

speaker: Seer
en: Tonight, your sleep will come without dreams.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am grateful for your help.

speaker: Seer
en: Memphis is grateful for yours.

speaker: Bayek
en: By all the gods! Have they sent a message from the sky? It's as if Ra has descended upon us.

speaker: Bayek
en: The fireball has revealed an entrance to this tomb. This is a sign from the gods.

speaker: Fallen Star
en: A large stone, glowing blue, that fell to earth from the sky.

speaker: Bayek
en: Could this be referring to a sun dial? I wonder.

speaker: Bayek
en: This number seems important.

speaker: Bayek
en: This must be the sun dial that was depicted in the tomb.

speaker: Bayek
en: It seems to be working.

speaker: Bayek
en: Light shining up to the gods? By Ra, what have I done? I should check the tomb.

speaker: Bayek
en: O you door-keepers who guard your portals, who swallow souls and who gulp down the corpses of the dead. What a journey I have made, the things I have seen. I am but one of you.

speaker: Bayek
en: A note from Isidora?

speaker: Bayek
en: Merti left offerings here, to atone for what the tomb robbers did?

speaker: Bayek
en: The priests of Amun were held in high regard.

speaker: Bayek
en: An inscription, the God's Wife of Amun was revered throughout Egypt.

speaker: Bayek
en: Isidora's mother sits at the right hand of Amun, as the God's Wife.

speaker: Bayek
en: The tomb robbers murdered Nitokris when she tried to stop them ransacking the tombs. Isidora had to bury her mother. The orb and her mother's legacy was passed to her. She vowed to revenge her, but she never had the means. Until now. Then years later, Merti came to try to make amends for what the others did.

speaker: Bayek
en: The true source of the curse. A girl who lost her mother begging the gods for vengeance.

speaker: Nena
en: The vestiges of darkness. They are here in the grave of Apep the encircler.

speaker: Essence of Darkness
en: Gathered from the scales of the world encircler the serpent Apep.

speaker: Bayek
en: True darkness seeps from this remnant of Apep.

speaker: Bayek
en: No! Could this be... a remembrance of the battle? Avenging light against the snaking darkness.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is enough. I will be glad to leave the world encircler at rest.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Pharaoh's heart, the blood of his beloved mother Tuya.

speaker: Bayek
en: Soldiers are excavating here. I need to find the songs before they do.

speaker: Bayek
en: The spoils of war? These are the Bas of People taken captive during Ramesses' battles.

speaker: Nefertari
en: Elect of Ra! His servant bears down upon you, carries his yoke. Keen your blade, cup-bearer.

speaker: Nefertari
en: The cunning must feast upon their own tail. He sees the sapphire, the cerulean, the turquoise as stars. The dust veil lifted from his eyes.

speaker: Bayek
en: The earth quakes. Take your place amongst the gods, Ramesses.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Get ready to move out! These vermin will be on the lookout. We have been successful in finding the King's enemy! We go now! Can't wait to see the King's face when we bring this villain in!

speaker: Theodoros
en: Release me! I'll wet my blade with their blood! You should have killed me! Now, you die!

speaker: Theodoros
en: Slaughter every last one of these dogs!

speaker: Theodoros
en: Break me out, will you?

speaker: Theodoros
en: You are Bayek of Siwa, aren't you? I've heard stories of the Medjay who crossed the desert. I am Theodoros, one of many who rebel against the Phylakitai.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is that what landed you in this cage?

speaker: Theodoros
en: Yes, a failed attack. I am hunting Derratos, a ruthless general of Ptolemy with a hatred for Egyptians. A killer of mothers and fathers and children. I won't rest until his body is food for the worms. Would you lend your sword?

speaker: Bayek
en: Gladly. Your plight is true.

speaker: Theodoros
en: Good joy! We will regroup with my men in Bacchias. Come along.

speaker: Bayek
en: How does a Greek find himself fighting an Egyptian cause?

speaker: Theodoros
en: My father was Egyptian. My mother, Greek. Long ago, a day came when I discharged every ounce of Greek blood from my body, and pledged to rid Egypt of men like Derratos. And we nearly did. We found his camp, but they had greater numbers. We were forced to disband. I was captured by a scouting convoy and beaten into giving up our retreat point.

speaker: Bayek
en: But you instead led them into a trap. Clever.

speaker: Theodoros
en: I knew my brothers would rescue me, but I did not know the Medjay from Siwa would be among them, too.

speaker: Theodoros
en: Good. Now, follow me.

speaker: Theodoros
en: You are rather celebrated among my group. We spent years tracking Rudjek, only to learn you made waste of him singlehandedly. You would not call us your ally but our goals seem to be aligned from time to time, don't they?

speaker: Bayek
en: You are not incorrect.

speaker: Theodoros
en: We will take shelter here and wait for the right moment to strike. I will get briefed.

speaker: Rebel
en: Dogs! They've sent out scouting groups. Theodoros! Derratos has left the camp. He's gone.

speaker: Theodoros
en: Derratos is gone. Nek! He continues to elude me.

speaker: Bayek
en: What should we do?

speaker: Theodoros
en: Let's be smart. We have an opportunity to claim two victories with one swift strike. We need to wait for Derratos to return to camp. I've learned his personal scribe has stayed behind in Karanis. We'll be targeted if we so much as take a piss nearby. You are unknown to them. Bring the scribe to us. He'll tell us what we need to know.

speaker: Bayek
en: How do I find him?

speaker: Theodoros
en: At night, he rests within the courtyard. During the day, you can find him working around the temple or at the terrace overlooking the lake. He dresses elegantly, and due to our failed attack, now has guards in tow. He'll be hard to miss.

speaker: Man
en: Must you follow me around everywhere?

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Strict orders from the general. We are not to leave your side.

speaker: Man
en: He's overreacting. I'm safe here.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Derratos won't take any chances. The rebels could strike again. We are all on high alert.

speaker: Man
en: Who're you? Gerroff... Ohhh. Hrm. Yes... There...

speaker: Bayek
en: The scribe himself. Drunk and dead to the world.

speaker: Bayek
en: It won't be long before he comes to. I need to bring him back to Theodoros.

speaker: Theodoros
en: That is him. Well done. We will find out what he knows. In the meantime, we must prepare our attack. Some of our brothers are stationed just west of Soknopaiou. Meet with them and wait for my arrival. We will put an end to that neket iadet.

speaker: Rebel
en: A scribe who knows his way around Karanis.

speaker: Theodoros
en: Derratos, where is he!?

speaker: Man
en: That name means nothing to me!

speaker: Rebel
en: Don't think us fools!

speaker: Man
en: Please, stop!

speaker: Rebel
en: Then talk!

speaker: Theodoros
en: We'll break your fingers. Then your wrists. Your arms!

speaker: Man
en: No! No, dont!

speaker: Rebel
en: Where's Derratos?

speaker: Rebel
en: Talk!

speaker: Man
en: I can't!

speaker: Theodoros
en: Your work here is done. We will get the information we need. Meet the others and wait for my arrival.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you Raia's brother? Ranofer?

speaker: Ranofer
en: Did I know you when I lived, seni (friend)?

speaker: Bayek
en: Your sister made you this amulet, it was stolen from you in life. I come to return it.

speaker: Ranofer
en: Anubis granted you passage? So my sister's offering would protect me even here? My words are feeble for such a gift.

speaker: Bayek
en: Stay well and strong under the radiant lights, Ranofer.

scene: A Tithe By Any Other Name
speaker: Bayek
en: I wish to serve Serapis further, if you have need.

scene: A Tithe By Any Other Name
speaker: Lysander
en: There is one thing. There has been food taken by the guards malignly in the name of Serapis. They take a tithe, then take double for themselves. They bring it to their arsenal and share it with their phylakitai. The people now starve, I worry it will get worse.

scene: A Tithe By Any Other Name
speaker: Bayek
en: Do not worry, Priest. I will see the people fed.

scene: A Tithe By Any Other Name
speaker: Lysander
en: I will await among the people at the docks.

scene: A Tithe By Any Other Name
speaker: Bayek
en: Stealing from Serapis? You guards are supposed to uphold the law. Pathetic. This food will be put to much better use. This food will serve the people well.

scene: A Tithe By Any Other Name
speaker: Bayek
en: One cart of food, Priest, as asked for. The Pharaoh's guards were happy to donate it.

scene: A Tithe By Any Other Name
speaker: Lysander
en: This, seni (friend), is more than I expected. The people will be served by Serapis today.

scene: A Tithe By Any Other Name
speaker: Bayek
en: May you walk lightly in his steps, Priest.

scene: A Tithe By Any Other Name
speaker: Lysander
en: And you, Medjay.

speaker: Diocles
en: I have my hands full with the magistrate Leander. I know he's corrupt but his ties to Flavius put him above the law.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then let us sever those ties.

speaker: Diocles
en: Easier said than done. He's either threatened or bribed, anyone who would stand against him. Simonides could help us if he wasn't such a drunkard. He was at Leander's villa last night and hasn't returned home.

speaker: Bayek
en: I could look for him?

speaker: Diocles
en: Excellent! Then I'll petition the other magistrates. Try the tavern, or the brothel southwest of the Arena for our wayward friend. We'll meet back at my house. It's the only one with a large terrace on the main street. Did you find Simonides? He's probably sleeping it off by the brothel.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you Simonides?

speaker: Simonides
en: Ow my head! Why are you shouting?

speaker: Bayek
en: Diocles sent me to find you.

speaker: Simonides
en: Tell him I'm dead.

speaker: Bayek
en: We need your help, with Leander.

speaker: Simonides
en: That demon is the one responsible for my befuddled mind and evacuating bowels. I'm sure someone spiked my wine.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am sorry, but I have to take you with me.

speaker: Simonides
en: Bacchus and his nymphs be buggered. You sir are a Fury sent to punish me. If I expire on the way, it's on your head.

speaker: Simonides
en: What is your name, torturer?

speaker: Bayek
en: Bayek.

speaker: Simonides
en: Egyptian?

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes. Diocles said you met with Leander last night?

speaker: Simonides
en: A party. At his villa. Everything was flowing. Wine, women, boys...

speaker: Bayek
en: Sounds...

speaker: Simonides
en: Ipthos lost his toga!

speaker: Bayek
en: Fun?

speaker: Simonides
en: Fun? Urgh... a mission... on a mission...

speaker: Bayek
en: Did you find anything?

speaker: Simonides
en: Urgh...

speaker: Bayek
en: Simonides? Are you alright?

speaker: Simonides
en: No. Curse you son of Ra.

speaker: Diocles
en: Hera mother goddess. Simonides? Are you drunk?

speaker: Diocles
en: I won't ask where you found him, Bayek.

speaker: Simonides
en: On the street! Some fool moved the brothel.

speaker: Diocles
en: Did you find anything at Leander's villa?

speaker: Simonides
en: Papers, records of bribes, treasury theft. His guards caught me before I could take them. I convinced them I was simply inebriated.

speaker: Diocles
en: A stretch indeed, Simonides.

speaker: Bayek
en: So the evidence is there, I just need to take it.

speaker: Diocles
en: We would be forever in your debt. But why would you risk your life to help us?

speaker: Bayek
en: Because those who abuse their power should be removed and the people freed from oppression, Egyptian or Greek.

speaker: Simonides
en: Ahhh, well said, our friend Bayek reminds me of Cicero. (belches)

speaker: Diocles
en: The villa is east of here surrounded by vineyards. We will gather the other magistrates at the Temple of Apollo. Find us there when you secure the evidence. Fortuna smile on you, my friend.

speaker: Simonides
en: Do you return to torture me? Go, my friend, go.

speaker: Diocles
en: Hopefully I can sober Simonides up before we confront Leander.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is Leander paying prostitutes for pillow talk?

speaker: Bayek
en: A lot of complaints from the people, no-one seems happy!

speaker: Bayek
en: Party orders to his slave. An expensive gathering.

speaker: Bayek
en: Bribery, expensive parties and missing money from the treasury. This is the evidence that Leander is corrupt. But what is this about Diocles? A coup? I should warn Diocles, he could be in danger.

speaker: Roman Soldier 1
en: How long do we have to wait?

speaker: Roman Soldier 2
en: Leander said to count to one hundred.

speaker: Roman Soldier 1
en: Oh, have you been counting?

speaker: Roman Soldier 2
en: No... have you?

speaker: Roman Soldier 1
en: Jove's beard, everyone's probably dead by now!

speaker: Diocles
en: Bayek will find the evidence.

speaker: Man
en: You don't know that. Leander's secrets are his alone.

speaker: Simonides
en: You bloody fools! Will you let that bloated old goat take everything we've worked for?

speaker: Diocles
en: We owe it to Cyrene to put an end to his corruption.

speaker: Bayek
en: Diocles! It's a trap! Leander is attempting a coup!

speaker: Leander
en: So, here you all are, plotting against me!

speaker: Diocles
en: You will answer to the people, Leander.

speaker: Leander
en: My Roman friends would beg to differ.

speaker: Diocles
en: Bayek! We must protect the magistrates!

speaker: Simonides
en: You demon, Leander! These men are unarmed.

speaker: Leander
en: You are traitors to Cyrene and Rome. And for that you will die.

speaker: Diocles
en: You saved my life, my friend.

speaker: Bayek
en: Praxilla would not have forgiven me if I had let you fall at Leander's hand.

speaker: Diocles
en: Why would he do this? Was his lust for power so consuming that he would commit murder?

speaker: Bayek
en: I have seen men do worse for less.

speaker: Diocles
en: We are only alive thanks to you, Bayek. Cyrene deserved better than him at her helm.

speaker: Bayek
en: I know you will lead them well, Diocles.

speaker: Man
en: Just a moment, I promise! Medjay! Please! These crops need to be loaded for transport by the day's end.

speaker: Bayek
en: A little more than a moment of my time, don't you think?

speaker: Man
en: I'm sorry. We are normally two, but my son cannot keep up.

speaker: Bayek
en: One thing at a time. Let your boy rest. I will help you collect your harvest. He is too young to be working the fields.

speaker: Man
en: I know it. But my field hands ran off when I couldn't pay. The tax collectors demand all my grain, or they will burn my house down.

speaker: Man
en: Thank you, sir. Now I'll be able to pay Sefetu's dogs off, this time at least.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tell me about these tax collectors.

speaker: Man
en: They ride the roads all round Sais, sticking mostly to the outskirts. Their rabid master, Sefetu, has them tax the people for all they have.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let me see if I can find them, and convince them to change their ways. You work on your farm, and raising your boy.

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes, neb! Now that he can get some rest, I think my boy will get back his strength. The gods praise you!

speaker: Man 1
en: Did you have any trouble bringing the crops to your market?

speaker: Man 2
en: I'll say! Getting past Camp Pyrrhos is torture. Those soldiers are thieving scum! Sefetu has given them a long leash.

speaker: Man 1
en: All they do is take advantage of us! It's not right!

speaker: Man 3
en: Did you see the poor crazed wretch trying to talk to Harkhuf? He made the strangest sounds!

speaker: Bayek
en: I must deal with Sefetu's archers in Sais. They are his eyes.

speaker: Bayek
en: That takes care of Sefetu's eyes.

speaker: Storyteller
en: Have you heard the story of courageous Captain Phoxidas? The magnificent Greek mercenary who single-handedly defeated the despised Gabiniani fleet in epic battle on the high seas? Then gather around, and I will amaze you with the legend of Phoxidas and the Goddess of Siwa! Listen closely and you will hear how alone on the wide, naked Mediterranean Sea, the two fearless titans sent no less than sixty Gabiniani ships to the bottom of the ocean!

speaker: Bayek
en: You said goddess of Siwa? What was her name? Which battle are you talking about?

speaker: Storyteller
en: You have not heard? Oh, my friend, then you are in for a treat! Let me tell you how it happened... Legend has it, the noble Greek captain and the Egyptian goddess sailed from Alexandria's golden coast, in search of the feared Gabiniani fleet.

speaker: Storyteller
en: With only their sturdy trireme and loyal crew against the Gabiniani's fabled warships. Floating mountains carrying ten-thousand men, bristling with oars and fire...

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Where are these mongrel Gabiniani? My informant assured me they would pass here. I'll throttle his scrawny neck if he told me wrong.

speaker: Aya
en: Who are the Gabiniani? Where do they come from?

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Exiles of Rome who took Egypt as their home. Traitorous rats, every one, with the discipline of Rome and the ruthlessness of Ptolemy. Worthy opponents for the likes of us!

speaker: Aya
en: Well, we have to stop them before they can join Ptolemy's fleet.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: We'll find them, Aya, and send them to ruin. Not one of the salt-soaked hull rats will pass us alive. What say you, shield boy?

speaker: Damastes
en: We are with you, Captain! Alala!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: There!

speaker: Aya
en: Is that their whole fleet?

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Poseidon's piss no, woman! That's only part of their full strength, and the lesser part by the looks. Triremes only. There's no sign of their damned Octareme. This works in our favor. We can work them down, ship by ship.

speaker: Aya
en: Strike oars and ready your bows! We attack!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Give no quarter, men! These devils will give us none!

speaker: Damastes
en: They have an Octareme? How will we face it?

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Show no fear, Damastes! They've not met our kind before. Their bloated barge won't save them.

speaker: Aya
en: That's two down!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: There's one more yet for Poseidon's collection!

speaker: Storyteller
en: The Gabiniani were vanquished! All twenty mountainous warships lay in Poseidon's slimy embrace. Alone, and with the fury of the wind and sea railing against them, they prevailed!

speaker: Bayek
en: Twenty warships? Pompey himself wouldn't claim so many.

speaker: Storyteller
en: You must not doubt me! I was told it by someone who saw it happen!

speaker: Damastes
en: Captain! We bested them! The Gabiniani are finished!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Don't be hasty, boy! My spies gave me a greater number than that. They must have split their fleet. We should head east.

speaker: Aya
en: Straight into the jaws of the crocodile, if your spies tell the truth.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Hahaha! What of it? I've wrestled more fearsome beasts!

speaker: Damastes
en: And none were a match for our Captain!

speaker: Aya
en: Your bravado will be your undoing, Captain. And ours!

speaker: Storyteller
en: As if rising from the very depths of the Underworld, a second bristling wall of hulls appeared. This time an unbelievable forty Gabiniani death ships faced our lone heroes. Then another ship rose behind the fleet, the size of which has never been seen before or since! Ten thousand warriors crowded its massive deck, smashing sword and spear against brazen shield.

speaker: Bayek
en: This may have been the largest fleet ever to sail the Mediterranean!

speaker: Storyteller
en: Silence... fell like fog. Suddenly one-hundred balls of fire leapt up from the Gabiniani decks and bore down upon Phoxidas and his stricken crew...

speaker: Damastes
en: The way they spring from the fog. It is like a nightmare!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Pah! Don't let their tricks trouble you, Damastes! It's a ruse to shake our nerve. They gain nothing by it.

speaker: Damastes
en: And their flames! The fire is intense!

speaker: Aya
en: Phoxidas! This weapon could really help our cause.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: I might know someone who knows someone. We could make it happen. Keep inside the range of their catapults, and the day is ours!

speaker: Aya
en: Let us finish this!

speaker: Storyteller
en: The heroics were spectacular! They fought like gods! But it was all to no avail. Yet more ships appeared. A vast, burning armada of war bore down upon them as if from Mars himself! The crew fainted, but were borne up again by the wild, thunderous cries of their fearless captain and the goddess!

speaker: Damastes
en: Yet more ships! From the east!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Hades' balls! This must be the full count of these bastards. There! Gods and piss! This is it, slackers! We win or we die! Alalala!

speaker: Aya
en: Prepare to evade!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Aya! Damastes! Slackers all! Listen to me! Scribes will break their pens writing of this day, on this blood-smeared ocean, we'll send these cursed Gabiniani to the Underworld! Let's see them tell that story without tears running down their face! The gods themselves will lift cups to our glory!

speaker: Aya
en: Steady, old man! Let's not bait the gods! Strike oars! Victory! By Amun, well done, all!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Alalalala! And that is the game! Alalalalala!

speaker: Storyteller
en: So Phoxidas and the goddess sailed into legend, over the backs of ten times ten thousand drowned Gabiniani! I tell you, I weep just to tell of it! And they say, if you whisper a prayer into a wave, or a fold of the sea, you can hear their war cry answer back. Alala, alala! And that is how it happened, to a word!

speaker: Bayek
en: What a tale. The goddess' name was Aya. And a goddess she truly is. That may be the only honest part of the story

speaker: Storyteller
en: What is truth? All is permitted in the realm of greatness! One must believe in the act of creation, or else they will join the Gabiniani!

speaker: Bayek
en: You are a fine storyteller, seni (friend). Though I cannot tell if you are playing a game with me or telling a story.

speaker: Storyteller
en: They are one and the same, my friend! Married to each other like the oceans and the rain.

speaker: Bayek
en: Alala!

speaker: Storyteller
en: You see it now! Hahaha!

speaker: Menehet
en: Bayek! What good fortune. I thought it would be years before we saw you again!

speaker: Bayek
en: Hail in peace, Menehet. How is your family?

speaker: Menehet
en: The children seem to grow larger by the minute! My wife and I have our hands full. And you? Is there any news of

speaker: Bayek
en: None.

speaker: Menehet
en: I forget myself... There are so many things in your life best not spoken of. Forgive me.

speaker: Bayek
en: I see by your garb that you've been promoted.

speaker: Menehet
en: Ah, yes. The High Priest, in his grace, made me his second. And my rank is not the only thing he has changed. You must see the temple!

speaker: Bayek
en: You will give me a tour?

speaker: Menehet
en: Of course, of course! At the moment of your pleasure.

speaker: Menehet
en: Ready to see our beautiful temple?

speaker: Bayek
en: After you, Menehet... or is it "Servant of the Goddess"?

speaker: Menehet
en: "Menehet" will do for one as good as family.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is far from the sorry ruin of my last visit.

speaker: Menehet
en: Yamu now plays constant host to ceremonies showing our "rustic" way of life... which attract many visitors with more gold than sense.

speaker: Bayek
en: A description well suited to Alexandrians. How does this sit with your faith?

speaker: Menehet
en: I confess that my thoughts are sometimes uneasy...

speaker: Bayek
en: Oho! Vanquished by a gang of ruffians, silent as (ghosts)!

speaker: Child 1
en: Uncle Bayek! Uncle Bayek!

speaker: Child 2
en: Hello, Uncle!

speaker: Menehet
en: Jewels of my life, why have you left your mother's side?

speaker: Child 3
en: Pick me up, Uncle Bayek!

speaker: Bayek
en: See now, there's no need to attack a man from behind when outnumbering him four to one.

speaker: Hasina
en: You told us to... secure every advantage possible over a dangerous foe.

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes, yes, yes...

speaker: Bayek
en: And I am very dangerous! Hide well, for the Wanderer stalks your path!

speaker: Menehet
en: Hasina loves to look at the sky. I think I saw her on her way to the upper floor. Soris might be bothering the sacred animals outside. He often plays at being a gladiator. I have told the children over and over that they are not permitted to play in the temple, but they never listen.

speaker: Nailah
en: You found me. Your turn to hide!

speaker: Bayek
en: Come away from there, Nailah. You're getting in the priests' way.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nailah, are you following me?

speaker: Nailah
en: You might get lost with me. It's a big temple!

speaker: Bayek
en: Your father wants you to go home.

speaker: Nailah
en: And I prefer to stay with you!

speaker: Nailah
en: I'm sure Soris is hiding near the animal cages. He likes to pretend he's a gladiator.

speaker: Bayek
en: Soris would be better off with opponents his own size.

speaker: Nailah
en: Are you going to sleep at our house again?

speaker: Bayek
en: Not this time, but I hope to pass by and visit your mother.

speaker: Soris
en: Beast, you will meet your end at the hands of the mighty gladiator, Soris!

speaker: Bayek
en: Soris! Stay back!

speaker: Soris
en: HELLLLLP!

speaker: Nailah
en: Do you want to hear a secret?

speaker: Bayek
en: Not if its about your father.

speaker: Nailah
en: Awww.

speaker: Nailah
en: My sister always sneaks up to the temple roof at night to look at the stars. But don't tell anyone -- the priests would be so angry!

speaker: Bayek
en: Hasina! You must come down from here.

speaker: Hasina
en: This would be a good place to watch the stars!

speaker: Bayek
en: Only the priests are permitted here. You know that.

speaker: Hasina
en: Yes, but I want to see

speaker: Bayek
en: Hush, come down now. We can watch stars from the riverbank.

speaker: Nailah
en: Wherever Keba hid, he's probably in trouble. He's always getting stuck in places. Once, we found him in a tree.

speaker: Nailah
en: My father is never at home these days.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why not?

speaker: Nailah
en: He has too much work with people coming from all over.

speaker: Bayek
en: Keba? What in the name of the gods are you doing down there?

speaker: Keba
en: I wanted to hide, but now I can't get back out... I'm scared.

speaker: Bayek
en: Stay calm. I will help you out of there.

speaker: Bayek
en: This way, through the tunnel.

speaker: Keba
en: Thank you, Uncle Bayek!

speaker: Bayek
en: Go straight home to your mother. She will be worried.

speaker: Bayek
en: That's the last of the children.

speaker: Man
en: Look at this! Fraud abounds in your market, and you claim you can do nothing?

speaker: Menehet
en: The dealings of the market are beyond me. Speak rather to the offending merchant.

speaker: Man
en: Priest, you have proven as false as your mummies!

speaker: Bayek
en: Menehet! Your brood is delivered safely home.

speaker: Menehet
en: Thank you, friend.

speaker: Bayek
en: What did that fool want with you?

speaker: Menehet
en: Some visitors, having purchased religious objects, are angry when our village has no more dead cats to sell them. Though not a merchant, I am often the means by which the aggrieved snuff their anger.

speaker: Bayek
en: This matter needs a firm hand.

speaker: Reda
en: Hey seni (friend)! Come here. One of my informants told me of some tomb robbers nearby. These maggots are stealing from the gods. We must stop them.

speaker: Reda
en: Do you know why our people forget our history, Bayek? It's because so many of our beautiful relics are stolen! We have the power to stop them! I heard of a group of these dungeaters who are near. Handle them, and I will make sure you are well paid.

speaker: Reda
en: Tomb raiders are taking the treasures of our people, Bayek! They steal from our sacred tombs, and leave our dead destroyed. We must stop them. And by we, I mostly mean you. But I will reward you well for dealing with these heathens!

speaker: Reda
en: Bayek, my Medjay! There are those who defile our holiest of places, stealing our sacred treasures. These bandits only want to make coin. Stop them. Keep our lands holy, alright, seni (friend)?

speaker: Reda
en: Thieves! They beat me to the item that I was hoping to procure for you, Bayek. This filth must be stopped. And look at you, Bayek, a Medjay after my own heart. Help me, and you will be well rewarded.

speaker: Reda
en: A completed task requires a reward, does it not?

speaker: Reda
en: A gift from me to you and not the gods, though we already know Ra smiles upon you.

speaker: Reda
en: Your payment, as promised.

speaker: Bayek
en: I saw the graffiti, looks like you have a problem.

speaker: Lanista
en: You could say that. My champion the Bear escaped. He is a trained killer, made as a hyena on heat. There's a bounty on him, good money if you survive.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why do they call him the bear?

speaker: Lanista
en: Not so fast, Egyptian. I will only hire you if you show me you are capable of ripping the bear apart. Let us see how you fare against some of my best fighters. Live, and we will talk.

speaker: Lanista
en: Polymestor's a deadly son of a bitch, fought in Arenas all across the Roman Republic. He won me a fortune and in return I treated him like a king. The best food, the best whores.

speaker: Bayek
en: Perhaps he valued freedom more.

speaker: Lanista
en: I earned my freedom through sweat and blood in the arena, not fleeing like a coward. Look. I don't care if that pox-ridden cunnus lives or dies, but he stole my sword. Caesar gave me that in my final fight and I want it back.

speaker: Bayek
en: Julius Caesar?

speaker: Lanista
en: You know another Caesar? Alright, Lads, come show this Egyptian some Roman courtesies!

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 1
en: Fight me!

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Hey, malakia!

speaker: Lanista
en: Now that was a show! You are a warrior.

speaker: Bayek
en: Have I proven myself?

speaker: Lanista
en: Yeah, alright do not get cocky. Rumor has reached me a farm east of Cyrene was attacked. Start there. That Thracian dogshagger won't come quietly. But the reward is for the weapon, you understand?

speaker: Bayek
en: I will find your champion and your trophy.

speaker: Lanista
en: Such confidence, I like it! I might even shed a tear if he guts you.

speaker: Lanista
en: You! Egyptian. You find my damn sword yet?

speaker: Bayek
en: What happened here? I must find Polymestor.

speaker: Bayek
en: Stab wounds and from many swords. Unless the lions came armed, they did not kill these people.

speaker: Bayek
en: Speared, then tortured. For what? Information?

speaker: Bayek
en: They shot him in the back. Was he trying to escape or hide?

speaker: Bayek
en: Swords, spears, arrows. This was not one man, it was a massacre.

speaker: Bayek
en: There is something beneath this. A hidden cellar?

speaker: Bayek
en: Polymestor did not kill these people, they helped him. Maybe he reached the fishing village?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am looking for a gladiator, the Thracian Bear.

speaker: Polymestor
en: Another of the Lanista's cronies. How much did he pay you to slit my throat?

speaker: Bayek
en: He only wants his sword.

speaker: Polymestor
en: Yes, covered in my guts. How did you find me, the farmers?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am sorry, Polymestor your friends are dead.

speaker: Polymestor
en: This is the Lanista's doing. I gave him my life and now I will take his. I threw the sword in the sea. Take it, it has brought me nothing but bad luck.

speaker: Polymestor
en: I threw the sword away. It can rust with the sea god for all I care.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Lanista's sword, I should talk to Polymestor.

speaker: Lanista
en: Ah here's the Egyptian clown. I knew he would lead me straight to you.

speaker: Polymestor
en: Let us end this. I will run no more, Lanista.

speaker: Lanista
en: Shut up you metrokoites.

speaker: Polymestor
en: For Thrace and true freedom!

speaker: Polymestor
en: That was a battle to make Charon weep! Thank you...

speaker: Bayek
en: Bayek.

speaker: Polymestor
en: Bayek. That bastard had no code, I earned my life back a thousand-fold. But I made too much coin for him. In the arena and the rich Roman beds. Keep Caesar's sword, it belongs to one who stands for freedom and honor.

speaker: Bayek
en: Thanks, I will stain it with the proper blood, the deserving blood. What will you do?

speaker: Polymestor
en: Fish, mend my nets and find a good, plump woman to settle down with. I will make the most of this new life.

speaker: Isidora
en: Amun-Ra-Horkhouti, secret of expressions and shimmering of form. Come forth. Purified, purified is the Lord of Thebes.

speaker: Isidora
en: You, lurking in the shadows.

speaker: Isidora
en: I should be angry, but you are in the house of the Hidden One. What is your business...?

speaker: Bayek
en: Bayek... of Siwa. I am looking for the source of the curse that plagues Thebes.

speaker: Isidora
en: You are not priest, or Phylakitai, and the oasis is far from here. What do you care for our troubles?

speaker: Bayek
en: Because they are not just your troubles. This curse... it stems from a relic. And countless suffered at the hands of the men who wielded another like it.

speaker: Isidora
en: You suffered more than most. Amun sees deep into your heart. But this is not men or relics, Bayek. Amun's ire is fearsome. The Pharaohs wreak his punishment for the thieves who desecrate the tombs.

speaker: Bayek
en: You believe this is your Lord's will?

speaker: Isidora
en: Amun comes at the cry of the poor and distressed.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then who in Thebes has reason to call him?

speaker: Isidora
en: Many things have been stolen from us. Relics, lives, innocence. The curse does not distinguish between rulers and subjects. But perhaps... the farmlands? Another Pharaoh walks there, but the people have escaped his ire.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will find out why.

speaker: Isidora
en: Speak to them, then tell me this is not the wrath of Amun. Amun protects those who cannot protect themselves. The farmers will know more.

speaker: Isidora
en: Self-made you fashioned your body. Creator uncreated. Lord of truth, maker of men, beasts and herbs, architect of all things above and below. Sole one, unique one, who traverses eternity.

speaker: Bayek
en: Can these farmers really welcome the curse?

speaker: Bayek
en: A lot of oil, more than a village of this size would need.

speaker: Oil Soaked Hay
en: Someone is looking to produce a voracious fire with this, a fire that burns forever.

speaker: Bayek
en: Not a typical village fire, this looks ceremonial.

speaker: Crazy Priest
en: He is the living Aten, he shall bless us! When you rise, they die. When you rise, they die. When you rise, they die. Die! Fie! Die! Fie! We must worship him! Honor him. Bring me the wine and the beer! He will come for us all, devour our hearts so Osiris will have nothing for his scales. Come, let us gather for the ceremony. I will lead you to salvation. Follow, follow!

speaker: Crazy Priest
en: You! He placed seed in all women! He is the nurse in the womb. He will take all who refuse to bow before him. Bow! Bow!

speaker: Pious Woman
en: My brother in Thebes calls us heretics.

speaker: Pious Man
en: Amun holds no dominion here.

speaker: Pious Woman
en: He deserted us, but for the Living Aten, we would all be dead.

speaker: Pani
en: I will say it Djehuty, just like you taught us. You alone, shining, risen! And when He comes, men hide, and the gods fly away. When you dawn they die. We fall at the feet of the king, the lord, the Sun, our god. 7 times and 7 times, both on the stomach and on the back.

speaker: Bayek
en: What game are you playing, child?

speaker: Pani
en: It's not a game! I'm making a ceremony to the sun!

speaker: Bayek
en: To Ra?

speaker: Pani
en: No! To the true god.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where did you learn that?

speaker: Pani
en: Djehuty. He protected us, saves us from the cursed one. But they stole him away.

speaker: Bayek
en: Some took Djehuty? Who?

speaker: Pani
en: Bad men.

speaker: Bayek
en: This... idol. Who is it? Crude and simply carved.

speaker: Old Woman
en: How do they live in Thebes? They do not worship the Aten.

speaker: Young Man
en: So many go about their business, as if their lives mean nothing to them.

speaker: Old Woman
en: They think the Pharaohs will spare them?

speaker: Young Man
en: Such hubris.

speaker: Soldier
en: You people owe us money, so pay up. Tychon's orders.

speaker: Old Villager
en: Hasn't he trampled us enough?

speaker: Soldier
en: Trampled? Don't make me laugh. You have these fields and your lives because of his good grace.

speaker: Old Villager
en: It's desecration! That's what they're doing!

speaker: Soldier
en: Keep your mouth shut or I'll feed you to Sobek.

speaker: Old Villager
en: Ra bless you, neb (sir). Two less of those vultures walking the black land.

speaker: Bayek
en: You have many troubles here?

speaker: Old Villager
en: Tychon's men are the least of it. People disappear every day, to the cursed lands, or those damned bandits...

speaker: Bayek
en: Bandits are taking people? Why?

speaker: Old Villager
en: Why do bandits do anything? For their own fiendish reasons. Beggars and crooks to a man.

speaker: Bayek
en: Djehuty must be the priest the bandits took! He will know more about this curse.

speaker: Storage Worker
en: Join me and we will rescue our priest! They will pay for taking one of our own.

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone took your priest?

speaker: Storage Worker
en: Yes, bandits. I am rounding up the able bodied to overrun their camp. I will not cower and cry as these neket iadets (pieces of shit) take our people!

speaker: Djehuty
en: I have nothing you want, thieves. My King, my Lord, my Sun, my God! My people need my protection! Release me from this prison.

speaker: Bayek
en: Bandits were afraid of Djehuty. They must believe he can summon the wrath of the Heretic King.

speaker: Djehuty
en: It is not just me you save, Seni (friend). Who are you that does Ahkenaten's bidding?

speaker: Bayek
en: Let us escape this place.

speaker: Djehuty
en: The Aten grants us sanctuary.

speaker: Djehuty
en: You risked your life for mine!

speaker: Bayek
en: The curse, I must have what you know.

speaker: Djehuty
en: He has killed many. I was trying to purify his shrine at the farm. But the bandits took me, they fear the Aten comes at my command.

speaker: Bayek
en: You worship the Heretic?

speaker: Djehuty
en: Akhenaten... We offer our piety... songs and rituals and he does not come for us. I can show you? But the farm, the animals rot, they must be burned...

speaker: Bayek
en: I will go to the farm, in return you will tell me what you know of the pharaoh.

speaker: Djehuty
en: Yes, yes! We must resume our nightly rituals. Find me at the southern farm after the sun sets and the corruption is gone.

speaker: Bayek
en: If nothing else the decaying animals will no longer taint the land.

speaker: Bayek
en: The priest said to find him after the sunset. They will be making preparations for their nightly ritual.

speaker: Djehuty
en: Meet me here after the sun sets. You will understand then.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have done what you asked.

speaker: Djehuty
en: Then we cannot act too soon, for the sake of all who make the farmlands their home. Please, Bayek join us for the ritual. See how we appease the Pharaoh Akhenaten.

speaker: Djehuty
en: You protected me and my people. Come, you should take part in our ceremony... Everything is prepared, the Aten rises.

speaker: Woman
en: Who is this man that aids us? He must be important or Djehuty would not allow it...

speaker: Djehuty
en: Will you honor him by gathering the sacred silica? Place it in the hands of the True King. Then will you see the strength of our hymns to the Sole God.

speaker: Djehuty
en: You rise, perfect, singular, on the horizon of the sky. The god that created all being. God without equal! Your form, the living Aten. Risen and resplendent, distant and near. Lord of the Two Lands, son of Ra, the one Living on Ma'at. Your strength lives within these offerings, sparse, but unbroken.

speaker: Farmer
en: I came from Thebes to join. Will it really protect me from the Pharaohs?

speaker: Farm Wife
en: When he was gone, I broke the statue of Amun I keep by my door. I hope the Pharaohs are pleased.

speaker: Nervous Man
en: The Aten is all-powerful.

speaker: Nervous Woman
en: Amun did not hear us when we called him.

speaker: Farmer
en: Djehuty saves us all.

speaker: Farm Wife
en: The Pharaohs have proven themselves more powerful.

speaker: Nervous Man
en: All will come to understand.

speaker: Aten Ritual Silica
en: This strange substance has an eerie feeling, which is why Djehuty offers it to the Pharaoh Akhenaten.

speaker: Woman
en: He has given him a great honor, to place the sacred quartz upon the statues of the Aten.

speaker: Djehuty
en: As long as they stand, whole and untainted. He will live in the Aten.

speaker: Djehuty
en: Please, Bayek, will you light the Aten?

speaker: Djehuty
en: You are our desire, there is no other who knows you. Our eyes fall upon your perfection.

speaker: Djehuty
en: O Living Aten, rejoice in your son, enfolding him in your rays. Living forever! All came forth in existence from your hand. When you rise they live, when you set they die. Splendid you rise, O Living Aten, eternal lord!

speaker: Woman
en: Alight! Alight! The Sole God shines his rays upon us!

speaker: Djehuty
en: Bayek! Join me and I will tell you what I know of Akhenaten.

speaker: Djehuty
en: Return to your homes and let the rays of the true god warm your hearths. He has spared us, rewarded us for our honor of him.

speaker: Djehuty
en: Have the scales fallen from your eyes?

speaker: Bayek
en: You believe the pharaoh Akhenaten is the son of the Aten.

speaker: Djehuty
en: I believe that his power is fearsome. In return for honoring him, we have our lives. Can you say the same for those who bow before Amun?

speaker: Bayek
en: This cult is heresy, what texts even speak of Akhenaten?

speaker: Djehuty
en: One. In the Theban Archive. But the chiseler Tychon has closed the library to all but his thugs and thieves.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will find a way in.

speaker: Djehuty
en: Look for a statue in the archives, pointing towards some crumbling scrolls. One speaks of the Aten, and a temple lost for centuries.

speaker: Djehuty
en: You think we worship an abomination. That I am damning my people.

speaker: Bayek
en: I cannot judge the path you took... not when mine is strewn with the dead.

speaker: Djehuty
en: I hope you find all you seek, friend.

speaker: Bayek
en: Finding Akhenaten's temple should lead me closer to the relic, and who has it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Djehuty said that a statue pointed him to the scroll?

speaker: Bayek
en: Doesn't seem to be pointing to anything in particular. Fine work, but this isn't the statue I'm looking for.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is it, the statue Djehuty spoke of. It's pointing high up on that shelf.

speaker: Bayek
en: The temple door is hidden.

speaker: Bayek
en: There is a scrawled note here!

speaker: Bayek
en: Tychon's men are also looking for Akhenaten's sanctuary.

speaker: Bayek
en: The light is shining there, that must be the way into the temple.

speaker: Bayek
en: The temple of the Aten.

speaker: Bayek
en: Living Aten who started life. Springing forth from the seeds of Amenhotep.

speaker: Bayek
en: Fed the son in the womb of his Mother the Great Royal Wife Queen Tiye. The beauteous, the long-haired.

speaker: Bayek
en: "The Aten. O sole god without equal." Your eternal resting place will live forever in the sands. You sleep with your father Amenhotep IV.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Royal Palace of Akhenaten. Watched over by the Akhenaten with his beloved wife, Nefer-nefru-Aten-Nefertiti.

speaker: Bayek
en: He denied the gods, all of them, including the Theban triad.

speaker: Bayek
en: So did the Son die, reborn as Re-Horakhty. Akhenaten, he who rejoices in the Horizon.

speaker: Statue of the Sole God
en: The statue that Bayek found in the temple to Akhenaten. The Pharaoh is holding something, something that closely resembles the artifact Bayek is seeking.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Pharaoh Akhenaten holding a relic! He worshipped it as the god Aten incarnate.

speaker: Bayek
en: If the Pharaoh had the relic then who has it now?

speaker: Bayek
en: Isidora must face the truth, this is not Amun's will. I need to speak to her, see how I can put the Pharaoh to rest.

speaker: Isidora
en: The curse yields another grim harvest. Did you find the answer in the farmlands?

speaker: Bayek
en: I found this.

speaker: Isidora
en: You dare to bring this into Amun's house?

speaker: Bayek
en: I found it in a temple dedicated to the apostate Akhenaten. What is he holding?

speaker: Isidora
en: He worshipped the disc of the sun, the Aten!

speaker: Bayek
en: It's not the sun he's holding. It is the relic I seek. This and the man who has it now are behind the curse, not Amun.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is this Amun's will? That he sends a heretic, the pharaoh who denounced him?

speaker: Isidora
en: Tuya! No! I sent her out into Thebes, told her she'd be safe... I did this.

speaker: Bayek
en: Akhenaten still walks. He is the key to the relic.

speaker: Isidora
en: I've been blind, hiding behind Amun's veil. Can this truly be?

speaker: Bayek
en: Isidora!

speaker: Isidora
en: This may not be the Amun, but Amun can stop him.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is not the gods... don't you understand?

speaker: Isidora
en: The Lord to the Limit still holds dominion over Thebes! And I am Amun's Wife. The people need to know that he still hears their cries.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then tell me his will.

speaker: Isidora
en: A single speck of dust from a God statue of Amun. it would purify Akhenaten's resting place in the valley, amongst the true Kings. But Tychon has taken everything of value from our temples and tombs, we have nothing left.

speaker: BayekL
en: This is not the first time I have heard of his thievery. His men harass the farmlands...

speaker: Isidora
en: While he lords it over us. Struts like a scorpion around Hatshepsut's temple.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then I will find him and his spoils.

speaker: Isidora
en: Bayek!

speaker: Isidora
en: The man who has your relic, what will you do when you find him?

speaker: Isidora
en: Then Amun watch over you.

speaker: Bayek
en: I must protect this great land. Alexandria is where the Snake thrives and Aya lives. I must find them both.

speaker: Bayek
en: May the gods help me, I am coming for you, Aya.

speaker: Bayek
en: Serapis... The Snake will get his answer.

speaker: Man 1
en: I wrote this!

speaker: Man 2
en: All writings are to be copied by the Great Library!

speaker: Man 1
en: You can't have it!

speaker: Man 2
en: I guess the works of Archimedes, Plato, Sappho and Aristotle won't have your scribblings to keep them company.

speaker: Man 1
en: Those are all in there?

speaker: Man 2
en: They are.

speaker: Man 1
en: I guess you can copy this, then.

speaker: Man 2
en: Too late, don't want it.

speaker: Man 1
en: Go ahead, take it.

speaker: Man 2
en: No!

speaker: Man 1
en: You can have it!

speaker: Bayek
en: How will I find Aya among all these scrolls?

speaker: Man 1
en: I find that Phanos talks too much.

speaker: Man 2
en: He has some interesting ideas. Very radical! It's almost alarming.

speaker: Man 1
en: You're right about that, but can't he express them concisely?

speaker: Phanos
en: The knowledge of the entire world is at your fingertips! Here, one can reflect upon the oppressive regime under which we find ourselves laboring! The Alexandrian Poets, have I mentioned them? ...Are a group of dramatic artists dedicated to promoting free thinking throughout the land, no matter what the pharaoh says. Despite the fact that the ruling pharaoh is given to arbitrary and despotic decrees, here at the library, we support free study! Any topic you like!

speaker: Bayek
en: Alright, Serapis. Now what? Where is Aya?

speaker: Phanos
en: Ah, Serapis. I wrote a tragi-comic-pastoral-epic centered on him.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah.

speaker: Phanos
en: You're Bayek, yes? Aya is eager to see you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is she safe?

speaker: Phanos
en: Quickly, follow me. I am sorry, my good fellow, you appear to be drunk. This library is for serious scholars only.

speaker: Phanos
en: She is in hiding.

speaker: Bayek
en: Who are you?

speaker: Phanos
en: Ah! Interested in Homeric verse, eh? This way, please.

speaker: Phanos
en: I am Aya's cousin, Phanos.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah, yes, Phanos, nice to meet you in person. Tell me what is happening with Aya, why are you being so discreet?

speaker: Phanos
en: Gennadios sent his men on a house-to-house search. Often, they drag people into the street and torture them for information. Typical of the system we live under.

speaker: Bayek
en: Gennadios?

speaker: Phanos
en: A monster. The phylakitai of Alexandria. He is ravaging the city to find her.

speaker: Bayek
en: And where is she now?

speaker: Phanos
en: I have a very powerful friend, Apollodorus. No doubt you have heard of him.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have not.

speaker: Phanos
en: You will. In any case, he made a hiding place available to Aya after she ran into trouble.

speaker: Bayek
en: But what happened? You do not answer me.

speaker: Phanos
en: It is a mess of political intrigue. She will explain all, fear not.

speaker: Man 1
en: Look! There's Phanos! He thinks he's a poet!

speaker: Man 2
en: The modern Sophocles!

speaker: Man 1
en: You must hear his epic poem, "Ode to a Nanny-Goat!"

speaker: Man 2
en: "...in Heat!"

speaker: Phanos
en: This is as far as I go. The way to Aya is found in the monument ahead. Right there. Have a little faith. I must get back. Good luck, my friend! Come visit me at the theatre! There are many things to do in Alexandria!

speaker: Aya
en: I missed you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Never again should we spend months apart. We only have each other. Without Khemu...

speaker: Aya
en: Ssh. Let us be together, us two, each to each.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have news.

speaker: Aya
en: You are scarred by justice.

speaker: Bayek
en: I bludgeoned Medunamun with this.

speaker: Aya
en: I hate that we have to do these things, but I am grateful that you did.

speaker: Bayek
en: If I am honest, I took pleasure in it.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have missed your touch.

speaker: Aya
en: I have missed touching you. I killed as well. Actaeon. I hunted him down and discovered a mask in his room. When he returned, I forced him to wear it. Then I thrust this knife through his eye slits.

speaker: Bayek
en: Aya.

speaker: Aya
en: But I was careless. Another of the masked ones tracked me to my home. He was even more difficult.

speaker: Bayek
en: We have one more. Then, we will be done.

speaker: Aya
en: Look at this. I took it from Actaeon. Apollodorus tells me it is a papyrus from the Royal Council. Which means the Snake is in Ptolemy's court.

speaker: Bayek
en: How does this Apollodorus know these things?

speaker: Aya
en: He has informants everywhere. Because of his work with Cleopatra.

speaker: Bayek
en: Cleopatra? She's been declared a criminal.

speaker: Aya
en: By her treacherous brother, yes. She plans to take back the throne. She wants the Snake dead as much as we do. And she trusts me. She gave me this to slit his throat.

speaker: Aya
en: It's an ancient blade that killed the tyrant Xerxes. A weapon of justice.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hahaha. Ingenious. I will go to the palace and discover who uses the seal of the Snake, and I will use this.

speaker: Aya
en: You'll find plenty of information in the Royal Scribe's office. He spends his time at the bath house. Go search the palace while he's away.

speaker: Bayek
en: And you?

speaker: Aya
en: I cannot leave here as long as Gennadios walks the streets. He is determined to kill me.

speaker: Bayek
en: In addition to the Snake, I will see what I can learn of this Gennadios and silence him.

speaker: Aya
en: Discover who the Snake is and show him the face of death. I'll met you at the Paneum when you have killed both the Snake and Gennadios.

speaker: Bayek
en: My heart aches until I see you again.

speaker: Aya
en: As does mine, my love.

speaker: Bayek
en: What's this?

speaker: Aya
en: That leads to the docks. I can't believe Phanos had you go through the pit.

speaker: Aya
en: Who is the Snake?

speaker: Bayek
en: I have yet to discover that.

speaker: Aya
en: The clue must be there in the palace. Search for the seal found upon the letter. It's too dangerous to leave this den as long as Gennadios and his men are searching for me.

speaker: Bayek
en: What in the name of Horus are the soldiers doing here?

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah! Aya's place.

speaker: Bayek
en: So much blood.

speaker: Bayek
en: I recognize this mask! It belongs to one of them.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is from Siwa. Aya kept it all these years.

speaker: Bayek
en: There is the man who tried to kill my wife. He should have known better.

speaker: Aya
en: My dearest.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Snake and Gennadios are dead. It was Eudoros. He died flailing in the baths.

speaker: Aya
en: I wish I had been there.

speaker: Bayek
en: My wife, my wife.

speaker: Aya
en: Forewarning, Bayek. Once we board this ship, there's no turning back. And we finish with the Queen on her throne, or each of our heads on a pike.

speaker: Bayek
en: I understand.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: It is rare that our cargo is a goddess. I apologize, we have no Kings or Queens on our ship, only gods and goddesses. So you should fit right in.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: All strange and terrible things are welcome.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Haha! I am worried that my quarters are not as comfortable as your palace.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Comforts? We despise them.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: My loyal shield boy, are you fit?

speaker: Damastes
en: I am in awe of this goddess. We must do her well. I can't believe she's on our ship.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Don't be fooled by her appearances. She needs us more than we need her. Aya, she is the real goddess.

speaker: Aya
en: There, in the distance.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Aya, already showing Bayek the best places to make love! Haha!

speaker: Aya
en: Enough, Phox. It is time to make war.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Brothers at sea! Today we carry a precious cargo, Queen Cleopatra, Great Lady in Perfection, She of the , with so many other cocksure titles my breath falters just to think of them! Now, if you'll direct your attention to the fore, you'll notice we have some friends bearing down upon us. Emissaries of our little Pharaoh! How kind of them to come forth! Let us welcome them, shall we? Warmly. With a ball of flaming refuse! Alalalala!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: This reminds me of a day twenty years back when I sailed with a group of pirates.

speaker: Aya
en: The Sicilians, was it?

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Ah, you heard the stories! That's right, I was a hired hull then, too. They were planning an inland raid on Antioch, and needed a few extra sails. It was my first and only dip into the life of a scoundrel. I prefer having a shred of decency. Only a shred.

speaker: Bayek
en: A shred can be hard to come by.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: He speaks? The Great Medjay.

speaker: Bayek
en: We are at sea, captain. Any greatness here is yours.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Ptolemites! Burn them! Alalalaaaaa! Send our arrows! Give them a taste of our fire!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Well done there! Seacraft comes naturally to you.

speaker: Aya
en: Easier to sail about when the sea is empty of ships trying to sink you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Won't a dozen missing triremes not alert the main fleet?

speaker: Phoxidas
en: It will take some time for them to find the wreckage. Onwards.

speaker: Damastes
en: Captain, my shield smells like charcoal.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Damastes, please, shut up! We press on.

speaker: Aya
en: With caution. We're not yet in calmer waters.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: There. More of Ptolemy's ships!

speaker: Aya
en: They'll want to box us in, and drive us against the shore.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: I see that look in your eyes. Why should we fight them? We can just barge on through and head straight for Alexandria.

speaker: Aya
en: I need to be sure the way is safe for Cleopatra. We have to do this!

speaker: Bayek
en: Those neket iadet (pieces of shit) will feel Ra's arrows!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Nice to hear Egyptian vulgarity on a Greek ship. Variety is what makes life interesting. And bloodshed! Alalalalaaaaa! The fleet awaits your command, Aya. Our catapults will fire upon your order. The fleet is at your disposal. One signal, and fire will burst upon them. Don't save our ammunition, Aya! Waste it, and them! Which one is the god of fire? Wake him up, and tell him it's time to unleash his wrath! This is not a battle we'll win without catapults! Alalala!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Take them, you slackers! Cut them off! Don't let them tack! Show no mercy! Send them to the abyss!

speaker: Aya
en: Is that all they've got?!

speaker: Bayek
en: We will burn like Ra!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: The air stinks. But not of oarsmen. Something else...

speaker: Aya
en: Hold, Phoxidas. Look there, at the water.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Two ships down! Damn Ptolemy. Did make a fine navy, though, I'm no poxy general with bottomless Roman coffers! Those were my men!

speaker: Aya
en: Easy, Phoxidas. We're not done yet. Our catapults will do their work. We'll make them pay!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: And dearly, by the balls of Zeus! I want the oceans turned dark with their blood! Damastes! Make the call, increase the rhythm!

speaker: Damastes
en: Yes, my captain! Alala!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: They've sent an Octareme! A floating city! Blast! Do the gods wish my fleet destroyed! Fickle Poseidon! This old fish will stick in your grizzled throat!

speaker: Aya
en: Bear up, old man, let's not offend the gods without cause!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: I'll take angry gods over docile ones right now. Open up the skies and rain some kind of shit down on us.

speaker: Aya
en: We have one last beast to hunt!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: And that is the game! Ah, the gods have such a humor, Aya. The day I met you, was the day danger found me again. Bayek, you are one lucky Medjay!

speaker: Bayek
en: As are we, lucky to be in your furious company.

speaker: Aya
en: Should I apologize for putting you back to work?

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Not at all, not at all! My blood runs quick now, with the roar of battle! By Zeus, I have not seen this much action since the earliest days of Cleopatra's father.

speaker: Aya
en: Let's not celebrate too roundly, old man. We're afloat in the sea with a cargo worth a thousand ships.

speaker: Bayek
en: I wonder if Cleopatra survived unmarked. Those clothes looked expensive.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: All are safe. We're done.

speaker: Damastes
en: Attacking starboard!

speaker: Phoxidas
en: We're not done! Ptolemy's malakia (assholes) are not dead yet! Get onto the reed boats. Use the fog to hide your escape. I will take care of this.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Destiny is a fucker sometimes, Aya. Enjoy the calm water. I will stay in the storm

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Agh! Flee, you fools! Don't mind the flaming arrows.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: Before battle, we will honor our goddess!

speaker: Aya
en: We cannot afford to spill any Roman blood.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: We cannot traipse into the palace armed to the teeth.

speaker: Aya
en: So we disarm, then.

speaker: Bayek
en: Armed or not, they will recognize her.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: For once, perhaps a Queen's entrance is unnecessary.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Act natural. We are meant to preside these grounds. Remember that.

speaker: Aya
en: Is our Queen alright?

speaker: Cleopatra
en: I'm fine.

speaker: Bayek
en: Who are we?

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Let me do the talking.

speaker: Roman soldier 1
en: None pass here without escort or a royal seal.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: I am the Nomarch of Heliopolis, these are my Phylakitai. We bring gifts from our local merchants.

speaker: Roman soldier 1
en: Let them pass, with an escort.

speaker: Roman escort
en: Follow me. This way.

speaker: Roman escort
en: Our Imperator appreciates the hospitality.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Have you received the warm welcome our Pharaohs always provide?

speaker: Roman escort
en: We will not celebrate until an alliance is sealed. Your vizier and your King have given us fine accommodations here in the palace. However, I cannot guarantee my Imperator will hold court with you.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: We understand, you are a good legionary. We will be patient.

speaker: Aya
en: Do you think we could take them all?

speaker: Bayek
en: Of course. We have better gods than them.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Are we there yet?

speaker: Roman escort
en: Guest legionary, at ease.

speaker: Aya
en: We are with the Great Pharaoh Ptolemy XIII, his envoys from the east, with gifts for your Imperator.

speaker: Roman soldier 2
en: Carry on, then. An offering?

speaker: Roman escort
en: Would you like me to help you carry your carpet?

speaker: Apollodorus
en: No, sorry, it is very sacred. Must be handled by the phylakitai. They understand the merchandise.

speaker: Roman Escort
en: Step aside, legionaries, official business for the Pharaoh.

speaker: Roman soldier 3
en: Who are you? You look like a hippodrome racer.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am. You should see me race.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: The Siwan Warrior.

speaker: Roman escort
en: Continue this way.

speaker: Roman escort
en: Guest legionary, at ease.

speaker: Caesar
en: We will stay in the palace until all politics are concluded.

speaker: Ptolemy
en: My palace is at your disposition, Gaius.

speaker: Flavius
en: Pompey was bound to be killed sooner or later.

speaker: Ptolemy
en: Pompey was your enemy, Caesar.

speaker: Caesar
en: He was my friend first. But you are right, Ptolemy, now let us discuss our alliance—What is this?

speaker: Aya
en: Forgive, Lord Caesar. We bring a gift from our Pharaoh, Cleopatra.

speaker: Ptolemy
en: Pharaoh? This is no gift, these are my sister's friends, it is a trap.

speaker: Caesar
en: In place of an envoy, Cleopatra sends a rug?

speaker: Cleopatra
en: I wonder how you all entered my palace?

speaker: Ptolemy
en: Guard! Kill these traitors!

speaker: Cleopatra
en: My wretched brother, he's let the wine go to vinegar... and my kingdom, to pieces.

speaker: Caesar
en: Great lady. Your audacity is equaled only by your beauty. Flavius, please.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: I can offer you what my brother failed at with me. Marriage. A true marriage, that is.

speaker: Ptolemy
en: If you ally with my sister, I will kill every last Roman in Alexandria.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Enough of the big words, little brother.

speaker: Caesar
en: Out, all. You will each be sent for when our congress is concluded. I wish to hear both Ptolemies' side of the story.

speaker: Bayek
en: Pothinus and Septimius, gone. We missed them.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: You will have your vengeance soon. This is Cleopatra's time, to officially become Queen.

speaker: Aya
en: If she is crowned Queen, we will be able to act from within. Crush the network.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Tomorrow, our Queen will have turned flattery into progress. We'll reconvene tomorrow at the Gardens. You proved your worth tenfold today. You truly are great Medjays.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Aya, dear one, thank you for coming. All is well with great Caesar.

speaker: Aya
en: Good, my queen. Soon, you will be on your throne.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Yes, yes. I must ask you a favor, though. The tomb... I feel Lord Caesar should have the honor to bear witness to the author of our kingdom, Alexander the Great.

speaker: Aya
en: You want to impress your new lover, I see. The tomb is sealed, no?

speaker: Cleopatra
en: It is, but by an act of Gaia, not by a royal decree. An earthquake in the early days of my father's reign has blocked the door. Do you know our metropolis well enough to suggest an alternate means of entry?

speaker: Aya
en: The underground.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: You would enter from below?

speaker: Aya
en: Well, I would find a way into the cisterns and canals below, work backwards and find a way to clear a passage into the tomb.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: That would solve our problem, but it seems idealistic.

speaker: Aya
en: Fortune favors those who ignore her. I'll examine the area around the tomb and figure this out.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Excellent. Rejoice.

speaker: Caesar
en: Did I tell you of the poet Catullus?

speaker: Cleopatra
en: I don't believe so.

speaker: Caesar
en: Another cur who made brief mention of me in . "I do not study overmuch to please and court you, Caesar, nor do I care much to know if you be black or you be white!"

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Impudent man! Plato's had merit.

speaker: Caesar
en: Yes, as pretty as their words can be, they are roaches by the best measure. Annoying, but easily handled.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: And how did you handle this one?

speaker: Caesar
en: I invited him to my house for dinner and drinks.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Know thy enemies as thy kin.

speaker: Caesar
en: And get them excessively drunk, when it needs be.

speaker: Roman soldier 4
en: It is a dead end, my lady.

speaker: Aya
en: I will double check. Ensure it is.

speaker: Roman soldier 4
en: Really? You insult our efforts. We tried everything.

speaker: Aya
en: I doubt it.

speaker: Aya
en: Broken spears. These Romans really did try everything.

speaker: Aya
en: They got it right, this way is completely blocked. That earthquake must have altered the structure. Hmm.

speaker: Aya
en: Strange. This wall is not as solid as it looks. Must be a way beneath. Around.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is a tighter squeeze than the caves west of Siwa.

speaker: Aya
en: We were smaller in those days.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where to now, my love?

speaker: Aya
en: It must be through the sewers. No one had the courage to plunge into Hades' rivers.

speaker: Bayek
en: We are the ones. After you, Aya.

speaker: Bayek
en: That was one big crocodile... May it's soul rest in peace.

speaker: Aya
en: About time you showed up!

speaker: Bayek
en: I was guarding your rear.

speaker: Aya
en: My rear is fine.

speaker: Bayek
en: The tomb.

speaker: Aya
en: Incredible. I hope you will provide me with a similar sarcophagus.

speaker: Bayek
en: Whatever you want, my love.

speaker: Aya
en: It is said that his sarcophagus is full of honey. Helps preserve the ka.

speaker: Bayek
en: Unbelievable.

speaker: Aya
en: Promise me you will bury me with my blade, so I can protect myself in the Field of Reeds.

speaker: Bayek
en: Promise.

speaker: Bayek
en: These markings along the bottom. They speak of Siwa... The vault... And a scepter that Alexander holds. Amun stands in a field of trees. Where a marked sphere meets its scepter. Man to King, King to God.

speaker: Aya
en: A marked sphere?

speaker: Bayek
en: What did you do with the orb I gave you?

speaker: Aya
en: I gave it to Apollodorus, he loves those things

speaker: Aya
en: We should let the others in.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am going to keep looking around, these paintings on the wall...

speaker: Aya
en: His birth. He was Macedonian. A Greek that became Egyptian, like me.

speaker: Bayek
en: He began the rule of our latest pharaohs. The dynasty of Ptolemies that have ruined Egypt.

speaker: Aya
en: He brought us Alexandria and brought us the Great Library where Aristotle mentored him.

speaker: Bayek
en: He abandoned education for bloodshed.

speaker: Aya
en: Hm. Not unlike us.

speaker: Aya
en: He was hailed as a savior when he first arrived in Memphis.

speaker: Bayek
en: He was a conqueror.

speaker: Aya
en: Here is when he crowned Ptolemy Lagos as his successor.

speaker: Bayek
en: So the rule of the Ptolemies began. And the Medjays ended. Medjays disappeared because of him.

speaker: Aya
en: You cannot blame one man for everything. All men are to blame. And women.

speaker: Caesar
en: Rex immortalis (Immortal king).

speaker: Apollodorus
en: The staff he is holding. The markings.

speaker: Caesar
en: Ever since I was a boy, I've idolized this man.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: He is similar to you.

speaker: Caesar
en: I wept at the base of his statue in Rome. At thirty, he was a god with an empire stretching across the known world. What have I done with my five long decades here on earth? Ita me di iuvent (So help me, gods)!

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Together, we can do more than Alexander did.

speaker: Caesar
en: Yes.

speaker: Bayek
en: How long before the Queen stops impressing Caesar and starts impressing us?

speaker: Aya
en: Our needs are hers as well. She will deliver.

speaker: Flavius
en: My Caesar. Our emissaries have been captured at the Southern Garrison of Alexandria. Soldiers have reported a hostile environment.

speaker: Caesar
en: Captured? Is this Ptolemy's diplomacy?

speaker: Cleopatra
en: I will send my guard. Greek soldiers will pass more freely in the city than Romans.

speaker: Aya
en: Let us settle this matter, my Queen.

speaker: Caesar
en: Flavius, come. Look, we have found the great King.

speaker: Bayek
en: Taking on the entire garrison will not be easy.

speaker: Aya
en: I may not have to take an entire garrison. A calculated kill and a shadowy presence will fare better.

speaker: Bayek
en: If you take on the armies of Ptolemy, I'd like to be at your side. I will distract the garrison with a brawl.

speaker: Aya
en: A fine idea. I will procure the emissaries.

speaker: Flavius
en: This is a truly wondrous sarcophagus. A tomb fit for a god.

speaker: Caesar
en: There must be more to this tomb than we see. We should set our soldiers to excavate it all.

speaker: Flavius
en: Yes my Imperator. What hidden powers lay amidst this tomb, we must possess.

speaker: Caesar
en: Yes, yes Flavius.

speaker: Flavius
en: I do feel privileged to be near this great man. It resonates, his aura is all-consuming.

speaker: Caesar
en: He is immortal. That is why.

speaker: Flavius
en: What he possesses is immortal as well.

speaker: Caesar
en: We should bring this sarcophagus to Rome!

speaker: Flavius
en: For now, I need to introduce you to some friends of mine. We have a lot to discuss.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: What do you think of this, Apollodorus?

speaker: Apollodorus
en: The scepter has value beyond words. I am sure of it.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: The gold in the sarcophagus would normally be enough to fund a war. These are offerings we can make to court Rome even more.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Tampering with the sarcophagus of a god-king is not the most fortuitous of acts.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: We are gods. It is our right to take what is ours. And it all is.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: As you say, my Queen.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: You should discuss with Caesar and Flavius. They will be wooed by riches and the glory of our great Alexandria. Bring them into the fold completely.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Aya, where are the emissaries?

speaker: Aya
en: I will get to it.

speaker: Flavius
en: The emissaries were meant to bring us an alliance with Ptolemy.

speaker: Aya
en: I will find them. In time.

speaker: Emissary
en: Somebody just kill me, finish the damn job...

speaker: Emissary
en: We need to alert Caesar.

speaker: Aya
en: What happened to you?

speaker: Emissary
en: ...Septimius. They are preparing a siege of the harbor, they want to take the palace.

speaker: Emissary
en: I will not betray Caesar!

speaker: Septimius
en: How many more heads must I chop off before Caesar understands?

speaker: Pothinus
en: This is futile. A change of plans. The Lion says we must march on the Pharos, and trap the Queen.

speaker: Emissary
en: Then they said... they left for...

speaker: Aya
en: Where? Where?!

speaker: Aya
en: This guy may have more valuable information. I need to bring him back to Caesar. I should find a horse.

speaker: Aya
en: You have loyal men, Caesar. Septimius plans on trapping you in the palace. You have no time.

speaker: Caesar
en: As I foresaw, war. Flavius, they want fire, let us burn the whole damn harbor. And if we change the Pharos' light, the rest of the fleet will know what to do. We will join them by chariot.

speaker: Flavius
en: Salve (Hail), Lord Caesar. I will make the order.

speaker: Apollodoros
en: My Queen. You should accompany me into battle.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: As these soldiers rip each other apart, I shall stay on my throne. I am Queen until a sword plunges through my heart. And even then, my blood will stay on my throne.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Good then, I stay. My life is yours to do with as you will.

speaker: Caesar
en: Now, the most crucial part of the plan.

speaker: Caesar
en: Put this into the brazier of the Pharos. She will accompany me through the city. Now, let havoc reign.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Aya, if you find my brother. (Make it so.)

speaker: Aya
en: I smell war!! We will put our Queen on the throne!
