speaker: Bayek
en: You are the only queen worthy of a throne!

speaker: Aya
en: Give me the powder. Caesar thinks a woman cannot do this job.

speaker: Bayek
en: Prove Caesar wrong, my love.

speaker: Greek soldier 1
en: Someone crush that tiny lotus.

speaker: Greek soldier 2
en: How did she get this far? Halt little woman!

speaker: Greek soldier 1
en: Just kill her so we can deal with the real problems: these Roman malakas (assholes)!

speaker: Aya
en: My blade is offended.

speaker: Guardian
en: I thought I heard a scarab crawling up my tower.

speaker: Guardian
en: You remind me of the Alexandrian whores I am gifted by the Order of the Ancients. Perhaps I will keep you around.

speaker: Aya
en: Now you've offended even my vulgar heart.

speaker: Guardian
en: This tower is Ptolemy's! Be gone!

speaker: Aya
en: This Pharos will only burn for Cleopatra.

speaker: Greek soldier 3
en: How in Zeus' name did you kill my captain?!

speaker: Bayek
en: By the gods, what has happened?

speaker: Padiaset
en: May you walk in the land of the Duat. Sobek be merciful to you. Ma'at find you worthy... Dua Sobek. Sobek the healer. He of the green plumage. The splashing one who came from the great goddess of sunlight... Forgive our weaknesses...

speaker: Padiaset
en: Medjay! You are late... Sehetep's men came to kill me.

speaker: Bayek
en: So I see. Not bad for a priest who abhors bloodshed.

speaker: Padiaset
en: I was not always a priest. I thought I had escaped all this...

speaker: Padiaset
en: Sehetep and I found faith together, joined the temple together. I knew he struggled, just as I did but... I have to stop him now.

speaker: Bayek
en: You cannot be seen to move against him. Not if the cult is to survive. A priest killing a priest looks bad. I should do this.

speaker: Padiaset
en: You are right. You will find him at the Northern Temple. I will meet you outside.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: There he is! For Sehetep! That is the meddling Medjay!

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Cut him off! Flank him!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: You are on the wrong side of Sobek, traveler! And in the wrong place!

speaker: Soldier 3
en: We are the future here. You should not have meddled!

speaker: Bayek
en: They were Sehetep's men. It is time to finish this.

speaker: Bayek
en: The main Temple of Sobek. Sehetep is inside. He will be well guarded.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Padiaset has gained the help of a strong ally.

speaker: Sehetep
en: The Medjay who raided our ship? Who is he?

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: He's not from Faiyum. A rogue traveller by all reports. One of the old kingdom some say.

speaker: Sehetep
en: The is dead. I don't care who he is. I will feed his infidel carcass to Petsuchos.

speaker: Sehetep
en: You filthy infidel! By what right do you touch me. I'm Sobek's chosen vessel. His right hand! Who are you!

speaker: Bayek
en: You're nothing but a murderer. And I am the hand of justice.

speaker: Bayek
en: It is done. Faith turns to treachery far too often it seems. I should meet Padiaset.

speaker: Priest
en: Do you think the Medjay will succeed?

speaker: Padiaset
en: Yes. He is a stranger yet Sobek guides him. When this is over, Sehetep's priests will seek forgiveness. Be stern, but treat them fairly. None of us is beyond temptation.

speaker: Priest
en: Yes Hem. Dua Sobek.

speaker: Bayek
en: Sehetep chose death.

speaker: Padiaset
en: Then it had to be. I lost a brother today. If I had acted sooner he might have been restored. Faith cannot be passive. This is my lesson. We will rebuild what has been damaged. But what of the soldiers? They had a hand in all this.

speaker: Bayek
en: They will always meddle. But stay strong. They know now not to mess with the temple. Sobek has warriors too.

speaker: Padiaset
en: You honor me, Medjay. May Sobek honor you.

speaker: Reda
en: If I told you that there is a reward to handle a group of bandits, would you be interested?

speaker: Reda
en: What do you think of addressing a bandit problem?

speaker: Reda
en: Bandits around these parts are getting cocky, making it harder to get my wares sold. You would do Reda a favor by handling them.

speaker: Reda
en: I heard there are bandits harassing people, likely with a reward already on their heads for dealing with them. I'd know, as I'm the one who put the reward out for them. Bandits are no good for business.

speaker: Reda
en: Medjay. Some of those neket iadet (piece of shit) bandits are raiding my customers!

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah. The stone circle. I brought Khemu here not so long ago.

speaker: Bayek
en: My son, you wanted the stars...

speaker: Bayek
en: The stone circles show the gods' place in the sky. And your grandfather once told me they also show our place in the world.

speaker: Khemu
en: I'm going to find every stone circle. The Sphinx and the pyramids, too. And I'll find my place.

speaker: Bayek
en: And you will have them.

speaker: Khemu
en: Papo (Father), why are there so many poor in Egypt? Yet those who don't belong here are rich.

speaker: Bayek
en: Egypt has forgotten who she is. Many chose wealth over honor. In the end, they got neither and lost justice as well.

speaker: Khemu
en: But we are Medjay. We will bring justice and honor back to Egypt.

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes, my son. We have not forgotten who we are. We will endure no matter our origin. Amun, the king of gods, divided into two forms as the great goddess of invisibility Amunet, and master of the wind. He upholds justice. Lord of the shadows and the silence, he comes at the voice of the poor. He hears the confessions of the humble and forgives them.

speaker: Khemu
en: Papo (Father), what is best in life?

speaker: Bayek
en: To seek justice and truth. To live with honor, to protect the weak and the poor. And to love your mother.

speaker: Khemu
en: My friend Kenon said it was to crush our enemies, and to hear the lamentations of their women.

speaker: Bayek
en: We are Medjay son, not barbarians. Apis, the bull god. He is the strength of the Pharaoh. Each year he is born as a calf with special markings. The Pharaoh finds this calf, and worships it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Medjay have a duty to the gods. We must be strong, and ready to fight. But we must only fight when it is just.

speaker: Khemu
en: I'll practice hard, Papo (Father). I want to be strong and hunt like you do.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are already better with your weapons than many men. You'll make a fine Medjay, son.

speaker: Khemu
en: Like mom says, "May your victories multiply!"

speaker: Bayek
en: The Divine Lion, the powerful one. Her breath formed the desert. The fiercest of hunters, she lead the armies of the Pharaoh into battle.

speaker: Bayek
en: Have you talked to this girl you like?

speaker: Khemu
en: I didn't say I like her. We were friends. But she's being strange and avoiding me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Maybe because she likes you too. We often do not say what we mean, it will come to you in bursts.

speaker: Khemu
en: Why would she avoid me if she likes me?

speaker: Bayek
en: This... is something your mother should explain. I am better with the stars. The Goat-Fish, called by the Greeks. The god has the head of a ram and the body of a fish. You see, even the gods do not always make sense.

speaker: Khemu
en: Papo (Father), you know how you're Egyptian and Mother is Greek. What if Egypt and Greece go to war?

speaker: Bayek
en: Egyptians and Greeks don't hate each other. We're all the same.

speaker: Khemu
en: It feels like they do. The priest in the temple schools said Greeks were destroying Egypt.

speaker: Bayek
en: He was wrong to say that. There is good and bad in everyone. You are a child of both Egypt and Greece. You are proof they don't hate each other. Ah, the Great Twins. To the Greeks, they are twin brothers. To the Egyptians, they are he-goats that rise from the underworld, bringing pestilence and protections. Even the gods have two sides.

speaker: Khemu
en: Papo (Father), when you met mother, how did you know she liked you?

speaker: Bayek
en: My heart lit on fire, of course! She smiled at me, and her eyes rendered me helpless.

speaker: Khemu
en: So if a girl likes you she smiles at you?

speaker: Bayek
en: Son, there are some things I can explain to you. The stars, how to fight. But this... is something not even the gods can tell. You will have to ask a goddess. Hathor, goddess of motherhood and joy. She is loved by all in Egypt, from the least to the greatest. Mistress of the West, she welcomes the dead to the afterlife.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is Horus, the Falcon. The Great Black One. God of the sky. The sun is his right eye and the moon is his left eye. Forever he flies across the heavens, making night and day.

speaker: Khemu
en: The eye of Horus is what the Medjay wear?

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes, Khemu.

speaker: Khemu
en: And the Pharaoh is Horus, right?

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes, my son. The Pharaoh is Horus in life, and Osiris in death. That is why the Pharaoh rules not only Egypt, but the whole world. Only a true Pharaoh though.

speaker: Bayek
en: Osiris was cut into fourteen pieces by his jealous brother, who scattered the pieces through-out the land. Osiris' wife Iset searched and found all the pieces except one.

speaker: Khemu
en: What happened to the other piece?

speaker: Bayek
en: It was eaten by a fish. It was his, ah... So Osiris was resurrected and became lord of the underworld.

speaker: Khemu
en: Oh... so he couldn't have children anymore, huh.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are growing up far too quickly. Osiris, the Father of Gods. Brother of Set who murdered him. It is said that Iset's tears for her beloved husband created the Nile.

speaker: Khemu
en: Papo (Father), why do people die?

speaker: Bayek
en: We are not gods. Everything must die. It is what Amun has ordained for us.

speaker: Khemu
en: Will we be together in the afterlife?

speaker: Bayek
en: Be brave and strong. Fight for justice. Do not lie. This is all anyone can do. Ma'at will decide if we're worthy to walk together in the Field of Reeds. I'm sure you will though. Your ka is good. , the two fish. Joined by the thread of this life, they are forever balanced between the afterlife and the underworld.

speaker: Bayek
en: Those are the Scales, called Khonsu. When we die, the goddess Ma'at weighs our hearts on them against her white feather.

speaker: Khemu
en: I remember this. If our hearts are pure and light, we walk in the Field of Reeds.

speaker: Bayek
en: Very good. You were listening. The Scales measure truth and justice. Which is why Medjay pursue these two things above all others.

speaker: Khemu
en: Papo (Father), how do you know if you're in love?

speaker: Bayek
en: Why Khemu? Do you think you are in love?

speaker: Khemu
en: I don't know. Love should feel good. You and mom are the only ones I love. But this hurts. Sometimes I can't even think straight.

speaker: Bayek
en: That sounds like love. It could be. I was once like that. I'm very sorry son. The scorpion goddess, Serqet. She protected Iset and Horus from jealous Set. She still protects against poisonous animals. But not love. Against that there is no protection, not even the gods can.

speaker: Khemu
en: Papo (Father), do you think I'll have many children?

speaker: Bayek
en: I hope you give your mother and I many grandchildren.

speaker: Khemu
en: I'll have to find a wife, then.

speaker: Bayek
en: You're young, my son. There's no reason to rush.

speaker: Khemu
en: I won't rush. But what if I already know.

speaker: Bayek
en: You need to learn how to be a Medjay first. Oh, Taweret, the hippopotamus who walks. Lady of the Birth House, she is the goddess of fertility and childbirth. Mistress of the Horizon, she brings with her the yearly flood of Ar.

speaker: Bayek
en: These stars are all we share now, Khemu. The Ankh gives me a view of your world, my son. It is carried along the Nile and through the waters of the sea of reeds, beyond the mouth of the gorges and forever. The Ankh is carried by Sheshat, goddess of writing. The great wife and daughter to Thoth, she reminds us that if we do not record that what was, it does not exist. The mistress of the House of Books holds you to the sky and oversees the most important of scrolls. I keep the Ankh of Ra, Horus and the sky, it reminds me we are always one, Khemu. Sheshat has stretched the cord and helped lay the great foundations of our Ankh. The symbol is buried with the skulls of falcons onto our rooftops and embedded in rock upon my heart.

speaker: Bayek
en: These stars are all we share now, my Khemu. But it is enough. Before us is the God who dared feast on Osiris, lover of thieves, cold and ruthless. Great Sobek, protector of the Nile, of Ra, of Horus, all the great gods confront you. I serve you yet I do not trust you. Anything is moral in your reign, for truth is something you ignore. Having eaten babies, sacrificed all for chaos and madness, you mate with the waves of the Nile and reign over all gods. And I will slay you if I must.

speaker: Bayek
en: That's the last one. I can take all the shards back to Siwa now.

speaker: Khemu
en: I'm going to find every stone circle. The Sphinx and the pyramids, too. And I'll find my place.

speaker: Bayek
en: My son. Your name, Khemu, means Egypt. Like Egypt, you have forever changed. The stars are yours now, and your place is with them.

speaker: Aya
en: Bayek, Caesar has been assassinated. Septimius is also dead. I have founded a bureau in the middle of Rome, yet no one knows of our existence. Like Amun, we are... the Hidden Ones.

speaker: Tahira
en: I believe in you.

speaker: Aya
en: The irony of freedom. We are free of each other, yet it brings me no happiness. We must move forward. Remain in our tempest of blood poetry. Despite it all, we dance and they die.

speaker: Aya
en: From darkness we have come, and in darkness we shall stay. Humans are not meant to last forever. But this Creed will. The Creed is the only immortal thing in the world.

speaker: Bayek
en: Go home. You are free.

speaker: Child
en: I don't want to go home by myself. I am scared.

speaker: Tahira
en: Should we take him to the bureau?

speaker: Bayek
en: No.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'll take you home.

speaker: Aya
en: Let nothing grieve you beyond measure. For your life is short, and time will claim its toll. But I am no longer who I was. I have renounced all love I once had.

speaker: Aya
en: I have renounced Aya. I have killed Aya. I am now the Hidden One known as Amunet.

speaker: Aya
en: May your victories multiply.

speaker: Khemu
en: Papo (Father)? Jump.

speaker: Bayek
en: Strange to see bodies left out like this. The embalmer must know more.

speaker: Bayek
en: It is a shame to see three dead left neglected. What happened?

speaker: Man
en: They were just brought here, Medjay. A family struck down by the sword... Only the daughter, Iras, survived. She carried them here one by one. Poor girl... all by herself now. A tragic story.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tragic, indeed. Where is she now?

speaker: Man
en: You can find her on the abandoned date farm near the road, where her family died.

speaker: Bayek
en: This Iras sounds like a woman worth meeting.

speaker: Bayek
en: Soldiers! They must be looking for Iras. Best lay low... and hope she does, too.

speaker: Soldier
en: Find the girl! Sophronios will reward us for today's work!

speaker: Bayek
en: She's in the well. I pray none of the soldiers heard that.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hail in peace, Iras. All I want is to speak with you.

speaker: Iras
en: The last man to say so murdered my family!

speaker: Bayek
en: I've come to help you, Iras.

speaker: Iras
en: How do you come to know my name?

speaker: Bayek
en: A priest told me of you.

speaker: Iras
en: My kin has owned this land for centuries, but left it barren until now. A soldier came to us, saying his master held a deed of sale. My father refused to concede the property. Then... Well, the rest is as you know it.

speaker: Bayek
en: What will you do?

speaker: Iras
en: The farm is my birthright. I will work it as long as I can.

speaker: Bayek
en: I can ensure you are not harassed by soldiers.

speaker: Iras
en: You may try. The villa they spoke of lies northwest of here, on the road to Alexandria. If you fail, tell the world I died preserving my family's legacy!

speaker: Iras
en: I can do this alone. I must carry out my father's dream. I do not ask your assistance.

speaker: Bayek
en: A letter on fine papyrus.

speaker: Bayek
en: Sophronios. Yet another man made butcher for the sake of wealth.

speaker: Sophronios
en: That farm should be mine by now! What is behind the delay? I don't want those merchants selling their filthy goods so close to my residence! Tell them I'll buy them out if they agree to take their business elsewhere.

speaker: Bayek
en: A pitiful end to a pitiful existence. I will tell Iras of this, if I see her again.

speaker: Iras
en: You came back.

speaker: Bayek
en: You will be bothered no longer.

speaker: Iras
en: You killed Sophronios?

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes.

speaker: Iras
en: I wish it had been I who slit his through.

speaker: Bayek
en: No, you don't.

speaker: Iras
en: ... My apologies. Truly, I am grateful for your help. My labor now is to rebuild the farm. But one day, I hope to return to Alexandria.

speaker: Bayek
en: Place looks deserted, where could he have gone?

speaker: Atut
en: Ooh, and you are...?

speaker: Bayek
en: Looking for the scribe.

speaker: Atut
en: You and half of Yebu. But no one's seen him since yesterday.

speaker: Bayek
en: I need to find him.

speaker: Atut
en: Well are you not strong and masterful? But why would I know where he is, I am only the one who pays his wages.

speaker: Atut
en: Wait, wait. I can't bear to see anyone so crestfallen. Try the hunter's village. He has a taste for exotic meat, if you know what I mean.

speaker: Bayek
en: No, no I don't.

speaker: Atut
en: Hippo, silly! Or maybe he headed to the papyrus village for more paper?

speaker: Bayek
en: Thank you, neb.

speaker: Atut
en: No, thank you... neb. And if you do find him, tell him he's fired.

speaker: Bayek
en: Signs of a struggle. This doesn't look good for the scribe, or the manifest.

speaker: Bayek
en: Bandits ambushed him. I need that manifest, they must have taken his belongings to their camp.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is the Lotus' ship, says it docked south of Yebu. Hopefully it is still there.

speaker: Bothered Woman
en: Those brutes are nothing but trouble, killing innocent merchants now!

speaker: Man on Shore
en: I am not sure that Lotus is innocent. But they can do what they want, no one would dare defy them.

speaker: Bothered Woman
en: They run the relic smuggling ring in Yebu?

speaker: Man on Shore
en: Everyone is a thief and a liar, the smugglers, the soldiers, all lining their pockets with blood money.

speaker: Bayek
en: Looks like it has already been boarded.

speaker: Bayek
en: All this food will go to waste.

speaker: Bayek
en: Pottery, very fine craftsmanship.

speaker: Bayek
en: They left the precious cargo untouched, looking for information, not profit.

speaker: Bayek
en: Pieces of broken relics.

speaker: Bayek
en: They tortured the sailors. For information?

speaker: Bayek
en: A lot of blood, someone dragged a body towards the edge of the deck. But where did it end up? In the water? A distraction maybe?

speaker: Bayek
en: There was a fight here. But someone dragged a body overboard to try and create a distraction. Did they make it to the shore?

speaker: Naked Man
en: That scallywag made off with my horse!

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone stole your horse? Did they come from the ship?

speaker: Naked Man
en: Yes! Some rust haired demon. Slithered from the river like an otter. Stole Ganymede and rode off towards the smuggler's village.

speaker: Bayek
en: And your clothes...?

speaker: Naked Man
en: A man can't even have a refreshing swim without thieves and vagabonds setting upon him. Now what am I supposed to do?

speaker: Bayek
en: Pray to Sobek to return your robes.

speaker: Bayek
en: Sutekh? Of course, how many more red-headed thieves are out there.

speaker: Sutekh
en: Thief! I'm no thief, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your uncle's auction? That fisherman's horse?

speaker: Sutekh
en: When you put it that way...

speaker: Bayek
en: I know you were on the ship. Who owns it?

speaker: Sutekh
en: Trouble dogs my every step. Am I responsible for those desecrators? Can I help it if one was my blood, another pays my wage?

speaker: Bayek
en: The ship, Sutekh!

speaker: Sutekh
en: Ah yes... Now that was an adventure! I was doing important work when we were boarded. Of course the crew panicked. Me, I was cool as a breeze at the Oasis. They were shouting for Merti to come out, but she was never on board.

speaker: Bayek
en: Wait? The merchant woman?

speaker: Sutekh
en: They searched the whole ship, killed anyone who got in their way. Until they found the captain. Dragged him out kicking and cursing. Killed his men in front of him until he told them where she was. I was the only survivor. Crocodiles below me, soldiers everywhere. I made my epic escape.

speaker: Bayek
en: By throwing a dead man in the water to distract the beasts. Now we have established your heroism, where is Merti?

speaker: Sutekh
en: Probably at her villa west of Yebu, the House of the Blue Lotus. It's by the pretty waterfalls. I could come with you? Fight by your side?

speaker: Bayek
en: I'll find her, and you keep out of trouble.

speaker: Sutekh
en: Of course, of course. I wonder... how would someone become a smuggler? I'm asking for a friend...

speaker: Bayek
en: Merti has visitors.

speaker: Merti
en: You? You're behind these soldiers at my door?

speaker: Bayek
en: You lied to me in Thebes.

speaker: Merti
en: Don't be naïve! I told you all I could. If I'd betrayed the others I would be dead already.

speaker: Bayek
en: The relic, you knew of its power!

speaker: Merti
en: No! Until you came to my shop, with bloody blades and a debt to be paid.

speaker: Bayek
en: A debt still owing.

speaker: Merti
en: Your Aten... we searched for it and it eluded us. A gilded myth of order, truth, justice, painted upon the walls of a Heretic's tomb. And after what happened I stopped looking.

speaker: Bayek
en: What happened?

speaker: Merti
en: Slaughter. Of some poor soul who tried to stop our desecration. I never knew who, didn't want to know. But I profited, and for that my heart is heavy.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then lighten it.

speaker: Merti
en: When you came to Thebes, I started searching again and I knew... someone had found it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Did you discover who has the relic?

speaker: Merti
en: That knowledge is shrouded. But it doesn't belong to men, it holds the power of the gods...

speaker: Bayek
en: And it won't be long before someone discovers how to harness that power completely.

speaker: Merti
en: Then Amun help us all.

speaker: Merti
en: This is where the trail led me, bought from an Antiquarian at the Necropolis of the Nobles.

speaker: Bayek
en: It says the relic was used in a Ma'at ritual, a ritual long forgotten...

speaker: Merti
en: Take it, I am ready to leave this cursed land.

speaker: Merti
en: The claimer of hearts comes for me!

speaker: Isidora
en: You are a traitor to our people!

speaker: Tahemet
en: You think I choose to do the Strategos' dirty work? I am not here freely, priestess.

speaker: Isidora
en: No, I'm sure he's paying you a pretty fortune for your betrayal.

speaker: Isidora
en: Do you care nothing for our ancestors? You rape their tombs, our history!

speaker: Tahemet
en: Athames will desecrate them without my help, at least this way I protect what I can.

speaker: Isidora
en: Protect? This is nothing but coin to you, more drachma to lose on the roll of a dice.

speaker: Tahemet
en: Priestess, I beg of you, be prudent. Trust me, justice will be served.

speaker: Isidora
en: These are not Pharaohs, they are our brothers, fathers... mothers. And trust me, our mothers will have retribution.

speaker: Tahemet
en: It seems to be habit of yours, Bayek. Arriving in the nick of time.

speaker: Bayek
en: Since when have you been working for tomb robbers, Tahemet?

speaker: Tahemet
en: Our little altercation at the gambling den didn't go unanswered. I had a choice, prison or helping soldiers catalogue the tombs.

speaker: Bayek
en: So you're the Antiquarian Merti spoke of? You've been researching the Maat ritual?

speaker: Tahemet
en: Ra's breath! Keep your voice down, if Athames' men hear I've been hiding things from them... Walk with me, and please try not to bring too much attention to yourself.

speaker: Tahemet
en: The Ma'at carvings are here, in the Necropolis of the Nobles. I haven't had a chance to review them all yet, but there are red-haired worshippers... an orb... wait, could they be Ramesses' descendants? Ah! Speaking of the great Pharaoh, I have a fascinating papyrus that...

speaker: Bayek
en: Perhaps I should see the ritual for myself.

speaker: Tahemet
en: Go carefully. The tombs are crawling with Athames' men. If you find the orb, I would love to see it? A relic passed down from the gods... a once in a lifetime find!

speaker: Bayek
en: Once...? I wish it were so.

speaker: Tahemet
en: May your blade be firm against your enemies, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone is using the orb, a Pharaoh?

speaker: Bayek
en: People, worshipping the relic? Priests of Akhenaten? But the rays are missing.

speaker: Bayek
en: Amun? Is this connected to the ritual?

speaker: Bayek
en: The descendants that Tahemet spoke of.

speaker: Bayek
en: A woman holds the relic aloft. The wife of the Aten? Nefertiti? Did it hold any real power then? Or was it just symbolic?

speaker: Bayek
en: They bring the descendants of Ramesses forward. But the ritual? It is not to the goddess of truth, but dedicated to another god. The twin plumes of Amun?

speaker: Bayek
en: The ritual restores Ma'at to everything under the sky. In honor of... the Lord of Thebes... And the God's Wife at his side. The priests have the relic... She's been lying to me from the beginning.

speaker: Bayek
en: Isidora, she brought down the Pharaoh's Curse. Tried to justify it to me. Isidora's argument with Tahemet... Could her own mother be buried here?

speaker: Man
en: Oh-ho! Medjay! Medjay! Come here! Medjay! Come and sit with me!

speaker: Bayek
en: What does this boatman want?

speaker: Man
en: Would you accept me as a travelling companion? I will take a new title! How about... Thutmose the Fearsome?

speaker: Bayek
en: I travel alone.

speaker: Thutmose
en: Of course. Have you heard about the palace? Crocodiles swarm its halls! Terrible! So many deaths. I am hired to slaughter the beasts, but someone is pouring blood in the water to frenzy them.

speaker: Bayek
en: And you want my help.

speaker: Thutmose
en: Yes, yes! You will shrug off a crocodile's jaws as most men would a 's. Kill crocodiles near the palace, and I will award you half my fee! What do you say, Medjay?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am good at killing crocodiles.

speaker: Thutmose
en: Ah, I knew I could count on you, Medjay the Mighty, Medjay the Majestic, Medjay the... mmm... Never mind! There is a hidden cave near the city's northern limit. Meet me there tonight. Wait... "Cave" rhymes with "brave"! Missed that one.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nek! (Shit!) The Crocodile God himself would cause less chaos. They are far more aggressive than usual.

speaker: Bayek
en: There. This pile of dead crocodiles should be high enough to please Thutmose. Pile... crocodile... Oh no, he's rubbing off on me.

speaker: Thutmose
en: Medjay, I am struck dumb with fear by what I see before me!

speaker: Bayek
en: The palace grounds are choked with Sobek's dead.

speaker: Thutmose
en: Did you see? In the pool... human body parts. Used to lure the crocodiles. Oh what horror!

speaker: Bayek
en: But why?

speaker: Thutmose
en: Who knows why evildoers do evil? I came just in time to see two people loading bodies onto boats and riding away.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will put a stop to this mischief.

speaker: Thutmose
en: Of course you will! And as your loyal companion, I will point you toward the mischief-makers. One went to toward the palace, and the other was headed for the mummification temple. Here is half my pay, as promised. I will meet you back at my boat! You have an easy life, yes? Go from place to place, see the world... One day I met an all-powerful Medjay, who kept the crocodiles away... Wait, do those rhyme?

speaker: Bayek
en: She is dumping body parts into the river to attract the crocodiles.

speaker: Bayek
en: One of the scum responsible for the crocodile attacks.

speaker: Bayek
en: Sobek's children will be more peaceful now.

speaker: Bayek
en: Those crocodile baiters are now bait. They were hired by a whole society of evildoers. And I will hunt them down, one by one.

speaker: Thutmose
en: A whole society! But how will you find them in all this vast land? It would be like chasing s down the Nile!

speaker: Bayek
en: I am a strong swimmer.

speaker: Thutmose
en: Of course you are. Those arms!

speaker: Thutmose
en: When you tell tales of this grand adventure, do not forget to mention Thutmose the Bold.

speaker: Thutmose
en: If you ever change your mind and seek a traveling companion, think of Thutmose the Faithful! Someday, everyone in Egypt will speak of you.

speaker: Selene
en: My dear, sweet, Halius... my poor, sweet baby. W-why are the gods so cruel? How could they do this t-to you? And now Icarius gone, t-too!

speaker: Bayek
en: Nebet, what grief has swallowed you?

speaker: Selene
en: We-we came to pay our respects to Icarus. To make an offering for him to ride victoriously in the next life, but, b-but...

speaker: Bayek
en: Shh. Gently now. I am listening.

speaker: Selene
en: Blue ruffians came at us! They jeered at our sorrow, and when my Halius spat in their faces they struck him down! They killed him! Then stole a bust of Icarus and ran. Now my younger son, Icarius, has gone off towards the shore, chasing after those blue demons. I fear he'll join his brother! We came to mourn our hero, and now my family is destroyed! Please, Medjay, save my last son! Don't let his life end today!

speaker: Bayek
en: Go bo back to your home. Try to rest. I will find him and bring him back to you.

speaker: Blue 1
en: Can't believe this idiot tried to attack all of us.

speaker: Blue 2
en: Shame you threw it into the river. Could have sold it for coin.

speaker: Blue 1
en: No! I'll give no respect to that bastard Icarus or the blasted Greens. Better to curse them in the upcoming races.

speaker: Blue 2
en: Can we ransom him back to his family? They looked wealthy.

speaker: Blue 1
en: Great idea! We'll send a message to his mother that if she doesn't pay his weight in drachma, he'll be joining his namesake in the mud.

speaker: Blue 2
en: Hahah! But for now let's drink!

speaker: Bayek
en: Quiet. I'm here to get you back to your mother.

speaker: Bayek
en: Time to go home.

speaker: Icarius
en: Wait, Medjay! These sagging cocks stole a bust of Icarus that my mother had prepared for the great charioteer's memorial. They threw it in the river to defile it and bring a curse upon the Prasina Green racers. We need it!

speaker: Bayek
en: Let me get you to your mother first...

speaker: Icarius
en: No! You must retrieve it before it is lost for good, or else my mother will never recover from her despair! I can make it home, but I am too weak to find the bust. Please, find the bust of my namesake, and bring it back to my mother.

speaker: Bayek
en: As I must.

speaker: Bayek
en: Even in death you ignite their passions, Icarus. Let's get you where you belong.

speaker: Selene
en: Medjay, you saved my son. A thousand thanks and more I owe you.

speaker: Icarius
en: The bust of Icarus! Now Prasina has a chance in the upcoming games.

speaker: Selene
en: You are truly a blessing sent from the gods! We will make an offering to Icarus and the Prasina Green in your name!

speaker: Bayek
en: There is no need for that. But if you must, make the offering for my son. I would have loved to show him the spectacle of the Hippodrome.

speaker: Icarius
en: We will. Come, mother. We have to prepare to deal with my brother's funeral.

speaker: Selene
en: Yes, of course. At least he is glad that the bust of Icarus was restored.

speaker: Raia
en: Pet xer ba-k ta xeri tut-k. Heaven hath thy soul, earth hath thy body. Ranofer, forgive me, I could not protect your earthly form.

speaker: Raia
en: Have you come to bring me home? Tell Anen I will not leave my brother.

speaker: Bayek
en: Anen did not send me, but these cliffs are not safe for a woman alone. There are bandits, soldiers...

speaker: Raia
en: Let them try and take me! It was one of those vultures who defiled Ranofer's tomb!

speaker: Bayek
en: Something was taken?

speaker: Raia
en: He was taken! The tomb desecrated and their bodies stolen. And his amulet, the scarab I made to protect him...

speaker: Bayek
en: I will find the neket iadets (pieces of shit) who did this.

speaker: Raia
en: His mastaba is at the top of the necropolis... but why would you help me...?

speaker: Bayek
en: Bayek. A man's Ka must not be trapped in the shallow sands.

speaker: Raia
en: So say the ancient songs. I am Raia. I will return to the village, find me there.

speaker: Bayek
en: They have plundered the tombs of the Pharaohs, and now they disturb our brothers... and sons.

speaker: Bayek
en: They took a hammer to the wall. No one would hear them this far from the village.

speaker: Bayek
en: What they didn't steal they destroyed.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ranofer was an embalmer, he prepared the dead for the Duat.

speaker: Bayek
en: A few ceremonial wrappings, they took the bodies. But where?

speaker: Bayek
en: A blacksmith's mark, an A within a sphere.

speaker: Bayek
en: The blacksmith in Set Ma'at... could he be the A on the hammer's handle?

speaker: Bayek
en: Raia? I was looking for the blacksmith...

speaker: Raia
en: He is in chains on his way to the fort!

speaker: Bayek
en: Why would they arrest him?

speaker: Raia
en: I ran down from the dunes, to tell him of your kindness and found their edict. But you also came looking for my husband?

speaker: Bayek
en: A hammer was used to break the walls of your brother's tomb.

speaker: Raia
en: The handle, this is... Anen's mark. You think he...? Never. Ranofer was my only blood.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then why take an innocent man?

speaker: Raia
en: You are not a calf, Bayek, guileless at the teat. The soldiers care only for their own pleasures...

speaker: Bayek
en: ...and they rob our ancestors to do it. I will find the truth of this, Raia.

speaker: Raia
en: Amun lead you to it, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: The soldiers arrested the blacksmith, took him to their camp in the Valley of the Kings.

speaker: Blacksmith
en: I told you. I don't have your tools. Liberate them from those thieving bandits!

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you the blacksmith Anen?

speaker: Blacksmith
en: Whatever you need of me, neb (sir), I will trade for my freedom.

speaker: Blacksmith
en: A bold rescue from under the noses of those Greek shiteaters! So what do you need of me?

speaker: Bayek
en: Information. A hammer with your mark was used in a tomb robbing.

speaker: Blacksmith
en: Thoth's cock, perhaps because my tools were stolen by those dung beetles hiding in the cliffs. But you look like a man who could scare the bull from his cow. Come, let's get back what's mine.

speaker: Bayek
en: Wait! They have more than your tools, they have taken the dead... your kin Ranofer.

speaker: Blacksmith
en: I'll wear their testes as a neckless!

speaker: Bayek
en: Return to your wife, I will go. She cannot lose both her men.

speaker: Blacksmith
en: You're right, make them piss themselves before Osiris.

speaker: Bayek
en: They do not fear the gods, they will fear me.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is monstrous, burning the bodies to get to the treasures.

speaker: Bayek
en: It will break Raia's heart to know his fate. But I should return the amulet.

speaker: Blacksmith
en: Back in one piece, eh? Made those cockless dogs answer to the Ram God?

speaker: Bayek
en: I found the bandits, but I could not save your brother's earthly form, Raia.

speaker: Raia
en: Thank you, any more was too much to hope for.

speaker: Bayek
en: Here, the amulet.

speaker: Raia
en: No, it was for him, to aid his passage in the Duat. Keep it, perhaps it can protect you?

speaker: Bayek
en: The weigher of hearts will not punish him for the crime of others, Raia.

speaker: Blacksmith
en: We will see him again in the eternal reeds, my wife.

speaker: Raia
en: This gives me comfort. Em hotep, Bayek.

speaker: Ibi
en: Bayek, the Medjay from Siwa? I recognize you. Please, my daughter has got herself in terrible trouble.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ibi! You're far from Siwa my friend.

speaker: Ibi
en: Yes, Medjay. I could not stay there after what happened. I cried for the people we left behind.

speaker: Bayek
en: What is wrong with your girl, Apate, yes?

speaker: Ibi
en: A few months ago, she met a Greek lad. He was so earnest and idealistic... He filled her heart with rebellion. Convinced her to help him cut out the Roman canker growing in our world. They were captured attacking the fort.

speaker: Bayek
en: Apate strode the same sands as Khemu. Our ancestors shared the wahat (oasis). Where do the Romans have her now?

speaker: Ibi
en: There is a place on the road to Cyrene where they inflict the cruelest punishment. A road lined with dead rebels.

speaker: Bayek
en: Don't worry. I will bring Apate back to you, Ibi.

speaker: Bayek
en: No! Apate of Siwa? Her and Khemu would hunt together in the scrubland.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is the crucifixion site, Apate must be here somewhere.

speaker: Roman Soldier 1
en: This is what happens to filthy rats who betray the Republic!

speaker: Apate
en: Murder me, I don't care, but you stand no chance against Egypt.

speaker: Roman Soldier 2
en: Stealing silphium is a serious crime, punishable by death.

speaker: Apate
en: Silphion should help the people, not fat patricians in Rome.

speaker: Roman Soldier 1
en: I should cut your tongue out, that'll keep you quiet.

speaker: Roman Soldier 2
en: Be thankful Brutus Severus hasn't taken you back to the fort for his amusement.

speaker: Apate
en: Tell Severus from me, he's the legion's best cocksucker. All the guards say so. We will not bow before you, neket iadets (pieces of shit). Not in Egypt and not in Cyrenaica.

speaker: Roman Soldier 2
en: You'll scream when we hammer the nails in. They all do.

speaker: Apate
en: Death before defeat!

speaker: Roman Soldier 1
en: The fight will desert you after two days on the cross. You'll be begging us to kill you. Apate, if your people don't end their rampage, we'll decimate them.

speaker: Apate
en: For each of us you kill, there will be a hero in the Duat.

speaker: Roman Soldier 1
en: my arse! You're just a few Siwan troublemakers.

speaker: Apate
en: Bayek of Siwa? Can that be you?

speaker: Apate
en: Bayek? Saved by my childhood hero, incredible, it has been so long.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let's get free of this barbaric place first.

speaker: Apate
en: Those neket iadets (pieces of shit) will send reinforcements. We shouldn't linger here, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: I feared it was you, Apate.

speaker: Apate
en: I could not stand by as the Roman contagion spread. You heard what they did in Siwa, Bayek?

speaker: Bayek
en: I saw it. You attacked the fort?

speaker: Apate
en: Yes. The captain of the Prasinos camp, Severus, is a psychotic butcher. Everyday finding new, sick ways to inflict suffering on our people. Then at night he goes who knows where to plot and plan. While Severus lives the rebellion is nothing but sound and fury.

speaker: Bayek
en: It was your strength and spirit that Khemu loved the most.

speaker: Apate
en: My days were filled with freedom then. Your boy and I hunted, laughed, lived. That is all I want for my children.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then I will kill the torturer, Apate.

speaker: Apate
en: Look him in the eyes and make him understand that he's a shit eater. I will gather my friends. If you attack the outpost, we'll join you.

speaker: Apate
en: Find that shit eater. I will round up what's left of the freedom fighters.

speaker: Apate
en: That butcher Severus must not live! Fortune favors the brave!

speaker: Severus
en: Golden is Apollo's mantle and golden is its clasp. Grant me wisdom to see our enemies among the reeds, and strength to cut them down. I give you my faith, I give you my arm, I give you my righteousness in service of Cyrenaica. The enemies of Rome will fall before us bright one. I will punish them for you and the huntress. I prostate myself before you Apollo Phoebus, bringer of light. For I am your servant. Away, away with the wicked!

speaker: Bayek
en: The Legion is losing its greatest neket iadet (piece of shit), Severus.

speaker: Sminthos
en: Bayek!

speaker: Bayek
en: Mouse?

speaker: Sminthos
en: They are going to kill me!

speaker: Roman Soldier
en: Shut up, you're convicted of murder.

speaker: Sminthos
en: They have the wrong man! I's as innocent as a babe.

speaker: Bayek
en: What trap has the Mouse fallen into now? Hold on Mouse!

speaker: Roman Soldier
en: Stop your mouth or I'll stop it for you. Dead man walking. This murderer will be punished with the full weight of Rome. The murderer of the money lender Paulus Aurelius has been apprehended. The streets of Cyrene are safe again.

speaker: Sminthos
en: Thank you sir Bayek! Get me out of this bloody cage! I'm hurt! They accused me of murder? Me? I value life above all...

speaker: Bayek
en: Of course you do. Don't worry you're safe now.

speaker: Sminthos
en: Thank you, Sir Bayek.

speaker: Sminthos
en: There is a real murderer out there. He is killing my friends!

speaker: Bayek
en: Slow down and tell me what happened, Mouse.

speaker: Sminthos
en: I was at the bathhouse meeting some associates, and suddenly a legion accosted me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Didn't you plead your innocence?

speaker: Sminthos
en: They wouldn't listen! They accused me of killing Paulus Aurelius, the money lender, gutted like a pig. Red hair in his fist... not my hair. I met with him, yes, but when I left the baths he was very much alive, drinking and whoring as usual. I am many things, but not a killer.

speaker: Bayek
en: It is alright, Mouse, I believe you.

speaker: Sminthos
en: But the Romans will not believe a cripple and an Egyptian.

speaker: Bayek
en: Have faith. Stay low and wait for me at the gardens of the Temple of Zeus.

speaker: Bayek
en: There may still be clues to the real killer at the bathhouse. I know Sminthos is not the murderer, but I must discover who is.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Romans have closed off the baths, I should look for another way in.

speaker: Bayek
en: So this is where he was murdered.

speaker: Bayek
en: The murderer left a message. "They will all pay for their crimes." Someone is seeking justice.

speaker: Bayek
en: A pin from a dress? Could the murderer be a woman?

speaker: Bayek
en: A scattering of beads. Someone broke their necklace, did Paulus Aurelius struggle with a woman?

speaker: Bayek
en: This strigil has blood on it, could be the murder weapon.

speaker: Bayek
en: Red hair, but it is horsehair. Maybe from a wig. That is why Sminthos was falsely accused.

speaker: Bayek
en: The body has been moved. I need to find it.

speaker: Bayek
en: The stench of death and something else, perfume? What will you tell me, Paulus Aurelius? Something is stuffed down his throat. A note.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hmm. "I will cleanse Cyrene of the hedonists. My next tragedy will strike down Cyrene's greatest Actor - Metrobius." And it is signed. Vesta? Vesta, Vesta... what is your problem with pleasure seekers? I need to find this actor before this murderer strikes again! Phanos would be appalled if an actor were to die.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why is Vesta targeting these men? Could she be a prostitute killing off her clients?

speaker: Bayek
en: I need to get rid of that lion before I can confirm my suspicions. But I think that is Vesta's second victim.

speaker: Man 1
en: Yes! The Egyptian has no fear! He will save you, Metrobius.

speaker: Man 2
en: Metrobius is dead you fool, but at least we stand a fighting chance.

speaker: Man 1
en: Our play will never see the light of day! My first big part, and it's ruined, ruined!

speaker: Man 2
en: Metrobius would have wanted us to continue performing it!

speaker: Man 1
en: Metrobius is a Martyr for Art and Theatre. Our play will go on.

speaker: Bayek
en: Metrobius, the murderer's second victim, there's not much left of him.

speaker: Bayek
en: Another note. "Metrobius took his final bow. Only the Whorer remains and he will die at the Wolf's den." This Vesta has a flair for the dramatic. The whorer's wolf's den must be the local brothel.

speaker: Bayek
en: My instincts were right, Vesta's a prostitute. But she is looking for her father, I only hope I find him before she does.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm too late!

speaker: Bayek
en: Another note, this must be the whorer. "Father you die. You will be quiet now mother?" By the gods, this Vesta is insane.

speaker: Vesta
en: That's it mother, it's all finished and I will join you and father soon. I cannot stop and I will not live without her.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why did you kill them all? I have tasted darkness too, but you are mad.

speaker: Vesta
en: You cannot understand what it is to be born into flames. To be born a piece of dust. I am ash.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hmm, woah. Vesta was not a prostitute but the forgotten son of one. I hope the Duat figures you out. I should return to Sminthos.

speaker: Sminthos
en: Bayek! Did you find the killer?

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes. The son of a prostitute. When his mother died, terrible grief overtook him. He believed her ka would not let him rest until he found his father.

speaker: Sminthos
en: He's dead?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am sorry, Mouse. He could not be reasoned with. I have his letters, the story they tell is a tragic one.

speaker: Sminthos
en: Poor boy, such sadness.

speaker: Bayek
en: What will you do? Won't the Romans be searching for you?

speaker: Sminthos
en: I have a plan, a new life in Apollonia. Where you can taste the sea it is so close. Find me there if you can, Sir Bayek?

speaker: Bayek
en: Good luck, Mouse.

speaker: Woman
en: This blasphemy will not stand!

speaker: Man 1
en: Where is the coward that did this?

speaker: Woman
en: Great cat goddess Bastet save us. Do not take vengeance!

speaker: Man 1
en: I will not rest until we find this fiend.

speaker: Man 2
en: Though I guess we can be thankful he was not crucified. Bloody Romans, they do not understand our ways.

speaker: Bayek
en: There is no way all this blood is from one cat. I still do not know what happened here. I should investigate further.

speaker: Bayek
en: A Roman soldier, dead. Only one wound. He bled out quick. Nek. The cat was attacked by the Roman soldier. Whoever did this was protecting them.

speaker: Bayek
en: Bloody footprints leading to the north. The trail goes to the north. I must follow it. These Egyptians are already looking to fight. I must find whoever did this.

speaker: Bayek
en: The blood trail ends here. The culprit must be close.

speaker: Bayek
en: I see your cat is injured.

speaker: Khalid
en: It is not mine. Cats belong only to Bastet. I am only her instrument, defending her from Roman scum.

speaker: Bayek
en: You took the life of a Roman because he killed cats, and now you risk a riot in Alexandria.

speaker: Khalid
en: Bastet swung her fury through my arm. I am her servant!

speaker: Bayek
en: I know a High Priestess who would love your... dedication. It would be best for you to serve Bastet at her temple in Bubastis.

speaker: Khalid
en: I have served Bastet my entire life. To serve her better would be an honor. Lead on, brother.

speaker: Bayek
en: We should keep our voices down. We don't need any untoward attention.

speaker: Khalid
en: I know the way! Let us fly. It will get me closer to the goddess faster.

speaker: Khalid
en: Roman soldiers, terrified of our tiny little kittens.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is there no end to your speech?

speaker: Khalid
en: Egyptians! Rise up! Retake the city in the name of Bastet!

speaker: Bayek
en: Serapis save me.

speaker: Khalid
en: Look at these girdle-wearers! It is like they think they are soldiers.

speaker: Bayek
en: Enough! We're almost through.

speaker: Roman Soldier
en: You want to see what a sword can do to you, scum? More than happy to demonstrate!

speaker: Khalid
en: Right, let us go.

speaker: Khalid
en: Roman cat-kickers! How would you feel if I kicked your gods!?

speaker: Bayek
en: Stay quiet!

speaker: Roman soldier
en: What was that, dog?

speaker: Bayek
en: Go to the temple of Bastet. Only, I beg you, not to mention my name to the priestess.

speaker: Khalid
en: I could, Medjay... But think of how a return to Alexandria might be served by the great warrior Khalid!

speaker: Bayek
en: I believe this is what the gods want you for.

speaker: Khalid
en: If the gods will it, it will be done. Safe travels, Medjay. May Bastet watch over you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Keep going...Keep going. Gods watch over fools.

speaker: Man
en: Thief! Thief! Medjay! Catch that little good-for-nothing. Hurry! Every (poor peasant) around here thinks they deserve a handout... Bring that neket iadet (piece of shit) back here! He will get a taste of the lash for every bite of fruit he steals. Why are you still talking to me? Go, go!

speaker: Bayek
en: The further you run, the worse it will go between us!

speaker: Child
en: A Medjay should be quicker than you!

speaker: Bayek
en: How can a child so small run so fast?

speaker: Bandit 1
en: What'd you bring us today, guttersnipe?

speaker: Child
en: An apple.

speaker: Bandit 1
en: An apple? Boy, get back out there and find us something heartier. A few apples aren't worth the cost of keeping you. Should we have Mistress Gaia deal with him?

speaker: Child
en: No, no!

speaker: Bandit 2
en: We will decide what to do with you later.

speaker: Bandit 1
en: Damn gutter brats. So unreliable.

speaker: Bandit 2
en: What do you expect? They ran wild in the streets for years.

speaker: Bandit 1
en: Quit your mewling!

speaker: Child
en: Hit them hard! Go, Medjay! Get them! Punch them in the teeth!

speaker: Child
en: You did it! I knew you could do it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Did you bring me here to get rid of these bandits?

speaker: Child
en: Sure did! I'm extremely smart – everyone says so.

speaker: Bayek
en: How did a smart boy like you get tricked into working for bandits?

speaker: Child
en: I don't work for them! This mean old lady locked up a bunch of us kids. She makes us steal for her.

speaker: Bayek
en: Locked up?

speaker: Child
en: Yeah. My sister was going to save us, and she said to meet her in the shipyard by the river, but she never came! Will you look for her? I'll steal you an apple...

speaker: Bayek
en: You don't need to buy my help. It is yours for free. What is your sister's name?

speaker: Child
en: Kawit. And mine's Iphri. If you find Kawit, tell her I'm mad at her!

speaker: Bayek
en: That ship will not sail any time soon.

speaker: Bayek
en: There's the mast from the burnt ship. A colorful sail. Unusual.

speaker: Bayek
en: They kept the children caged.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah. The ship was dry-docked when it caught fire. Traces of oil. Hmmm.

speaker: Bayek
en: Must have been a blaze to make Ra jealous.

speaker: Man
en: Yes, they say the ship caught fire in the harbor last night.

speaker: Bayek
en: Know how it happened?

speaker: Man
en: No, I am just here to repair it.

speaker: Bayek
en: An oil-seller. He may have seen Kawit.

speaker: Man
en: You break my pots, I break your face! Keep your distance or I will break your face!

speaker: Bayek
en: Easy now. Did you see a young girl around the shipyard yesterday?

speaker: Man
en: I see lots of girls, most not worth looking at twice.

speaker: Bayek
en: They would likely say the same of you.

speaker: Man
en: If it is information you want, you have just tripled its price.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'd rather throw my coin-pouch in the river.

speaker: Man
en: Back off, I tell you! I despise thieves and loiterers. Get away from here before you break something.

speaker: Bayek
en: There must be another way to make him talk.

speaker: Man
en: Stop, you brute! I will talk!

speaker: Man
en: By the limbs of Osiris, you are a cruel man!

speaker: Bayek
en: What happened with the girl?

speaker: Man
en: I looked at her twice. The second time, she was stealing my biggest jar of oil. She vanished like a demon in daylight. When I came back, ruffians were destroying my stock! May the lot of you sink to the bottom of the Nile.

speaker: Bayek
en: I think I understand what happened here.

speaker: Bayek
en: Kawit stole an oil jar from that oaf of a merchant, then hid until nightfall. Under cover of darkness, she spread oil on the ship and set it aflame. The blaze spread to the whole vessel. While the ship burned, Kawit freed the children held on the docks. But the bandits must have caught her. Whoever owns this ship was responsible for the kidnappings.

speaker: Bayek
en: A child hiding. And there's that colorful sail. The bandits are out searching for the child.

speaker: Bandit 1
en: That little witch who set the fire probably freed them.

speaker: Bandit 2
en: Should we set the bushes on fire?

speaker: Bandit 3
en: Where are those little shits?

speaker: Bandit 1
en: Birds hiding among reeds—we'll scare them out.

speaker: Bandit 3
en: If we don't find those kids, Mistress Gaia'll have our hides!

speaker: Bandit 2
en: They're children. They can't have gotten far.

speaker: Child
en: The bandits won't stop looking for me! I can't get away!

speaker: Bayek
en: I will see to it. Cover your eyes.

speaker: Bayek
en: I need to talk to that child.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your brother sent me here. Where is Kawit?

speaker: Child
en: They took her and everyone else to a house in the city. Some rich lady named Gaia owns it. It's by the temple of Hathor. Will you save my family?

speaker: Bayek
en: By the Mother Goddess, I will.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: So what do you miss most about your family?

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Oh, Mother's cooking, definitely. She makes a delicious mustard partridge. She always took such good care of us. Sometimes I wonder why I left home.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: I know why I left home.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: I'd hate to see what she'd think of me now.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why would the guard carry this key? It must unlock something important.

speaker: Bayek
en: Gaia kept up quite an exchange of letters. I could learn more about her reading these.

speaker: Kawit
en: Over here!

speaker: Bayek
en: I do not have the key to your cell.

speaker: Kawit
en: Then go get it from one of those sun-struck cows of bandits! Go and get the key from those wax-for-brains! I said that one of those dung-stuffed bandits has the key! Go kill them and get it! The key! Go... and get... the key!

speaker: Bayek
en: Why would the guard carry this key? It must unlock something important.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have the key.

speaker: Kawit
en: Then use it, by Amun's hairy nipples!

speaker: Kawit
en: Live forever! Did Nef send you?

speaker: Bayek
en: No, young Iphri did.

speaker: Kawit
en: Where is he?

speaker: Bayek
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Child
en: I followed you the whole way!

speaker: Kawit
en: Take Matia home. Go!

speaker: Bayek
en: Hey, why don't you go with them?

speaker: Kawit
en: I'm going to track down the Roman bitch who did this to my family. If you want to help me kill her, meet at the House of Nef.

speaker: Bayek
en: I should find this Zervos, and see what he knows about Sefetu. See if he is connected to the Scarab. I will ask among the merchants. See which are friendly to him.

speaker: Merchant 1
en: You look like a strapping sort. Looking to improve your armor?

speaker: Bayek
en: Long night?

speaker: Merchant 1
en: Very. Sorry. What are you interested in?

speaker: Bayek
en: At the moment, I'm looking for Zervos.

speaker: Merchant 1
en: The harbormaster? Of course. Zervos is... uh... away.

speaker: Bayek
en: Away?

speaker: Merchant 1
en: Yes. Uh, he's gone to Letopolis. Attracted by the promise of a new life.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then he's not dead.

speaker: Merchant 1
en: Dead? Why would you think he was dead?

speaker: Merchant 2
en: Finest metal work in Sais! Good day to you, neb. Any metal work I can do for you this day?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am just looking. You know about a man named Zervos?

speaker: Merchant 2
en: The harbormaster? Ahh... Why are you asking about him?

speaker: Bayek
en: I've heard he's missing. In hiding? Perhaps dead?

speaker: Merchant 2
en: What would you do if Sefetu put a price on your head?

speaker: Bayek
en: I see. I am not one of Sefetu's men.

speaker: Merchant 2
en: I don't know anything about it. I don't stick my neck out. I have nothing to tell you.

speaker: Merchant 3
en: What are you looking for today?

speaker: Bayek
en: The harbor master. Zervos.

speaker: Merchant 3
en: Do not ask about him! The guards killed him!

speaker: Merchant 4
en: Care for some dates? Finest in the area. Same ones the brewery uses for its famous beer.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm just looking. You know about a man named Zervos?

speaker: Merchant 4
en: Zervos? The harbormaster is dead.

speaker: Bayek
en: Good day for business?

speaker: Merchant 5
en: Not half bad! What are you looking for today?

speaker: Bayek
en: For Zervos, the harbormaster. Do you know where to find him?

speaker: Merchant 5
en: You are looking for who? Why? I don't know him! I heard he was dead! Why are you bothering about him? He was a good man!

speaker: Bayek
en: A good man? So you do know him.

speaker: Merchant 5
en: I don't! I just heard others say it. Leave me be!

speaker: Merchant 6
en: You want some fish, or what?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am looking for Zervos, the harbor master.

speaker: Merchant 6
en: Oh! I heard Sefetu gutted him.

speaker: Bayek
en: Everyone has a different story about Zervos. I wonder if one of them knows more than they are telling me.

speaker: Soldier
en: No one on the streets after dark! By order of Sefetu! By order of Sefetu, a curfew is imposed in town after dusk!

speaker: Man
en: How are you keeping?

speaker: Zervos
en: As best I can. I'm tired of hiding.

speaker: Man
en: There is a stranger in the market asking about you.

speaker: Zervos
en: What? Who is he? Is he one of Sefetu's curs?

speaker: Man
en: I do not know. I do not think so. He wears an old-fashioned badge. But he does look dangerous.

speaker: Zervos
en: Badge? What kind of badge?

speaker: Man
en: A Medjay badge, I think.

speaker: Zervos
en: A protector? Hmm. Keep a watch on that one.

speaker: Zervos
en: We are not fighting men. You can take the bounty off my head.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm not one of Sefetu's men. I'm searching for Zervos, on behalf of Harkhuf.

speaker: Zervos
en: Good. I am Zervos, mighty harbormaster of Sais. Heh. Forced to hide on my own docks.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why is Sefetu after you?

speaker: Zervos
en: That dog. He is strangling the whole town!

speaker: Woman
en: Taxes us to death!

speaker: Man 1
en: He burned my cousin's farm!

speaker: Man 2
en: That's right!

speaker: Zervos
en: I've been doing what I can. Helping people hide their imports and exports. What Sefetu does not see, he cannot tax.

speaker: Bayek
en: And he figured it out.

speaker: Zervos
en: His men raided my business and my house, but I hid my records on my felucca. If they haven't found my boat yet, they soon will.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Zervos
en: My felucca is tied up at the Sais docks. I would prefer to have it back in one piece, but if you must destroy it... Go carefully. Sefetu's men watch the harbor like hawks!

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: You find anything yet?

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: No, that blasted Zervos hid his papers as well as he hid himself.

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: Keep looking. If we find something to hang him on, Sefetu will reward us!

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: And if we don't find anything?

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: Then you get to tell Sefetu. He won't be pleased, Serapis knows.

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: I'll keep looking.

speaker: Bayek
en: You needn't hide any longer. I secured your felucca. Your documents are safe.

speaker: Zervos
en: You saved my felucca! Here, take this as a small token of thanks.

speaker: Zervos
en: You have made things better here.

speaker: Bayek
en: You clearly have people who are willing to help you out, Zervos. Why don't you take on Sefetu?

speaker: Zervos
en: Sefetu is too powerful, too greedy. He knows there is no one strong enough to stop him. We are not fighting men. Sefetu surrounds himself with soldiers. His base at Fort Nikiou is guarded with . Fool that I am, I helped him import them.

speaker: Bayek
en: May Amun watch over you.

speaker: Reda
en: Good timing. I've been told that... hyenas? No... hippos? Ah, nek, I can't remember, some sort of beast has been attacking a village I've taken an interest in. Should you help them, I would be well pleased.

speaker: Reda
en: Cursed beasts take on village after village and they cry in fear. But you are not scared, are you, Medjay? Deal with these beasts, Medjay.

speaker: Reda
en: Medjay, your help is needed! My customers were complaining that there were some animals stopping them from coming to me. I am sure a warrior like you would have no trouble dealing with a few beasts.

speaker: Reda
en: Medjay. You know the old saying "a merchant scorned by dangerous beasts has no customers at all"? No? Well, I do. I'd be thankful if you could help my customers deal with their problem.

speaker: Reda
en: Your payment, as promised.

speaker: Reda
en: You never cease to impress, Bayek.

speaker: Reda
en: You did it? Ah yes, of course. I never doubted you.

speaker: Reda
en: Well done, Medjay! As promised, this is for you.

speaker: Sobek Worshipper
en: God of the Waters, The Rager, the Lord of Faiyum. You whose seed is potent, whose appetite is voracious. You come from the eternal chaos, the churning waters to avenge us. To punish those who take the flesh of your children. And so we honor you. Help us restore the balance of this land.

speaker: Bayek
en: You worship the crocodile god?

speaker: Sobek Worshipper
en: We honor Sobek who walks. He is risen from the raging waters to punish our enemies.

speaker: Bayek
en: You have seen him?

speaker: Sobek Worshipper
en: Yes! Fighting a hundred soldiers, the tyrants who kill and skin his children for their own profit. We who live off the land are left with nothing.

speaker: Bayek
en: I should see his prowess for myself.

speaker: Sobek Worshipper
en: Do not fear him, he will not tear the flesh of those who honor him.

speaker: Bayek
en: Another God walking... Is this the orb's doing?

speaker: Bayek
en: That is no god.

speaker: Bayek
en: You're a little broken for a god.

speaker: Sobek Hunter
en: Did that damnable captain at the wharf send you to mock me?

speaker: Bayek
en: I heard you stand against the soldiers who kill the crocodiles.

speaker: Sobek Hunter
en: I am just trying to protect my family! Sobek allows us to take what we need to survive, nothing more. It is one of the commandments.

speaker: Bayek
en: You thought to frighten them away? Make them believe Sobek strides from the reeds?

speaker: Sobek Hunter
en: Why should the Pharaohs curse not do some good?

speaker: Bayek
en: Your last performance nearly got you killed. I will deal with your poachers.

speaker: Sobek Hunter
en: Tread carefully through the reeds, neb (sir). Bring the fight to him, seni (friend)!

speaker: Bayek
en: This captain doesn't respect the natural balance, so he will pay the price.

speaker: Bayek
en: They thought the hunter was truly Sobek.

speaker: Bayek
en: What is this now? The Hunter's shack aflame?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am glad to find you un-scorched!

speaker: Sobek Hunter
en: You said you would deal with the captain, and yet he came and burned my hut to ashes.

speaker: Bayek
en: Rest assured the captain is dead.

speaker: Sobek Hunter
en: Then like Osiris he has risen again. For he was here, shouting for me to face him as I cowered in the bushes!

speaker: Bayek
en: That cannot be, I killed him.

speaker: Sobek Hunter
en: Something is very odd, neb (sir). Has Sobek cursed me?

speaker: Bayek
en: You do his work, why would that be? Where did the captain return to?

speaker: Sobek Hunter
en: The outpost above the fields.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will see how a poacher cheats the Jackal. But it is no longer safe for you here.

speaker: Sobek Hunter
en: A truth is spoken. I will go south, where they honor the god. The Rager grant you teeth, neb (sir).

speaker: Bayek
en: Truly, if the captain is here, something is very strange.

speaker: Bayek
en: And the mist clears. Twin brothers each one as brutal as the other.

speaker: Nanefer
en: Everyone! Be careful! The curse of Wadjet! Snakes! Near the villa! At night! Fellow Greeks! Stay in your homes after dark! We have lost our harmony, and an Egyptian curse is upon us. Snakes! From the Egyptian serpent goddess! I've seen them! With my own eyes!

speaker: Bayek
en: What curse? What are you talking about?

speaker: Nanefer
en: Greeks and Egyptians have lost harmony with each other. The gods are displeased because of it. I'm Nanefer and I don't know if I'm Greek or Egyptian. I'm an orphan.

speaker: Bayek
en: Lost harmony? What do you mean?

speaker: Nanefer
en: The Egyptian goddess, Wadjet is sending snakes into Greek Quarters at night! Only Greeks have been killed! We are out of balance! See for yourself! Just North of the villa.

speaker: Bayek
en: Okay, I'll look into this curse.

speaker: Bayek
en: That was harder than it should have been.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nek! (Shit!) What was that? The gods are rumbling! It came from just North of here. Must have something to do with this curse.

speaker: Bayek
en: What happened here? I should ask around.

speaker: Bayek
en: This man was pinned down and died in the blaze. The structure is badly damaged. I cannot go any further. The trail leads outwards. I should look around the courtyard.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ugh. I can smell the burnt flesh.

speaker: Bayek
en: This jar doesn't belong here. I think there's movement inside!

speaker: Bayek
en: Gah! A snake! The jars have been used to transport them.

speaker: Bayek
en: Neb, did you see what happened?

speaker: Man
en: It was the curse of Wadjet! A fool and his friends feasted at the Dromos. I told him "this is a sacred place, we cannot eat here!" What did he expect would happen?

speaker: Bayek
en: And you believe in this curse?

speaker: Man
en: You Egyptians have your gods, we Greeks have ours. All I know is I don't want to anger any of them.

speaker: Sheshanka
en: Another foreigner cursed by Wadjet. That is three this week. Those useless Greeks had it coming, if you ask me. But what do I know? I am just the lowly Egyptian caretaker who cleans up after the neket iadet (pieces of shit).

speaker: Bayek
en: Be careful what you say! People have died! I need to look around.

speaker: Sheshanka
en: What you need to look at is the color of your skin, son.

speaker: Bayek
en: Harmony is what we need. Not more senseless judgement.

speaker: Sheshanka
en: Look, some of us have built a shrine in a cave under what is left of the great Temple. Why don't you come and honour Wadjet with us? Egyptians have to stick together.

speaker: Bayek
en: Maybe I will, after I look around.

speaker: Bayek
en: These jars are the same as the ones I saw in the Greek area.

speaker: Bayek
en: They are breeding the snakes here. Gods, I hate snakes!

speaker: Bayek
en: An elaborate shrine to the serpent goddess, Wadjet.

speaker: Bayek
en: By the sound of it, I won't have to find the Caretaker after all. He's already found me.

speaker: Sheshanka
en: He is inside! Get him when he comes out! He cannot escape!

speaker: Bayek
en: Caretaker! The snakes were yours.

speaker: Sheshanka
en: You serve Greeks?! Come on then you worthless Ionian slave. Do your master's bidding like a good Greek dog. I fight for Egypt! Who do you fight for?

speaker: Bayek
en: I serve no one and I fight, for everyone.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is what Ptolemy has done to Egypt. A land out of balance, full of hatred and strife. At least I can rescue the hostage. He's being held by the Caretaker's men at Pannouki. The Caretaker is using the goddess to kill Greeks. Why such hatred? Aya would be sad. It is just as Nanefer warned through his stutter. Egypt has lost harmony.

speaker: Bayek
en: More of the Caretaker's handiwork. These unfortunate Greeks were in the wrong place at the wrong time.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Caretaker's hideout must be up ahead.

speaker: Bayek
en: Argh. The smell of rotting flesh.

speaker: Bayek
en: Another of the green Wadjet masks.

speaker: Bayek
en: The body looks to be a Greek. It has been here a while. That explains the smell. He was struck down from behind.

speaker: Man 1
en: What is going to happen to that stupid stuttering Greek inside?

speaker: Man 2
en: He's going to be sacrificed to Wadjet when the Caretaker gets here.

speaker: Man 1
en: Blood sacrifice? The priests stopped that years ago.

speaker: Man 2
en: Our ancestors followed the true path, before it was corrupted by false teaching. That's why Wadjet abandoned us to the bastard Greeks.

speaker: Man 1
en: Well, at least he won't escape. You beat him so badly he's lying in his own blood. He can't even stand.

speaker: Man 2
en: Ha-ha! Stupid Greek. He had it coming. He hasn't even started to bleed yet. Wait till the Caretaker gets to him.

speaker: Bayek
en: Fresh fruit, grain, wine. These must be gifts from the Caretaker to his men.

speaker: Bayek
en: Another shrine to the snake goddess Wadjet.

speaker: Bayek
en: Can you stand?

speaker: Nanefer
en: Thank Serapis you're here! I don't think so. They beat me...

speaker: Bayek
en: Be still. I will carry you out.

speaker: Bayek
en: Can you walk?

speaker: Nanefer
en: They beat me! They beat me because they thought I'm Greek!

speaker: Bayek
en: Wait, what happened to your stutter?

speaker: Nanefer
en: I was scared when I first met you. It makes me stutter.

speaker: Bayek
en: By the gods, is nothing true! Well, you are alive, Nanefer. Be thankful.

speaker: Nanefer
en: I'm alive, but Egypt is out of balance. You must know, Medjay, the law is harmony between all peoples. May Serapis unite us all.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is the end of the Caretaker's cult. But Nanefer is right. Egypt is out of balance. And that is the Order of the Ancients' doing.

speaker: Agatha
en: Please save my boy. He's not a criminal! Will no-one help my son? He's served Rome well!

speaker: Agatha
en: Thank you for stopping, my husband was a protector like you. I have screamed myself hoarse for days. No one cares.

speaker: Bayek
en: What seems to be the problem, nebet?

speaker: Agatha
en: My Titus, my poor Titus. Imprisoned at the barracks for trying to leave the army.

speaker: Bayek
en: He's a deserter?

speaker: Agatha
en: No, a hero. He'd had enough, stood up against the Roman army and joined the rebels. Please, he's my only child and all I have left.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will look into it, don't worry.

speaker: Titus
en: Let me out you dogs! Release me or execute me. I will not rot in a cell.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you Titus? Your mother sent me.

speaker: Titus
en: Yes, by the gods, thank you protector, but Egypt is in danger, I must get free.

speaker: Titus
en: I will not die on Roman soil.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why would the army lock up their own men?

speaker: Titus
en: Papo taught me to be a fighter, but he believed in honor and justice. The Navarch of the Roman fleet at Apollonia Marcellus Asina, is planning an invasion.

speaker: Bayek
en: They mean to take Egypt...

speaker: Titus
en: Yes, so I deserted. I will not stay here doing Leander and Flavius' dirty work.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where is the Navarch?

speaker: Titus
en: On his ship. He patrols the waters between Cyrene and Apollonia. Killing him will throw the fleet into chaos.

speaker: Bayek
en: Go with Iset, Titus. I will deal with the Navarch.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your reckoning is between you and the gods.

speaker: Bayek
en: Entire villages of people have disappeared in Psenhyris. There are rumors at the caravanserai that Demons have invaded. Demons? I've never seen one. I should check this out.

speaker: Addaya
en: I escaped Anubis. I looked the demons in their black and burning eyes. Then the gods danced me from my shackles! Ha-ha! I saw the beasts with my own eyes! Demons! Twenty hands tall, with cruel forked tongues and black skin. Their eyes... burned me...

speaker: Addaya
en: Everyone is gone! The monsters took them while we farmed. Gods! Save us!

speaker: Bayek
en: What happened to you?

speaker: Addaya
en: We were all attacked by demons. They took the boy.

speaker: Bayek
en: What boy? Why didn't anyone stop them?

speaker: Addaya
en: I tried... I'm just a farmer, not a warrior. The boy was mad! He thought he could fight the demons. He's just a boy, at the broken tower. I ran away. I'm... (sobbing)

speaker: Bayek
en: A ruined tower? I cannot leave a boy alone in the desert. I must find him.

speaker: Bayek
en: This must be the ruined tower the madman spoke about. Not all of his story was insanity, then.

speaker: Bayek
en: Boy, what are you doing out here alone?

speaker: Rahotep
en: My business is my own. Why is a protector coming here?

speaker: Bayek
en: There are rumors of disappearing villagers, demons, and a missing boy.

speaker: Rahotep
en: Our village did not disappear! We were taken by bandits. I'm the only one left. But I am going back to save my father.

speaker: Bayek
en: If you go into the desert alone, you will die.

speaker: Rahotep
en: Then I die. I can do nothing else.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are brave, but foolish. A son's duty to his father is to live. I cannot let you go alone.

speaker: Rahotep
en: Okay, where were we? Come if you want to. My duty is to save my father.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are just a boy, but you have the conviction of a man. Your father would be proud.

speaker: Rahotep
en: We have to hurry. The desert will take us if the hyenas do not find us first. Follow me!

speaker: Bayek
en: Sandstorm. We must face it straight on.

speaker: Rahotep
en: I don't have the time to wait.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your father... are you certain he lives?

speaker: Rahotep
en: No, but I have to try. My mother passed many floods ago. I do not remember her. My father raised me alone. I have to return his horse to him. Alive or dead, he will need it in the afterlife. If he lives, I will save him. If he does not, I will honor him with my death. And we will ride through the Field of Reeds together.

speaker: Bayek
en: Boy, you must stay here. The way forward is dangerous. I will do everything in my power to rescue your father.

speaker: Rahotep
en: Saving my father is my duty, not yours. I am not a boy. I am Rahotep of Dionysias, and I am going.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am Bayek of Siwa and I will not take you into danger.

speaker: Rahotep
en: You are not taking me. I am taking myself.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah, damn you, Rahotep. I should have tied you to a tree.

speaker: Rahotep
en: You have only just met me. Yet I have answered all your questions truthfully. I am going to save my father. You have no duty here. You cannot forbid me anything. I am not your son.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are not the only one with a duty. I am a Medjay, and my duty is to protect.

speaker: Rahotep
en: Medjay? There are none of you left. Just Phylakes who sack our villages and kill our mothers. Protectors are corrupt. We need new Medjay. New protectors.

speaker: Bayek
en: We need people and Medjay to be as one, Rahotep.

speaker: Rahotep
en: I don't see it. Is the goddess the answer? Cleopatra?

speaker: Bayek
en: I cannot say for certain. But someone has to do what the Medjay did. Honour and Egypt are both dying.

speaker: Rahotep
en: I will have children and teach them. So that honour will live on in them.

speaker: Rahotep
en: Over here! Stay low! We're near the bandit camp. Their guards can see us.

speaker: Bayek
en: Rahotep, my son was like you. He also fought a man's battle, and died doing it. Would you stay hidden?

speaker: Rahotep
en: All right, Bayek. I will listen to you in this. But if you fall, I will take your place. See the lookout tower there? The guards, from time to time, abandon their post to piss. We can pass through then.

speaker: Bayek
en: You have an eye for strategy. Your father should be proud. Now keep to the shadows, and wait.

speaker: Bayek
en: Villagers! Let's go.

speaker: Turo
en: We need to leave this area. Quickly, this way. They left horses over here. Hurry! Let's go!

speaker: Turo
en: Rahotep! You are alive!

speaker: Rahotep
en: Is everyone ok? Where is my father?

speaker: Turo
en: Rahotep, I'm sorry. The demons took him to their crocodile pit. How can anyone fight them?

speaker: Rahotep
en: Demons do not bleed as these do. Listen to me. Each of you owes your life to my father. Turo! Remember he took a lashing to protect your daughter's honor? And you! Remember he crossed the desert to get your sick father a healer? Now my father needs you. If he lives, we save him. If not, we avenge him. Either way we fight!

speaker: Turo
en: Truly you are your father's son. You are right, Rahotep. Demons or not we will follow you!

speaker: Bayek
en: Are we ready?

speaker: Rahotep
en: We have been ready since the day the demon bandits attacked. We ride to save my father. And may Amun ride with us! Hyah!

speaker: Man 1
en: You have my spear! Death to Son of Ra's bandits!

speaker: Man 2
en: Death to those who profit from The Crocodile's stench!

speaker: Bayek
en: A friend. Can you walk? We need to get you out of here.

speaker: Rahotep
en: Father! You live! ...What's wrong?

speaker: Turo
en: He saved us all! He slew five of the demons alone! I saw it!

speaker: Rahotep
en: Father, Bayek of Siwa is also here. He fought with us.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your son is brave. I am glad to have helped him... though I doubt he will need help in the future. He will lead you well. Now I must go to hunt my own demons.

speaker: Torturer
en: Your taxes are long overdue Halakuf.

speaker: Halakuf
en: Tell Tychon I will find his money! I just need one good harvest, the curse...

speaker: Torturer
en: Curse...? Pharaohs returned from the dead? Nothing but tales to frighten feeble-minded infants.

speaker: Halakuf
en: No! I have seen him, the Pharaoh who walks, please!

speaker: Bayek
en: This man speaks the truth. Stop, or I will stop you.

speaker: Torturer
en: Ha! A would-be hero! You gurgle like a . Come any closer and we'll tear your tongue out.

speaker: Bayek
en: He won't extort you again, neb (sir).

speaker: Halakuf
en: Halakuf, please. You struck them down for their cruelty! Why does the Pharaoh not punish them? They pick over our bones like vultures!

speaker: Bayek
en: You cannot pay your taxes?

speaker: Halakuf
en: We cannot pay because we cannot work. And now Sobek is angry with us, he sent the Pharaoh to flood the fields closest to the great river.

speaker: Bayek
en: You have seen the one who walks?

speaker: Halakuf
