en: A waking nightmare, an abomination. My brother, fell at the King's deathless gaze. I ran, I was a coward.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your brother would not want you dead. Show me the fields, we will find the source of your suffering in honor of your kin.

speaker: Halakuf
en: I have always paid my due. But with the curse, many have left. Their fields lie fallow.

speaker: Bayek
en: These charms, have they not protected you?

speaker: Halakuf
en: Symbols mean little daubed on the walls of empty houses and hearths. But we do what we can or we starve.

speaker: Bayek
en: And now Sobek is angry with you?

speaker: Halakuf
en: I work the fields everyday, pray for a bounty. Instead he sends the Deathless King. Where he walks a flood gushes forth. A flood that washed my tools away.

speaker: Bayek
en: Into the Great Silt River.

speaker: Halakuf
en: And any who venture in feed his gnashing children. A tragedy, we cannot weather. And without pickaxes we cannot bring water to the fields. The Pharaoh may as well have taken me with my brother. Wheat ready to be harvested. But without our sickles it will wither and die.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will recover your tools, Halakuf. I do not fear Sobek's weath.

speaker: Halakuf
en: I believe it! You would scare the bull off his cow. Thank you, seni (friend). Sobek's children are frenzied. The god is angry.

speaker: Pickaxes
en: Used by the farmers to dig canals to irrigate their fields.

speaker: Bayek
en: They will be happy to get these back from the silt waters.

speaker: Some Sickles
en: Used for bringing in the harvest and cutting down the wheat.

speaker: Bayek
en: Keen as a blade.

speaker: More Sickles
en: Used for bringing in the harvest and cutting down the wheat.

speaker: Bayek
en: The tools of an honest farmer.

speaker: Bayek
en: Halakuf and his people can bring in their harvest.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your tools, a little weathered, but still strong and sharp as Sobek's teeth.

speaker: Halakuf
en: A wonder! I was wrong... the wards we painted, did not stop who walks they brought you. An eagle amongst vultures.

speaker: Bayek
en: Take care of yourself and your people, Halakuf. Honor your brother with a fine harvest!

speaker: Halakuf
en: May you be seated before a thousand loaves, neb (sir).

speaker: Halakuf
en: You saved our livelihood, gave us real hope. The curse has a foothold here no longer.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your brother would be proud.

speaker: Farmer 1
en: We will bring these fields back to life. Honor Halakuf's brother with beer and bread!

speaker: Farmer 2
en: Working on these fields is a blessing, a blessing you gave us.

speaker: Farmer 3
en: The fearless one, who braved the silt river. Without you our fields would lie barren.

speaker: Aya
en: What is it?

speaker: Bayek
en: The Snake. What if he was not the last?

speaker: Aya
en: Of course he was the last! They are all dead. Justice is done!

speaker: Bayek
en: Hmph.

speaker: Aya
en: If there is any question, Apollodorus will know. He knows all.

speaker: Bayek
en: And where will I find this man who knows so much?

speaker: Aya
en: He is with Cleopatra. But find his man first near the hippodrome.

speaker: Bayek
en: Eh!

speaker: Aya
en: Hmph. I'll tell Phanos that Gennadios is dead and meet you later. Enjoy the hippodrome. Don't lose all your money at the races.

speaker: Machus
en: Two hundred drachmae on Prasina! And I'll buy everyone beer with the winnings!

speaker: Man
en: Can't do it. The betting's too lopsided. Everybody's taking Prasina in tribute to Icarus.

speaker: Machus
en: What if we say Prasina has to win by two lengths?

speaker: Man
en: Two lengths? You have yourself a bet.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am Bayek. Aya sent me to speak to Apollodorus.

speaker: Machus
en: Ssh! I'm sure you can appreciate that my master takes precautions concerning those he meets.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have a question only he can answer.

speaker: Machus
en: I will tell him you seek his council and that Aya recommends you. Wait for tonight. If he sees fit to meet you, he will be found near the lighthouse then. Until then, the hippodrome's commemorating one of its greatest racers. Plenty of drinking and festivities along with the races themselves, of course. If that appeals.

speaker: Bayek
en: Apollodorus.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: You there! Are you here to kill me or to be my friend?

speaker: Bayek
en: Friend. Bayek of Siwa.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Ah! Then your help, please.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: You are Aya's Medjay, huh?

speaker: Bayek
en: Any other survivors?

speaker: Man
en: Only Damastes. They took him prisoner.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: And the scroll! What of the scroll?

speaker: Man
en: Damastes had it.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: That ass Damastes should have destroyed it!

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Cleopatra owes you much. Can you get to a healer by yourself?

speaker: Bayek
en: I've killed Eudoros.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Huh? Well done.

speaker: Bayek
en: He was the Snake, yes?

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Man to man, Bayek, there is much you have yet to understand.

speaker: Bayek
en: Man to man, I need an answer.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: I must take the measure of you first. Rescue Damastes and recover the scroll. And then I will know if you are the man that Aya claims you to be.

speaker: Bayek
en: Argh! Where is this Damastes?

speaker: Apollodorus
en: He should be on the docks in Kanopos harbor. I can't risk that someone reads the scroll he carries.

speaker: Damastes
en: Dear Amon, save me! Get me out of here ! I have to sleep in my own filth in here! Don't forget about me !

speaker: Damastes
en: Thank you! It was very unpleasant in there. You have killed them all! Bastards, they deserved to die. Get me to a safe place! Then we will talk.

speaker: Damastes
en: I was going to kill all of them. That damn cage was too hard to get out of, is all.

speaker: Bayek
en: Apollodorus sent me to help you. Give me the scroll.

speaker: Damastes
en: Scroll? I do not have any scroll.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your job was to carry it.

speaker: Damastes
en: I hid it on our ship. I did not want it to fall into the wrong hands.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where is this ship?

speaker: Damastes
en: At the bottom of the lake! They sunk it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Argh, very well, I will get it. Apollodorus is waiting for you at the lighthouse.

speaker: Damastes
en: I will tell him to find you near the sunken ship.

speaker: Bayek
en: That precious scroll, nek (shit).

speaker: Bayek
en: Here is your precious .

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Well done, Bayek. I see you are a capable man. Someone I may be able to trust. The scroll was meant for the Roman general Pompey in an effort to sway Rome to Cleopatra's side. She will be grateful to you for keeping the communication secret. She is at my estate, we're headed there now.

speaker: Bayek
en: How does Aya fit into all this?

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Her cousin Phanos informed me that she was a driven woman stalking deadly prey. It so happened that I, also, had reason to bring down this prey. When Aya was successful, I stepped in to protect her.

speaker: Bayek
en: We are grateful.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: And we are grateful that you have eliminated Eudoros. He was an odious individual.

speaker: Bayek
en: I should tell you that in addition to Eudoros, I put an end to the phylakitai of Alexandria, Gennadios.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Gennadios? I am very glad he is dead, but it will cause serious problems for you. The Phylakes are a tightly bound group. And murderous. They will certainly come after you.

speaker: Bayek
en: So be it. Can I ask why you wanted Eudoros dead?

speaker: Apollodorus
en: As you know, Cleopatra's brother, Ptolemy, is too young and pliable to be a strong leader. We believe Eudoros was the force behind Ptolemy responsible for so many of Egypt's current ills. You will learn more at the villa.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Here we are. The villa is up ahead. The queen enjoys the life of high society. I'm pleased that Aya is bringing some sober substance to Cleopatra's social circle. She is an extraordinary woman, your wife.

speaker: Bayek
en: I know.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Bayek. Before I can disclose all secrets, Cleopatra must meet and approve of you. She can be particular. Let me give you some advice. When you approach the queen, bend your knee in deference. Speak only in reply. Yours is not to question, but to answer. Do not be distracted by the festivities. She has a large entourage and they like to amuse themselves. Sometimes to excess. Speak clearly, in measured tones, and above all, do not meet her gaze! Ready?

speaker: Bayek
en: I cannot wait.

speaker: Courtier 1
en: Catch me! Catch me!

speaker: Apollodorus
en: This way.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Where is my opium pipe? I will sleep with anyone! As long as they agree to be executed in the morning!

speaker: Courtier 2
en: Like Xantides?

speaker: Cleopatra
en: He was well satisfied with his bargain.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Who is this toothsome fellow? (Would you pay such a price?)

speaker: Apollodorus
en: My queen, this is

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Well?

speaker: Bayek
en: It is a generous offer, but I have already pledged my life to this woman.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Aya, you have chosen well. Come, we have much to discuss.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Celebrate, my friends!

speaker: Apollodorus
en: You were meant to kneel.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Ah, Pasherenptah! Meet Aya and Bayek. They put an early end to Eudoros.

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: Delightful! You are joining our efforts, then?

speaker: Bayek
en: We do not know what your efforts are.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Eudoros was a member of the Order of the Ancients, they are responsible for my exile. They tore me from my throne.

speaker: Bayek
en: And why should I care about them?

speaker: Apollodorus
en: The Snake has many heads. Those heads make up the Order.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Snake is the man who killed my son.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: It is not so simple.

speaker: Bayek
en: What are they talking about?

speaker: Aya
en: I don't know, they must know something.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: The Order of Ancients seeks to control all Egypt. Ptolemy is but their puppet.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: We have informants in each region. But they have been unable to touch the Order.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Across Egypt, mysterious forces work against us. For instance, here, in the Nile Delta—The endless sands swallow up whole villages. Yet a malignant human force moves with them. That force is one of the Order of Ancients called the Scarab.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: And over here, in most sacred Giza...

speaker: Apollodorus
en: A shadowy figure called the Hyena controls all that occurs.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: What is certain is that Giza is the land of death... and loss.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: And then there's Memphis.

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: All is cursed in my land, even the sacred Apis Bull himself. The one called the Lizard has worked a sort of diabolical power.

speaker: Bayek
en: So the Snake is the Order of Ancients?

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Yes. Eudoros was known as the Hippo.

speaker: Aya
en: You were right, my love. He was not the last one. All of these are.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: When the Order wants something, as in Siwa, it does not hesitate to crush all in its path.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: First Siwa, now Faiyum. It is the most opressed region in all of Egypt. Where the Crocodile wields cruel power. The denizens live in constant fear. That is the fate that awaits all Egypt if we fail to stop the Order.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: We need decisive action. It is time for assassinations.

speaker: Aya
en: We still have not found the man who killed Khemu. Our son's shade will weep with joy when we clear the map of those figures.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: You are my Medjay now! Protector of the true Pharaoh of Egypt.

speaker: Bayek
en: So it shall be! Tonight, we drink, celebrate, make love! Tomorrow...

speaker: Aya
en: The Order of Ancients has no idea what is coming their way. I will be heading north soon to defend Cleopatra at sea. You should begin your journey my love. Ouf, my head still aches from last night...

speaker: Bayek
en: Looks important. Locked.

speaker: Bayek
en: These are the rooms of the Royal Scribe.

speaker: Bayek
en: Looks important. Locked.

speaker: Bayek
en: A ladder. Hmm.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah. A key.

speaker: Bayek
en: Official papers. This chest belongs to the Royal Scribe himself, Eudoros. Hm... a false bottom.

speaker: Bayek
en: A letter.

speaker: Bayek
en: Stamped with the seal of the Snake. The Snake is Eudoros, the Royal Scribe. Aya said that the Royal Scribe is often at the bath house. I will kill that neket iadet (piece of shit) Eudoros there.

speaker: Visitor 1
en: Aristo is taking Eudoros to court for plagiarism.

speaker: Visitor 2
en: No!

speaker: Visitor 1
en: I was visiting the docks and heard it from Aristo's wife herself!

speaker: Visitor 2
en: His wife? She works herself into histrionics over nothing.

speaker: Visitor 1
en: Eudoros stole whole paragraphs from Aristo's book about the Nile!

speaker: Visitor 3
en: Kyros chooses his horses badly. Have you seen his wife?

speaker: Visitor 4
en: I love coming here, the building alone is worth the trip. Look up at that expansive ceiling! Simply divine.

speaker: Visitor 5
en: Eudoros is here again.

speaker: Visitor 6
en: I pity him. His skin affliction is an endless source of discomfort.

speaker: Visitor 5
en: As do we all.

speaker: Simonides
en: Ptolemy is a chinless simpleton.

speaker: Visitor 7
en: Simonides, you have consumed too much wine!

speaker: Simonides
en: I have, and I will again. But had I not, would our pharaoh be any less a goose?

speaker: Soldier
en: Is everything to your liking, my lord?

speaker: Eudoros
en: The water's a bit tepid today. Such incompetence.

speaker: Soldier
en: My lord. Are you properly served?

speaker: Eudoros
en: Quite. See that my towels are readied.

speaker: Soldier
en: Can I do anything for you, my lord?

speaker: Eudoros
en: Stop annoying me, if you please. Idiot. Ah! My skin! Sure an affliction. I should never have consorted with that sailor. Bring me my roast piglet! I love to eat in a warm bath.

speaker: Bayek
en: Die, and be done with it!

speaker: Eudoros
en: May the gods curse you! What cause have you to kill me?

speaker: Bayek
en: It was you who murdered my son before my eyes.

speaker: Eudoros
en: You are a fool!

speaker: Bayek
en: At the temple in Siwa.

speaker: Eudoros
en: That forsaken shit hole? I had nothing to do with that disaster!

speaker: Bayek
en: It is too late for your lies. Anubis awaits.

speaker: Bayek
en: It is worth the loss to slay the Snake at last.

speaker: Eudoros
en: The Snake?... The Snake will never die.

speaker: Bayek
en: Son of Apep, the lord of the Duat awaits.

speaker: Visitors
en: Eudoros! Killed! Oh, dear gods! He's been murdered! But he was so handsome! It's Eudoros! Poor soul! Look at the blood!

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 1
en: Did you ever see work as fine as ? I Wish I could afford one of his weapons. Did you ever see the Serpent of Serapis? A spear light as a feather, and sharper than Sobek's tooth. With such a spear, I could be a champion in the amphitheater!

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 2
en: Shame about what happened to it...

speaker: Bayek
en: That is quite the story.

speaker: Sokar
en: Ah, the Serpent of Serapis! You have heard the tragic tale?

speaker: Bayek
en: Not the whole of it.

speaker: Sokar
en: Oh, it was a true masterpiece. The shaft wrapped with water-hardened leather, the blade hammered out of the metal of heaven.

speaker: Bayek
en: I would love to see it.

speaker: Sokar
en: Impossible! I crafted it for one of Apollodorus's captains when I lived in Sais. But Sefetu's soldiers killed him. That is the reason I left.

speaker: Bayek
en: Sefetu?

speaker: Sokar
en: Yes! Sefetu the Firebrand, who governs Sais with flame and fear. One of his bootlickers stole the spear that bears my mark.

speaker: Bayek
en: Outrageous! Can you not get it back?

speaker: Sokar
en: The man is beyond my reach. He sails on one of Sefetu's triremes on Mariotis Lake.

speaker: Bayek
en: I hate a bully. My travels take me far and wide. If I come across him, I will look for your spear.

speaker: Sokar
en: I would love nothing more than to hear of his fall! If you manage it, the Serpent of Serapis is yours!

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: See anything yet?

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: Another gods cursed rebel?

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: No.

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: What are you looking for?

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: Trouble.

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: Expecting any?

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: Always.

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: Uh, good talking with you.

speaker: Bayek
en: This spear is magnificent – clearly the work of that master from Sau Village. This Serpent of Serapis is a weapon worthy of the gods!

speaker: Bayek
en: Teremun. Not like him to give up.

speaker: Farmers
en: That's Bayek! He will save us!

speaker: Bayek
en: Quickly, go!

speaker: Bayek
en: Where is Teremun? Ah! Dear Amun, he has died from his wounds.

speaker: Bayek
en: His family will want to bury him properly.

speaker: Bayek
en: What have they done to Teremun's farm?

speaker: Bayek
en: I bring sad news. Where is Issa?

speaker: Man
en: She lies here... with her son and daughter.

speaker: Bayek
en: The entire family?

speaker: Man
en: Sadly. I see Teremun also paid the price for his recklessness. I warned him that his rebelliousness would bring torment and suffering.

speaker: Bayek
en: But what happened?

speaker: Man
en: They saw the soldiers coming and hid in the cellar. But the soldiers burnt the house to the ground to teach everyone a lesson.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am sorry.

speaker: Man
en: Put the body down there. They will journey to the Duat together. So many deaths in the wahat (oasis). We cannot give them a proper burial.

speaker: Bayek
en: It is not your rebelliousness that got you killed seni (friend). It is Ptolemy's sick regime. He is a bad pharaoh.

speaker: Bayek
en: Find peace, Teremun.

speaker: Man
en: He will find more than he had here.

speaker: Woman
en: Neb! Please! I must speak with you! I saw you with the Phylakitai of Karanis. Are you a protector?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am. Is there something wrong?

speaker: Woman
en: Please, we need your help. Yesterday my husband witnessed something... frightening. Soldiers dragged a poor man beneath the temple. Then he heard screams! We're already hungry because there's no grain. Now I'm terrified the soldiers will take my husband. We don't know who we can trust, not even the Phylakitai.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let me talk to your husband. Where can I find him?

speaker: Woman
en: He's a stonemason working near the temple. Please be careful. The soldiers mustn't see you talk to him!

speaker: Bayek
en: Stonemason, your wife has been to see me.

speaker: Stonemason
en: Shhh! How die you get up here? By Amun, that woman interferes. I told her, "What can we do?" Just act normal. Yeah, that's it. Stay normal.

speaker: Bayek
en: Calm yourself! She said you saw soldiers take someone below the temple.

speaker: Stonemason
en: Yes. No! Yes. Okay, it's true. It wasn't the first time, but yesterday was different. There were screams that would wake the gods themselves! So many screams! Now please, just leave me alone before someone sees you. Just act normal. (Humming and whistling)

speaker: Bayek
en: Some people just should not whistle.

speaker: Bayek
en: This looks like the place the Stonemason told me about.

speaker: Bayek
en: By Amun! What has been done here?

speaker: Bayek
en: Blood, and a lot of it. That must explain the screams.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is a lot of grain when most people do not have enough. This looks like a temporary storage area. Are they moving grain?

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone called the Butcher is strong-arming farmers. I need to find him. I should follow this trail of loot. A bathing Sobek. Bathing... must be in water. A Sobek in water... hmmm...

speaker: Bayek
en: There's a Sobek ruin not far from here. The Butcher's loot could be nearby.

speaker: Man
en: They take our gods and turn them into abominations. Serapis!? Half Greek, half Egyptian, all whore of Alexandria! Those lying Greeks are working us to death, tearing down our own temples! This is what their culture means! The death of Egypt and Egyptians! And who does all this work to build Greece on top of Egypt? Egyptians of course! Last week our brother Metjen died while working on the temple. His wife just gave birth to their first son!

speaker: Bayek
en: Those are guards. This must be the place. The "Bathing Sobek" should be close.

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: He was asking for it. We can't have these sand-rat Egyptians getting brave. Now hurry! This shipment goes to Dromos' holy corridor tomorrow.

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: I've never taken a man's arm before. Did you see how clean the cut was? Right through the bone. That's talent.

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: Haha! Gods, did he scream. Not one farmer will have the guts to resist now.

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: If they knew the Butcher they wouldn't ever consider it. He was lucky it wasn't his head. Few cross the Butcher and live.

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: We shouldn't even be talking of it. If word got back to him we'd get in trouble. Best just get on with our work.

speaker: Bayek
en: There's an engraving on the chest depicting Soknopaiou. That is a village West of here. The coins are in bags normally used to store grain. Did this come from a storehouse?

speaker: Bayek
en: That is a lot of guards for a simple storehouse. This must be the place. I have to get past them if I want answers.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Butcher will be nearby. What are these goons hiding?

speaker: Soldier 1
en: I heard they took his arm at the Butcher's order. I guess we are common thugs now, not soldiers.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Shh, keep your voice down!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: This is not what I joined the army for.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: It is what puts grain on your table. You are here now. When the Butcher says jump, we jump. That is how it is. Now shut-up before someone hears us.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is where they're hiding all the grain. Taken straight from the tables of Faiyum families. Damn these greedy neket iadet. I should look around.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ledger entries showing payments for grain. The Butcher is not paying the farmers even enough to live. I need to find information on where he is.

speaker: Bayek
en: More grain. The poor are starving while the rich fill their storehouses. This has to stop. I should keep looking around.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah, this is it. The Butcher is in the villa nearby. It is time this Butcher and I had a talk.

speaker: Bayek
en: A palatial villa. Built on the backs of Faiyum's farmers, no doubt.

speaker: Butcher
en: Once the shipment arrives, leave immediately. We can thank those fanatical Wadjet cultists in Karanis for taking the attention off us.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: All this grain. Shouldn't we leave some for the farmers?

speaker: Butcher
en: Shut your mouth and do your job. That grain is what pays for your beer and women. Or did you think they like you because you're a soldier?

speaker: Butcher
en: Ah, here's the vlaka who's been messing with my business. We were just discussing you.

speaker: Bayek
en: You've been stealing grain from Faiyum... starving people for profit.

speaker: Butcher
en: You're not from Faiyum, are you? Your speech reeks of the countryside.

speaker: Bayek
en: That grain belongs on Egyptian tables.

speaker: Butcher
en: You naive backwater malakia. I take orders from above. If not me, someone else will do this. This is business. People pay what they owe, or I take it. It's not personal. I give you a choice now. Leave me alone and live, or die here.

speaker: Bayek
en: Others thought they way you do. Then they murdered my son. Everything is personal, you filthy neket iadet.

speaker: Bayek
en: It ends here!

speaker: Butcher
en: Guards! Take care of this!

speaker: Bayek
en: May the Hidden One greet you. The Lord of the Duat awaits.

speaker: Hotephres
en: It is true. The soldiers were only the beginning. We have to deal with this Commander.

speaker: Khenut
en: We need more information. How far does the corruption go? It may rise as far as Ptolemy's inner circle. We cannot trust any Phylakitai. We cannot do it alone, we need Faiyum.

speaker: Hotephres
en: Most of the farmers will not talk for fear of the soldiers. But they are angry. It will not take much to convince them.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let me talk to that farmer the captain was threatening. I'll spread the word.

speaker: Bayek
en: Seni (Friend)! I saw what happened with the soldiers.

speaker: Man
en: Nebet Khenut took a big risk. I appreciate what she did, but it won't change anything. I'm sorry, but I must keep working. I've got a stack of fires to light.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let me help, then.

speaker: Man
en: What are you doing?

speaker: Bayek
en: Lighting your fires.

speaker: Man
en: You don't give up, do you?

speaker: Bayek
en: Ra will ensure your crops are fertile, seni (friend).

speaker: Bayek
en: There you are. It's time to rise up against the soldiers. Hotephres will fight with you.

speaker: Man
en: Hotephres? He abandoned us long ago! His father was a good man. He gave his son an Egyptian name. We loved him for that. But he could not give him an Egyptian heart. Hotephres means 'satisfied' in our tongue, but he never was. He soon left us to the hyenas and crocodiles...

speaker: Bayek
en: Yet crocodiles may still be defeated. The Captain is no more. Rise, Seni. Spread the word.

speaker: Man
en: You defeated the Captain? Wow, you are a madman! Okay, if you are willing to do this, I will join you. I will spread the word, seni (friend).

speaker: Hotephres
en: I did not know things were this bad. I mean, I knew there was trouble, just... not like this. This is my fault. I did not want the responsibility here in Faiyum. The inheritance was forced on me. I wanted to stay on my ship, the adventure... Now I realize... giving up is a choice... and I am still alive.

speaker: Greek soldier
en: They must be in the villa. Take the back! You, come with me.

speaker: Hotephres
en: Soldiers!

speaker: Greek soldier
en: Where are you, maláka? Come down. We need a talk.

speaker: Hotephres
en: Looks like the choice has been made for me. Come brother. Let us talk to them... with our swords!

speaker: Bayek
en: I've got your back! And it's good to have you back, brother!

speaker: Hotephres
en: Rush in and die, you dogs!

speaker: Greek soldier 1
en: He's got a sword! Take him!

speaker: Greek soldier 2
en: Your mistake, old man!

speaker: Bayek
en: You fight well for someone retired.

speaker: Hotephres
en: Ha! I am not old yet, Siwan.

speaker: Khenut
en: I can see that.

speaker: Bayek
en: But it will not be enough. The soldiers will come in greater numbers now.

speaker: Hotephres
en: I inherited more than a strong sword arm. I will hire a private army if I need to!

speaker: Khenut
en: I might have a better idea. Bayek, could you accompany me on a short journey?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am ready. Let's go.

speaker: Khenut
en: You two make a good team. Hotephres has lost none of his fire.

speaker: Bayek
en: You sound proud of him.

speaker: Khenut
en: It is nice to have back the man I married.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where are we going?

speaker: Khenut
en: There is a rebel camp nearby. It is east of here, by Fort Boubastos. We are going to meet with them.

speaker: Bayek
en: Rebels? Will dealing with them not earn the wrath of Alexandria?

speaker: Khenut
en: Alexandria is no stranger to intrigue, Medjay. Favors are sometimes traded for information or protection. Such alliances are necessary, if not officially acknowledged.

speaker: Khenut
en: This way. Their camp is just up ahead.

speaker: Bayek
en: We should be cautious. Rebels are not known for their hospitality.

speaker: Khenut
en: I sent word. They are expecting us.

speaker: Khenut
en: I am Khenut. I sent word from Philadelphia that we were coming. We need your help.

speaker: Rebel
en: You wasted your time. Sorry, we cannot help you.

speaker: Khenut
en: We are not asking for charity. We can offer food, supplies and information. All we require in return is protection for our people.

speaker: Rebel
en: I said we cannot help. Soldiers captured our leader down at the dam.

speaker: Khenut
en: Then perhaps we can help you. This is Bayek of Siwa

speaker: Rebel
en: You are Bayek of Siwa? We were told what you did at the Arena. Beating the brothers like a madman!

speaker: Bayek
en: And I suppose today I play the madman again.

speaker: Bayek
en: Go! Now!

speaker: Rebel leader
en: Thank you. Who are you to attack soldiers so openly? Don't you fear waking Greece?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am Bayek of Siwa. And I am more afraid of Egypt sleeping.

speaker: Rebel leader
en: The Crazy Siwan... My men spoke of you! Fighting in the Arena single-handed like a madman! Nek! (Shit!) The Ptolemy dogs have no chance if you're on our side.

speaker: Bayek
en: And I will need you on my side when it matters.

speaker: Rebel leader
en: Right, let us continue. We should move.

speaker: Bayek
en: The way back from here is clear. Before you go, I need a favor. Khenut is waiting at your camp. She will ask for your help to protect her people.

speaker: Rebel leader
en: I owe you my life. You have my word it will be done.

speaker: Bayek
en: Could you also tell her I go to Fort Boubastos. I have business with the Commander there.

speaker: Rebel leader
en: Alone against a fortified garrison? Are you crazy?

speaker: Bayek
en: Perhaps. I am Bayek of Siwa.

speaker: Bayek
en: Horns. Voices. Someone else is attacking the fort. It seems all of Faiyum has turned against the commander.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is the end of his corruption. I should meet the others.

speaker: Bayek
en: It is done.

speaker: Hotephres
en: You had help. The farmers staged a protest to distract the soldiers. They were fearless! The rebels also did their part. You've inspired them, Bayek. In truth, they are in awe of you. Our farms will be well protected. They love their crazy Siwan.

speaker: Bayek
en: They will not let another Crocodile plague the Faiyum again. Your people are free now. It is a good start Hotephres. It is time to live up to your name.

speaker: Hotephres
en: And my duty as a husband.

speaker: Khenut
en: Shadya liked you immediately, you know. You always have a home here, if you need it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Who is this shrine dedicated to?

speaker: Man
en: I am praying for the people killed by fires in Dionysias. Someone is burning down their farms. You, Medjay, could help to stop it.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will try to help.

speaker: Bayek
en: Just as the praying man said. This farm was torched as if by Ra himself.

speaker: Bayek
en: That farm has been torched as if by Ra himself. There is nothing left.

speaker: Farmer
en: A man is coming. He is armed. What should we do?

speaker: Zahra
en: I am armed too. We are not in any danger. Be calm.

speaker: Bayek
en: My name is Bayek, a Protector...

speaker: Man
en: A protector? We could use one. Talk to my lady.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am Bayek, a Medjay.

speaker: Zahra
en: A real Medjay? Not a Phylakitai I hope! I'm Zahra. This was my farm.

speaker: Bayek
en: Who burned it down?

speaker: Zahra
en: Hordes. The neket iadets (pieces of shit) trying to drive us out. They are lucky I wasn't here I would have spread their guts across my fields. I am going to warn my Greek neighbor. His farm might be next. Please join me.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will follow you, Zahra. We have to protect this land.

speaker: Zahra
en: Yes, it is rich and fertile and worth fighting over. Like me! His farm isn't far from here. See if you can keep up, Medjay.

speaker: Zahra
en: What brings you to the Faiyum? We get few visitors this way. Medjay especially.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am... hunting murderers.

speaker: Zahra
en: You came to the right place. Full of dogs worth killing. The Faiyum is not the oasis it once was.

speaker: Bayek
en: How long have your farms been getting burned?

speaker: Zahra
en: Since the dawn of the new Ptolemy. Most of the farmers... they could not fight back and got pushed out. My family was amongst those who fought. The struggle became our way of life. I fought so much I forgot to fall in love. I am a romantic though. My father warned me to marry and give him lots of grandchildren. Gods! Me with a bunch of screaming kids! Our land needed protection, so I learned to fight.

speaker: Bayek
en: Egypt needs fighters. It was a good decision.

speaker: Zahra
en: Turns out I am apt at shit kicking.

speaker: Bayek
en: A warrior farmer. You must have stories.

speaker: Zahra
en: So many. We should swap tales around the fire sometime. With your help, maybe I'll have time to fall in love.

speaker: Bayek
en: I do not suppose your Greek neighbor is harboring these fire bandits?

speaker: Zahra
en: That would make things simpler. But no. Those are definitely uninvited guests.

speaker: Bayek
en: Keep a safe distance. I'm going to...

speaker: Zahra
en: Nek (Shit) no! You are not! You keep a safe distance. I will be amidst the blood splatter!

speaker: Bayek
en: A farmer warrior with a Duat wish. Fine, let us dance together.

speaker: Zahra
en: Damn these wretched cowards!

speaker: Bandit
en: You have been looking for us, we know. We thought we would save you time and come to you. We are here to help. When we bring you to the fire, you will understand. You will be purified. The flames will release your pain. It will all burn away. Son of Ra will set you free.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you alright?

speaker: Bion
en: I... I don't think so. The bindings were so tight I can't feel my legs. Get me out of here before more bandits come!

speaker: Zahra
en: Bion! What a mess.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will carry you. Let's go.

speaker: Bayek
en: You're heavier than you look!

speaker: Zahra
en: Maybe you would like me to carry him?

speaker: Bion
en: Zahra. That was frightening!

speaker: Zahra
en: Nek! (Shit!) Bion, we cannot live scared! You must fight back!

speaker: Bion
en: You truly are a gift from the gods Zahra. I tell all my Greek friends of Zahra, the warrior farmer.

speaker: Zahra
en: We need to find the bandits' nest.

speaker: Bion
en: I might know where it is. Servants tracked riders coming south from the White Desert. There is nothing out that way except some ruins. And they mentioned the name Son of Ra. I think he is their leader.

speaker: Zahra
en: Son of Ra? He will soon be the Son of Nothing. Into the desert we go, Bayek. Bayek, we need to get moving. It's a long damned way.

speaker: Bayek
en: Okay, let's get there.

speaker: Zahra
en: Gods, by Anubis I love the desert! It awes me. It always has. I cried like a little girl the first time I came here. I didn't know why. My father told me I was being silly.

speaker: Bayek
en: The desert brings out different sides to us.

speaker: Zahra
en: Yes. It gets cold at night.

speaker: Bayek
en: A fighter like you must have a few farmers interested. Have you never wanted a family of your own? You do not have anyone in mind?

speaker: Zahra
en: I fight too much. Well, maybe a Medjay warrior could change that. (laughs)

speaker: Bayek
en: That's an invitation.

speaker: Zahra
en: ' That looks like ruins up ahead.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is insanity! They killed themselves in honor of their leader.

speaker: Bandit 1
en: You know the Son of Ra is crazy right?

speaker: Bandit 2
en: Why? Because he's not like everyone else? He opened our eyes! He never lied to us. He doesn't even take anything from the farms.

speaker: Bandit 1
en: But they have caught him now.

speaker: Bandit 2
en: The Son of Ra will never give up and neither should we. Don't you know what happened to him? His family? They burned his farm for no reason. He watched his family die!

speaker: Bandit 1
en: Which is why he hates farmers more than he hates soldiers. They all just stood back and watched. Well they'll burn too, one by one.

speaker: Bandit 2
en: But they are going to execute him now. What do we do?

speaker: Bandit 1
en: He already told us this would happen. We know what to do.

speaker: Bayek
en: This was not their leader. The Son of Ra, their real leader, has been giving orders from prison. He's being held by soldiers at a nearby Caravanserai. He has been ordering the burnings. He thinks he is a god, and invincible.

speaker: Zahra
en: Then we'll make the neket iadet bleed and prove him wrong.

speaker: Bayek
en: Old mementoes and trinkets. These look personal. All of them are marked by fire.

speaker: Bayek
en: Oil, and lots of it. This is how they are starting the fires.

speaker: Zahra
en: You fight well, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: As do you. Your study was not wasted.

speaker: Zahra
en: The bandits believe this Son of Ra is a god? How did he convince them of that? Ra's son? That's insane. And it's creepy.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have seen it before. If you want to believe in something badly enough, you will believe anything. And do anything.

speaker: Bayek
en: Zahra, do not argue with me about this. I have to do this next task alone.

speaker: Zahra
en: Stop saying that camel shit! I'm not waiting around while you do the fighting.

speaker: Bayek
en: Look, it is cleaner this way. It will be easier for me to get in alone.

speaker: Zahra
en: Alright. Have it your way. I'll be near by.

speaker: Son of Ra
en: I was asleep in a mound of dirt, now I rise from the buried earth.

speaker: Guard 1
en: That crazy is not right in the head. Did you see his eyes? Do you think he's really the Son of Ra?

speaker: Guard 2
en: He is a dangerous little madman. But he has got his own private army. They do whatever he says.

speaker: Guard 1
en: I'm more scared of what they will do next.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Somehow he's still communicating with them. Could a normal man do that? If he is a god a cage won't stop him. Is he even still there?

speaker: Guard 1
en: I just finished my rounds. He is there. The Captain wants him executed, but someone higher up is protecting him.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Then we'll have to get his followers before they get us.

speaker: Son of Ra
en: I live. I sniff the air. I feel the dirt beneath my feet. I grow, and swell.

speaker: Son of Ra
en: I am the egg. I rise and watch.

speaker: Son of Ra
en: I am the first-born of Ra, the light of the sky. I breathe power, under the belly of the sky, on the shoulder of Egypt.

speaker: Son of Ra
en: My breath is like a child, hanging sweet in my nostrils. I am the blue egg. I am the Bird of Fire.

speaker: Bayek
en: You die easily for a god.

speaker: Son of Ra
en: I am nobody. Nobody. But when the Son of Ra stands on the mountain and says "do it", it gets done.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nek! You told them to murder.

speaker: Son of Ra
en: I am not sorry. Is Bayek of Siwa sorry? I lost my family, you lost your family. We have the right to do anything we want to anyone.

speaker: Bayek
en: No, we are different. You burned farms. You killed innocents. You are insane.

speaker: Son of Ra
en: Hypocrite! You can pile up one thousand dead bodies in front of me. It doesn't change me. The world will burn! The Order won't save it! You will burn with it, Medjay...

speaker: Bayek
en: May you walk the Land of the Duat.

speaker: Bayek
en: He is dead. I should tell Zahra.

speaker: Bayek
en: Son of Ra is dead. It was disturbing. His madness almost made sense.

speaker: Zahra
en: If you stare deeply enough into any madness, there is a logic.

speaker: Bayek
en: So what now? The fires are stopped. Your farms are safe.

speaker: Zahra
en: I don't know. I am hungry though. Now we return to the farm to feast in peace.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is that an invitation?

speaker: Zahra
en: Ha-ha, you are the Medjay. You figure it out. My gate is open and my fruit is sweet.

speaker: Bayek
en: My life was undone here. Yet now there is a shrine, a memorial where none should be. Could this be for Rudjek? None could care for that snake that began this twisted quest, could they?

speaker: Bayek
en: Rudjek's arrow. I marked his name off my list with this. Now it sits on the ground, forgotten.

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone has sealed this room. The smell of blood I spilled still lingers here.

speaker: Bayek
en: A mummified heron. For resurrection? No, whoever did this must have known of Rudjek's place in the Order.

speaker: Bayek
en: Rudjek does not deserve a tomb, but this is an insult. This tomb was made for a Pharaoh. Whoever did this has defiled this place.

speaker: Bayek
en: Rudjek's mask. I barely remember what happened after I stabbed him.

speaker: Bayek
en: This room has told me all I need to know. This place was a beginning for me, and an end for Rudjek. The arrow marked both of those things. After I stabbed that bastard, things went dark. When I came back to myself, Rudjek was dead. Rudjek's body should have been left to rot. He has been laid to rest with respect by someone who wanted him to enter the Duat prepared. Whoever buried him also left this heron mummy to honor Rudjek with his gods damned namesake in the afterlife. They then returned here to pay respect to Rudjek, if these candles are any indication. No matter what, I know Rudjek's heart was found lacking. That bastard suffers in the afterlife, no matter what was done here.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will be judged one day, but I do not regret my actions. The feather will always be lighter than my heart.

speaker: Dennu
en: A little sunstroke will not stop me, I must have justice!

speaker: Priest
en: You must rest, neb (sir)!

speaker: Dennu
en: And every minute I keen like a sick infant, that cheat has my father's ring.

speaker: Dennu
en: They fuss like clucking hens!

speaker: Bayek
en: How did you end up here, neb (sir)?

speaker: Dennu
en: A fisherman on the road to Swenett, said I tore his nets and set the soldiers on me! They took everything I owned.

speaker: Bayek
en: The soldiers stole from you?

speaker: Dennu
en: Recompense for the injury. As if nets are worth my father's ring! The Steward should do something, but I waited all day in the sun to see him.

speaker: Bayek
en: A suspicious scheme indeed.

speaker: Dennu
en: And the road is busy, many head to the desert west of the village. More will fall foul of it!

speaker: Bayek
en: I will talk to this so-called fisherman.

speaker: Dennu
en: And I will go again to the Steward. One way or another justice will be done. The Steward must listen, or others will be in danger.

speaker: Hagiel
en: No! My nets! You've ruined my livelihood. Will no one give me justice?

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Another troublemaker.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Pay for the damage, neb (sir). Or face the cells.

speaker: Hagiel
en: Please, it's not what you think! Please!

speaker: Bayek
en: I think that you and the soldiers are working together. Extorting travelers on the road.

speaker: Hagiel
en: Ah, so it is what you think. But I am as much as a victim as the merchants.

speaker: Bayek
en: How so, a ratty little thief like you?

speaker: Hagiel
en: Ratty? No, the steward is to blame! He holds my family captive, threatened to kill them if I did not go along with his scheme.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your family?

speaker: Hagiel
en: My cat! Lord Furface is all the family I have. Most pay up without a fuss, those that don't the guards convince. And the steward takes all.

speaker: Bayek
en: I do not want to see you here again.

speaker: Hagiel
en: No! No, you won't. A man can always get a new cat.

speaker: Bayek
en: The merchant puts his head in the lion's mouth, I must find him first.

speaker: Man 1
en: The steward goes too far! I turned a blind eye to his corruption because he let me be, but this is murder.

speaker: Man 2
en: Dennu was no threat, he just wanted his father's ring returned.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why would they do this? He was no threat.

speaker: Bayek
en: This man was murdered as a warning to me?

speaker: Bayek
en: The steward's oppressive reign is about to end.

speaker: Bayek
en: You should have protected these people, now you will answer to Osiris.

speaker: Bayek
en: His father's ring. I wonder if there is a way to return it to him.

speaker: Bayek
en: His father's ring. Perhaps if ever I venture into his afterlife, I can return it.

speaker: Setna
en: Only my oblivion will please him! Can I ever be a man in his great eyes?

speaker: Setna
en: How can I hope to best those beasts? Father can command all he wants, but I'm no warrior.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your father has you hunting scorpions, boy?

speaker: Setna
en: Boy? Another come to patronize me. Forgive me, I am tired of trying to make him understand. Him and his damned trails. I do not want to walk his path, neb. (lord).

speaker: Bayek
en: Bayek. You wish to choose for yourself. Tell me of this ceremony you risk your life for.

speaker: Setna
en: He thinks it will make me a man, accept my responsibilities. Recover the symbols, strength, protection, power. Folklore and fallacies.

speaker: Bayek
en: But you don't want to defy him. Even if that means oblivion. Perhaps I could be your champion.

speaker: Setna
en: And what would that make me? A coward? A failure...

speaker: Bayek
en: Smart. Such trials are not the only thing that makes a man. I would teach my son this.

speaker: Setna
en: By Ra's light you are right, Bayek. I will wait for you north of here. Not even Serqet's protection could save me from their venomous embrace.

speaker: Golden Scorpion Blood
en: The symbol of strength needed by Setna for the trials set by his father.

speaker: Bayek
en: A scorpion's blood. A vigorous symbol of strength.

speaker: Bayek
en: Setna will want to know he does not have to face Serqet's child.

speaker: Setna
en: You did it? You got the blood? Was it terrifying? Pitted against a fearsome foe, not knowing if you would live or die?

speaker: Bayek
en: You have a way with words.

speaker: Setna
en: Do you think? My dearest wish is to be a scribe.

speaker: Bayek
en: Does your father know this?

speaker: Setna
en: The mighty warrior? It would shame him to have a writer for an heir?

speaker: Bayek
en: He will want his legacy to be a good son. What is our next trial?

speaker: Setna
en: The symbol of protection. We must steal an from the Caverns of the Valiant. Can it be desecration, in the realm of the dead?

speaker: Bayek
en: I will return to you when I have it.

speaker: Setna
en: For the final trial... Come find me at the end to the caverns. Stealing a symbol of life from the hands of the dead. Irony thy name is father.

speaker: Ankh
en: A symbol of long life and protection. The second of the trophies demanded by Setna's father.

speaker: Bayek
en: An ancient token of life and protection.

speaker: Bayek
en: Setna's father means to show him a tenet of manhood. Protect those in your care.

speaker: Setna
en: Such a small thing, was it very hard to get? Did the spirits of the fallen scream and shriek? Wrap their icy fingers around your throat?

speaker: Bayek
en: You have a vivid imagination.

speaker: Setna
en: It is both a blessing and a curse.

speaker: Bayek
en: What happens when the trials are done?

speaker: Setna
en: I will confront my father. Do you think he will hear me?

speaker: Bayek
en: Stand strong and proud. He will hear you.

speaker: Setna
en: The last trial is to take the Pharaoh's postiche from the great sand sea. It will be spewed forth from the desert.

speaker: Bayek
en: The symbol of power is the beard?

speaker: Setna
en: A boy is a boy no longer with hair on his chin. I will meet you at the Sanctum of Har-si-ese. I would like to grow a beard, do you think it will be red as my hair?

speaker: Bayek
en: Can the Jackal's guardian have the postiche?

speaker: Bayek
en: They say a man's strength lies in his beard, and yet I let Aya shave mine off.

speaker: Bayek
en: What will Setna's father do with such a trinket?

speaker: Setna
en: Great Ramesses, keeper of harmony and balance. My father, your trials are completed, your will done. But I will not follow you.

speaker: Setna
en: My path is my own to walk.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then go with Ra, my son.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are not the lion leading an army of sheep, Bayek. But their destinies are forged in the flames you lit. Let that bring you peace.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ha! The story of our quest, he has cast me as the conquering hero. I almost blush.

speaker: Bayek
en: Would Khemu have followed my footsteps? Or carved his own path?

speaker: Bayek
en: The Instruction of Amenemope, a father's advice to his son on living a pious life.

speaker: Man
en: Be quick! They are selling fast. Unique and valuable treasures from Siwa! Rare treasures, straight from the hands of the gods! Genuine treasures, all the way from Siwa. Would you like?

speaker: Man
en: Hey, how much do you want for that badge?

speaker: Man
en: I see you bear the markings of old Siwa. Is that a real Medjay badge? How much would you sell it for?

speaker: Bayek
en: Siwa is my homeland. And it is not for sale.

speaker: Man
en: Everything is for sale here. You should visit Valley Market, to the east. They have Siwan treasures. Not the normal fake stuff. These are real.

speaker: Bayek
en: I would be interested to meet anyone selling genuine Siwan treasures.

speaker: Man
en: Are you sure you do not want to sell that badge? No matter. Look for the stall under the bird nests. You will thank me.

speaker: Man
en: Did you hear about that new stall with treasures from the Temple in Siwa?

speaker: Woman
en: From a Temple? Are you crazy? You don't want something stolen from a god! Wait, are they real?

speaker: Man
en: Why do you think they're so expensive? I would sell my whole life for an Ankh of Amun!

speaker: Kenthap
en: Welcome! We have many unique treasures for sale. Would you like?

speaker: Bayek
en: This is meant to be genuine, but it's a fake. And not a very good one.

speaker: Kenthap
en: It is not fake, it is real! Would you like?

speaker: Bayek
en: This is your stall?

speaker: Kenthap
en: Yes, mine! Many unique treasures from faraway Siwa! Not fake! Not fake!

speaker: Bayek
en: Have you got anything... real? I'm sure these are not your best pieces.

speaker: Kenthap
en: What do you mean! These are real! Hmm. More expensive ones at my camp. I can take you. Not far from here. You follow.

speaker: Kenthap
en: That Medjay badge not very good you know. We have better ones. Would you like?

speaker: Bayek
en: I like this one. These other treasures of yours, are they fake as well?

speaker: Kenthap
en: I told you, not fake! Aw, how did you know. My treasures aren't really real, but not fake! My mother has some real ones anyway.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hey, I have a secret. I was once a Medjay in Siwa. I have seen the real treasures.

speaker: Kenthap
en: Aw, not fair! I made them all myself, you know. No one else can tell!

speaker: Bayek
en: Do not worry, they're very good fakes. I won't tell anyone.

speaker: Kenthap
en: I said not fake! Were you really Medjay? Maybe you are fake!

speaker: Bayek
en: You're a very cheeky child. Let's see what your mother has.

speaker: Kenthap
en: We go along the canal.

speaker: Bayek
en: You lead. I will fake it.

speaker: Kenthap
en: Does not even make sense!

speaker: Kenthap
en: My mother! Oh no, what can we do? Something is wrong!

speaker: Bayek
en: Do not be afraid. Lucky for you, I am real. Stay here and keep hidden.

speaker: Man
en: Counterfeit treasures are our game. We are the Fake Bandits here. Give us the money, and we might not kill you.

speaker: Woman
en: There is no money left! It was all given away. Please, check yourself. I've got nothing.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have got a nice sword. Would you like?

speaker: Bandit
en: Who in Hades are you?

speaker: Woman
en: Take anything you want. As I told them, I do not have any money. But I have many unique treasures from Siwa.

speaker: Kenthap
en: Mother he is not a bandit! He is my friend. Thanks for saving us. I guess you are real. Sorry I said you were fake.

speaker: Woman
en: He saved us? We have to give him something. We always repay kindness, remember. I've got something... here. This is a genuine Imitation Siwan Khopesh. It is very rare, they don't make them anymore. Please take it with our gratitude.

speaker: Kenthap
en: Mother, he already knows...

speaker: Bayek
en: Thank-you. I'm honoured. Yes I can tell. This one's really real. There are almost none like it.

speaker: Woman
en: May you multiply happy years!

speaker: Bayek
en: Hello again! How are your Siwan treasures selling?

speaker: Kenthap
en: No, no. No Siwa. Too much trouble! We sell real treasure from Giza now! Not fake! Would you like?

speaker: Bayek
en: Ha-ha. You are still a cheeky child.

speaker: Iakchos
en: There is nothing to be gained from unrest! Zeus will protect our founder.

speaker: Iakchos
en: Phylakitai, please! Are you a protector? If you have a moment? The fate of our founder is at stake!

speaker: Bayek
en: I am not a Phylakitai. I am a Medjay.

speaker: Iakchos
en: Oh yes, of course, I should have noticed. These people don't understand, our Roman 'friends' do not take kindly to civil disobedience.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why are they protesting?

speaker: Iakchos
en: They fear all is not well with our founder, the great Battos. The Centurion locked his tomb, some say he desecrated the dead in there, left a scrawled note on on the door and sauntered back to the Akropolis. Please, someone should investigate, without alerting the Romans. And if that someone were to find anything they could meet me here, and I'd be happy to help.

speaker: Iakchos
en: The Romans have no respect. Did you find anything?

speaker: Bayek
en: The Greeks also treat their dead with great honor. And now they suffer like Egyptians.

speaker: Bayek
en: Empty! Drunk and stupid is a troublesome combination.

speaker: Bayek
en: Have the Romans no respect for the dead?

speaker: Bayek
en: The tomb's been ransacked. The Romans were looking for something.

speaker: Bayek
en: Something is missing.

speaker: Bayek
en: The founder must have been buried with these treasures. The bow and the medallion are gone. The Romans are little more than tomb robbers! The Greeks are learning what it feels like to be Egyptians, have your land, your dead and your relics desecrated by an invading force.

speaker: Bayek
en: Battos' medallion.

speaker: Bayek
en: This must be the bow of Battos'.

speaker: Bayek
en: The priest will be glad to see the relics returned.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your suspicions were well founded. The Romans took Battos' treasure.

speaker: Iakchos
en: You have the relics?

speaker: Bayek
en: I do, they were not given the respect they were due.

speaker: Iakchos
en: Those filthy desecrators! I will keep Battos' medallion safe. Legend says if it leaves the city so will our fortunes.

speaker: Bayek
en: And the bow?

speaker: Iakchos
en: It longs to be in the service of Cyrenaica again. Please, keep it, maybe teach the Romans a lesson in honoring the dead?

speaker: Bayek
en: Gladly.

speaker: Iakchos
en: The founder sent you to us. Farewell, Medjay.

speaker: Reda
en: Sometimes, these old relics need a bit of help to be perfect again, but I'm missing a few things...

speaker: Reda
en: Ah! Medjay, just the man I needed. I have the perfect thing for you, but I need a few things to fix it...

speaker: Reda
en: I need some things to finish a piece I'm working on. Since you wander the desert perhaps you can find a few things for Reda.

speaker: Reda
en: A completed task requires a reward, does it not?

speaker: Reda
en: You never cease to impress, Bayek.

speaker: Reda
en: You did it? Ah yes, of course. I never doubted you.

speaker: Reda
en: Well done, Medjay! As promised, this is for you.

speaker: Bayek
en: I need to hunt for leather.

speaker: Bayek
en: This will be enough. Thanks to Neith, goddess of hunting.

speaker: Bayek
en: This will work perfectly.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: A solid breastplate. That will help!

speaker: Gennadios
en: See that workers on the docks are rounded up and questioned. When I say questioned, I mean beaten. They must know something. Find this woman! She has murdered a friend of the royal court.

speaker: Guard
en: At your command, Phylakitai!

speaker: Gennadios
en: Why have you dragged me into the land of the dead?

speaker: Bayek
en: You sought to kill my wife!

speaker: Gennadios
en: Your whore of a wife is a murderess! Willfully and wantonly. I did my duty as a Phylakitai. And for this, you have taken my life.

speaker: Gennadios
en: Is your vengeance above all law, Medjay? Be warned, the Phylakes will hunt you down and exact revenge.

speaker: Bayek
en: May the Hidden One walk beside you. The lord of the Duat awaits.

speaker: Khui
en: Wash the scales from my eyes! Do not take them, they are my sole comfort.

speaker: Khui
en: Have the shrouded ones sent you to me?

speaker: Bayek
en: What happened to you, neb (sir)?

speaker: Khui
en: I grieve for the true gods. This is my crime.

speaker: Khui
en: Are you the Lord of Thebes...?

speaker: Bayek
en: I will return you home.

speaker: Khui
en: Home? It lies south-west of the bridge, but my hearth is dark with the lioness fled.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why were you imprisoned, neb (sir)?

speaker: Khui
en: Titans stand upon the shoulders of men. I speak of things they have forgotten. A black beaked ibis, a cawing hawk...

speaker: Bayek
en: Some memory haunts you.

speaker: Khui
en: The quick claws of the cat...The sun sears my eyes. It should not blaze so.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hush, old man you are nearly home.

speaker: Bayek
en: What is eluding you, neb (sir)?

speaker: Khui
en: Who do you honor? Your family, your gods?

speaker: Bayek
en: I still honor the gods.

speaker: Khui
en: Then you are blessed. Each moment they fade a little further into shadow. Only in the inky hours do they come. Tenebrous, hidden, but they whisper as I sleep.

speaker: Bayek
en: They send you dreams? What do they say?

speaker: Khui
en: The chaos waters swallowed two. The blue hawk lies with the forgotten treasures, the black cat gasps for air with the old idols. The green Ibis, flaps his great wings but he cannot escape the jaws of the bloodless titan.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will help you remember.

speaker: Khui
en: In a state of ruin my mind remembers, returning to another time, the time of the gods.

speaker: Bayek
en: Now I can restore the gods to Khui.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Akhenaten heretic still walks.

speaker: Bayek
en: I hope these likenesses of the gods soothe Khui.

speaker: Khui
en: Yes! I remember him, lord of the hidden sun, Amun-Ra!

speaker: Khui
en: You think you betray your past, Bayek?

speaker: Bayek
en: This path you walk now, the tenets you live by, they are within us all. We too value the innocent, we too long for peace. If you desire peace, Bayek, accept it.

speaker: Bayek
en: There is an inscription here. Thoth, Revealer of the hidden, Soul of the Becoming, Scribe of the nine gods. As a boy the priests would make us pray to him for 'wise council'. Thoth seldom granted it to me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Horus, Lord of the Sky. (soft laugh) Khemu would beg and beg me to tell him the story of Set and Horus. How they turned themselves into hippopotamus to see who could remain under water the longest.

speaker: Bayek
en: The goddess Bastet. Hepzefa told me a story of a Persian King who turned the tide of battle. He ordered her image painted upon his soldiers' shields and our men refused to fight!

speaker: Bayek
en: This place, the shrine. It prickles with divine power. The Oracle is drawing me to her, I can feel it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Offerings and prayers to the Oracle from the great and good of Cyrenaica.

speaker: Phoebe
en: Apollo's lyre, Apollo's song, I speak with the voice of light.

speaker: Phoebe
en: I have felt your presence in my visions, Eagle. Apollo spoke of you. The King cried when he killed the . For it was the huntress bewitched, pale and beautiful with a halo of gold. Apollo bade Gaea cradle the King's sorrow, a lake of tears above the plains. The sun god drove his fist into the mountain, took his beloved inside and spake. "None shall seek you. None but the Eagle. He will soar above the five cities with the Halo of the Huntress in his beak."

speaker: Bayek
en: Why do you call me Eagle?

speaker: Phoebe
en: Yours is the sacred relic, Eagle. Find it and expand your riches.

speaker: Bayek
en: A lake of tears high in the mountains? Apollo means me to find this Halo of the Huntress.

speaker: Phoebe
en: When the Aten rises, those who bore the will walk. He walks in splendor in the footsteps of the Therans. A god made flesh. A new peace will come. Seek out the triumvirate. The healer, the architect, the judge. The healer's staff is not what it seems. The viper uncoiled lies in whispers. The she-wolf comes from the waters. But vultures will feast upon the jackal's marrow. Whether by sea or between the sheets, the black land is conquered. He who was born of the thunderbolts holds the relic of the elder ones. The Macedon Rex will sink in the Crocodile's tears. Heed the Ides of March. Trust the trickster. His whiskers do not lie. What you seek is legion. The hog wallows in the mud, stuff an apple in his mouth, Eagle. The eaglet waits for you in the fields of your forebearers. If the Eagle spies the true ram, the descendant of Ra will fall. You walk a path in the shadow of We That Came Before. The Hidden One will greet you, but not yet, not yet. Sanguine is the key that unlocks the door. Your soul is shrouded. Trapped in the shadowlands between being and oblivion. Paris will have his Helen, no matter the cost. Orpheus and Eurydice will be torn asunder. Do not look back. There is no certainty, Eagle. You may as well hold a wolf by the ears. Beware the three-headed , for he will devour the asp. An empire will arise from his ashes. A death among kings will set ablaze the house of Amun. More terrible men will arise in his place. Then you will know the true meaning of tyranny.

speaker: Bayek
en: The lake of tears. What was the next part? The sun god drove his fist into the mountain?

speaker: Bayek
en: Cracks in the rock, something is behind.

speaker: Bayek
en: The divine huntress Cyrene, herself.

speaker: Bayek
en: The legend of Cyrene and Apollo.

speaker: Bayek
en: Apollo fell in love with her.

speaker: Bayek
en: The girl lion-killer. She sounds strong and brave, reminds me of Aya.

speaker: Bayek
en: A crown? This must be the halo from the prophecy. I thank Apollo for this sacred gift.

speaker: Thanasis
en: Do you have any idea how much those men are worth?

speaker: Egidio
en: I will find some mercenaries to help get them back.

speaker: Thanasis
en: Where do you think we are? There are no mercenaries here. Idiot. Ten years! I trained those men for ten years! I finally had the talent to get me to Rome. Rome!

speaker: Bayek
en: What has this man done to deserve such abuse?

speaker: Thanasis
en: He fled like a rank coward, leaving my gladiators to be taken captive.

speaker: Bayek
en: Gladiators? Can't they protect themselves?

speaker: Thanasis
en: They were sleeping. Egidio here was meant to keep watch... Kosey and Wamukota! My two best gladiators!

speaker: Egidio
en: We were on our way to the arena and were ambushed by bandits. I managed to escape.

speaker: Thanasis
en: You damn coward!

speaker: Bayek
en: I will get your gladiators back, but leave this poor man alone.

speaker: Thanasis
en: When you find my men, bring them to the Cyrene Arena right away.

speaker: Egidio
en: We were attacked northeast from here. Near a wooden bridge on the road to Cyrene.

speaker: Thanasis
en: Come Egidio. We may win the championship yet!

speaker: Bayek
en: This is the bridge Egidio mentioned. The bandits must be nearby.

speaker: Bayek
en: Here is one gladiator. He appears to be drugged. I will get him out of here.

speaker: Wamukota
en: Uuuh... who... are you?

speaker: Bayek
en: Egidio sent me to find you. Can you walk?

speaker: Wamukota
en: I'll try.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you all right? Where is the other gladiator?

speaker: Wamukota
en: That bastard. He betrayed us. He faked his own abduction!

speaker: Bayek
en: What?

speaker: Wamukota
en: The bandits spoke to Kosey as a friend and gave him a horse.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do you have any idea where he went?

speaker: Wamukota
en: They told him everything was ready at the lake in the mountain to the north. If you find him, punch him in the face for me, will you?

speaker: Bayek
en: Sure. Thanasis and Egidio are at the Cyrene Arena, waiting for you. You should rest first, though.

speaker: Wamukota
en: Be careful, friend. Kosey is very strong!

speaker: Bayek
en: A child all alone?

speaker: Bayek
en: Hello, little one! What are you doing here?

speaker: Zalika
en: I'm not little! I'm five years old!

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm sorry! My name is Bayek. What is yours?

speaker: Kosey
en: Zalika! Get home to your mother. Now!

speaker: Bayek
en: I am not here to fight you, Kosey.

speaker: Kosey
en: I'm done with all of it! You'll be the last man I kill.

speaker: Hesper
en: Kosey! Stop!

speaker: Hesper
en: Excuse my husband. It has been a difficult journey.

speaker: Bayek
en: Wamukota told me what happened.

speaker: Kosey
en: I'm glad he's safe. I didn't want him to get hurt.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why fake your own abduction? Could you not buy your freedom from Thanasis?

speaker: Kosey
en: I tried, but he refused. As his best gladiator, I can bring him fame beyond price.

speaker: Bayek
en: Stay with your family, Kosey. I will deal with Thanasis.

speaker: Hesper
en: You are truly sent by the gods!

speaker: Kosey
en: Hesper is a strong woman. She raised Zalika by herself. Look at her. I missed her first few years, but I'll be there for her now. The bandits drugged Wamukota. I needed him to keep silent until I got away.

speaker: Hesper
en: Kosey is an even better father than he is a fighter. Let us hope that all this is behind us now. Zalika is so much like her father. You should see her when she's angry!

speaker: Zalika
en: Can I play with your bow? If you hurt my father again, I will beat you! Don't walk there! You will scare the ants!

speaker: Thanasis
en: I'll show the Romans. They think I'm not good enough. They think no one is as good as they are.

speaker: Egidio
en: We'll show them, master.

speaker: Thanasis
en: We must formally enter soon, or we will not be permitted in the tournament. I cannot believe I'm so close. Where are they?

speaker: Thanasis
en: Did you find replacement gladiators?

speaker: Egidio
en: No, Thanasis. No one would accept at that price.

speaker: Thanasis
en: Ah! There you are. Where are my gladiators?

speaker: Bayek
en: They will not come. Wamukota is wounded, and Kosey has declared his freedom.

speaker: Thanasis
en: What? I own Kosey! I say whether he's free or not.

speaker: Bayek
en: He is gone. I advise you find other fighters.

speaker: Thanasis
en: Now there is an idea. I have a deal for you. You fight for me. Win and I'll give you rich rewards.

speaker: Bayek
en: That and sign formally for Kosey's freedom.

speaker: Thanasis
en: I like your style! Enter the arena. And win! Make me proud!

speaker: Bayek
en: Just remember. I do not work for you.

speaker: Thanasis
en: After a round, yell out that you fight for Thanasis. You win, Kosey will be free. Simple! It's over there. Hurry!

speaker: Bayek
en: I won. Where is your master?

speaker: Egidio
en: Please, you must help Kosey. Wamukota came back and told us what he did. Master Thanasis paid some Roman soldiers, and they all went to get Kosey back.

speaker: Bayek
en: That rat. Egidio, you'd best find a new master. Nek. I hope I am not too late.

speaker: Egidio
en: Kosey deserves a happy life. I knew it was a trick, but I played along to fool Thanasis. Please help Kosey, whatever it takes.

speaker: Thanasis
en: You belong to me, Kosey! I decide your fate, boy.

speaker: Zalika
en: Leave my father alone!

speaker: Kosey
en: Zalika! Stay back!

speaker: Thanasis
en: You want to keep your family safe, don't you? So calmly come with me. You can send them money from your winnings.

speaker: Hesper
en: Let him go, Thanasis! He's done enough!

speaker: Thanasis
en: Quiet, you! I tolerated your little love story long enough. You ruined everything!

speaker: Kosey
en: Please, leave them alone.

speaker: Thanasis
en: I'll keep an eye on them. Why would you fight for me if there is no carrot at the end of the stick? Think about that. You not only betrayed me, you also sent someone after me. He's probably lying dead in Cyrene Arena by now.

speaker: Thanasis
en: Louder, boy! I cannot hear you!

speaker: Kosey
en: I will make you pay.

speaker: Thanasis
en: Such ingratitude. Zalika. Tell your father to obey me or I will make him suffer more!

speaker: Zalika
en: My father will kill you first!

speaker: Thanasis
en: She clearly is your daughter, Kosey.

speaker: Thanasis
en: You?! Kill him!

speaker: Hesper
en: Bayek!

speaker: Bayek
en: Hesper! Take Zalika and hide!

speaker: Thanasis
en: I thought you'd be dead in the arena.

speaker: Bayek
en: We had a deal, Thanasis.

speaker: Thanasis
en: You are a fool. I trained Kosey since he was eight years old. I own him!

speaker: Kosey
en: I won't go back!

speaker: Bayek
en: You will own nothing in the Duat.

speaker: Thanasis
en: You do not know who you are dealing with.

speaker: Bayek
en: I know enough.

speaker: Thanasis
en: You would have made a fine gladiator. The money we could have made.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are a free man now, Kosey.

speaker: Hesper
en: Our son will be named after you.

speaker: Bayek
en: A son? Your family is growing?

speaker: Hesper
en: Yes. And thanks to you, Kosey will be here to see it.

speaker: Kosey
en: It's not much, but take this. I have no use for it now.

speaker: Kosey
en: Farewell my friend. I hope our paths cross again.

speaker: Kosey
en: It feels good to be a free man. I never talked to you about it. You really won that tournament? I'm impressed. Zalika is excited to have a little brother.

speaker: Hesper
en: Zalika is happy to have her father around. You are welcome here any time.

speaker: Zalika
en: My father could have killed that man alone! When I grow up, I want to fight in the arena! Do you have a wife? You're old, you should have a wife.

speaker: Ebio
en: I have not seen my husband since yesterday. Help me find him! Give me your aid! I order you! Will you not accompany me? Sekhmet favors the generous!

speaker: Ebio
en: Medjay! Help me... I will pay you!

speaker: Bayek
en: What do you need?

speaker: Ebio
en: Last night, my dear husband Klaudios took a boat out to see the ruins across the lake. He has not returned! None of these brutes honor a wife's pain. I beg you...

speaker: Bayek
en: I will seek him out.

speaker: Ebio
en: Do be quick. I will await you here.

speaker: Klaudios
en: Let me be... me in peace! (Leave me alone!) Foulest of foul beasts...

speaker: Bayek
en: And here is Klaudios.

speaker: Klaudios
en: I... did you... (Crocodiles) can talk! Always something new from Africa. Why are you so angry? Oh, gods... I think I am going to... Hey, you! ... Hello?

speaker: Bayek
en: Klaudios? Stay where you are!

speaker: Bayek
en: The crocodiles are dead. Now to speak to Klaudios and find out why he came out here.

speaker: Klaudios
en: Why did you... kill them? We had only just met!

speaker: Bayek
en: Klaudios, you're drunk.

speaker: Klaudios
en: Yes! That is me... and NO! I am not. I had only two or ten beers.

speaker: Bayek
en: All right, let's get you back to your wife.

speaker: Klaudios
en: I have a wife?! Mother will be so pleased!

speaker: Bayek
en: What was your reason for going out there, Klaudios?

speaker: Klaudios
en: I was going... mhhmm... I do not really remember. I came from Alexandria for the festival... and some kind of... person... someone... offered me to drink all night. For free! Impossible to resi... resist. What were we talking about?

speaker: Bayek
en: How you got here.

speaker: Klaudios
en: Oh, right! Then I woke up here, with those (crocodiles) all around. Tell me, can they really speak?

speaker: Bayek
en: Egypt' is a land full of magic and ancient mystery.

speaker: Klaudios
en: Amazing! My friends in the city will never believe it. Did you say something about a wife?

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes. Yours.

speaker: Klaudios
en: See, I do not understand that. How could I have a wife? I am a virgin. At least. I think I am...

speaker: Bayek
en: I will hear no more on this subject. You can take it up with your wife.

speaker: Klaudios
en: But you do not understand! Every woman I've ever tried to f

speaker: Bayek
en: Please shut up.

speaker: Klaudios
en: I am sorry. This fresh wind off the river is good for me. I am feeling much more clear-headed now!

speaker: Bayek
en: Splendid.

speaker: Ebio
en: There you are, my dear! I was worried about you.

speaker: Klaudios
en: Oh, by Dionysos! I remember. I went to the island because of her! She... She got me drunk, married me, and told me I owed her a "virginity tax". Whose virginity?

speaker: Ebio
en: You can go. This is between me and my husband.

speaker: Klaudios
en: No, no... no! No, don't-- don't go. They'll kill me.

speaker: Ebio
en: Show him what happens when you try to cheat a woman. Forget him! He's just an idiot Greek. They have taken enough from our land!

speaker: Klaudios
en: Please, help me!

speaker: Ebio
en: Yes, that is right! Taste your own blood!

speaker: Klaudios
en: Mercy! Mercy!

speaker: Ebio
en: Your tax collectors never listened when we begged for mercy. Go on! Hit him harder!

speaker: Klaudios
en: Why do you let them do this?

speaker: Ebio
en: My brothers! You have slain my brothers, You were suppose to help me, not him!

speaker: Klaudios
en: Praise and thanks! You saved my life... and my purse.

speaker: Bayek
en: In future, be careful when drinking with strangers.

speaker: Klaudios
en: Oh, my aching head. I was so looking forward to surprising mother with my new bride. I will never drink again.

speaker: Bayek
en: And you. I had no wish to kill your brothers, but the three of you brought this on yourselves.

speaker: Fenuku
en: Chenzira!

speaker: Bayek
en: Fenuku! It is dangerous here. Get on home.

speaker: Fenuku
en: Bayek? You're back?

speaker: Bayek
en: Where is Chenzira?

speaker: Fenuku
en: He wanted to see the skulls in the hyena den. But the hyenas came back. I ran this way. Chenzira ran over by the tomb.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are lucky the hyenas didn't chase you. Go back to the village. I will find your brother.

speaker: Fenuku
en: Um...

speaker: Bayek
en: What?

speaker: Fenuku
en: Do I have to tell my parents?

speaker: Bayek
en: Chenzira got you into this. He will have to talk to them. Now go ahead.

speaker: Bayek
en: Chenzira! Stay there. I'm coming to get you.

speaker: Chenzira
en: Bayek? Is that you? You've come back?

speaker: Bayek
en: How did Chenzira get through here?

speaker: Bayek
en: Chenzira! Are you all right?

speaker: Chenzira
en: I can't believe you're back.

speaker: Bayek
en: You should not be in here!

speaker: Chenzira
en: I'm hiding from hyenas.

speaker: Bayek
en: Fenuku told me about that. It is not enough to get yourself in trouble? Now you put your little brother in danger?

speaker: Chenzira
en: But... it's... with Khemu gone...

speaker: Bayek
en: All right, I understand... Let's get you out of here.

speaker: Chenzira
en: Bayek! Look at that! What is it?

speaker: Bayek
en: I would like to know myself. Must be very old.

speaker: Chenzira
en: Someday I'll learn to read what it says.

speaker: Bayek
en: Which way did you get in?

speaker: Chenzira
en: That way. But that's where the hyenas are. Bayek. I want to tell... well...

speaker: Bayek
en: What is it, Chenzira?

speaker: Chenzira
en: It's my fault about Khemu. They asked where you were and I didn't think it would hurt anybody if I told them.

speaker: Bayek
en: Chenzira, don't feel bad. You had no way of knowing what they would do. Anyone would have done the same thing in your place.

speaker: Chenzira
en: I guess.

speaker: Bayek
en: Keep close.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hyena! Chenzira, hide!

speaker: Chenzira
en: They're still here! Help me!

speaker: Bayek
en: It is safe now. You better get home.

speaker: Chenzira
en: Bayek. Can I ask you something?

speaker: Bayek
en: Go on.

speaker: Chenzira
en: Could I be a Medjay like you one day?

speaker: Bayek
en: Well, you can start by looking out for your brother and not taking him to dangerous places.

speaker: Chenzira
en: I promise!

speaker: Bayek
en: Now get back home.

speaker: Tjepu
en: Tefibi, you will be the death of me.

speaker: Tefibi
en: No, mother, I will be your salvation. No more olives! No more payment to rent a press!

speaker: Tjepu
en: Pay attention to what you have in front of you, idiot boy! Not the mirage you see in the distance.

speaker: Tefibi
en: But what a mirage, mother! The white linens of a philosopher, and with that, drachmas!

speaker: Tjepu
en: Coins would come from the papyrus you lost! Are you sure this is where you lost it?

speaker: Tefibi
en: I already told you! The papyrus was taken from me!

speaker: Tjepu
en: Just admit that you lost it!

speaker: Tefibi
en: It was taken from me mother. Do not fret, I'll get it back. I only need a small bit of help!

speaker: Tjepu
en: Medjay! Your help is needed... again. my idiot son left my offering in his papyrus. Which he lost. I cannot sell my oil without giving thanks!

speaker: Tefibi
en: I did not lose it. The guards took it. That papyrus is my life, Medjay!

speaker: Bayek
en: They go too far, these guards.

speaker: Tefibi
en: The papyrus had my notes! Those bastards threw it on a boat.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will look into this, Tefibi. And I will find your offering, little mother.

speaker: Tjepu
en: My soul is troubled. The Pharaoh's guards have yet to forget Tefibi's actions.

speaker: Tefibi
en: I will find us a better path, Medjay. Never fear.

speaker: Bayek
en: This must be the boat that Tefibi spoke of. I might well be able to get in unseen.

speaker: Bayek
en: These guards will know better than to trouble Tefibi from now on.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is the papyrus... and the offering. Both Tefibi and Tjepu will be happy.

speaker: Tefibi
en: Now I'll prove to them I can match them in wits.

speaker: Tjepu
en: Still spouting your nonsense! The Greeks will never accept you!

speaker: Tefibi
en: Yes, they will! I will be a philosopher soon!

speaker: Bayek
en: Your offering. Now you can return to selling your olive oil.

speaker: Tjepu
en: I worry about him forever. It is hard to understand when you do not have children.

speaker: Bayek
en: ...Allow Tefibi his chance. He'll be alright.

speaker: Khati
en: Medjay, help me! O glory, a protector of Egypt, please, we are in grave danger.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are Khati, yes?

speaker: Khati
en: I will not ask how you knew, but for the future of Egypt, we must flee.

speaker: Bayek
en: Who are you?

speaker: Khati
en: An Egyptian like yourself seni, for the safety of Egypt, we must flee.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why did the Romans capture you?

speaker: Khati
en: For the knowledge I have... but we should not talk here.

speaker: Khati
en: How did you find me, Medjay? Did the spymaster send you?

speaker: Bayek
en: The Centurion's list led me here.

speaker: Khati
