en: You have the list? The names of the shrouded ones in Cyrenaica?

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes, you and another of Apollodorus' agents survived. I freed him from the barracks in Balagrae.

speaker: Khati
en: You have done Egypt and Apollodorus a great service, Medjay. Amun Ra reward you.

speaker: Khati
en: I am one of Apollodorus' most trusted spies. Part of his divine manipulation of the threads

speaker: Khati
en: Someone betrayed us, gave up our agents in Cyrenaica. That is how the Centurion found me, he has a list of names.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then it cannot remain in his hands.

speaker: Khati
en: He patrols the border towers. Find the bastard, see what information he has, what others can be saved.

speaker: Baeks
en: For Egypt.

speaker: Khati
en: For a free Egypt. May our victories multiply.

speaker: Bayek
en: There is another spy in Balagrae? He's in great danger.

speaker: Hypatos
en: You killed my master and left me for dead. That was a mistake.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your master was a murderer.

speaker: Hypatos
en: I am his sworn bodyguard. It is a question of honor.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am the Medjay of Siwa.

speaker: Hypatos
en: Then you are a worthy opponent. You are quick, Medjay. But I am powerful. I will be proud to have fought the last Medjay. I respect your tenacity. You have fought well. You will have an honorable death.

speaker: Hypatos
en: A broken weapon won't save you. This place will serve as tomb to one of us. Let it be you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let us call truce. You are not one I've sworn to kill.

speaker: Hypatos
en: Question of honor. It is a fight to the death.

speaker: Bayek
en: So be it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Anubis awaits you. No way out.

speaker: Bayek
en: This wall...

speaker: Bayek
en: Soldiers. Of course.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Where's your Medjay friend?

speaker: Bayek
en: Hepzefa! Watch out!

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Bayek! Is that you? It is an ambush!

speaker: Bayek
en: You are telling me!

speaker: Soldier 2
en: There's the Medjay! Kill him!

speaker: Captain
en: Kill his friend and I'll take care of the Medjay.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: You are supposed to be dead!

speaker: Captain
en: And you will be, we'll make sure of that!

speaker: Bayek
en: That is Horus, the Falcon. The Great Black One. God of the sky. The sun is his right eye and the moon is his left eye. Forever he flies across the heavens, making night and day.

speaker: Khemu
en: The is what the Medjay wear?

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes, Khemu.

speaker: Khemu
en: And the Pharaoh is Horus, right?

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes, my son. The Pharaoh is Horus in life, and Osiris in death. That is why the Pharaoh rules not only Egypt, but the whole world. Only a true Pharaoh though.

speaker: Haganu
en: In the dark mountains, oh traveler, take care. The howls of the dead echo in pain. A spirit of evil won't let them rest. Never to enter the Hall of Anubis. The dead do not sleep, they know only torment. Woe to any who trespass amongst them!

speaker: Haganu
en: The mountains of the Sinai, hide the tortured souls of the dead.

speaker: Bayek
en: What is this all about?

speaker: Haganu
en: Have you not heard? The old necropolis up in the mountains is haunted by all the dead who cannot enter the afterlife.

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone should look into that.

speaker: Haganu
en: Under the clang of iron, beneath the rule of Rome. Our children wail all night as our land is shipped away... When Nabatea was free, we could all die with our heads held high, and the sky was an endless banner of happiness... Give me the hand of the old pharaohs, the old kingdom will one day rise again. Oh Sinai... Oh Sinai... Oh... Sinai.

speaker: Demet
en: Oh! Dearest Iset, protect me and my poor wife!

speaker: Bayek
en: Neb. (Sir.) Do you need help?

speaker: Demet
en: My wife is ready for her journey to the Hall of Anubis, but my knees quake with fear. What awaits me at the necropolis? I have heard stories to turn a young man's hair white!

speaker: Bayek
en: I am headed there. I will take your wife's body if you like.

speaker: Demet
en: Would you? I will be a thousand times grateful!

speaker: Bayek
en: I have a grim foreboding.

speaker: Bayek
en: What fiendishness is this? The stories of evilness may be true.

speaker: Bayek
en: What evil lurks here?

speaker: Bayek
en: The storyteller's song may be true. These are the sounds of a wicked spirit.

speaker: Bayek
en: These are the arms and legs of the dead! Someone is desecrating them.

speaker: Set
en: Who dares interrupt me? I am the incarnation of Set, god of chaos! He who dismembered Osiris and spread pieces of him all across Egypt!

speaker: Bayek
en: You are a desecrater and a murderer.

speaker: Set
en: You are the incarnation of Iset! Come to stitch her husband together. You shall not!

speaker: Bayek
en: You will trouble the dead no longer.

speaker: Demet
en: Is my wife at peace?

speaker: Bayek
en: No one will prevent her journey to the field of reeds.

speaker: Demet
en: Thank you, my friend.

speaker: Sab
en: Help! Stay away, children of Sobek. Return to the chaos waters! Why does the Rager punish me?

speaker: Bayek
en: You climbed all the way up here?

speaker: Sab
en: Amun granted his poor servant strength. How else could I escape the Rager's sons? But it is all for nothing, I deserted my friend. Another priest of the Lord of Truth!

speaker: Bayek
en: I will get rid of them. Then you can tell me your story.

speaker: Sab
en: Yes! Try and shoo them off, the Lord of Strife will not be happy if you shed sacred blood.

speaker: Bayek
en: Shoo a crocodile? I... Wait here.

speaker: Sab
en: Did they leave? Did you convince them?

speaker: Bayek
en: Of a sort. Come down!

speaker: Sab
en: How? I'll break my neck! No, I must be brave! Mut, consort of the Hidden One, grant your servant... wings!

speaker: Bayek
en: Wait! I don't think...

speaker: Sab
en: Did you see me jump? And the haystack! Amun must have spirited it here to break my fall!

speaker: Bayek
en: Clearly. So, what are priests of Amun doing this far from Thebes?

speaker: Sab
en: Seni (friend), I do not mean to frighten you, but... the dead Pharaohs... they walk.

speaker: Bayek
en: So I have heard.

speaker: Sab
en: Onnos and I we were to perform a sacred ritual for Amun, reclaim these lands from the curse. But we were attacked by bandits on the road. I am ashamed to say I fled and did not look back.

speaker: Bayek
en: You left him?

speaker: Sab
en: Do you think they killed Onnos? Amun's plumes they killed Onnos!

speaker: Bayek
en: Peace, priest. I will look for him.

speaker: Sab
en: We were on our way to the top of the mountain. I will make my way there. Amun's grace he lives. Stay strong, Onnos! Each turn of the hourglass he could be dead, or worse. Curse my cowardice.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why would bandits risk Amun's wrath?

speaker: Onnos
en: Onnos. Amun put you upon the black sands for this purpose. Do not falter now!

speaker: Onnos
en: You will not turn me from my path, seni (friend)!

speaker: Bayek
en: Onnos?

speaker: Onnos
en: By Amun! You know me? Are you real, or a mirage?

speaker: Bayek
en: Are we in the desert? No. Your friend Sab sent me to aid you. Come, I will bring you to him.

speaker: Onnos
en: I cannot leave Amun's statue in their unwashed hands! I have a plan to rescue it!

speaker: Onnos
en: I just need the fresh carcass of a rabbit, some rope, a bandit's garb, a bladder of wine and...

speaker: Bayek
en: I will find the statue. Join Sab at the ritual site.

speaker: Onnos
en: You are sure? But Thoth has granted me great insight and...

speaker: Bayek
en: Go!

speaker: Bayek
en: The bandits just wanted the statue. Perhaps they think Amun can protect them from the curse?

speaker: Bayek
en: Done. And without the need of dead rabbits and disguises.

speaker: Onnos
en: ...a distraction, perhaps a mountain goat or...

speaker: Sab
en: The Lady of Slaughter is angry! her kin will not be deterred by carrion!

speaker: Onnos
en: Great mirage returns! You have the statue?

speaker: Bayek
en: I do, and you have more problems with animals.

speaker: Sab
en: Sekhmet's offspring will sharpen their claws on our bones!

speaker: Onnos
en: Simply a pride of hungry lions, but I have a plan, all I need is some twine, a bushel of hay, a shovel to dig a hole and...

speaker: Bayek
en: Stay here, and keep quiet.

speaker: Sab
en: You killed the lions! You truly fight with the wrath of Ra!

speaker: Onnos
en: We must start the ritual!

speaker: Sab
en: Hail to thee, Amun-Ra, Lord of the thrones of earth, ancient of heaven, father of all things.

speaker: Onnos
en: Deliverer of those who suffer, you hear their cries and come at their behest.

speaker: Sab
en: Lord of wisdom, lord of mercy, opener of every eye, thou whose name is hidden.

speaker: Onnos
en: Your people are struck down, terrorized, tormented...

speaker: Sab
en: Help us cleanse this land and protect your suppliants. Keep them safe in your shining radiance.

speaker: Europa
en: Pardon, neb, I cannot sell any chariots today... By Serapis, I cannot believe my eyes! That looks like a Medjay badge.

speaker: Europa
en: Please forgive me. For a moment I thought you wore the sign of the Medjay, the lost protectors.

speaker: Bayek
en: I do. I am. What pains you, nebet?

speaker: Europa
en: My heart is broken. My truest friend, my husband, Eryx, has been murdered.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tell me what happened.

speaker: Europa
en: He was renowned for his work. A soldier ordered him to build war chariots for the Pharaoh. He was happy to do so. But when the soldier returned to collect, he only offered to pay half the agreed price. Eryx refused, and the soldier cut him down and stole the chariot. If you are truly a Medjay, will you help me to get justice? Find the soldier and destroy the war chariot, so he may not insult my husband's memory!

speaker: Bayek
en: I can do that for you.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Shame the captain killed the chariot maker. His work was masterful.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Don't cry for these mouthy peasants.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: No, I was just saying... Do you think his widow is still running their shop?

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Why? Do you fancy her? You into short, older women?

speaker: Soldier 1
en: She's a handsome woman!

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Yes, well, good luck convincing her to let you into her bed while we ride around in the chariot her dead husband built.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: When does the next patrol head out?

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Soon I think.

speaker: Bayek
en: It is done. A sacrifice made to honor the builder who was cut down.

speaker: Europa
en: Honorable Medjay, what news do you bring?

speaker: Bayek
en: I have destroyed the war chariot that Eryx made, and was stolen by the vile captain of Anthylla. Your husband's memory is restored.

speaker: Man
en: You are Bayek, yes? My master is anxious that you get this letter. It is urgent!

speaker: Bayek
en: Your master? Do I know him?

speaker: Man
en: His name is Otis. You haven't met. All is explained in his letter.

speaker: Bayek
en: Will Siwa never know peace? I will go to the Saragina Camp to learn if there is any truth to this letter.

speaker: Bayek
en: I must let Rome know that Siwa is never to be harmed again. None of these men will survive.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier
en: Take it quickly and our Roman patron will pay well. Anyone offers resistance, show no mercy. Strike the fear of Anubis into 'em. Soon men, soon. Sharpen your swords, men! You'll need them.

speaker: Bayek
en: So much for the commander. He may be carrying important information.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah! This may tell me what their plan is.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will destroy these carts. And Jibade will soon meet Anubis.

speaker: Bayek
en: That must be one of the carts!

speaker: Bayek
en: That is one. Now the other two.

speaker: Bayek
en: There. One more.

speaker: Bayek
en: Jibade must be somewhere in this fortress.

speaker: Bayek
en: Very well. Now Jibade will meet my blade.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier
en: The fort commander is still unwillingly to join us.

speaker: Jibade
en: Soon more soldiers will arrive. We'll outnumber him four to one! He'll have to give in.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier
en: He'll try to hold out his fortress. We'll impose a siege and starve them out.

speaker: Jibade
en: Excellent idea.

speaker: Jibade
en: Any news from Siwa?

speaker: Egyptian Soldier
en: No. I've sent a patrol to establish contact. Captain Adras is probably busy burning the bodies.

speaker: Jibade
en: If the rumor is true, the object from Siwa will give us the power to make all Egypt ours.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier
en: I confess I'm uncomfortable with forcing Egyptian troops to join us. I swore alliance to Cleopatra just as this general has.

speaker: Jibade
en: Don't be an idiot. This man's allegiance is for sale. Enough troops to intimidate him and he'll be happy with the price. Wait patiently, commander.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier
en: I'll release extra rations of beer in the meantime. Good for morale.

speaker: Bayek
en: So much for their bribery.

speaker: Jibade
en: You'll get nothing from me. It wasn't coercion, it was liberation! We only mean to bring glory to Egypt!

speaker: Bayek
en: Very well. I've done what I can. Now I will see Otis in Alexandria. He may have found out what this is all about.

speaker: Bayek
en: What are all these soldiers doing here?

speaker: Bayek
en: What has happened here?

speaker: Bayek
en: This body. I fear it is Otis.

speaker: Bayek
en: Wearing the robes of a scribe. It is indeed Otis, poor man. Signs of torture, someone tried to make him talk.

speaker: Bayek
en: Poor girl. One of the servants.

speaker: Bayek
en: Scrolls about the palace budget, nothing of interest.

speaker: Bayek
en: Letters and papers from the Royal Palace, nothing of use here.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is Otis' blood. He tried to flee.

speaker: Bayek
en: They were determined to leave no witnesses.

speaker: Bayek
en: He was attacked in his sleep.

speaker: Bayek
en: This jar has something in it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hidden notes. Must be important.

speaker: Bayek
en: You did a fine work to gather this information, Otis. As you traverse the duat, I swear to you: If I get the chance I will make certain this General Rufio pays.

speaker: Bayek
en: A steep ascent to Khepri's shrine! I could reach up to the heavens, touch the god himself.

speaker: Nena
en: These scarabs were weighed against the feather of Ma'at during the final judgement. It will protect us from the profane rite we must perform.

speaker: Bayek
en: Faithful is his watch, for in the home of Night and Darkness lives Khepri, the great Soul of the Universe. He whose emblem is the beetle, the god of resurrection. In the form of a scarab he watches the coming of Ra. And he flies upon the Boat and awaits there the time when he shall bring Life back to the god.

speaker: Amulet of Khepri
en: Taken from the shrine of Khepri with the blessing of the Scarab god.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do not stand as a witness against me, Khepri.

speaker: Bayek
en: Heh, how can I ease the burdens of an old friend.

speaker: Menehet
en: Tonight we will stage a grand spectacle. Our goddess Sekhmet defends the people against Isfet's chaos. But Pamu, our champion, is nowhere to be found! The high priest will judge me responsible for his absence!

speaker: Bayek
en: I'll have a look.

speaker: Menehet
en: Sekhmet bless you! His home is near the market... but check the tavern first. It pains me to ask for a further favor... Pamu does like a drink now and again.

speaker: Bayek
en: This must be Pamu. Ugh. The man stinks of beer.

speaker: Woman
en: Oh, thank you. I've been trying to get him to leave for hours.

speaker: Bayek
en: Menehet...

speaker: Menehet
en: That is Pamu! What has happened to him?!

speaker: Bayek
en: His passion for toasting Sekhmet has exceeded his head for drink.

speaker: Menehet
en: This is a disaster! People have come from the Red Land and the Black to see him fight!

speaker: Bayek
en: If a fight is all that's needed, I could replace him.

speaker: Menehet
en: Of course, Medjay! You honor yourself in saving me from disgrace. Speak to the High Priest in the temple courtyard. He will take care of the rest.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your Holiness, I am here to fight for Sekhmet.

speaker: High Priest
en: You're not Pamu. He was meant to play Sekhmet.

speaker: Bayek
en: Pamu is... ill. He's recovering at the temple.

speaker: High Priest
en: Fine. Follow me.

speaker: High Priest
en: Beloved of Sekhmet, who illuminates the Double Land with her flame...

speaker: Menehet
en: Though this is a friendly bout, you must stay vigilant.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do not fear. Sekhmet will receive a fine tribute.

speaker: High Priest
en: We give thanks for your presence on this sacred night. We invite your witness on the solemnity of our customs. We unveil to you a ritual that has guarded us for century upon century.

speaker: Menehet
en: For about five years, really.

speaker: High Priest
en: Make every eye to look upon the warrior for whom the two skies open. Sekhmet, Lady of Slaughter! The light rises with Sekhmet and falls as she falls.

speaker: High Priest
en: Should malice cling too strongly to your hearts, Isfet, the Evil One... shall smite the Goddess and condemn Yamu to a hundred seasons of darkness!

speaker: High Priest
en: But... should your hearts be pure—The Goddess shall favor us, shielding us from the obscurity of chaos.

speaker: High Priest
en: Let the battle begin! Since a time unknown, Sekhmet the Lioness has shielded us from Isfet's greed. Isfet was once husband to Ma'at, Goddess of Order. Tampering with her Scales of Judgement, he grew fat on the souls of mortals. Ma'at cast him out of the Hall of Justice. In his hunger, he returned. But Sekhmet knew his heart, and guarded the door against him. Their battle lasted twenty days and nights before Sekhmet subdued the Lord of Chaos.

speaker: High Priest
en: The warrior of Sekhmet beats back chaos! Look, his weapon is bathed in Sekhmet's fire! The Lioness's fangs will cleave the darkness! Sekhmet's might enlivens your arm! In thy chest glows the red heart of the Goddess's flame. See how Sekhmet imbues her beloved with power!Warrior, thy spine is golden and blazes with splendon. Sekhmet's breathes heat into her warrior. Sekhmet's might enlivens your arm. The goddess protects her favorite from every impurity.

speaker: Audience
en: May Sekhmet protect us! Sekhmet, chase away our bad luck! Wait, which one is Sekhmet and which one is Isfet? Isfet will fall before the Goddess! You can do it! I've bet on Sekhmet! Her fighter can't lose! Sekhmet, grant us to live!

speaker: Child
en: You have to win, Uncle! Watch out, Uncle! Isfet is strong! Go, Uncle Bayek! Uncle Bayek is a good fighter. I want to see him fight a wild beast. Let me fight him for you, Uncle Bayek.

speaker: Menehet
en: I could swear you were the Blood-Eater herself!

speaker: Bayek
en: Ha! The priest's recounting of the battle between the Goddess and Isfet was new to me.

speaker: Menehet
en: It is a tale of his own invention! You will not hear it outside Yamu. Would that you'd agree to stay with us longer... but I know that greater duties call you.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'll say goodbye to the children before I leave.

speaker: Menehet
en: Do so; they'll miss you. You are always welcome in Yamu, whenever your journeys bring you to our nome. Keep the mask and staff of the goddess as poor tokens of our respect.

speaker: Bayek
en: Goodbye, Soris. I'll give you a lesson in swordplay on my next visit.

speaker: Soris
en: Yeah! You are so good at fighting!

speaker: Bayek
en: Keba', some advice – go nowhere from which you cannot return.

speaker: Keba
en: Yes, Uncle Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: May your eyes remain on the stars, Hasina.

speaker: Hasina
en: They will. Don't worry!

speaker: Bayek
en: Your knowledge is like a chest of books, Nailah. Share it carefully!

speaker: Nailah
en: I'm always careful!

speaker: Dennu
en: Do I know you? I feel I should, as if the knots of our lives are entwined... I was once a merchant.

speaker: Bayek
en: And you died at the hand of a rabit dog steward. I avenged you and have your father's ring.

speaker: Dennu
en: How can one living traverse the Summerlands? But this means so much. I thank you, avenger.

speaker: Aya
en: Bayek, it has been too long.

speaker: Bayek
en: Flavius is dead. I have gone through shit to get our son out of the Duat. Khemu is at peace.

speaker: Aya
en: May he walk in the Field of Reeds. I head to Rome to

speaker: Bayek
en: Rome? You still entertain folly with these ambitions.

speaker: Aya
en: I have made mistakes, you have made mistakes

speaker: Brutus
en: Aya!

speaker: Bayek
en: You waste your energy!

speaker: Brutus
en: Ah, you are the famous Medjay. Phanos never ceases to speak of your exploits.

speaker: Aya
en: I have assembled a group.

speaker: Aya
en: This is Brutus and Cassius. Our Roman brothers.

speaker: Phoxidas
en: We're going to cut these bastards down from across the seas. Septimius and Caesar.

speaker: Aya
en: The Order is no longer an Egyptian problem only.

speaker: Bayek
en: Does Cleopatra still rule?

speaker: Aya
en: There is no ruler in Egypt. Plunged into the will of various tyrants.

speaker: Phanos
en: Our queen has abandoned us for Rome. Nothing has changed here. Memphis is overrun by the Order. Aya, we need you.

speaker: Bayek
en: I cannot end it like this. Aya... That cursed marked sphere should stay hidden forever. Caused so much pain.

speaker: Bayek
en: Our victories have multiplied, our bond not so.

speaker: Aya
en: We could never have been. Everything has told us our love is impossible.

speaker: Bayek
en: You were right: something bigger has called us. But our love lives in the Duat.

speaker: Aya
en: Only now we are letting go.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let the gods decide.

speaker: Aya
en: The gods are dead.

speaker: Bayek
en: We must sacrifice our personal lives for the greater good. All this darkness was for a reason.

speaker: Aya
en: I was wrong to be so reckless in public with our killing. We must work in the shadows.

speaker: Bayek
en: Egypt has fallen. Greece also. And Rome will fall too. All will fall to the creed. Yet no one will know.

speaker: Aya
en: When we assassinate, we assassinate only those who deserve it. The few sick souls who try to control us... but they will never know who we are. Cold, calculated poets of the kill.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am fine with this. I am not a father anymore. I am not a husband. I am not a Medjay. I am a Hidden One.

speaker: Aya
en: Yes... We are the Hidden Ones.

speaker: Bayek
en: We sharpen our blades... and pull what hope is left from this foul earth.

speaker: Aya
en: Good, Bayek of Siwa. What are you of now?

speaker: Bayek
en: A new creed. Ours is finished.

speaker: Man
en: I have news from Thebes! Come listen! Soldiers! Hear me!

speaker: Man
en: I have heard the tales, south, near Thebes, things beyond mortal understanding have been loosed upon the land. Heralded by ghostly, golden light!

speaker: Bayek
en: Golden light near Thebes? I should see this for myself.

speaker: Man
en: Captains, Lieutenants, men of arms! Egypt needs you to fight a remorseless foe, come from the other side of death! Yes!

speaker: Woman
en: Come listen! Our earthly travails have come to an end! Hear me! The world will soon be no more! We will all walk in the Duat together!

speaker: Woman
en: We hear the tales from Thebes! Light of gold brings forth restless souls to wander the desert.

speaker: Bayek
en: "Light of gold." "Restless souls." What could this mean?

speaker: Woman
en: It comes from the south, friends. The gods send us the gift of death! It is a deliverance! For well we know that this life of blood and bone is mere fantasy.

speaker: Man
en: Come, listen! Everyone! Will no one listen to me? We are all in danger!

speaker: Man
en: Rumors from Thebes abound! The gods are angry! Stories of horror unimaginable, brought forth by golden light from the gods!

speaker: Bayek
en: "Golden light from the gods!" on the road to Thebes? I may want to investigate these "horrors".

speaker: Man
en: Join me, Egyptians, we must redouble our tributes to Osiris and Iset. To Horus and Hathor! To Apep and ! We must keep Amun-Ra in our thoughts at all times.

speaker: Bayek
en: This was not like this when I last came. It is the light I saw in Siwa.

speaker: Bayek
en: What sort of men are these?

speaker: Bayek
en: He smells like death!

speaker: Bayek
en: Have the dead risen? Some dark spirit has unleashed these soldiers. Do I dream?

speaker: Parh
en: Aaah! My leg. Help me!

speaker: Parh
en: I was lucky to be alive. I was attacked by corpses dressed like soldiers.

speaker: Bayek
en: I met them myself. How did you come to be here?

speaker: Parh
en: I came here in search of the Lost Army of Cambyses.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is an old legend. Thousands of men lost forever in a sandstorm.

speaker: Parh
en: I believe they carried much gold. As I approached, I saw a golden light. "At last" I thought, "The gods have chosen me for the treasure of the Lost Army!"

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you an adventurer or a grave robber?

speaker: Parh
en: A man must live. I entered and saw many bodies, dead these centuries. And beyond them, a glowing object. I grabbed it and immediately heard strange sounds. I quickly loaded it onto my camel when suddenly horrifying soldiers attacked! The camel fled into the desert.

speaker: Bayek
en: Here. I will help you get to safety.

speaker: Parh
en: No. You must find my camel and bring back the glowing object. I am certain that it brought the Lost Army back from the dead.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will find out what happened. Stay hidden here.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is a soldier. Could the Legend of the Lost Army of Cambyses be true?

speaker: Bayek
en: Poor animal. This is it.

speaker: Unidentified Artifact
en: A translucent stone that shines brightly. It radiates a heat beyond anything felt in the desert sun.

speaker: Bayek
en: What possesses these men?

speaker: Bayek
en: I must return it to its place and end this nightmare.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have recovered the object!

speaker: Bayek
en: Where has he gone? Are you here?

speaker: Bayek
en: Something must be behind here. Let's get you where you belong.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where am I?

speaker: Woman
en: Ah, you're awake at last.

speaker: Woman
en: We found you wandering dazed in the desert.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where is the adventurer? And the object?

speaker: Woman
en: We found only you, muttering about the "Lost Army".

speaker: Bayek
en: I battled with soldiers returned from the Duat.

speaker: Woman
en: Let us pray you were simply overcome by heat! These strange rumors from Thebes terrify everyone. Pray Osiris that none are true!

speaker: Bayek
en: Tell me more about these rumors from Thebes.

speaker: Woman
en: Stories too strange to repeat. I am sure they are foolish fantasies, but I will not go there myself. That eagle deserves your thanks. Nomads saw it circling the desert.

speaker: Bayek
en: She is a good friend.

speaker: Roman Soldier
en: Away with you! I'm sure I taste terrible!

speaker: Roman Soldier
en: You there! Help me! Drive these beasts away! Please, I beg you! Else these beasts will eat me alive!

speaker: Roman Soldier
en: We spent weeks in this long green nightmare, capturing animals for gladiators to slaughter.

speaker: Bayek
en: The amphitheater hunts.

speaker: Roman Soldier
en: In Cyrene I once saw a hundred lions killed to honor the gods. I will no longer risk my life to capture a beast, just so some politician can win over the voters' hearts.

speaker: Bayek
en: Sounds wise.

speaker: Roman Soldier
en: I will seek my fortune in Herakleion. May the gods favor you!

speaker: Fire Eyes
en: Yes, it is me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Amun be praised.

speaker: Fire Eyes
en: The actor, the poet, the musician. I am the one they call Fire Eyes, the singer from Memphis.

speaker: Bayek
en: Memphis? You are a long way from that city, neb (sir).

speaker: Fire Eyes
en: I am pining for my lyre.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your... what?

speaker: Fire Eyes
en: My instrument. She sank to the depths of the black waters. Lost when those... sunk our ship down river.

speaker: Bayek
en: Everyone is a music critic.

speaker: Fire Eyes
en: She paid me a King's ransom to sing at her villa. How could I know that money came from smuggling wine? Would you find it? I will give you my fee from, the Lotus?

speaker: Bayek
en: This shipwreck is too old to be the smugglers.

speaker: Bayek
en: Wine amphorae from the Lotus' villa.

speaker: Bayek
en: I wonder if I'll regret returning this to him?

speaker: Fire Eyes
en: I never thought I would see you again, my dearest!

speaker: Bayek
en: That is kind but... ah, you are talking to the lyre.

speaker: Fire Eyes
en: And you, savior, I will compose an epic song in your honor. An ode to the mighty... and your name?

speaker: Bayek
en: Bayek of...

speaker: Fire Eyes
en: Bayek... Bay-ek, Baaaay-ek. There is no rhyme for that, I will call you after my father... Shet.

speaker: Bayek
en: So you'll be heading back to Memphis?

speaker: Fire Eyes
en: No! I am done with that backwater. Thebes awaits! Come find me there when you tire of this cultural desert.

speaker: Reda
en: Missing weapons! It's all anyone will talk about! But no one has found them, Bayek. Not until today... Because you will! You take whatever you need. The circle of life in the desert.

speaker: Reda
en: Medjay! There's a shipment of weapons meant for those Phylakitai that has our name on it. Go and get them!

speaker: Reda
en: Finally! You were almost too late. An informant of a shipment of weapons that went missing this very day. If we hurry, both of us win! Go!

speaker: Reda
en: Medjay! A shipment of weapons has gone missing. If you were to find it, I think you might find something of interest. Feel free to grab what you'd like from the stash.

speaker: Woman
en: Please, Medjay, if I can trouble you... Harkhuf's assistant, Nesamun, took a delivery of beer down the southern road. He never made it to Yamu. Please, can you find him and make sure he's ok?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am on the case.

speaker: Woman
en: That beer was meant to honor Sekhmet! If he drank all that beer, he'll be whipped!

speaker: Bayek
en: These jackals will continue to prey on the good people of this region. I must deal with them. Broken beer jars. Someone could not wait to get into the beer.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you Nesamun? Are you all right?

speaker: Nesamun
en: Thank Hapi, yes!

speaker: Bayek
en: What happened?

speaker: Nesamun
en: I was bringing a delivery to Yamu when I was ambushed by these bastards!

speaker: Bayek
en: And...?

speaker: Nesamun
en: Yes, okay, I stopped for a quick nap. But still, they drank or smashed all the beer! And threatened to kill me if I did not brew more for them!

speaker: Bayek
en: Take the oxen back to Sais. You'll have to prepare a new delivery, I imagine. Try not to stop along the road this time.

speaker: Het
en: Are you married, seni (friend)?

speaker: Bayek
en: Once, but no longer.

speaker: Het
en: I'm sorry, I don't mean to open old wounds. My wife would chide me for prying... if she was here. She passed through the Hall of Two Truths, I am sure of it. But then why hasn't she joined me? Even the damned Ren ritual didn't work.

speaker: Bayek
en: You spoke her true name?

speaker: Het
en: Should I accept that I will never see her again?

speaker: Bayek
en: Thy souls rejoined. Without diminution and without defect, unto Ra eternal. It is promised.

speaker: Het
en: Perhaps... The Annuls of the Gate? It records all who enter. But it a forbidden codex heavily guarded in the Lodge of Names.

speaker: Bayek
en: If your wife is here, I will reunite you.

speaker: Het
en: Take this remembrance, she will know it. An eternity of blessings on you, brother.

speaker: Het
en: The bread, the incense, I gathered it all, but the ritual did not work. Did you find Anuke? Is she here in the sacred fields?

speaker: Bayek
en: The Lodge of Names, the scrolls of the dead will be here.

speaker: Bayek
en: Her name changed to Yinepu when she entered the afterlife! Would Anubis have decreed this? I could reattempt Het's ritual with her true name. He spoke of bread and incense...

speaker: Ritual Bread
en: Used for the Summoning of the Ren ritual.

speaker: Bayek
en: The ritual loaf for the Ren ceremony, I need a few more.

speaker: Incense
en: Needed for the brazier in the Summoning of the Ren ritual.

speaker: Bayek
en: Incense for the ritual. I must find a brazier for Het's spell.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nefer en Yinepu pen hena ren-f anx Yinepu pen hena ka-f.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is that the... Ren? It draws me after it!

speaker: Bayek
en: The Ren, it fled into the servant of Anubis. I must release it!

speaker: Anubis
en: You gave her peace. She was my sword for a millennia but all are reunited when duty is done. And so shall it be for you.

speaker: Anuke
en: I did not believe I would see you again.

speaker: Het
en: In my darkest hours I feared the same. Your death... it was foul, obscene?

speaker: Anuke
en: Bandits came to the village, killed many, beat many. I could not tremble behind our door as our neighbors died.

speaker: Het
en: The Lord of the sacred land made you his champion.

speaker: Anuke
en: I offered my afterlife to the scales, served the great balancer.

speaker: Het
en: And when your duty was done, he released you. To me.

speaker: Anuke
en: You are my heart's hunger.

speaker: Het
en: And you my soul's feast.

speaker: Miane
en: We gaze in wonder at the abyss and let ourselves fall into slumber. Our Ka journeys, leaves the body, traverses the drowsy passages and dreaming rooms. Until finally it stumbles into the infinite light and shades of the multiverse. Feels each breath of wind, each brush of the deathless feathers. It shows us that which we cannot see. Reveals the secrets of the night's journey. And only then do we understand.

speaker: Miane
en: How can I find meaning in their dreams when I cannot clear the mist from my own night's journey.

speaker: Bayek
en: What did the gods show you?

speaker: Miane
en: I stand on the edge of a deep well. I can hear the beating of a vulture's wings and a man cries my name. I fear that the Greeks took Besa, a well signifies imprisonment.

speaker: Bayek
en: Would the soldiers dare take the Master of the Secret things?

speaker: Miane
en: The curse... carries bad omens with it, people are desperate.

speaker: Bayek
en: If the Greeks took Besa, it would be to Luxor. I will find him.

speaker: Miane
en: Thank you, neb (sir). May your walking times be bountiful. If they took Besa, it is because they fear the dreams the curse brings.

speaker: Miane
en: Be calm. Tell me what you saw as you slept.

speaker: Woman
en: A dead king, feasting upon the entrails of my children! Where is Besa? I must speak with the Master of the Secret Things.

speaker: Miane
en: He will return but...

speaker: Woman
en: When? Where did he go? The Pharaohs haunt our sleep and waking hours and he leaves Thebes? Even the god hides! Will no one protect me from these night terrors?

speaker: Bayek
en: The soldiers defy belief, would they really take the Master of Secret things?

speaker: Besa
en: Your demons will haunt your waking and sleeping hours. You brought the curse down upon us all.

speaker: Besa
en: Did Miane send you, seni (friend)?

speaker: Bayek
en: She dreamed you were in trouble.

speaker: Besa
en: It is worse than she knows. But come, we cannot speak here.

speaker: Besa
en: I knew you would come. As I lay feverish, I dreamed of an eagle soaring high above my cage.

speaker: Bayek
en: The soldiers were bold to arrest you, neb.

speaker: Besa
en: Their dreams needle them like scorpion stings. But I am more fearful for Miane. Her brother, Tapti, he stole my scared dream scrolls.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why would he do this?

speaker: Besa
en: I know not, but last night I dreamed of him feasting on ears of corn, scavenging in the dust with wild dogs.

speaker: Bayek
en: An ill omen. Where did he take the papyrus?

speaker: Besa
en: He and Miane grew up on a farm east of Thebes. When I took her as my apprentice, he withdrew to the cellar under the house.

speaker: Bayek
en: Return to Miane, I will find her brother and your texts.

speaker: Bayek
en: Miane's brother will have the truth of this.

speaker: Bayek
en: This does not bode well. Besa spoke of a cellar Tapti retreats to, I might still find him alive.

speaker: Bayek
en: Killed defending the farm.

speaker: Bayek
en: A bandit raid? At least the farmers fought back.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tapti... the gods punished him, but just for stealing the book or is there more to this?

speaker: Bayek
en: An unhealthy obsession with his sister. But he hid Besa's scroll under the table.

speaker: Bayek
en: There is nothing here, the bandits must have taken it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tapti loved his sister too much. But the dream texts, perhaps the bandits took them to sell?

speaker: Dream Papyrus
en: The Egyptian dream book with interpretations and representations of our sleeping hours.

speaker: Bayek
en: The dream scrolls. I should return to Besa and Miane.

speaker: Besa
en: The eagle returns!

speaker: Bayek
en: With your scrolls, Besa.

speaker: Miane
en: My brother, he's dead isn't he? I bent my face to the ground, heard his voice under the endless sands. "Betrayal, betrayal." Thank you, eagle. I don't know if this was the curse or fate, but he was my only family.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am sorry, Miane. But whatever he did, he loved you deeply.

speaker: Besa
en: The curse, it comes for those whose conscience weighs heavily upon them, Miane. They dream of reed boats drifting from the shore.

speaker: Bayek
en: Keep safe, Besa... Miane, these are dangerous times.

speaker: Besa
en: Your journey is not yet done. Return to me when your living feet have walked where none should.

speaker: Miane
en: My brother's letters... I did not know he felt so strongly.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your loss is great, Miane.

speaker: Besa
en: You have come to consult with the Master of Secret things? I will tell you what I have seen as I slumber. Men seeking wisdom, they hide in the temple of the tenth son of David. They will pit themselves against the Hidden Ones. I men standing upon the plane of Khonsu. They claim the shifting sands for a new order of . Chittering and swarming from the stygian waters, bringers of death. But Alexander's will halt tide. One will come from the of the Gazelle. fathers born of earth and air. Like Osiris he will die and , enshrouded in ancients. The wisdom of Thoth will thread throughout the world on the . Like actors, we become others, decide their fates, as does the creator Amun. Choices, paths, they are puppets in our play. In the land of the bull's captive, they will rear a fearsome beast. It will shake the land on its , from the sky. . He regards me with his ageless eyes and sees everything. Stronger, faster, more knowing, ? Amun dissolves the ordered world and returns us to the waters of chaos. Only the creator will remain, and so shall we be resurrected. The dead need us to listen, I could hear them calling when I put my face to the ground. I saw you standing under a shining moon. You will find forgiveness at the end of your path. You plunged into the icy waters. The absolution you seek. It will come.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Not ready yet? I understand. So much to do in Siwa. People need you here. Are you ready? It is a long journey. Be sure you are ready before you go.

speaker: Bayek
en: I must leave Siwa. There are others to whom I must deliver justice. Especially the one known as the Snake.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: How will you find these men?

speaker: Bayek
en: Aya has been tracking them in Alexandria. I must find her.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: She said she would be visiting her cousin at the Great Library.

speaker: Bayek
en: Great Library?

speaker: Hepzefa
en: And she said if you were coming to tell you one word: "Serapis".

speaker: Bayek
en: Serapis? The god that Greeks and Egyptians share... of course... I see.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: And Bayek. Do something about that beard.

speaker: Bayek
en: Goodbye, my friend.

speaker: Reda
en: A friend of mine went missing. Medjay, I would not ask but he would be missed by his family. Please find where he has gone.

speaker: Reda
en: Medjay, you hear of that villager that went missing? I only ask because, like you, he's one of my favorite customers. Maybe you go looking for him? Maybe if you find him I'll have something nice for you. Maybe.

speaker: Reda
en: Come Bayek. I heard tell of a local man who went missing. Being a generous man, I would be very happy if you were to find him. For the village, of course. Not because he is one of my informants.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is the man Reda spoke of. Dead.

speaker: Bayek
en: Here is Reda's man. Dead.

speaker: Bayek
en: The man lies here, dead. Reda will be sad to hear of his passing.

speaker: Reda
en: Dead men need no weapons, so how about you use his. Special order, it'll suit you just fine.

speaker: Reda
en: He won't be needing this anymore, Medjay. Best give it to you. I'm sure you'll find a use for it.

speaker: Reda
en: May he find peace in the Duat, Medjay. Since you found him, you can have the weapon I got for him special. He would have liked it that way.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ugly to kill in front of the little ones. What happened here?

speaker: Bayek
en: Who was he?

speaker: Kawit
en: Nef. The children called him Father. This is his house. This is his house!

speaker: Bayek
en: You are injured.

speaker: Kawit
en: I don't give a shit. The Roman hag who did this leaves by boat for Alexandria today. Help me feed her to the crocodiles one piece at a time.

speaker: Bayek
en: I can go alone. No need for you to bloody yourself further.

speaker: Kawit
en: It has to be me!

speaker: Bayek
en: Is your need worth leaving the children unprotected?

speaker: Kawit
en: Destroy her name, Bayek of Siwa.

speaker: Child
en: Who's going to take care of us now?

speaker: Bayek
en: I need to move quickly, or this monster will flee Memphis. Senu can find a ship with colored sails faster than I can.

speaker: Gaia Afrania
en: I cannot wait to wring the neck of that wretched girl, Kawit. Can we turn the ship a little to one side? The sun is in my eyes. This will be a useless trip. So little cargo, and none of it human. The river breeze is like to the breath of the north wind! Ambrose, go below and fetch my woven shawl. The red one.

speaker: Gaia
en: Guards! An interloper has boarded my ship! My men will gut you if you damage my smallest fingernail! Keep your distance! I will make sacrifice to you, Pluto, if you spare me! Dates, figs—a black pig!

speaker: Bayek
en: Kawit has her vengeance now. I hope it quiets her heart.

speaker: Kawit
en: Is it done?

speaker: Bayek
en: It is.

speaker: Kawit
en: My sword is yours.

speaker: Bayek
en: It is my honour.

speaker: Kawit
en: Honour means nothing to me. Only survival counts.

speaker: Bayek
en: I fight for the survival of Egypt. Will you lend your arm to my cause?

speaker: Kawit
en: Don't be stupid.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will take that as a yes.

speaker: Epigonos
en: Keep back! This doesn't concern any of you. Carry on with... whatever it is you do.

speaker: Woman 1
en: Another murder! Amun, how horrible!

speaker: Woman 2
en: It's the young priest from the temple. Gods save us!

speaker: Man 1
en: Who will be next? No-one is safe!

speaker: Man 2
en: It is this cursed temple. I told you. It is a blasphemy! The gods are angry!

speaker: Epigonos
en: Move back! Back!

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you the Phylakitai?

speaker: Epigonos
en: Yes. Try not to trample the scene. My job is hard enough as it is.

speaker: Bayek
en: My apologies, as a protector I am attracted to such scenes.

speaker: Epigonos
en: A fellow protector? Ah yes, I see your badge. You are a Medjay? From the , wow! Forgive me. This gruesome business has us all on edge. This is the latest in a series of chilling ritual murders by Wadjet cultists. To be honest, I'm a little out of my depth.

speaker: Bayek
en: I may be of some use to you. I am not unfamiliar with murder scenes.

speaker: Epigonos
en: Perhaps you could help investigate? The cultists usually leave a message. I haven't figured it out yet. We could check the temple.

speaker: Bayek
en: You said there have been other murders?

speaker: Epigonos
en: The cultists are murdering temple acolytes, public figures in Karanis. No-one knows why. Anyone could be their next target. The Greeks are terrified. They're saying locals are involved and are calling for blood.

speaker: Epigonos
en: The timing is inconvenient. Years of work building over the poorly constructed Egyptian temple. Endless delays and problems. Now this. There's a lot of pressure to solve this. But please, take your time, enjoy the temple.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is a lot of blood. Someone was bound and tortured here, in front of the statue. By the signs, they were cut up badly then dragged outside.

speaker: Epigonos
en: It must have been the poor acolyte. There was no-one else here. Why did they do this?

speaker: Bayek
en: A Greek god where an Egyptian god once stood. This would make some in Egypt very angry. Someone has smeared the god with green paint. The head's also been covered. Wait... something else is up there.

speaker: Bayek
en: Serapis' face is hidden and defaced with more green paint. A green mask of Wadjet has been placed here. Wadjet is goddess protector of and . Someone is making a clear statement. But how did they get up here carrying all of this?

speaker: Bayek
en: Amun, this is written in blood. It is still wet!

speaker: Bayek
en: The murderers are going to kill the High Priest next. We have to find him. The Phylakitai should know where he is.

speaker: Bayek
en: Phylakitai! I found the cultist's message. They're going to kill your High Priest next.

speaker: Epigonos
en: The High Priest! By Serapis no! Karanis' spirit will die if he does!

speaker: Bayek
en: We need to find him. Where is he? Think Phylakitai!

speaker: Epigonos
en: His villa is nearby. I know of a spot overlooking it from a safe distance. This way!

speaker: Epigonos
en: We can see the whole area from the temple wall.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your temple is the reason for this trouble. It is a bitterness for the locals.

speaker: Epigonos
en: That's absurd! It has increased industry and trade. Everyone has benefitted.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your dead acolyte and High Priest may not agree.

speaker: Epigonos
en: Gods, the trouble I'll get if the High Priest lies dead! We must hurry.

speaker: Epigonos
en: That's the High Priest! Those men have him surrounded. You must help him!

speaker: Bayek
en: Quickly! Get to the main entrance and act when I do.

speaker: Epigonos
en: Yes, ah... or I could stay up here as lookout! I'll warn if more bandits approach. You go!

speaker: High Priest
en: This is madness! You gain nothing by killing me. Greece and Egypt will grow together. Our gods do not fight. Why do we?

speaker: Cultist
en: Hypocrite and blasphemer! You defiled our temple, replaced our gods with your own! Your life is forfeit!

speaker: High Priest
en: They were going to sacrifice me!

speaker: Bayek
en: You are safe now. It is fortunate you were not at the temple. You would already be dead.

speaker: High Priest
en: Serapis! They would have butchered me! These Egyptians are prayerless demons, and not men!

speaker: Bayek
en: It was an Egyptian who saved you, priest. Remember that when you pray and give thanks. We Medjay protect all, regardless of their class.

speaker: Epigonos
en: I came as soon as the fighting began. I see I am too late! Thank you for your help, Medjay. it certainly made my work here easier.

speaker: Bayek
en: You have interesting timing. What do you know of these bandits?

speaker: Epigonos
en: Egyptians unhappy with the Greeks here. Who knows what holes they crawl from? Seeing a Greek god in place of their own incensed them, no doubt.

speaker: Bayek
en: Understandably. You have not seen the last of such trouble, I think. The Ptolemies tend to divide us at times.

speaker: Epigonos
en: Sadly, I agree. Greece has brought Egypt much wealth, yet some resist all progress.

speaker: Bayek
en: This depends on your idea of progress. Progress for Egypt, or for Greece? Farewell Phylakitai. Next time you protect, remember my code.

speaker: Darius
en: Hey, Egyptian, come see! Are they not the worst nags you've ever seen?

speaker: Bayek
en: I heard Cyrenaican horses are the best in the world?

speaker: Darius
en: They are! Which is why that cursed Roman Quartermaster stole my prized stallion Hermes. Hermes wasn't only my fastest horse, but my best breeder. The mares miss him. I miss him. I'll pay you...

speaker: Bayek
en: You want me to rescue a horse?

speaker: Darius
en: I love him like a brother, actually my brother's a donkey's arse. I love him more than my brother. That drunken thief Quartermaster is probably already at the Archile Pandocheion by now. It's on the road to Alexandria. Could you find Hermes and bring him home to me?

speaker: Bayek
en: That must be the thieving quartermaster.

speaker: Bayek
en: The quest for Hermes continues.

speaker: Bayek
en: Alright Hermes, there's a good boy. So what's so special about you Hermes? The way your master talked about you, I half expected you to fly! (laugh) That's it boy! You do feel more powerful than other horses I have ridden. Strong and lithe!

speaker: Darius
en: Hermes my boy! You really found him!

speaker: Bayek
en: Here you are boy, back with your master.

speaker: Darius
en: Hermes! You will get the best hay and my best mare tonight, old friend.

speaker: Bayek
en: Quartermaster gave him to the Centurion up at the East fort. He won't come looking for him.

speaker: Darius
en: Those forts! They steal everything from us! Ah well, we will breed a strong line of champions from you, won't we, boy. Here's your reqard, friend, and well earned.

speaker: Mysterious Papyrus
en: was a virtual representation of one of Bayek's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the portable Animus HR-8.

speaker: Kanika
en: Let me out you cockless hyenas! I must find it.

speaker: Bayek
en: What must you find?

speaker: Kanika
en: Who are you that asks me this?

speaker: Bayek
en: We can stand here trading questions or I can free you and help your cause.

speaker: Kanika
en: Then let us leave, before the treasure is lost for good.

speaker: Kanika
en: Do you care about our history, seni (friend)?

speaker: Bayek
en: Bayek. I fight to defend it.

speaker: Kanika
en: I am Kanika, seeking a relic of great significance. It belongs in a temple.

speaker: Bayek
en: A worthy sentiment.

speaker: Kanika
en: The Papyrus of Pentju holds the key. I was haggling with the merchant for it. Then all was blackness and I awoke in a cell accused of his murder.

speaker: Bayek
en: With the Papyrus no-where to be found...

speaker: Kanika
en: You have a talent for deduction. But without the Pentju's words... nek (shit), my only lead!

speaker: Bayek
en: Where were you ambushed?

speaker: Kanika
en: South of here near the mountain roads. Will you recover it, seni (friend)? I will go to the excavation site, if the soldiers find the treasure first, all is lost.

speaker: Bayek
en: A stolen papyrus, a race to find a relic, my blood quickens.

speaker: Bayek
en: Stabbed in the chest. A senseless waste of life, but he fought back, against the thief?

speaker: Bayek
en: Horse dung but no horse. Now we know how our thief got away.

speaker: Bayek
en: A Blood trail, someone is badly injured. He couldn't have got far. Kanika needs that papyrus, so let's follow the thief.

speaker: Bayek
en: Kanika will need to interpret this at the excavation site.

speaker: Bayek
en: These damned soldiers. Sifting through the sands, razing our history.

speaker: Kanika
en: You found the papyrus? Who took it...? No, I don't care, the relic is all that matters. Hurry, they have doubled their efforts to secure it!

speaker: Kanika
en: No... it can't be... I hoped... but this is incredible! We must go, now, to the Cave of Endless Sorrows.

speaker: Bayek
en: Lead on, Kanika, I will deal with anyone that dares to defy us.

speaker: Kanika
en: A good job they are digging in the wrong place.

speaker: Bayek
en: You will know the relic when you see it?

speaker: Kanika
en: I will know.

speaker: Bayek
en: How much of a living can you make saving relics?

speaker: Kanika
en: For my shame, I made my money as a smuggler. I am paying off a great debt to Egypt.

speaker: Bayek
en: There is no one more righteous than a reformed thief.

speaker: Kanika
en: You destroy our heritage, our past! We reclaim history a relic at a time. The Pharaohs treasures will not be plundered.

speaker: Kanika
en: This is the place. The Cave of Endless Sorrows!

speaker: Kanika
en: Such beauties! Come see for yourself, Bayek.

speaker: Kanika
en: It cannot be!

speaker: Bayek
en: You found it?

speaker: Kanika
en: Not it, Bayek. And beautiful they are. The gold hilts, the ba-en-pet blade... the lily and jackal-adorned sheathes.

speaker: Bayek
en: Daggers?

speaker: Kanika
en: More than daggers, the blades of the son of the Aten, Tutankhamun.

speaker: Bayek
en: A Pharaoh's weapons?

speaker: Kanika
en: The whereabouts of his tomb has been lost to the desert for centuries. Here, you must take them.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am no thief, Kanika!

speaker: Kanika
en: Perhaps someday they can lie with the Pharaoh again. Until then they must be in the hands of one who truly serves Egypt.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will use them to exact punishment on the men who rape our history.

speaker: Kanika
en: That's the spirit! May their hilts never tarnish in your service, Bayek.

speaker: Kanika
en: I will head to the Moon Curser Village. There are many smugglers there who need a history lesson.

speaker: Kanika
en: Bayek! My friend, have you sent many desecrators for judgement with the daggers of the boy king?

speaker: Bayek
en: They serve Egypt well.

speaker: Kanika
en: I am on the trail of another relic, some say it holds the power of the gods.

speaker: Bayek
en: An artifact such as that should never be found.

speaker: Ramessu
en: Welcome, welcome to Letopolis! Dream of the great Taharqa. A new life awaits you in the glorious city of Letopolis! A chance to begin again in a golden land of opportunity and adventure! This entire city was lost to the cruel desert in the time of our ancestors. But the great Taharqa rediscovered its secrets! He is uncovering it to shine again under the sun, and dedicating the city to Horus. With bright wings, we will reach the stars!

speaker: Ramessu
en: Welcome, friend! A new life awaits you here, in Letopolis, the city of Horus! Come, find your path, and walk into a new age with us!

speaker: Ramessu
en: Come, Neb, are you ready to work to free yourself? Join us, and take a house as your reward!

speaker: Man
en: I have heard the stories!

speaker: Ramessu
en: A guide will show you your new house. You have to dig it free, and to help with the public works, to be welcome here.

speaker: Ramessu
en: Welcome, Nebet! The city of Egypt's future welcomes all!

speaker: Woman
en: Is it true forgotten secrets are discovered every day?

speaker: Ramessu
en: Hah! Many lost works and fragments of the old world are found here. Perhaps not every day, but often enough to make us wonder.

speaker: Ramessu
en: Welcome, welcome to Letopolis! I never forget a face and I have not seen yours before. You've found it! Your new home! A miracle of a man's labor! The great work begins!

speaker: Bayek
en: No, that's not wha

speaker: Ramessu
en: You just don't know it yet! We give every new arrival a house. Only dig it out, and help with the public works. A fresh start!

speaker: Bayek
en: I am not here to live in these tough sands.

speaker: Ramessu
en: Speak to some of our new inhabitants, like Nehi. He can tell you how liberating it is to leave the past behind.

speaker: Bayek
en: I cannot my past like a snake sheds his skin.

speaker: Nehi
en: My cart is gone! Can anyone help?

speaker: Man
en: Pathetic fool. Stop bothering me!

speaker: Nehi
en: Khufu and Chiera are gone!

speaker: Man
en: Eh? Who are they?

speaker: Nehi
en: My beloved oxen! Can you help me get my cart?

speaker: Man
en: Crying over oxen? Hah! Piss off!

speaker: Nehi
en: Please! I need help!

speaker: Woman
en: Ugh. Get away from me! I have things to do!

speaker: Nehi
en: By the gods, what am I to do?

speaker: Bayek
en: Peace, friend. What happened?

speaker: Nehi
en: The gods have cursed me! I lost my f-farm and m-my wife to my brother, in Y-Yamu, and now I've lost what little I owned! M-my cart got stuck in a ditch far from town! As night came on, I heard terrible roars... And I just left them! My poor oxen! Everything I owned! What-what am I to do?

speaker: Bayek
en: Roars? There are no large beasts in this region.

speaker: Nehi
en: I did not stay to find out! They were the last gift I got from my father, Khufu and Chiera! And-and I left them there! With all I own!

speaker: Bayek
en: When I am out that way, I will see what I can find. For now, do what you can on your new house.

speaker: Nehi
en: My-my thanks. My house is to the right of the entrance to the temple. May you fly with the bright wings of Horus!

speaker: Bayek
en: Quiet there, let's see how you are tangled

speaker: Bandit
en: Hah! Another sacrifice to the Mistress of Dread! Spill the outsider's blood! For the Lady of Slaughter!

speaker: Bayek
en: A good thing I came looking for you. I fear Nehi would be dead, and you'd be lion food otherwise.

speaker: Nehi
en: Bayek! You found Khufu and Chiera! Today I cry tears of joy!

speaker: Bayek
en: Look how much you've done since I've been gone.

speaker: Nehi
en: I found something strange inside the house. It arouses my curiosity, and yet terrifies me. W-will you look?

speaker: Bayek
en: Show me.

speaker: Nehi
en: As I dug out the main room, I f-f-found ominous writings on the wall. Old writings. I have no idea what they say, but it scares me in my bones.

speaker: Bayek
en: These are old. But incomplete. Too much is missing.

speaker: Nehi
en: Erased by time and sand. Do you... d-do you think it's a curse?

speaker: Bayek
en: I will ask around town.

speaker: Nehi
en: All r-right. What should I do? I don't know if I c-c-can sleep here!

speaker: Bayek
en: You will be fine.

speaker: Nehi
en: You should s-speak to Ramessu. He knows everyone in town, and everything that happens here.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm sure he does.

speaker: Ramessu
en: I've seen that dour face before. You've come for your house!

speaker: Bayek
en: No, I

speaker: Ramessu
en: You would clear a house in no time.

speaker: Bayek
en: Enough! At Nehi's house, he showed me strange writings.

speaker: Ramessu
en: Nothing to worry you, friend. Three others have said the same thing. But these signs are too old to be made sense of.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will check with them.

speaker: Ramessu
en: You are wasting your time, but as you will.

speaker: Man
en: Yes? What can I help you with?

speaker: Bayek
en: Ramessu said you found strange hieroglyphs in your house?

speaker: Man
en: Yes. I thought they were kind of creepy. I think someone else may have found the same thing.

speaker: Bayek
en: May I look?

speaker: Man
en: Sure. Go on and take a look.

speaker: Bayek
en: Looks like the same style. Perhaps part of the same message.

speaker: Bayek
en: May I ask you something?

speaker: Woman
en: Hmm? Yes, what?

speaker: Bayek
en: Nehi found a strange symbol in his house, like you. May I take a look?

speaker: Woman
en: Certainly. He's new, yes? He'd be cute if he didn't look like he was always about to cry. Tell him I asked how he was. My name's Nebefer.

speaker: Bayek
en: More of the message.

speaker: Man
en: Are you new here?

speaker: Bayek
en: Passing through. But looking into a mystery. Did you find ancient hieroglyphs in your house?

speaker: Man
en: Didn't everyone? Didn't worry me much. Why, does it mean something?

speaker: Bayek
en: Not sure yet. May I look?

speaker: Man
en: Don't see why not. Tell me if I should worry!

speaker: Bayek
en: Another part of the message.

speaker: Bayek
en: That's the whole message. It appears to be a prophetic vision. Where is the temple?

speaker: Bayek
en: What did the priests hope to achieve in their last ceremony, so long ago?

speaker: Bayek
en: These men... they were wab priests. Were they killed, or did they choose this fate for themselves?

speaker: Bayek
en: Some ancient concoction, long since dried up.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hm. A prayer.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Lady of Slaughter. This place was dedicated to Sekhmet, then. I thought Letopolis was home to Horus.

speaker: Bayek
en: Letopolis was sacrificed to the gods by the ancients so the rest of the Nile could be granted to the realm of men. These priests made an invocation for protection to the One Before Whom Evil Trembles. In drinking their concoction, they gave their lives, as well as their city, to Sekhmet. In their eyes Taharqa's project would be sacrilegious.

speaker: Nehi
en: Ah! Bayek! I'm g-getting used to living with these symbols. Nebefer even came by for a meal. Did you find out anything?

speaker: Bayek
en: I did. Though I'm not sure you are going to like it.

speaker: Nehi
en: A curse! I knew it!

speaker: Bayek
en: No, not exactly... Letopolis was an offering to Sekhmet, to protect the rest of the Nile.

speaker: Nehi
en: We have offended the L-Lady of Slaughter!? No wonder the sands always blow! She wants to reclaim the city. Are the officials blind, or mad? I can't stay here. Maybe Nebefer will come with me. What about you?

speaker: Bayek
en: My time here is but temporary.

speaker: Nehi
en: You were kind to me when others were not. Maybe we will see each other again in this world.

speaker: Bayek
en: Three dead, as promised.

speaker: Tahira
en: That leaves Rufio.

speaker: Bayek
en: He will be drawn to the Sinai by the news of these deaths.

speaker: Tahira
en: Gamilat is now hero of the land. The people speak of no one else.

speaker: Bayek
en: You seem troubled.

speaker: Tahira
en: The cause of the rebels is just, but I've seen how often simple villagers get caught in the battles, many losing their lives.

speaker: Bayek
en: Have you spoken to him about this?

speaker: Tahira
en: To him, they are martyrs. Their deaths inspire their families to join the rebels.

speaker: Tahira
en: Kashta!

speaker: Kashta
en: Fire! Get out now!

speaker: Roman Soldier
en: Smoke them out!

speaker: Bayek
en: Carry her out!

speaker: Bayek
en: Through the passage!

speaker: Roman Soldier
en: We have their leader!

speaker: Roman Guard
en: The vultures will have their meal today. (laughs)

speaker: Bayek
en: I will kill you all.

speaker: Bayek
en: Amunet!

speaker: Amunet
en: Put some clothes on. Show some decency.

speaker: Amunet
en: ...and you attracted too much attention, even in Rome we heard of the Sinai bureau.

speaker: Bayek
en: I know, the fire was proof of this. Right now we need to find Tahira and Kashta.

speaker: Amunet
en: They are imprisoned in Fort Clostra.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will head straight in.

speaker: Amunet
en: I'll check the perimeter, there are centurions everywhere. Meet me at the far side of fort Clostra.

speaker: Bayek
en: We will reunite once we have our Hidden Ones.

speaker: Amunet
en: We are wasting time, Bayek.

speaker: Tahira
en: Bayek!

speaker: Bayek
en: Come on Tahira! I will carry you out of here.

speaker: Tahira
en: I cannot go on, leave me a bow and I will fight them to my death!

speaker: Bayek
en: Stop speaking of your death! The Hidden Ones need you!

speaker: Tahira
en: My body is on fire. The blood of Romans is the only thing that eases this pain!

speaker: Tahira
en: Kashta is still captured. We need to free him! He may be as hurt as I am!

speaker: Bayek
en: You are right. We leave no one behind!

speaker: Tahira
en: Oh lord of the Duat, please pass me through to the field of reeds...

speaker: Bayek
en: Stay with me Tahira! Fight it, do not give up!

speaker: Tahira
en: The world is fading from my sight, Bayek...

speaker: Bayek
en: Kashta is still in the fort!

speaker: Tahira
en: You have to get him! I'll be fine here!

speaker: Amunet
en: Make haste, Bayek.

speaker: Kashta
en: Bayek, thank gods you are here! This fort was designed by Osiris!

speaker: Bayek
en: It is madness.

speaker: Kashta
en: Tahira is badly burned. I fear for her life. They took her away.

speaker: Bayek
en: Follow me, be ready to fight.

speaker: Amunet
en: We need to get out of here, Romans could come at any time. Follow me to my camp.

speaker: Bayek
en: It sickens me to see Tahira like this!

speaker: Amunet
en: At my camp we can help her.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nek! (Shit!) Why gods! Do not take my great sister!

speaker: Amunet
en: We must have a traitor among the Hidden Ones, who could have let this happen?

speaker: Bayek
en: All swear an oath. We have been played for whekas!

speaker: Amunet
en: All? Are you sure of this? We can no longer trust anyone.

speaker: Bayek
en: Our wisdom is faltering.

speaker: Amunet
en: The same happened with Brutus and Cassius. The more known we are, the less safe the brotherhood is.

speaker: Bayek
en: Well, let us pray the gods will keep Tahira for us, she is invaluable to maintaining Nabatea.

speaker: Amunet
en: We're almost there.

speaker: Tahira
en: Great Amun, be merciful...

speaker: Tahira
en: I let you down, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: You let no one down. You are as loyal as a mountain.

speaker: Tahira
en: We built something I believe in.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are the first oath taker, savior to many, and a Hidden One.

speaker: Tahira
en: Don't let our creed fade.

speaker: Kashta
en: I will kill everyone. All the Romans.

speaker: Amunet
en: You will take Tahira to the mountains. Somewhere she can be given a proper burial.

speaker: Amunet
en: We will carry on. Let us kill Rufio.

speaker: Bayek
en: If the relic was stolen from a Pharaoh's tomb, someone here must know the thief.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is this all you have? I was told this market sold artifacts from the tombs?

speaker: Shopkeeper
en: There is no money to be made in relics, neb. (sir.) All anyone wants is protection from the curse, scarabs, amulets.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where would I find something rare, golden like the sun?

speaker: Black Marketeer
en: I have gold, you need a trinket for a lady friend? Whatever you want, neb (sir) you won't find better in Thebes.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm looking for something... special, ancient, I have coin.

speaker: Shady Shopkeeper
en: Talk to Siamun if you want that kind of trinket, he has the best in Thebes.

speaker: Siamun
en: Welcome, Seni (friend) to Siamun's Curios. Are you looking for something special? I have the rarest stock in Thebes.

speaker: Bayek
en: An artifact... from the tombs.

speaker: Siamun
en: Such a treasure will cost a Pharaoh's ransom... but not here neb (sir), the soldiers are stupid, but their swords are sharp. Come.

speaker: Siamun
en: Not many merchants will sell to a stranger.

speaker: Bayek
en: Now why is that?

speaker: Siamun
en: You are in the heart of the black market. Relics are everywhere, trust is hard to come by. But you can trust Siamun.

speaker: Bayek
en: You alone amongst all the merchants?

speaker: Siamun
en: Some might take advantage of a man fresh off the boat in Thebes. One so laden down with coin. You should be more careful, Neb. (sir.)

speaker: Bayek
en: Let's try this again, I'm looking for an artifact, stolen from the tombs.

speaker: Siamun
en: Oh, that artifact! Yes, yes but Irsu must not know we spoke.

speaker: Bayek
en: Irsu?

speaker: Siamun
en: You really don't know anything do you?

speaker: Bayek
en: I know how to slit a man's throat before he can cry for help.

speaker: Siamun
en: There's an auction, very exclusive. I tried to get in, but Irsu and I don't see eye to eye.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where can I get an invitation?

speaker: Siamun
en: Tahemet has one... the historian? I tried to win it from her in our last dice game. We play on a roof north of here. By Horus, that's all I know. Just let me live.

speaker: Tahemet
en: Beetle dung from a horse's ass, what is? Let me roll again, if I lose, I'll give you twice what I offered.

speaker: Soldier
en: By all means.

speaker: Sutekh
en: I know you have an invitation. I will play you for it. I have coins!

speaker: Tahemet
en: Maybe I want to keep my invitation! Ever thought of that?

speaker: Sutekh
en: I guarantee, you can't possibly want it more than me. Please! My mother, she's sick. She has one wish

speaker: Tahemet
en: Your uncle's a better liar.

speaker: Tahemet
en: Who invited the thug? He's here with you?

speaker: Sutekh
en: Never seen him before.

speaker: Soldier
en: Pay up, woman!

speaker: Tahemet
en: You cheated! Just like you cheated him!

speaker: Gambler
en: I knew it!

speaker: Soldier
en: You hiring muscle now, Tahemet?

speaker: Tahemet
en: You better leave while you still can.

speaker: Soldier
en: Not a chance, swindler.

speaker: Tahemet
en: On your head be it.

speaker: Soldier
en: You picked the wrong camel to back!

speaker: Tahemet
en: I already lost all my money er... neb (sir)?

speaker: Bayek
en: Bayek. I don't need coin, I need information... and your invitation.

speaker: Tahemet
en: To Irsu's auction? You heard what I told that rust-haired clodpate Sutekh.

speaker: Bayek
en: But the boy didn't just save your life, Tahemet.

speaker: Tahemet
en: Alright, it's all getting a little hot for my blood anyway. Desecration, curses, Pharaohs returning from the dead...

speaker: Bayek
en: Do you know what Irsu is selling?

speaker: Tahemet
en: Whatever it was brought the curse down upon us. Look, Irsu is a crook. He and his cronies found Queen Nefertiti's tomb, stole something from it.

speaker: Bayek
en: And now she wants it back.

speaker: Tahemet
en: No one deserves death more than that dung-peddler, but she comes for us all. My invitation's at my villa near the entrance to Karnak. Take it... if the gods allow.

speaker: Bayek
en: The gods?

speaker: Tahemet
en: You'll see. I have a game on the other side of Thebes. May the dice fall in your favor, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: Maybe Tahemet's study is somewhere underneath?

speaker: Bayek
en: This is from Mehen, the game of Snake. I used to play with Aya.

speaker: Bayek
en: What was it that Tahemet said? If the gods allow?

speaker: Bayek
en: Wheels? Perhaps the statues can be turned?

speaker: Bayek
en: They all seem to turn in one direction.

speaker: Bayek
en: That did it!

speaker: Bayek
en: Papyrus from the , myths of the Pharaohs.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tahemet has been researching the root of the curse!

speaker: Bayek
en: A list of relics stolen from the tombs. Does she know about the orb?

speaker: Bayek
en: Like the orb of Siwa. How much more bloodshed and madness will this one bring?

speaker: Bayek
en: I should hurry to the island before the relic is sold!

speaker: Bayek
en: That stink on the wind... another of Memphis' curses. I will speak to the priests he mentioned in his note. Aya's nose is finer than mine. She could uncover the origin of the smell in a moment.

speaker: Child 1
en: Khemwy smells!

speaker: Khemwy
en: No I don't!

speaker: Child 1
en: Yes you do! I can smell you everywhere. I can smell you in my sleep.

speaker: Priest
en: Hail to you, Osiris! Your limbs are lasting, you do not know corruption. Hail to you, Osiris! Your limbs are lasting, you do not know corruption. There are no worms with you, you are not repugnant. There are no worms with you, you are not repugnant. Here is the tomb of Osiris, motionless, motionless like Osiris; motionless his limbs like Osiris. Let them not remain motionless, let them not corrupt. They move not, they stir not: be it done for them as for Osiris. I am Osiris.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hail, Pure One.

speaker: Priest
en: May your heart be joyful, Medjay.

speaker: Bayek
en: Joy is scarce while Memphis chokes on the scent of the grave. I am here to discuss Pasherenptah's complaint on the Informant Table.

speaker: Priest
en: Indeed! We seek a capable person to investigate this tomb. Most are too fearful of the demons within to enter.

speaker: Bayek
en: But demons would fear a priest. Why not investigate yourself?

speaker: Priest
en: I am a vessel of the gods—I contribute through prayer.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then I will face the demons. Pray that your faith shields me.

speaker: Priest
en: Ptah grant you safety.

speaker: Bayek
en: This stench! Vile as the Devourer's breath. The entrance is barred. There must be another way inside the tomb.

speaker: Bayek
en: Gah! I can hardly breathe! The source of this poison is closer than before.

speaker: Bayek
en: Departed, forgive my violation of your rest. Grant that I may pass by you.

speaker: Bayek
en: These mummies are sound. Not the cause of the smell.

speaker: Bayek
en: An offering to chase the smell. Someone has been here recently... someone who does not fear demons.

speaker: Bayek
en: What in the name of the gods is that foulness? I should trace it to its source.

speaker: Bayek
en: The mummies. They are rotted! This is a crime against the dead.

speaker: Bayek
en: Here. The flesh has decayed, but the wrappings are still intact. If the wrappings are sound, the fault lies in the embalming. Fear of demons kept the crime from being discovered. I will pay the mummification temple a visit.

speaker: Bayek
en: Fresh air... A better blessing than that priest's.

speaker: Bayek
en: The guarding of temples was once a sacred duty entrusted to the Medjay. Now it falls to no one.

speaker: Head Embalmer
en: Peace be on you! May Osiris shield your loved one's journey.

speaker: Bayek
en: I do not need your services. I'm here to inspect the temple.

speaker: Head Embalmer
en: You are not a priest. In whose name do you dare profane our grounds?

speaker: Bayek
en: In the High Priest's name. Prove this by messenger if you wish.

speaker: Head Embalmer
en: ...Ah yes. Poor Pasherenptah. The curse weighs heavy on us all. I have had two embalmers run off since it began. Only untrained laborers are free to take their place. Such coarse fellows! I hope to discharge them soon.

speaker: Bayek
en: I look forward to meeting them.

speaker: Head Embalmer
en: If you are here in the High Priest's name, you must be a man of power.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is this where bodies are delivered?

speaker: Embalmer 1
en: Yes. This is the gate to the ibu—the place of purification. The dead are brought here by their families. Then we wash them with tears wept by the gods at the death of Osiris. Or maybe just water. Hard to say.

speaker: Bayek
en: The mummies would not be tampered with so early in the process. This man is likely innocent.

speaker: Bayek
en: How old are the bodies of the dead when you get them?

speaker: Embalmer 1
en: A few days along. The families don't bring them right away so we that we aren't tempted to defile them. Hehe.

speaker: Bayek
en: I can see why they chose you to welcome the bereaved.

speaker: Embalmer 1
en: Wonder if we'll get any pretty ones today.

speaker: Bayek
en: What do you

speaker: Embalmer 2
en: Yes, yes, I know. You want to learn what I do here. I wash the bodies of the dead. It's a job—been doing it for ten years now. There's little to say about it, really.

speaker: Bayek
en: A man of my own nature. He bears watching, though.

speaker: Head Embalmer
en: Is your curiosity satisfied?

speaker: Bayek
en: Not yet.

speaker: Head Embalmer
en: Be quicker. You disturb our work and the dead's rest.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tell me a few more details of your work.

speaker: Embalmer 2
en: Fine. After being washed in palm wine, its cavity is stuffed with myrrh and cassia bark. If you want to know more, read Herodotus instead of pestering me.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Father of Lies? I hear he's overrated.

speaker: Embalmer 3
en: Anubis is my bearer, for he who lulls me to rest is the god in Lion form. The god saves me! I am He who comes forth as one who breaks through the door. "I know the deep waters" is my name. Behold the Lord and his Flood! See, the Shoulder is fastened on his neck and the Haunch upon the head of the West. Offerings which the two goddesses of the West present to me... When the weeping bursts forth from me at what I witness... As I am borne round on the seventh feastday in Abydos and the bolts on the gateways above you are in reach in your hand.

speaker: Embalmer 3
en: Behold the Lord and his Flood!

speaker: Bayek
en: Hail in peace. I wish to

speaker: Embalmer 3
en: See, the Shoulder is— the Shoulder is, uh, fastened upon his neck.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do you have a

speaker: Embalmer 3
en: Your face— your face is that of a hound, whose nostril... sniffs at the covert to which my feet convey me.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is a little unfair.

speaker: Bayek
en: I've never seen eye to eye with priests.

speaker: Bayek
en: I would not want to make an enemy of you.

speaker: Embalmer 4
en: I have no enemies, and no secrets, either. This is just how we get rid of the brain—a useless organ! Next I will open the flank and take out the liver, stomach, lungs, and intestines. They are the first parts of the body to rot.

speaker: Bayek
en: Fascinating.

speaker: Embalmer 4
en: We never get visitors here. Come see us any time!

speaker: Bayek
en: A friendly face can hide guilt... yet I do not suspect him.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are the internal organs discarded as well?

speaker: Embalmer 4
en: Osiris, no! We put them in canopic jars, each guarded by a son of Horus. The heart is left inside the chest, where Ma'at can weigh it against the Feather of Truth.

speaker: Bayek
en: You seem to enjoy this.

speaker: Embalmer 4
en: The dead are good company. They do not complain, and if they stare, you can always look away.

speaker: Bayek
en: If only it were so easy to escape their gaze.

speaker: Embalmer 4
en: Sorry? I did not hear you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Never mind.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is this salt you are working with?

speaker: Embalmer 5
en: Not salt. Natron. It dries out the body... and it fries my hands to shit. I have got burns all over! Although they have been better lately.

speaker: Bayek
en: Has the natron changed somehow?

speaker: Embalmer 5
en: The texture's been a little off. Powdery. They must be getting it from a new supplier. If you want to talk natron, man out back is the expert.

speaker: Bayek
en: If natron is used to dry the bodies... There may be something wrong with the natron. I should speak to the worker out back.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tell me more of the natron.

speaker: Embalmer 5
en: The dead man sleeps beneath a mound of the stuff for forty days. Then he is brushed off, washed in wine, and wrapped in linen. You can see more bodies drying in the courtyard.

speaker: Bayek
en: These bodies are dried with natron?

speaker: Worker
en: Mmmph. Who might you be?

speaker: Bayek
en: A temple inspector.

speaker: Worker
en: Right, about time you got here. Memphis has been stinking of rot for months!

speaker: Bayek
en: I suspect a problem with the natron. Where does it come from?

speaker: Worker
en: Not far from here. Guarded by good men near the canal. Watch out for crocodiles.

speaker: Bayek
en: And lizards...

speaker: Worker
en: Did you say "Lizard"?

speaker: Bayek
en: It means something to you?

speaker: Worker
