en: I have heard it whispered in taverns. Rumors only.

speaker: Bayek
en: If you have nothing of substance to offer, I will be leaving.

speaker: Worker
en: Wait! I can tell you this—our natron is tainted. It is mixed with sand. Go to the warehouse just north of the Great Temple. The gods be with you.

speaker: Bayek
en: So the mummies rotted due to the tainted natron. Let's see what is in this warehouse he mentions.

speaker: Bayek
en: Here's the warehouse. I need to be careful.

speaker: Bayek
en: Only the guilty aim to disgrace the innocent.

speaker: Head Embalmer
en: Oh! May the gods be kind!

speaker: Bayek
en: Salt is cheap. There must be more than gold to your crime.

speaker: Head Embalmer
en: Gold had nothing to do with it. A priest in a blue sash brought my orders.

speaker: Head Embalmer
en: He did this to me. He threatened to do the same to my daughter. I brought foulness on the city only to protect her, I swear it! Please...

speaker: Bayek
en: Help me, and I will end this.

speaker: Head Embalmer
en: Here, I kept it... Take it.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'll send its writer to the Devourer. The seal of Anubis. A priest sabotaged the natron. The letter mentions a bandit cave. I will go clear out this viper's nest once and for all.

speaker: Bayek
en: Sand. They have mixed it with the natron.

speaker: Bandit
en: I guess some neket iadet (piece of shit) was listening after all!

speaker: Bayek
en: May the kas of those lost haunt you forever! The Devourer waits for your hearts! Ma'at will judge you in the afterlife!

speaker: Bayek
en: Memphis' dead will sleep peacefully now.

speaker: Priest
en: I did not think to see you again. You seem like the wandering type. So the mummies were tampered with. May the perpetrator of this crime suffer for eternity. It seems my prayers were successful in shielding you.

speaker: Man
en: His name was Icarus, the glory of the raucous Hippodrome, the much-lauded and short-lived beloved of Kanopos. Jealous Fate, numbering his victories instead of his years, thought him old, and stole him away in his twenty-fifth year. Icarus, a champion from thirteen when he won his first race, to his thousandth win as Miliarius, there is no honor higher. His horses, as blessed by the gods as he, Abraxas, and Santana, whom he rode to victory over five hundred races, the definition of equine pride. Icarus, lead racer for the populist Prasina Green, won them wreaths of olive, laurel, and pine. Now they are lost in a turbulent sea. The Veneta Blue who gnashed their teeth and tore their breasts when he beat them, even they weep bitter tears at his loss. Oh! Tragedy, that you, Icarus should be cut down in the bloom of youth, and be summoned so soon to harness the dusky steeds of Serapis. The chariot race was never long enough when you drove with the lightning, but oh, why should your own race have ended in a flash?

speaker: Bayek
en: Sennefer? Is it you?

speaker: Claridas
en: Bayek, you sour-faced Siwan! Hah, hah. I—I'm Claridas now. What are you doing here?

speaker: Nikias
en: Icarus was a thousand times better than you!

speaker: Archippos
en: Who's going to lead you Greens now, malakia?

speaker: Maleos
en: You're a babe at the teat! You think you can win the Cursus Magnus (the great race)? Horseshit!

speaker: Claridas
en: Leave Nikias alone. Icarus's death was a dark day for all of us. Let him weep in peace.

speaker: Claridas
en: So? Is Aya with you?

speaker: Bayek
en: Ahh, eh! I am alone.

speaker: Claridas
en: I was just asking.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ask my foot next time.

speaker: Claridas
en: No matter. Join us at the tavern later!

speaker: Man 1
en: I saw you ride last month when five chariots all crashed at the turn!

speaker: Claridas
en: Yes, that was an amazing race.

speaker: Woman
en: Your horses look so strong, so sleek. How do you choose them?

speaker: Claridas
en: I have an eye for flesh.

speaker: Man 2
en: So I said... it's not your pig I'm talking about, it's your wife.

speaker: Claridas
en: Bayek! How long has it been? A decade? More?

speaker: Bayek
en: You left Siwa a long time ago. And you left your name behind too.

speaker: Claridas
en: I had to. Claridas is a name better suited for the Hippodrome.

speaker: Bayek
en: Remember the horses we rode outside Siwa?

speaker: Claridas
en: Those nags? Hah! Never thought you would leave that shithole. Ah, Siwa. Small, poor, and ugly. The only beauty there was Aya. Has it changed much? Has she?

speaker: Bayek
en: Things change. People change.

speaker: Bayek
en: I need another drink.

speaker: Nikias
en: Pardon, neb. I overheard Claridas say you once rode together? My father sponsors the Prasina Greens, and we are in need of a mighty racer.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am only here to drink. And forget.

speaker: Claridas
en: Leave him alone, Nikias. Hehe. Real men are drinking her tonight!

speaker: Claridas
en: Haha... Bayek, come. Let me show you something inspiring, ah?

speaker: Claridas
en: Come, move your ass!

speaker: Bayek
en: Where are you taking me, Sennefer?

speaker: Claridas
en: Please! Claridas! I have not been Sennefer in years.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why did you change your name?

speaker: Claridas
en: To succeed in the Hippodrome, one must be welcomed by the Greek houses. So a Greek name.

speaker: Bayek
en: You abandoned your name, your home

speaker: Claridas
en: Siwa was nothing to me. The Greeks may look down on us... but screw them! I eat and drink well on what I win!

speaker: Bayek
en: I have no ambition to race at the Hippodrome

speaker: Claridas
en: You? No, never. They cheer for me! Besides, you would need a sponsor, a real chariot... Now Icarus, he was a true hero. Did you know he won a thousand races? And survived twice as many! See how they loved Icarus!

speaker: Bayek
en: You have adopted their gods, too.

speaker: Claridas
en: Our gods never did anything for me! You're lucky I left. If I had stayed, Aya would have been mine.

speaker: Bayek
en: You're drunk. And an ass.

speaker: Claridas
en: You have no idea what I gave up.

speaker: Bayek
en: The world is hard.

speaker: Claridas
en: You always looked down on me in Siwa. Thought you were better.

speaker: Bayek
en: I never

speaker: Claridas
en: Doesn't matter. I have found fame!

speaker: Bayek
en: At what cost? You gave up your home, your name, your gods! You chose this path.

speaker: Claridas
en: And it has brought me all the coin and cunt I want!

speaker: Bayek
en: You always wanted glory. It's not what drives all of us.

speaker: Claridas
en: And all you wanted was Aya and little Bayeks. What made you abandon your dr

speaker: Bayek
en: Enough!

speaker: Claridas
en: You alive?

speaker: Claridas
en: Hah. You are old. Time for me to dunk my head.

speaker: Bayek
en: The beer hits harder than you.

speaker: Claridas
en: What in Dionysus' name were you talking to Nikias about last night?

speaker: Bayek
en: Nikias? Who?

speaker: Claridas
en: Don't bullshit me. I saw you. What, you think his father will just welcome you onto the Prasina Green team? You really think you can roll onto the track and win races with no training? No skill? Piss on you!

speaker: Bayek
en: Maybe I should seek this Nikias out and hear his offer. If you can win, Claridas, it can't be that hard.

speaker: Claridas
en: You might want to pray first. You'll need all the help you can get to survive the Hippodrome!

speaker: Bayek
en: The gods will watch us race and decide.

speaker: Claridas
en: You have your gods, I have mine. We'll see who rides out covered in glory! Enough has been said. Let the gods judge you in the Hippodrome.

speaker: Woman 1
en: If Diocles was my lover, I would chain him to the bed before I let him leave me for Cyrene.

speaker: Woman 2
en: Have you seen the ? The most comely man in Cyrene, nay, the world!

speaker: Woman 1
en: That is because you think of nothing but men. Praxilla has her own life here with her clinic.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Bayek! I heard what happened in Cyrene.

speaker: Bayek
en: How is our brave widow?

speaker: Praxilla
en: Good, as you can see.

speaker: Bayek
en: Small victories and joys like these. We take them where we can.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Bayek, Flavius was here. But that is not the worst of it. Mothers and wives of the Temple are sick and wailing in the streets. Their pleas to see their loved ones unanswered.

speaker: Bayek
en: Since Flavius came? It cannot be coincidence.

speaker: Praxilla
en: No. Can you speak to my friend Crios? He is a water bearer at the temple. My task is the priestess Melitta. She is overzealous, but I cannot believe she would prey on the sick and dying.

speaker: Bayek
en: Be wary. I will return here when I've spoken to Crios.

speaker: Woman 3
en: Listen! Listen! The Lion cast his gaze upon me and I was with child! Have you seen the proconsul? The most comely man in Cyrene, nay, the world! Flavius! Flavius! We must all sing his name! I left my husband for Flavius. If only he would look my way. I would die today if I could get to see the great Flavius' eyes again. You must stop and hear me! I will wither without the great Flavius' love. I would kill my family for a night with the Lion. What am I saying? Help me please, my love for Flavius threatens to consume me. None can satisfy me, not you, or you, none but the proconsul of Cyrene!

speaker: Bayek
en: That poor woman, Flavius has taken her from her husband, her child.

speaker: Bayek
en: They believe that if they give Asclepius these votives, he will heal them.

speaker: Bayek
en: Crios? What has Flavius done to you?

speaker: Bayek
en: Wake up! Where is Flavius? Where is he?!

speaker: Crios
en: Fly away home, crow!

speaker: Bayek
en: Another life spat on by that Roman shit-eater.

speaker: Crios
en: Whispers... whispers...

speaker: Bayek
en: What's that?

speaker: Crios
en: Melitta, the viper of the staff...

speaker: Bayek
en: The priestess?

speaker: Crios
en: No, no my lord Flavius, please...

speaker: Bayek
en: Praxilla! Praxilla!

speaker: Woman 4
en: Stop your screeching, the sick need their rest.

speaker: Bayek
en: Praxilla!

speaker: Woman 4
en: Alright, alright, just keep your voice down. She left to speak to the priestess.

speaker: Crios
en: No! The priestess... a snake in the apple... she has them, she keeps them hidden... lies in whispers... secrets... shrouded. Her shrine of whispers.

speaker: Woman 4
en: Is this poor witless thing your doing?

speaker: Bayek
en: Did Praxilla tell you where she was going?

speaker: Woman 4
en: The mountains... but...

speaker: Bayek
en: Look to this man, he needs help. I will find this Shrine of Whispers.

speaker: Bayek
en: A secret in the mountains. I pray Praxilla and the others are alright.

speaker: Melitta
en: You should be grateful, you serve Rome now. And the work will be over soon. We must know its secrets, don't you see, Praxilla? It is simply progress. A marriage of science and magic.

speaker: Praxilla
en: You are nothing but Flavius' pawn.

speaker: Melitta
en: How unimaginative you are. But why would you understand the will of Gods? This sacred object, it's a thing of wonder and terror.

speaker: Melitta
en: Call off your rabid dog, Praxilla! Killing me does nothing. Semper Flavium.

speaker: Praxilla
en: You must stop Melitta, Bayek.

speaker: Praxilla
en: She was a healer, she makes me ashamed.

speaker: Praxilla
en: The priestess, she was torturing these people.

speaker: Praxilla
en: I would burn this place to ashes if I could. There is terrible evil here, Bayek. I am terrified for the fate of my Cyrenaica.

speaker: Bayek
en: Melitta was mad.

speaker: Praxilla
en: That relic, the one Flavius used at the farm. He used it here.

speaker: Bayek
en: When I found Crios, I knew. I could feel it clawing, digging in my mind.

speaker: Praxilla
en: That is what it does, insidious like a parasite. Control men's minds and make us slaves.

speaker: Bayek
en: Our fates are our own, Praxilla, we will always fight for that.

speaker: Bayek
en: Melitta could not be saved.

speaker: Praxilla
en: After what she did? I would have slit her throat myself. Thank you, for me, for Balagrae, it is more than I would have asked.

speaker: Bayek
en: And that is why I give it freely, while freedom still means something.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Don't you ever get sick of saying so many good byes?

speaker: Bayek
en: Part of me, yes. But it is part of the journey and on it I find those who give me hope. Your land will not die, Praxilla. You are its healer, its protector, its Medjay.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Now is our time to emerge from the madness, Bayek of Siwa.

speaker: Bayek
en: I wonder how Diocles is faring?

speaker: Diocles
en: I'm no actor, Simonides.

speaker: Simonides
en: And I'm no playwright, but in vino veritas (in wine there is truth), Diocles!

speaker: Diocles
en: Bayek my friend! We were just talking about you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Should I be worried?

speaker: Diocles
en: No, no! Simonides wants me to play myself in a comedy he's written about Leander - The Laudable Triumph of the Luminaries of Cyrene.

speaker: Bayek
en: Catchy title.

speaker: Diocles
en: He'd be the first to admit it's drivel, but we're hoping a festival will restore some goodwill. To that end I have one last favor to ask...

speaker: Bayek
en: No acting required?

speaker: Diocles
en: Ha, ha, ha... Leander's villa should return back to the people, but without the deed that's impossible. The Romans won't let us search Leander's office at the Acropolis

speaker: Bayek
en: They will let me. I will find it.

speaker: Simonides
en: Bayek! Did you hear? I gave birth to an opus. It burst forth from my creative loins!

speaker: Bayek
en: You er...

speaker: Simonides
en: I wrote a play my dear fellow. Of our exploits! O' Meander, scourge of Cyrene, I Hiocles will stop your scurrilous schemes! Ha, ha, I changed the names no-one will know.

speaker: Bayek
en: My poet friend Phanos used a similar ploy in Alexandria.

speaker: Simonides
en: Ah, excellent, we poets are unified in our cleverness. Come, let us raise a cup of wine to our savior, the furious and fecund Dimonides! (not reciting) Hm... That one might be a little too much.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where better to find the deed but hidden quarters?

speaker: Bayek
en: The villa papers! Diocles will be happy.

speaker: Bayek
en: The deed is yours Diocles.

speaker: Diocles
en: The people had lost faith in us magistrates. This will restore a lot of it.

speaker: Bayek
en: You will win hearts and minds Diocles, with actions.

speaker: Diocles
en: Vitruvius is a friend of yours, yes? A visiting merchant said he saw him on the road near the citadel and he appeared to be in trouble.

speaker: Bayek
en: That architect is a good man.

speaker: Diocles
en: I've heard his public works have revitalized South Cyrenaica. I would love to meet him in person.

speaker: Bayek
en: Perhaps we can meet at the Oracle of Apollo? I will check on Vitruvius, that rare Roman dreamer.

speaker: Bayek
en: Vitruvius! Diocles told me you were attacked!

speaker: Vitruvius
en: On my way to the citadel. Some accursed marauders took my manuscript, my life's work, De Architecture.

speaker: Bayek
en: These are dangerous times, but I would not take bandits for scholars

speaker: Vitruvius
en: I dread to think what they'll do with it. Certainly not appreciate the function and form of the modern approach to architecture.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then I'll get it back before they use if for kindling, or worse.

speaker: Bayek
en: Vitruvius' book, saved for posterity. Knowledge in the wrong hands is a sad waste.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: You found it? Praise Jupiter!

speaker: Bayek
en: They were sad to lose it.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: I'm sure they had already started using it to improve their rattrap! Thank you my friend, I will dedicate a chapter to you.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am honored. Actually my friend Diocles is very interested in reading it. I said we would meet him at the Oracle Shrine.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: A capital idea!

speaker: Bayek
en: I have someone I need to see and I will join you.

speaker: Bayek
en: I should go and see Praxilla. Because she should be at this meeting of the great minds of Cyrene.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Bayek! I heard what happened in Cyrene.

speaker: Bayek
en: It is done and my son Khemu is at peace.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Bayek, I did not think I would see you again! But I heard, Flavius is no more.

speaker: Bayek
en: It was a day I had long wished for. But how has it been in Balagrae?

speaker: Praxilla
en: Romans are co-operating more now that Melitta is gone.

speaker: Bayek
en: We will see about that. And your friend Crios?

speaker: Praxilla
en: I am teaching him the healing arts. But I sent him out a day ago to the east hills to gather herbs and he's not returned. I was just about to go look for him.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will find him, if you go to the Oracle Shrine? There is a friend there who would like to see you.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Is it... no I will not dare to hope.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will join you when I find Crios.

speaker: Crios
en: Help! Help! Someone help me, please!

speaker: Crios
en: You! You saved me before. I thought you were a dream! You are a friend of Praxilla's!

speaker: Bayek
en: You are making a habit of getting into trouble.

speaker: Crios
en: Yes, the plant reveals what is in the seed... I will take more care in future. Thank you, protector.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: Yes, yes Diocles, I understand your argument, but function should not be the only consideration. What of perfection of form, beauty for beauty's sake? It is obvious you appreciate that in other spheres, eh, Praxilla?

speaker: Praxilla
en: You are making him blush, Vitruvius.

speaker: Diocles
en: You have brought us all together, Bayek.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: Cyrene's Triumvirate! Heralds of a new peace for this outpost of Rome.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Each thinks his own horizon is the limit of the worlds, but through you we found a greater purpose...

speaker: Diocles
en: And Praxilla and I are to be married.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Diocles! I have not said yes yet.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: If you have a garden and a library, you have everything you need. But, now a toast!

speaker: Praxilla
en: To Bayek and Cyrene!

speaker: Diocles
en: To peace and order.

speaker: Bayek
en: To love and weddings.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: , Cyrenaica.

speaker: Praxilla
en: So you will come back to Balagrae, with me?

speaker: Diocles
en: If that is where you want to build our home.

speaker: Praxilla
en: You could do a lot of good there.

speaker: Diocles
en: You already have, dearheart.

speaker: Besa
en: Bayek, I saw you in my slumbers. You alone have returned from the Duat.

speaker: Bayek
en: You saw this? Het and his wife, Ramesses' son, Khui's gods... Septimius. I... was there, but I didn't truly understand.

speaker: Besa
en: Then perhaps with the blessing of Thoth I can guide you thorough the chaos. A warrior, answering Anubis' call, sacrificing love for duty. But you and your beloved will not be parted in the eternal fields. A son defiant, refusing to walk the path gouged in the sand by his father's feet. A leader is not a tyrant, Bayek. Caesar, Ptolemy, Flavius, oppression, fear... You may work in the dark but you serve the light. An old man, forsaken and fearful. But every day you honor the gods, in your words, your deeds. Their lessons cannot slip through your fingers like a thousand grains of sand. The foul heart, corrupt, fetid. This is not your fate. You will enter the Duat without your enemy, Bayek and you will find serenity.

speaker: Bayek
en: Thank you, Besa, this is a comfort.

speaker: Bayek
en: "Bayek of Siwa, styling himself as a Medjay, is sought for crimes against the rule of our glorious Pharaoh..." Orders to kill me. Those who hold them must die before I do.

speaker: Bayek
en: A key with the Eye of Horus. What could it unlock?

speaker: Bayek
en: Another key, same as the first. How many of the Phylakes have these?

speaker: Bayek
en: A third key. Must be part of a set. Clearly they protect something of value.

speaker: Bayek
en: "Abar refuses to hand over the last key... She busies herself with simple tasks in that sad fishing village east of Herakleion". The last key, eh? Maybe I'll pay that "sad fishing village" a visit.

speaker: Bayek
en: That woman has a warrior's bearing. She could be the one spoken of in the letter.

speaker: Abar
en: Halt! Who are you?

speaker: Bayek
en: A man who respects his elders.

speaker: Abar
en: I know all the warrior castes. You speak like a Medjay.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am one, and I seek your key.

speaker: Abar
en: Why would I give it to you, when I refuse it to my brothers?

speaker: Bayek
en: Your brothers are dead. They had orders to execute me.

speaker: Abar
en: These are the times we live in. Prove yourself as a protector, and I will give you the one thing I have left—the key. Crocodiles plague our village. You'll find them roaming east of here.

speaker: Abar
en: The blood on your sword will be proof of your Medjay oath. Convince me of your strength by handling our crocodile problem. The crocodiles haunt a small island east of the village.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your village should be safe from crocodiles for a time.

speaker: Abar
en: Good. You know, I always admired the Medjay. I wish I could have been one of you.

speaker: Bayek
en: There are so few of us left.

speaker: Abar
en: The Phylakes were always short on honor. Here is the key to my warrior's chest. Make something of my legacy in this wretched world. You will find the chest sunk in Mother Nile, a little south of here.

speaker: Bayek
en: Four keys, four locks. Now I will see this great warrior's treasure.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Bayek! Just the Medjay I was looking for. We know how to rid ourselves of Gennadios' phylakitai.

speaker: Bayek
en: You've found the neket iadets?

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Indeed! One group patrols the waters. Another sits in wait in the armory, seizing whoever they wish. The final man proclaims loudly against us, in a chariot along the Canopic Way. Once rid of them...

speaker: Bayek
en: Your poets can spread their good word throughout the city. We will deal with these phylakitai.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Go, brother, and deal with these metrokoites. Once they are dealt with, we can send our poets to spread the truth.

speaker: Bayek
en: A phylakitai is in that chariot. I must rid Alexandria of these horrible beings.

speaker: Bayek
en: These are Gennadios' phylakitai. This must be the armory Phanos told me of.

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: We're down one man, the orders are to recruit by force if necessary.

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: Saw a good one down by the docks. No one would even notice if he was missing. He was spouting some inflammatory poetry. I hate poets.

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: Good. He'll be a useful pisspole.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Bayek! You have returned. Is it done? Are the streets free for the Alexandrian poets to spread our revolution?

speaker: Bayek
en: I have dealt with all of Gennadios' phylakitai, Phanos.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Bayek, you are a Poet of the Kill.

speaker: Bayek
en: Fill the city with your words.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: I love you Bayek of Siwa. You will be remembered more than any Medjay in history.

speaker: Man
en: I must honor him, Flavius, our leader, our liberator. The Lion. I will paint his name on every wall from here to Rome for the whole Republic to see. Everyone will know the name of Flavius. Flavius the shining, the golden, the majestic, the most benevolent. All must know it, Flavius! Flavius! He is the God who walks among us. His divine feet will stomp a path to Rome. And all those who oppose him will fall.

speaker: Bayek
en: People act against nature! Could Flavius really do this?

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you Kade? Your mother sent me to find you.

speaker: Kade
en: By Iset, is that you Bayek of Siwa? Let me out and I'll help you kill those Roman vultures.

speaker: Kade
en: Egypt will not be your lapdog! Help me, Bayek!

speaker: Kade
en: We are free of those Roman tyrants.

speaker: Bayek
en: The farm you came from, I saw what Flavius did. How he sucked the life from our people.

speaker: Kade
en: My mother Nenet? Is she alright?

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes. Praxilla took her to Balagrae.

speaker: Kade
en: Thank you, Bayek. You protect us even this far from the land of our ancestors.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why did the Romans bring you here?

speaker: Kade
en: To feed their hunger for war and conquest. They have ballista. We load it with a substance of hideous, burning devastation. Vitruvius, a Roman engineer up at the aqueduct invented it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Vitruvius? I know this man, I cannot believe he would make something like this.

speaker: Kade
en: We are free of those Roman tyrants.

speaker: Bayek
en: Vitruvius! We need to speak.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: What's the fuss, my friend?

speaker: Bayek
en: I believed you when you said you cared for the Siwans here. And all the while there are more at the citadel, forced to work on a weapon you created!

speaker: Vitruvius
en: It is not what you think. Walk with me and we'll get to the bottom of this.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then I will find this merchant of death. Go to your mother, she will be glad to see you safe.

speaker: Kade
en: We are free of those Roman tyrants.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: Please understand Bayek, I was not always so focused on architectural wonders such as this aqueduct. As a hotheaded youth I came up with many means of death and destruction. One of those was a Greek Fire of sorts.

speaker: Bayek
en: Greek fire?

speaker: Vitruvius
en: A substance with such potential for unspeakable suffering, I vowed never to produce it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Well the general is producing it, and forcing Siwans to arm his ballista for a war against their own country.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: Curse my pride, I should have burned my notes. General Agrippa must have found them.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then Agrippa must be stopped.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: Do what your conscience dictates, Bayek. But understand I cannot be part of a plot against a Roman General. No matter how I may feel personally. Recover the formula and I will destroy it. I will not have the immolation of Egypt on my conscience. Jove protect you. Bayek. I dread to think what Agrippa will do with my weapon, please hurry.

speaker: Bayek
en: All who ally with monsters and demons will die, General.

speaker: Bayek
en: They used the formula. I should destroy the Greek fire stockpiles!

speaker: Bayek
en: Vitruvius will want to know his formula is in safer hands.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: Bayek, did you find it, did you find my formula?

speaker: Bayek
en: Egypt will not burn today.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: Or any day I hope. And General Agrippa?

speaker: Bayek
en: He did not give it up willingly.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: He was a good Roman. But he never understood that doesn't mean you cannot be a good man. Flavius fed Agrippa's pride and ambition with talk of empires. I fear the path his supporters have taken will end in many deaths.

speaker: Bayek
en: It will end with their own. But you are a good man Vitruvius. I have seen that in your words and deeds.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: I am trying to be. Thank you again, Bayek of Siwa, you are a true protector of your people.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 1
en: Why can't the Pharaoh's soldiers just leave us alone?

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 2
en: We refuse their rule. Neither they nor their supporters can suffer us to live.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 1
en: A false pharaoh is no true ruler of ours. Defiance is our only option.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 2
en: I'm afraid there won't be any of us left to show defiance at this rate.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 1
en: It does not matter how many the Ptolemies send to hunt us down. We will win. Somehow.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 3
en: I'm worried about the children. Istellah doesn't usually go adventuring for so long.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 4
en: She knows how to be careful. And she'll bring Hetanu back unharmed. She always does.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 3
en: Of course. But will she remember to bring herself back unharmed?

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 4
en: I am more worried that the pharaoh's killers might have caught them.

speaker: Nawa
en: And so it was proven that Ptolemy was a false pharaoh. Not a god, not an Egyptian even. Nothing but a puppet. They called us heretics. Stole the Pissa Oros Citadel from us, and hunted us down.

speaker: Child 1
en: But other people, they know the Pharaoh is a bad man, right, Nawa?

speaker: Nawa
en: That's right. But they are too afraid to speak out. And not without cause. There are those in high positions who will do anything to keep their power. it is dangerous to speak out against the Pharaoh. And that is why, with Sebni away, we will discuss politics.

speaker: Nawa
en: So, the scouts were right. You're Bayek. The Medjay from Siwa. Son of the Nile and defender of the people. I am Nawa, and the rebel cause needs your strength.

speaker: Bayek
en: My oath is to protect. Tell me more.

speaker: Nawa
en: Sebni, my cousin, told the children stories of Alexander the Great. Of course, two of the children decided that meant there was treasure of his to discover nearby.

speaker: Bayek
en: As children will do.

speaker: Nawa
en: Indeed. Sebni and one of our warriors went to search for the children, but the pharaoh's soldiers captured them.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do you know where they are?

speaker: Nawa
en: Yes. One of our scouts saw them. They're being held prisoner in camp Hetoimazo, north of here. Please find them. Sebni is the only one who knows where those children have run off to.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will find him, and then the children.

speaker: Nawa
en: Thank you for agreeing to help us, Medjay. Anyone who fights against the tyranny of the Pharaoh is a friend of ours.

speaker: Sebni
en: Get us out of here.

speaker: Sebni
en: Thank you for rescuing us.

speaker: Sebni
en: This is my fault. By Anubis I swear, I just wanted them to dream a little! If only I had not told them those stories.

speaker: Khamet
en: Enough, Sebni. Children will be children. Let's just find them.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is why I'm here. Any idea where they went?

speaker: Sebni
en: The ancient temple of Alexander the Great, maybe? That is the one I was telling them about. It is northwest of here.

speaker: Khamet
en: It's been a while. They might have gone west, to Theos Elpis Rift. We have a camp there.

speaker: Bayek
en: Very well. I will scour the temple area, you head for the camp.

speaker: Khamet
en: I'll go with you. Sebni will go back to the chasm campo. Where it is safer for dreamers to be.

speaker: Khamet
en: The children used to run free, here. But ever since the Pharaoh's guards arrived...

speaker: Bayek
en: What was once a playground is now a death ground.

speaker: Khamet
en: Yes. The Pharaoh's men are snakes, coiled in the sand beneath our feet. They kill adults and children alike. The desert is meant for old souls. Hunters, and poets. Not the slaughter of innocents.

speaker: Bayek
en: You know this place well?

speaker: Khamet
en: I grew up here. I love it. But the Pharaoh's men spoil everything they touch.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tell me about the children.

speaker: Khamet
en: Hetanu is a good student. He'll be a scholar one day. Istellah... I am training her. She is always protecting her friend. Strong. A good little warrior.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do you train all the children to become rebels?

speaker: Khamet
en: They are free to choose as they please. But they all hate the Pharaoh's men. People will blame Istellah for this.

speaker: Bayek
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Khamet
en: She is loud, and outspoken. He has the adventurer's heart. Istellah protects. People just don't listen.

speaker: Bayek
en: They are loyal to each other.

speaker: Khamet
en: They are good children.

speaker: Khamet
en: This is it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let's split up. We should be able to find traces of their presence faster that way.

speaker: Khamet
en: Istellah is smart. Upon seeing the bandits, she would have known to vanish, and find a hiding place. Amunet favors her.

speaker: Bayek
en: Fresh footprints. Child-sized. They were here.

speaker: Bayek
en: These ostraca are similar to those used by the children Nawa was teaching. They must have dropped it here. Notes on Alexander the Great, and the temple. And many wild theories as to what treasures might be here.

speaker: Bayek
en: Children's sandals. Removed to climb this wall?

speaker: Bayek
en: Cloth. From a child's...

speaker: Hetanu
en: Is someone out there? Help! Please hurry! There are snakes!

speaker: Bayek
en: Keep still and try to stay quiet. I will be right there. The entrance is barred. I'll have to find another way inside.

speaker: Bayek
en: I believe Hetanu is here. Stuck, inside the temple.

speaker: Khamet
en: I'll stand guard while you retrieve him.

speaker: Bayek
en: A hidden entrance. It must lead inside the temple.

speaker: Bayek
en: This snake was dispatched by a small blade. A good, clean kill.

speaker: Bayek
en: Child!

speaker: Hetanu
en: Watch out! Do not let the snakes get you! And—please do not let the snakes get me!

speaker: Tehanu
en: You got them all!

speaker: Hetanu
en: I am Hetanu. Thank you, wer neb, for rescuing me.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am no lord. You may call me Bayek. Now. Tell me what happened here, child.

speaker: Hetanu
en: We came looking for the legendary treasure of Alexander the Great. Our teacher told us all about him, and we knew there had to be more! We managed to get into the temple, but then the snakes came out of the water, and surrounded us.

speaker: Bayek
en: What about Istellah?

speaker: Hetanu
en: She did not want to leave me, but I told her to go and get help. She used the shield for protection. Not a single snake touched her! But that was hours ago and I am worried. She should have been back with help by now. If she is not with you... something must have happened to her.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let's get you out of here first. Follow me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Something of importance was here. I wonder who took it.

speaker: Hetanu
en: I told Istellah to take the shield, so she could get out. But the spear was too heavy for us. I cannot wait until we get back. We really did find Alexander's treasure!

speaker: Hetanu
en: Khamet! I am so happy to see you, Khamet!

speaker: Khamet
en: I trust you have learned your lesson.

speaker: Hetanu
en: I know. If not for Bayek, those snakes would have eaten me whole.

speaker: Bayek
en: Well. Perhaps not whole. But it would have been a dire fate nonetheless. Now. Did Istellah say where she was going?

speaker: Hetanu
en: She went to the chasm camp to find help.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will go look for the little warrior.

speaker: Hetanu
en: Have you been to the camp yet? Was Istellah there? I hope Istellah is safe.

speaker: Khamet
en: Istellah has yet to return. Best you head out. Knowing Istellah, she's found more trouble.

speaker: Bayek
en: Smoke. It is coming from the camp.

speaker: Sebni
en: Curse you, fiends! Over here, Medjay! The gods will not forgive you this evil! The Medjay is here! Fight! We can defeat them!

speaker: Sebni
en: Once again, you have come to our rescue. We will forever be in your debt, at this rate.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hetanu is safe. Khamet is with him.

speaker: Sebni
en: Oh, thank the gods. I wish I could say the same for Istellah. Their leader, Medon, took her as she arrived. He wanted the great shield she was carrying, and when she refused to give it to him, he snatched her up. He kept asking her if there was more treasure. Pissa Oros. That is where he probably took her. No one ever comes back from there. Please, you must go find her. Medon will torture her to get what he wants.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will find her. And I will take care of Medon.

speaker: Sebni
en: The citadel is in the southwest mountains. Medon patrols between here and the citadel. Just look for an angry bald man, surrounded by bodyguards.

speaker: Egyptian soldier
en: They snuck up on us, attacked like cowards. But we showed them! They'll think twice before they attack us again. Thank you for your help, Medjay.

speaker: Sebni
en: The Medjay rides to the Citadel! Finally, a protector to defent us! Have you found them yet?

speaker: Bayek
en: Bald, angry-looking, and with bodyguards... No doubt. Medon.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Stupid girl. Thinks she can hide treasure from me, does she? She will talk soon enough. Everyone talks under the heat of the iron.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am your first judgment, Medon. Prepare to die.

speaker: Medon
en: Did those rebels send you? How pathetic! After I'm done with you, I will wipe out every last one of those rats.

speaker: Bayek
en: The gods will punish you harshly for what you have done.

speaker: Medon
en: Nonsense. The gods are on my side! And I shall keep all the riches from the Temple, with the Pharaoh's blessing!

speaker: Bayek
en: Now you face the gods' judgement.

speaker: Bayek
en: Good riddance. This should offer some measure of respite to the rebels. Now to find the Citadel, and save the child.

speaker: Rebel
en: They brought a child earlier, but she escaped. She must be hiding nearby. Find her and get her out of here while I distract the guards! The child in the cell escaped, and is hiding in the hay cart. Help her back to one of our camps! I will buy you both time!

speaker: Bayek
en: This must have been the cell they held Istellah in. She killed the guard. Such a strong child.

speaker: Istellah
en: Pssst! You! The tall one! Over here. Hey. Over here!

speaker: Bayek
en: Istellah? I see you have an escape route planned out.

speaker: Istellah
en: You understand. Now climb on the cart, and drive us out of here. Let's go. They'll notice soon enough.

speaker: Istellah
en: Yes! Well done! Now go to our camp nearby! We'll be safe there! That's right! Head for the big pile of rocks with trees! We have a camp there! We're here!

speaker: Istellah
en: Thank you, brave warrior. That was a chariot ride worthy of Set himself. Did the rebels send you? Those men were going to kill me.

speaker: Bayek
en: You show much fire, for one your age.

speaker: Istellah
en: You would too, in my place. The Pharaoh's dogs seek to wipe us out and control everything. They do not understand. Life must flow freely, or else everything rots. They wanted my treasure, so I fought back. Besides, I had to protect Hetanu. If they had found him, they would have killed him. I have been so worried...

speaker: Bayek
en: Your friend is safe. He is back at the camp with the others. Where you should be, as well.

speaker: Istellah
en: I know, I know. Be more careful, Istellah. Stay out of trouble, Istellah. One day, though... One day, I'll be just like you. I will liberate the desert so we can all be free.

speaker: Bayek
en: On that day, come find me, young warrior. It will be an honor to fight by your side.

speaker: Istellah
en: I'm going to ask Khamet for more warrior training. Just you wait. Greetings Medjay.

speaker: Egyptian soldier 1
en: Did you hear? The Medjay of Siwa found the children, and killed Medon.

speaker: Egyptian soldier 2
en: The gods are looking out for us! It was good of them to send the Medjay our way.

speaker: Egyptian soldier 1
en: Truly, we are blessed, for being worthy of his protection.

speaker: Egyptian soldier 2
en: Right. Until the children find more trouble again.

speaker: Egyptian soldier 1
en: Well, yes. Though they were right about the treasure.

speaker: Egyptian soldier 2
en: And they will not ever let us forget that.

speaker: Nawa
en: Thank you, Medjay. It is a relief to have Sebni and the children back. You really made an impression on Hetanu. He's been asking me for every bit of knowledge I have on the Medjay.

speaker: Hetanu
en: I am so happy to be back here. There are no snakes here. This is a good place. Thank you again, Medjay!

speaker: Oba
en: Pssst! You there! Is that a Medjay badge? Over here! Please, I am weak! Get me out of here! I will show you all of Giza's secrets. I know everything!

speaker: Oba
en: Could you carry me? I will fall on my own. Help me!

speaker: Oba
en: The gods are smiling! You are a true hero!

speaker: Bayek
en: Keep quiet. Head down.

speaker: Oba
en: Freedom!

speaker: Bayek
en: You recover quick...

speaker: Oba
en: Now, how about we loot some tombs!?

speaker: Bayek
en: Have I helped another criminal of Egypt?

speaker: Oba
en: Oh, that is right – you are a Medjay. No! Not a criminal. I'm an opportunist!

speaker: Bayek
en: I know your kind. What did you dig up this time? It sure caught the eyes of those bandits.

speaker: Oba
en: A ring of unparalleled riches, as you can see, everyone wants it. Those bandits dragged me around trying to find it. Me? I just want what it is worth. You think I enjoy being a scavenger?

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes.

speaker: Oba
en: Hmm. Come. Follow me to my palace. My safety is your duty, is it not? You saw how dangerous it is out here.

speaker: Bayek
en: I suppose...

speaker: Oba
en: Yes! My very own Medjay! What a treat. I thought you were all buried beneath the sands of time!

speaker: Bayek
en: Not all.

speaker: Oba
en: You should join us. We could use a strong warrior like yourself.

speaker: Bayek
en: To get you out of all the trouble you get yourself into?

speaker: Oba
en: Yes... It is hard out here for us, you know? Bandits always up our asses.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then you should trade this ring and be done with it.

speaker: Oba
en: I know, but Giza has so much wonder, and mystery. You just have to look hard enough! And the rewards... Oh, the rewards!

speaker: Oba
en: Ah ha! That is my palace – up ahead!

speaker: Bayek
en: Some palace...

speaker: Oba
en: Nebti! My seni (friend)! Why didn't you come searching for me!? I was locked in a cell for days! Nek! Where is the ring?

speaker: Nebti
en: Okay, calm down. Rashidi has it. Who is this?

speaker: Oba
en: This is my brother, gonna help us find the ring.

speaker: Nebti
en: Are you serious?

speaker: Bayek
en: Okay, yeah. Why not? I've got time.

speaker: Nebti
en: Hah! Luck is always on your side, isn't it, Oba?

speaker: Oba
en: If it was, I'd have my ring.

speaker: Nebti
en: Our ring, yes, yes!

speaker: Oba
en: That ring is worth millions of drachmas. Cleopatra would lay you if you gave it to her.

speaker: Nebti
en: We should check for our other brothers. They have the ring.

speaker: Bayek
en: There are bandits all around here. I'll start there.

speaker: Nebti
en: Rashidi went south. Likely ran into those bandits camped by the Sphinx, the fool...

speaker: Bayek
en: Rashidi is in danger. I have to get him out of that bandit camp.

speaker: Bayek
en: Who's Rashidi?

speaker: Oba
en: Another brother! But between you and I, I do not trust him with the ring. Nebti either. I would spend the ring's money on my family. Do you have any idea how many children I have!? Guess!

speaker: Bayek
en: None.

speaker: Oba
en: Hah. Sixty! You were not even close.

speaker: Bayek
en: What happened to Rashidi?

speaker: Nebti
en: Bandits got a hold of him. Like Oba. I will tell you a secret though. I do not trust either of them with the ring. In fact, I think they are going against me.

speaker: Rashidi
en: What did I do to deserve this? Is someone there? Hello? Get me out of here! They will be back any moment!

speaker: Bayek
en: Rashidi?

speaker: Rashidi
en: Huh? You know my name?

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm here to get you out.

speaker: Bayek
en: This ring you've found is certainly sought after.

speaker: Rashidi
en: You know about the ring!?

speaker: Bayek
en: Oba and Nebti said you might be in trouble. I think you'd all be better off giving up this life, hmm?

speaker: Rashidi
en: We could, if we had the ring!

speaker: Bayek
en: Wait, you mean you don't have it?

speaker: Rashidi
en: Turo punched me straight in the face and took off to the Hemon Tombs to trade it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Agh... Who is Turo?

speaker: RashidI
en: A brother!

speaker: Bayek
en: Of course. I will go make sure he's alright. Go back to your brothers. You'll be safer with them.

speaker: Rashidi
en: Hardly!

speaker: Bayek
en: I wonder what tale Turo will tell me.

speaker: Bayek
en: You should get back to camp with your brothers. I'll find Turo.

speaker: Rashidi
en: Make sure he leads you to that ring! We're supposed to share it, but I think he ran off to sell it himself.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ugh. Looks like the bandits caught up but crossed some hyenas. Is Turo among the dead?

speaker: Bayek
en: This must be Turo.

speaker: Bayek
en: What's this? Ugh. His hand was eaten. A hyena must have swallowed the ring, too. This is absurd.

speaker: Bayek
en: At last. The ring Oba, Nebti and Rashidi were looking for. Time to put an end to this.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have bad news.

speaker: Oba
en: You lost the ring!?

speaker: Nebti
en: You lost the ring!?

speaker: Rashidi
en: You lost the ring!?

speaker: Bayek
en: Turo is dead...

speaker: Oba
en: Oh, tragic... and the ring?

speaker: Nebti
en: Yes, quite unfortunate. And what of the ring?

speaker: Rashidi
en: Did you find it!?

speaker: Bayek
en: ...I found it. Did you not hear me? About Turo?

speaker: Oba
en: This mess is their fault! Give it to me! My Medjay, come on!

speaker: Nebti
en: These men are ungrateful. It belongs to me.

speaker: Rashidi
en: It is mine! I am the one who does all the work! Give it to me!

speaker: Oba
en: It is mine!

speaker: Bayek
en: I should be on my way now, brothers.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you not sad? Your friends have died.

speaker: Oba
en: In Giza, a friend dies everyday.

speaker: Oba
en: Where is it!?

speaker: Nebti
en: Nek! (Shit!) The ring!

speaker: Oba
en: Damn those two! I have to find the ring before they do!

speaker: Bayek
en: Keep looking. I'm sure it'll pop up somewhere.

speaker: Oba
en: Gah! I will never give up!

speaker: Nebti
en: I am keeping far away from the others, and when I find that ring, I will go even further!

speaker: Bayek
en: You better hurry. They might find it before you do.

speaker: Rashidi
en: Shh, the ring is still missing but I think it is somewhere close by!

speaker: Bayek
en: I think the others found it.

speaker: Rashidi
en: They have not... Have they? Have they?! Gah! You are playing tricks on me.

speaker: Tahira
en: Here, Bayek. The gods still have need for us.

speaker: Bayek
en: What are your plans now, Tahira?

speaker: Tahira
en: Sobek is not done with me yet, and thus he still has use for you. Are you game?

speaker: Bayek
en: I have much to do. What more do you need?

speaker: Tahira
en: The Roman hunters still infest this area like maggots. In time, they will come together and undo our work. They will consume everything. But if we strike now, while they are alone and seperated, we may bloody them enough to drive them off.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do you truly need my help?

speaker: Tahira
en: I would not ask, otherwise.

speaker: Tahira
en: Quiet now. Hunters ahead.

speaker: Tahira
en: Now... fall upon them like Sobek's wrath!

speaker: Tahira
en: Quick work. Though I do not know what they do with the flamingos.

speaker: Bayek
en: They eat the tongue. A Roman delicacy, boiled with dates... or so I've heard.

speaker: Tahira
en: Sounds terrible.

speaker: Bayek
en: How long have you been out this way?

speaker: Tahira
en: Long enough for scar tissue to grow over some wounds. But some are still raw.

speaker: Tahira
en: Wait. That is not a right sound.

speaker: Roman Soldier
en: Beat the bushes for the great sacred crocodiles! Glory and reward for whomever finds and catches them!

speaker: Tahira
en: Those pus-filled scabs! They are defiling the shrine and trying to recapture Sobek's children!

speaker: Tahira
en: Good. Sobek's children can grow fat off Roman bones.

speaker: Bayek
en: I think you might be Sobek's adopted daughter.

speaker: Tahira
en: Oh, hush! Come, there are more of these Roman maggots to find.

speaker: Tahira
en: When we parted, you still had more names to find.

speaker: Bayek
en: I found them.

speaker: Tahira
en: And did they ease your night terrors?

speaker: Bayek
en: No. Rather, they unlocked a whole new world of atrocities.

speaker: Tahira
en: Be on guard. These Roman leeches prove their courage by caging hippos.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Romans are fools. Rampaging hippos endanger every living thing.

speaker: Tahira
en: That was god's work, Bayek. It was good to be at your side again.

speaker: Bayek
en: My father always said to be wary of a smiling crocodile, but I will take Sobek's favor if he's offering.

speaker: Tahira
en: I do not know how long he will continue to smile. Cities like Herakleion are a blight upon the land, driving the gods away from here. We are witnessing the end of an age.

speaker: Bayek
en: I thought I was supposed to be the somber one.

speaker: Tahira
en: You are right, my brother.

speaker: Bayek
en: It was good to see you, Tahira. May all the gods watch over you.

speaker: Tahira
en: And you. I will follow Sobek's children into the green. I hope you find what you are looking for.

speaker: Imprisoned priests
en: ... I am dying of thirst. Please. You cannot lock us up like this! This is a holy place! The sacred Temple of Amun! Water! Please! Water. The gods will not forgive you! By the love of Amun, please!

speaker: Priest
en: Bayek! Is that really you?

speaker: Priest
en: There are other priests being held. Four of them.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hide here until you can get out without being seen.

speaker: Priest
en: Bayek! What are you doing here? Careful. The soldiers are everywhere. Bayek! They will kill you if they find you.

speaker: Priest
en: Get me out of here! If someone's there, let me out and fight me! Is someone there? Damn you all!

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you all right?

speaker: Priest
en: Bruised and beaten, but I can move.

speaker: Bayek
en: Stay hidden until you can slip out of the temple.

speaker: Priest
en: Please! Let me out! My family needs me! Let me at least talk to my wife. What do you want me to tell you? I know nothing!

speaker: Priest
en: Bayek? Is that you? Get me out of here! Thanks be to Amun you came along, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hide right here. When you are certain no one's around, get away from the temple.

speaker: Bayek
en: By the grace of Amun, that's all of them.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you Theodoros' men?

speaker: Egyptian Rebel 1
en: Yes. And who are you?

speaker: Egyptian Rebel 2
en: He is the Siwan.

speaker: Bayek
en: I come on his behalf. He'll be joining us shortly with instructions.

speaker: Egyptian Rebel 1
en: Good! The soldiers are reeling, but it won't be long before reinforcements arrive. Come.

speaker: Egyptian Rebel 1
en: Theodoros!

speaker: Theodoros
en: Ready your blades and check your arrows. Derratos will be back at the camp before sunrise.

speaker: Theodoros
en: You're with me. But don't forget, he's mine!

speaker: Bayek
en: What is your stake in this? This is more about him than it is about your war.

speaker: Theodoros
en: My father grew figs in the Faiyum. The best. Derratos taxed him. An Egyptian has no choice but to pay. One season, the harvest was so poor that my father struggled to give his cut. Derratos figured him for a cheat, and took a bite of fruit to prove his point. He got a mouth full of worms. His men laughed, but Derratos was furious. I watched as my father was hanged from his own tree and picked at by every animal in the region. Derratos embodies the unjust. He is why I am who I am. I need you, Bayek.

speaker: Egyptian Rebel
en: Trireme!

speaker: Theodoros
en: The gods have brought us together for this. Justice will be served today.

speaker: Theodoros
en: For Egypt!

speaker: Egyptian Rebel 1
en: For your father, Theodoros!

speaker: Egyptian Rebel 2
en: Derratos dies today!

speaker: Egyptian Rebel 3
en: Leave no one alive! Clear the camp!

speaker: Theodoros
en: There is no escaping now, Derratos. Face me!

speaker: Derratos
en: Ha ha ha! This one knows me by name. Good! I will crush your puny skull!

speaker: Theodoros
en: You don't remember, do you? Before this is over, you will. I have waited too long for this! Come on! Your tyranny is over!

speaker: Egyptian Rebel 1
en: Get him, Theodoros!

speaker: Egyptian Rebel 2
en: Let us overpopulate the Duat!

speaker: Egyptian Rebel 1
en: No one leaves here alive.

speaker: Egyptian Rebel 3
en: Do not clean your blades until all are dead.

speaker: Theodoros
en: You remember now...

speaker: Theodoros
en: May the Field of Reeds elude you always.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier
en: Glory to Theodoros!

speaker: Theodoros
en: Derratos has fallen. Finally. My father's ka is at peace. Let's move. We have a long trek ahead.

speaker: Bayek
en: One more villain in the dirt. You've had your vengeance, Theodoros. Was it worth it?

speaker: Theodoros
en: Hah, I was wondering the same. I have not visited my father's tomb since he was killed by Derratos. I had to do right by him. And now, I have. Thank you, Bayek. Shame there are so few Medjay left. Your reputation precedes you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Save your blessings. There will be more battles to win.

speaker: Theodoros
en: Yes. May our victories multiply.

speaker: Theodoros
en: Now I share a story with you, Medjay. I will tell the rebels about this day. Thank you Bayek. Come visit us in our hideout. I'm sure we could find some more use for you.

speaker: Egyptian Rebel 1
en: It's done. It's over.

speaker: Egyptian Rebel 2
en: Derratos was a terror in this region.

speaker: Egyptian Rebel 1
en: And Theodoros experienced it first hand. My only regret is that we didn't snuff out this bastard sooner.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is no farm, but a major military encampment.

speaker: Bayek
en: These were no soldiers. Simple farmers, bones ground up, heads like smashed cabbages.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hm. War plans... They are harnessing elephants to fight? And they are honing their killing instincts on the farmers?

speaker: Bayek
en: By the horns of Amun! The size of this beast! The power behind it must be immense. It must have taken a full cow just to make this harness!

speaker: Man
en: Please, sweet Iset, grand me release!

speaker: Man 2
en: Why call on the gods, fool? They have clearly abandoned us!

speaker: Man
en: Shh! Quiet! You will just bring them back to us!

speaker: Roman Soldier
en: Shut your mouth, wretch! If you don't quiet down, I'll make sure you 're thrown into the field, next!

speaker: Iuseneb
en: You there, please, if you have any decency in your heart you will free us! Beware the guards! Free us!

speaker: Bayek
en: Those ragged voices. Those must be the last of the farmers that they've imprisoned.

speaker: Man 1
en: May Iset and Horus and Serapis and Anubis and...

speaker: Man 2
en: Hurry, fool! Thank them later!

speaker: Bayek
en: Does anyone know Iuseneb?

speaker: Iuseneb
en: What? That's me!

speaker: Bayek
en: Thank you, friend. While scouting the Roman forces, I foolishly fell into their hands. It's barbaric! They train elephants to battle with bloodlust, and force them to kill hapless prisoners to harden them!

speaker: Bayek
en: Can you make it back from here?

speaker: Iuseneb
en: Of course! I will find Apollodorus and tell him!

speaker: Reda
en: Bandits bad, caravan good. Get Reda back his stuff, you get paid. Easy enough, Medjay.

speaker: Reda
en: Medjay! Your help is needed. I might even owe you a favor after this.

speaker: Reda
en: Ah Bayek, I need your help with something.

speaker: Bayek
en: A Hidden One. We cannot leave his body to be treated like common refuse.

speaker: Bayek
en: I shall honor you, loyal servant to our creed.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let Horus guide you to the field of reeds. And Amun stretch his light across your ka.

speaker: Maqwat
en: I will stay with the Hidden One to see him off to the field of reeds. Thank you, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: Senu!?

speaker: Tahira
en: And what are you looking out for, hmmm?

speaker: Tahira
en: Take care of your eagle. Roman hunters capture every beast they find.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tahira? What are you...?

speaker: Tahira
en: It's nice to see you, too, Bayek. You look better.

speaker: Bayek
en: You knew I was in the region?

speaker: Tahira
en: I hoped. You leave a wake when you pass. Even I have heard stories of "Bayek of Siwa."

speaker: Bayek
en: Why are you so far out here?

speaker: Tahira
en: I'm defending this valley from becoming a Roman slaughterhouse. They capture our beasts, and they slaughter them in Rome before their gods.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hmm. I've heard the stories.

speaker: Tahira
en: I cannot stand against them alone. I prayed to Sobek, and he delivered... you. Come!

speaker: Bayek
en: Tahira, wait...! Hey!

speaker: Tahira
en: How did your path ever bring you this far?

speaker: Bayek
en: After we parted ways, I found myself caught by strong currents.

speaker: Tahira
en: Did you ever return to Siwa? To your role as Medjay?

speaker: Bayek
en: Briefly. It was no longer home. And you? How did you end up here?

speaker: Tahira
en: I took inspiration from you. Consider me a protector.

speaker: Bayek
en: Of what? There's no one out here.

speaker: Tahira
en: Of the green.

speaker: Bayek
en: What is this place?

speaker: Tahira
en: Shrine to Sobek. Very old. Very dangerous. Climb. It is not safe down here.

speaker: Bayek
en: Old ruins, old gods.

speaker: Tahira
en: Perhaps, but that doesn't mean it isn't without power. Shh. Watch.

speaker: Bayek
en: By Amun's horns!

speaker: Tahira
en: Sobek's child.

speaker: Tahira
en: Where is she? There's one missing! The Romans... Find me near the Roman camp.

speaker: Bayek
en: By Amun, she's fast.

speaker: Tahira
en: Find me when you are ready.

speaker: Tahira
en: Ah, you are eager! That is the Bayek I remember. The blasted Romans have taken her to their camp. With your help, we can free her.

speaker: Bayek
en: Well entrenched, I see.

speaker: Tahira
en: I told you. The Romans' hunger is insatiable. Sobek's daughter is inside.

speaker: Bayek
en: By Amun... that is a crocodile.

speaker: Tahira
en: Awesome, isn't she? What are you waiting for? Smash the cage!

speaker: Bayek
en: There, now, I'm not trying to harm you, Sobek knows. Or so I hope.

speaker: Tahira
en: Bayek, we must ensure she reaches the shrine safely!

speaker: Tahira
en: Thank you. With Sobek's favor, the Nile will flood again this year.

speaker: Bayek
en: You're welcome. Never thought I would think of crocodiles as romantic.

speaker: Tahira
en: Fearsome, but beautiful in their ferocity. See me at my home before you leave here, yes?

speaker: Bayek
en: All right, I will.

speaker: Tahira
en: Here, Bayek. The gods still have need for us.

speaker: Paanchi
en: Osorkon has been missing for two weeks. He is the shadow tasked with surveying the Quarry.

speaker: Bayek
en: Yet the shadow became lost.

speaker: Paanchi
en: It may be too late for Osorkon, he went to a merchant ship at the docks several days ago and that place is crawling with Romans. Would be a shame to lose him, his passion for the people and the Hidden Ones knew no bounds. I would die for him.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will find this Osorkon.

speaker: Bayek
en: These cages are small... were they for children? This boat has been ransacked.

speaker: Bayek
en: A broken shield of the Hidden Ones. Osorkon was here.

speaker: Bayek
en: Osorkon? Where are you?

speaker: Bayek
en: Poor child.

speaker: Bayek
en: These cages for children are atrocious.

speaker: Bayek
en: A merchant killed, and dead Romans? Someone who disposed of these Romans did so with great skill. It must have been a Hidden One.

speaker: Bayek
en: The merchant was robbed. Curious.

speaker: Bayek
en: Dear gods! Nabatean children sold into the quarry as slaves. These innocent souls are kept in an underground holding pen in the Quarry. I should go there.

speaker: Bayek
en: Osorkon must be held here.

speaker: Osorkon
en: My lips are sealed.

speaker: Roman Soldier
en: We will rip your lips off. Your eyes... your everything.

speaker: Osorkon
en: Unlike you myrmidons, the oath I take means something. Send me to the Duat! I will have Osiris rip me limb from limb before I tell you an iota of anything. Nothing works within me except the fire to destroy those who take food from workers, those neket iadets (pieces of shit) like you.

speaker: Roman Soldier
en: Enough! He obviously has important information, torture him for as long as it takes. Keep him alive.

speaker: Osorkon
en: My wife Zagura will avenge my death, she is a great warrior too.

speaker: Osorkon
en: I knew you would come! The mentor has come to save me!

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone has robbed this Roman warehouse. A brave thief.

speaker: Bayek
en: Chains used on these poor children. Gods!

speaker: Osorkon
en: Let's get out of here.

speaker: Osorkon
en: You must be the great Bayek. Understand this: I investigated the docks, and found a woman liberating the children on a slaver's barge.

speaker: Bayek
en: A liberator is behind the pillaging?

speaker: Osorkon
en: A Nabatean warrior known as Shaqilat. She hands out the spoils to the people—and strikes with incredible swiftness. I was following her but was captured by Romans. She has found safety with the children in a courtyard between the bureau and the quarry.

speaker: Shaqilat
en: Let your hearts be still children. I am your protector. The Sinai is your home.

speaker: Child 1
en: You are so brave Shaqilat.

speaker: Child 2
en: O great warrior, you are Iset!

speaker: Shaqilat
en: By Amun-Ra I will not let these centurions take you to be sold off like bags of grain.

speaker: Child 3
en: Please do not let them take us again!

speaker: Child 4
en: I cannot wait to eat a good meal.

speaker: Shaqilat
en: Soon my darlings. Soon.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are stealing for the workers in the quarry?

speaker: Shaqilat
en: If you wish to arrest me you will have to rip my heart out before I take chains on.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do not worry. But your ways may lead to Roman reprisal. You are trying to defend yet harm could come of your actions.

speaker: Shaqilat
en: Nek! (Shit!) I am not to blame for their oppression! I am a liberator!

speaker: Bayek
en: You beget oppression! Liberation is a subtle work of art, not simple petty theft! You cannot take freedom, you must create it.

speaker: Shaqilat
en: I know the shape of freedom. I lived it with my husband here in the Nabatea before he was crucified like a fly by Tacito.

speaker: Shaqilat
en: There they are.

speaker: Bayek
en: Now earn your reputation.

speaker: Shaqilat
en: I will show you how nothing stops me.

speaker: Roman Soldier 1
en: There is the so-called liberator!

speaker: Roman Soldier 1
en: She robbed our outpost, get her!

speaker: Shaqilat
en: For Nabatea!

speaker: Bayek
en: Well-struck, Shaqilat!

speaker: Shaqilat
en: Defend these children with me! You will not regret it! Curse you, Roman jackals!

speaker: Bayek
en: Where are you going?

speaker: Shaqilat
en: I'll stay no longer. I will draw the other Romans away from these innocents!

speaker: Bayek
en: There are no more.

speaker: Shaqilat
en: There will always be more...

speaker: Bayek
en: Not if you join us.

speaker: Shaqilat
en: I do not understand what you ask of me.

speaker: Bayek
en: You fight well, a warrior of your kind is rare. Follow our path and you will not regret it.

speaker: Shaqilat
en: I do not join cults.

speaker: Bayek
en: We are liberators, and do not abide by the rules of false oracles and tyrants. You are a chosen one.

speaker: Shaqilat
en: I work for good, I want to help heal our lands.

speaker: Bayek
en: Shaqilat, I am sure you have the ka of a Hidden One.

speaker: Shaqilat
en: But... How can I trust a stranger? I work alone to save my people, I only trust myself.

speaker: Bayek
en: We have the same values. You must only decide whether you apply your skills for the benefit of few, or all.

speaker: Shaqilat
en: Look me in the eyes and tell me there will be no more hate, no more war, no more men in chains.

speaker: Bayek
en: These are all broken by our creed.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your creed. And if I do chose to give myself to it, to believe it, what must I do?

speaker: Bayek
en: Jump.

speaker: Shaqilat
en: How do we proceed? I do not understand what you ask of me. I work for good, I want to help heal our lands. I will show you how nothing stops me.

speaker: Shaqilat
en: That was incredible, I thought I was going to die.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are reborn, as a Hidden One.

speaker: Shaqilat
en: How do we proceed?

speaker: Bayek
en: We have a bureau, and a ceremony celebrating your pledge.

speaker: Shaqilat
en: I will enter the shadows.

speaker: Bayek
en: Welcome to the brotherhood.

speaker: Man 1
en: Is that him?

speaker: Man 2
en: It could not be, could it? Oh, gods! It is!

speaker: Man 1
en: Quiet, he'll hear you! Don't look at him.

speaker: Nefertari
en: You're either very brave or very foolish, setting foot back here.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nefertari... isn't it? A thousand blessings are long overdue.

speaker: Woman
en: Bastard! Neket iadet!

speaker: Nefertari
en: That was Rudjek's wife. Did you expect anything less?

speaker: Nefertari
en: This way, Bayek – and bring along your thousand blessings. You will need them.

speaker: Bayek
en: I feel bad for her. But it had to be done.

speaker: Nefertari
en: You look well. Better than the last time I found you. Are you just... better... at killing now?

speaker: Bayek
en: Rudjek was only the beginning.

speaker: Nefertari
en: Yes, your hunt. The Heron.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where are you taking me?

speaker: Nefertari
en: To make amends with Anubis.

speaker: Bayek
en: Amends? I do not know what you're talking about.

speaker: Nefertari
en: Hmph! Of course. How could you? You left the moment you woke. You know all the natron for Egypt is collected here. We send it mostly to Memphis, to cover the bodies of the dead.

speaker: Man 1
en: Look at me. No, you're unwell.

speaker: Man 2
en: I am alright.

speaker: Man 1
en: You just spat up your meal and you can barely stand straight.

speaker: Nefertari
en: Natron has other uses, though. I could use it to disinfect a wound or wash the stains of blood off my hands, for example.

speaker: Nefertari
en: It looks better, Neb. I will have one of my aids bring something for the pain.

speaker: Man
en: And my brother?

speaker: Nefertari
en: Recovering. He needs rest.

speaker: Bayek
en: You do not need to remind me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why are so many of your people ailing?

speaker: Nefertari
en: Because Anubis is displeased. Ever since you left, the torches by his shrines have lost their flame. We are no longer protected.

speaker: Bayek
en: From what? The wrath of Anubis?

speaker: Nefertari
en: Whatever it is, we have suffered grave injuries trying to reignite them. Some have even vanished. It has become clear that Anubis demands your appeal, and yours alone.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'll ignite the torches and end this curse, or omen... or whatever it is.

speaker: Nefertari
en: You would do well to, if you ever hope to appease Anubis and gain my pardon.

speaker: Nefertari
en: Suphia, give some frankincense to the men at the pool, would you?

speaker: Nefertari
en: I don't need to tell you to be careful. There are three shrines. One to the south, one atop the natural well, and one inside the bent pyramid. You know your way to that one...

speaker: Bayek
en: One of the torches of Anubis should be here.

speaker: Bayek
en: This torch has fallen over. Where's the head?

speaker: Bayek
en: This fence is broken. Was there a struggle?

speaker: Bayek
en: There's blood here. Someone fell, or was pushed.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nefertari was not exaggerating. This one died trying to light the torch.

speaker: Bayek
en: There's the torch head. It must have fallen from the ledge when the torch was tipped over.

speaker: Bayek
en: Charms?

speaker: Bayek
en: This should do it. All I need to do now is to light it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Gatekeeper of the Duat. I honor your name.

speaker: Bayek
en: A shrine. One of the torches must be here.

speaker: Bayek
en: There's blood on these linens. Someone hung these.

speaker: Bayek
en: Oh, this rotting meat gives off an attractive stench. Is someone luring predators here?

speaker: Bayek
en: Charms of Anubis. Someone has put these here, but why?

speaker: Bayek
en: Gatekeeper of the Duat. I honor your name. That was no simple task. Are there other forces at work here?

speaker: Bayek
en: The bent tomb of Sneferu.

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone has been here recently...

speaker: Bayek
en: It's blocked. There must be some way through. The tracks here are fresh. There must be another way inside the tomb.

speaker: Bayek
en: Something must be behind here.

speaker: Bayek
en: It should be clear now.

speaker: Bayek
en: This room... This is where my quest began. Someone has taken great care of this chamber.

speaker: Bayek
en: More charms. What were they trying to achieve?

speaker: Bayek
en: Gatekeeper of the Duat. I honor your name. That is the last torch. I should return to Nefertari.

speaker: Nefertari
en: What news do you bring?

speaker: Bayek
en: The torches burn with a relentless flame.

speaker: Nefertari
en: Then I pray Anubis will grant us pardon.

speaker: Bayek
en: There were charms left beside each one. Does that mean anything to you?

speaker: Nefertari
en: Beside the torches?

speaker: Bayel
en: Most likely to ward off the omen.

speaker: Nefertari
en: I will keep my eyes open. In the meantime, some rebels nearby need treatment. I normally make the trips, but I am needed here. Suphia has offered to go in my place, but only if you escort her.

speaker: Bayek
en: It will be done.

speaker: Nefertari
en: Bayek... I hope this hunt of yours end soon, before you cannot return from what you have become.

speaker: Merkes
en: This beast will be my death! Gods save me from bandits and blasted camels! Faster! Run, you plodding beast! If they catch us, who knows what will be lost? And they will probably eat you!

speaker: Bandit 1
en: Do not let him escape!

speaker: Bandit 2
en: Try to cut him off!

speaker: Merkes
en: Oh, well, look at that! Good, good. That was a bit too close, hmm? Is that a Medjay badge? Fascinating. I thought they were all extinct. As skilled as I'd read.

speaker: Merkes
en: That was extraordinary! Well done. Who sent you? Was it Kition or Heraclides? They thought I couldn't handle myself out here, but we've shown them, haven't we?

speaker: Bayek
en: Have we? What are you doing out here?

speaker: Merkes
en: Are you joking, neb? We are searching for the lost vault of the great Sneferu, the founder of the golden age of the !

speaker: Bayek
en: And how are we doing that?

speaker: Merkes
en: Didn't they tell you anything before they sent you after me?

speaker: Bayek
en: Remind me.

speaker: Merkes
en: Acording to my research, Sneferu hid three artifacts in his pyramids. One in the Meidum, his first, and failed, pyramid. Another in the Bent, whose design he obviously modified after the Meidum's collapse. And one in his final masterpiece and tomb, the Shining Pyramid. I have one artifact, but those bandits stole another from me. You'll need to get it back for us!

speaker: Bayek
en: Where was this?

speaker: Merkes
en: They camp in the cliffs to the west of Memphis. You can find them by following the stream. Also, you'll need to find a way into the Shining Pyramid, to get the last artifact. I think there's an opening high up, but it's quite the climb. In my youth I could have done it, but...

speaker: Bayek
en: I will take a look. How many bandits were there?

speaker: Merkes
en: All of them, I think.

speaker: Bayek
en: What makes you think the third artefact is in the Shining Pyramid?

speaker: Merkes
en: Each of the three tombs held one, according to my findings. These pyramids were built by Pharaoh Sneferu during his reign, you see. He took what Imhotep had designed for Pharaoh Djoser, and improved upon it. Meidum was the first, but a design flaw led to a grave collapse. Then came the Bent. Its unique shape is due to an alteration that saved it from suffering the same fate as its brother. The Meidum and the Bent could not keep their secrets from me. Inside each, I found the artifacts indicated in Manetho's . You've read it, yes?

speaker: Bayek
en: Mmm.

speaker: Merkes
en: So you'll remember that the third is said to be contained within the Shining Pyramid, his masterpiece. Of course, it's also the pyramid that has stifled my progress.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Shining Pyramid?

speaker: Merkes
en: Yes. Sneferu, whose light shines eternal, lies within.

speaker: Bayek
en: Of course.

speaker: Merkes
en: I'll head back to camp to try to unravel the mystery. My camp is in the shadow of the last pyramid. Meet me there, at Sneferu's Tomb, when you've found the other artifacts.

speaker: Meidum Pyramid Artifact
en: A scaled replica of the Meidum Pyramid. This is one of the artifacts. Merkes believes this will help reveal the location of Sneferu's vault.

speaker: Bayek
en: This must be the artefact the bandits stole from Merkes. Strange thing.

speaker: Merkes
en: Do you have both artifacts yet? I'm still trying to decode some of Manetho's writings, but I'm sure we're close!

speaker: Shining Pyramid Artifact
en: A scaled replica of the Shining Pyramid. This is one of the artifacts Merkes believes will help reveal the location of Sneferu's vault.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hmm. This plain-looking artefact must have some hidden value if it was stored among such treasures. Time to find Merkes, and see what these three artifacts add up to.

speaker: Bayek
en: I've retrieved the other two artifacts.

speaker: Merkes
en: Ah hah! This confirms my theory! By Ra! That's it! The artifacts form a diagram, but a part is missing. There's no way to connect them. But there's a passage in the Aegyptiaca that says, "The path is clear atop the Shining tip." And the inscriptions on this artifact must mean the pyramidion on top of Sneferu's tomb, the Shining Pyramid. I'm sure the key to the mystery is up there. Why don't you just run up and take a look?

speaker: Bayek
en: What are we looking for, at the end of this?

speaker: Merke
en: The priceless treasures of Sneferu have been lost to the ages. We will be heroes when we recover them and bring them out into the light of day.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm no grave robber.

speaker: Merke
en: No, no, no, of course not. I promise you this will not disturb anyone's rest in the Field of Reeds.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hmm, I will climb up and see what I can find.

speaker: Bent Pyramid Artifact
en: A scaled replica of the Bent Pyramid. This is one of the artifacts Merkes believes will help reveal the location of Sneferu's vault.

speaker: Bayek
en: The top of the Tomb of Sneferu. There are strange slots here. Hmm. Maybe if I...

speaker: Bayek
en: These three artifacts fit perfectly into the slots of the capstone. It's a diagram... From here at the Shining Pyramid, it seems to indicate those ruins out east, That's where we will find the vault.

speaker: Merkes
en: And? What did you see? Was it as I said? Don't keep me in suspense. Did you find anything?

speaker: Bayek
en: Quite the view. The markers fit into place upon the capstone, and create a complete diagram.

speaker: Merkes
en: You are remarkable! And, does it explain the riddle in the histories? About where to find the vault?

speaker: Bayek
en: Mm-hmm. I suspect it meant something to the east of us. I could make out what looks like a ruined temple, now.

speaker: Merkes
en: Follow me! I'll get us there!

speaker: Bayek
en: Do not rush into trouble again.

speaker: Merkes
en: With you at my side? Never!

speaker: Bayek
en: How did you cross paths with the bandits, earlier?

speaker: Merkes
en: Hmmm? Oh, I enlisted their help to find the missing artifacts.

speaker: Bayek
en: What? You mean you hired them?

speaker: Merkes
en: Well, their leader, Bellosh, claimed he knew the desert better than anyone. I didn't think they would turn on me. I didn't know they were those kinds of bandits.

speaker: Bayek
en: There are no other kinds of bandits. They all pillage and kill for coin.

speaker: Merkes
en: Yes, they seemed rather intent on both, having stolen one artifact from me and then trying to kill me for the other.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are a hazard to yourself.

speaker: Merkes
en: I've been told that before.

speaker: Merkes
en: Here we are! The entrance will be hidden, of course. By Ra, I wonder what we'll find.

speaker: Bayek
en: These statues have survived the ages. They look exactly like what was described in the writings of Manetho... fascinating. But who do they mean?

speaker: Bayek
en: What do you see, hmmm?

speaker: Merkes
en: The remains of this statue, the watcher, is supposed to be looking towards the entrance. But where is it now?

speaker: Bayek
en: The ground seems soft here. Let's see what is beneath the sand.

speaker: Merkes
en: One last deadly obstacle.

speaker: Merkes
en: I told you there was nothing to worry about. Come along. This way, Uh, you first. We are the first to set foot here in more than two thousand years! The treasures that must be here...

speaker: Merkes
en: Nothing to worry about. You did exactly as I would have told you, if you hadn't acted so quickly. I hope we aren't angering Wadjet.

speaker: Merkes
en: Oh, oh my! By Ra... all that is divine beauty. Do your eyes see what mine see?

speaker: Bayek
en: This room has been perfectly preserved.

speaker: Merkes
en: Untouched since Sneferu's reign!

speaker: Bayek
en: A perfectly preserved pyramidion. A relic of the gods, and the origin of all good things. The first rays of Ra would fall upon it, and light the way for the bird, who flew over the waters of Nun.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is this it? It is mostly filled with old scrolls... not much gold.

speaker: Merkes
en: Such treasure! Look at all this history! Kition and Heraclides will be in awe. I'll be famous. We'll be famous!

speaker: Bayek
en: Glad I could help.

speaker: Merkes
en: Once I've catalogued what we've discovered, I'll cart it back to the Library of Alexandria so it can be studied and preserved for the ages.

speaker: Merkes
en: Once it is safely in the Library, it will be protected from time and the elements. Hmm. I should send for Roussis to help me cart all of these documents back to Alexandria. So many lost wonders contained within... How to get all this back to Alexandria? Now we can finally remember how Imhotep and Sneferu built the pyramids.

speaker: Woman
en: The ka is gone! So few Egyptians are coming to temple! Where are my seni (friend) and senu (companion)!

speaker: Bayek
en: Great Serapis. Are you as merciful as Amun?

speaker: Lysander
en: Welcome, brother.

speaker: Bayek
en: Thank you, Priest.

speaker: Lysander
en: It is good to see Egyptians come back. Since my drummer was jailed, it has been... quiet.

speaker: Bayek
en: The silence is striking.

speaker: Lysander
en: A tanner jailed my drummer. Accused him of stealing a precious Nubian lion skin from the dye vats. Poor soul even worked for him. Tragic. He is an honest man.

speaker: Bayek
en: Leave this in my hands, Priest.

speaker: Lysander
en: Medjay! My drummer is in the Kibotos arsenal nearest the library. Serapis walk with you.

speaker: Bayek
en: And you, Priest.

speaker: Drummer
