en: You! Yeah, big guy! You have got the look of a man who can heft things. Namely... me. And my injured foot.

speaker: Bayek
en: I come on the priest's request, drummer.

speaker: Drummer
en: Then get me out of here, Medjay!

speaker: Bayek
en: I cannot help but think you seem cheerful for a man unable to walk.

speaker: Drummer
en: You jest, surely? This is the best day of my life. My foot will cost that tanner!

speaker: Bayek
en: Surely your health is worth more than that.

speaker: Drummer
en: If I can prove nothing, you would be correct. That is where you come in, friend.

speaker: Bayek
en: What is it you think I can do?

speaker: Drummer
en: Find the fools who stole it, of course. Return that skin and clear my name!

speaker: Bayek
en: Who stole the lion skin?

speaker: Drummer
en: I turned away from the lion skin for a moment and a bandit nabbed it, and ran away. I lost him in the crowd. It happened in the Egyptian district. The guards, of course, blamed me. Though life, being an Egyptian in Alexandria.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will find them, then.

speaker: Drummer
en: Go on! Get that skin! I will be fine. Just need to rest my leg. Then I will go and meet the Priest. You clear my name!

speaker: Bandit 1
en: Tanner lied about that skin. It is almost worthless.

speaker: Bandit 2
en: You know the Greeks. Easy enough work, stealing from him. Skins for days.

speaker: Bandit 3
en: This is better than fishing. I've yet to get the smell of crocodile out of my nose.

speaker: Bandit 2
en: Wonder what skin that tanner will destroy next?

speaker: Bandit 3
en: His own. His face is leather already. Would only improve it.

speaker: Bandit 2
en: Look! This one has a Medjay badge! A dead breed should stay dead.

speaker: Bandit 1
en: You think you're tough? I'll show you tough!

speaker: Bandit 3
en: Look at that sword! I'll take that from you, big man. Wouldn't want you to get hurt playing with it. Take him out!

speaker: Bandit 2
en: We're not doing anything wrong, Medjay! I swear on Serapis himself.

speaker: Bandit 1
en: Why attack us? We've done nothing wrong. Well, mostly nothing wrong.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is the skin? Oh, this poor beast. Blue is no color for a lion.

speaker: Tanner
en: This man is a thief!

speaker: Lysander
en: Peace, Theon! He claims to not have stolen a thing. Do you wish Serapis displeased with you?

speaker: Theon
en: No...

speaker: Drummer
en: I am going to sue you for my broken leg you neket iadet (piece of shit).

speaker: Lysander
en: That is not helping.

speaker: Theon
en: I knew you Egyptians were all alike! This is what I get for hiring you! Thieves all!

speaker: Lysander
en: I have my best man on this. We will fix it.

speaker: Theon
en: I'm the wronged party here! My skin was stolen.

speaker: Bayek
en: And if you want it back, you'll pay him for his suffering. And make amends by kneeling to Serapis.

speaker: Theon
en: This is your answer, Priest? Extortion? Fine.

speaker: Lysander
en: I fear Serapis and I have a long road ahead of us. Blessings on your journey, brother.

speaker: Rai
en: The bandits will be here soon, brothers. We'll make our final stand. Give them a few scars before they slit our throats.

speaker: Sayyum
en: We're with you, Rai. We're all tired of running.

speaker: Rai
en: Our blood oath to this soil is unbreakable.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why are you hiding amongst these ruins?

speaker: Rai
en: A Medjay! The gods show mercy at last! My name is Rai, and this is what's left of my family. Bandits chased us from our farms. We have nowhere else to go.

speaker: Sayyum
en: We have nothing of value, yet they've pursued us for days across this wasteland!

speaker: Bayek
en: I have seen many bandits, they are cynical and callous.

speaker: Rai
en: They killed so many. My father, my son. Those here are all who remain of our village. The bandits will come again to finish us. Stand with us, Medjay. Help us get vengeance at least!

speaker: Bayek
en: Vengeance is my creed. I will help you. Tell me your plan.

speaker: Rai
en: There's a cliff not far from here. From there we'll be able to see the whole area, and plan our defense. Let's go.

speaker: Rai
en: This wasteland is perilous. If it's not bandits, its hyenas, or some other beast. Thank Ra my father taught me how to use a bow.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is a nice weapon. It has an unusual make.

speaker: Rai
en: When my father gave it to me it was taller than me by three hands. Boys teased me without mercy. Now it's a sadness to me. It only reminds me of him.

speaker: Rai
en: Did you see that, near the entrance? There are markings on the wall.

speaker: Bayek
en: I saw. There is a symbol of Horus, but it is changed slightly.

speaker: Rai
en: They look ancient. What is this place?

speaker: Bayek
en: You are fast along the rocks Rai!

speaker: Rai
en: I know these caverns. They are a natural temple. What is that necklace you wear?

speaker: Bayek
en: An old eagle skull.

speaker: Rai
en: I hope it brings us luck!

speaker: Rai
en: Gods, it's beautiful! I could stay here for hours...

speaker: Rai
en: Okay, enough of the view. We have to plan. Wherever the bandits come from, my brothers will be ready for them in the ruins. I'll stay up here and keep watch. When they show I'll give a signal. Then I'll attack from behind.

speaker: Bayek
en: I mean no disrespect Rai, but you are not soldiers. These bandits are killers. Your farmer friends may not walk away from this fight.

speaker: Rai
en: I know, Bayek. I'm scared out of my mind. If your family died in your arms, you would understand I cannot walk away now.

speaker: Bayek
en: Believe me, I do understand. And I will fight with you. For now I will head back to the others.

speaker: Rai
en: You should hurry. It's a long way back down the mountain.

speaker: Rai
en: Bayek! What... you are no eagle!

speaker: Rai
en: Are you alright?! That was crazy, but amazing!

speaker: Man
en: I thought the old Medjay were all gone. You give me hope again. Medjay, we cannot thank you enough for your help. You are sent from the gods. I was sure we were going to die, but now I have hope.

speaker: Sayyum
en: Medjay! You've returned!

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes. Your sister is staying on the cliff. She will signal when the bandits approach. These ruins are narrow. It could be worthwhile setting traps. Fire and oil, perhaps... do you have supplies?

speaker: Sayyum
en: Fire, a fine idea. Yes, we do. They're nearby.

speaker: Bayek
en: Good. Head up to that roof and keep watch. I will join you soon.

speaker: Bayek
en: I could use the oil jars to set traps for the bandits. Either way, I should speak to Rai's brother again when I am ready.

speaker: Man
en: With you we have a chance. These bandits are demons. But whether we live or die, I am thankful for your help.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am ready.

speaker: Sayyum
en: Then we wait... and pray.

speaker: Sayyum
en: There they are! The bandits are here!

speaker: Bandit 1
en: We see you, little mice. Think you can hide from us?

speaker: Bandit 2
en: Where's the woman! Hand over the bow. Maybe we'll let you live. Or maybe not! Haha!

speaker: Rai
en: We did it!

speaker: Sayyum
en: But there are more of them out there, and they will return. They were after father's bow!

speaker: Rai
en: What? All this just for an old bow? Gods, why?! It doesn't make sense! I would have given it to them!

speaker: Sayyum
en: Maybe we still can...

speaker: Bayek
en: They would have killed you anyway. There is only one way to stop men like this. I have to hunt down their leader.

speaker: Rai
en: I saw them come in from the Southeast. They could be camping in the foothills nearby.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then that is where I will begin my search.

speaker: Rai
en: Bayek, before you go... please, take the bow. We'll be safer if you have it. It was damaged in the fighting, and it only brings me sadness now, anyway.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am sure it still has some power. You honor me Rai.

speaker: Bayek
en: The bow is Egyptian, but older than anything I have seen. It's deceptively light, and the balance is perfect! The limbs are made partly of a strange black stone. It is familiar... I will look into it after I have dealt with this murderous leader!

speaker: Bandit
en: The others should have been back by now. They couldn't have lost the fight... could they? Against that bunch of dirt eating mud rakers? Haha, of course not! What am I thinking! They'll be back soon. Yeah, nothing to worry about.

speaker: Bayek
en: A letter from the bandit leader. He is collecting ancient weapons. He wanted this bow so badly he killed for it. But why? He's not here. They have a new hideout in a nearby tomb. They think themselves unfindable. Well, my friends, here I come.

speaker: Bayek
en: This must be the place. The bandit leader is in this tomb. Gods, this is ancient. There is something unusual about the stonework. The markings are similar to those of Rai's bow...

speaker: Bandit 1
en: Blackstone... great godly rock... I knew there was ancient treasure in these mountains! But this... I've never seen nothing like it!

speaker: Bandit 2
en: This is the domain of the gods themselves! We could sell it all back in Krokodilopolis! And never return to this wasteland! We've got a whole tomb full of Blackstone!

speaker: Bayek
en: Murderous, greedy neket iadet. He won't be troubling the farmers anymore. He was carrying shards of black stone, probably found in the tomb beyond. It is the same material used on Rai's bow.

speaker: Bayek
en: It fits. Should do the trick. Now it is a fine weapon.

speaker: Sayyum
en: Medjay! We heard you took care of the bandit leader for us. It is thanks to you that we can even begin thinking about rebuilding our lives.

speaker: Rai
en: My family and I are gathering supplies for a long journey ahead. It won't be easy making it out of this wasteland.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nothing is easy. Stay safe my friends.

speaker: Rai
en: Good bye Medjay.

speaker: Gupta
en: I will not betray the black land, despots!

speaker: Gupta
en: I am an Egyptian like yourself, Medjay. For the safety of Egypt please, we must escape.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you Gupta?

speaker: Gupta
en: Who sent you? Apollodorus? I would not have betrayed Egypt!

speaker: Bayek
en: You serve Apollodorus?

speaker: Gupta
en: I am part of his divine manipulation of the threads. A viper in the long grass of Cyrenaica. We are compromised. I know not how or by who, but that is how the Centurion found me. He has a list of spies.

speaker: Bayek
en: Not all men will stand up to torture as well as you.

speaker: Gupta
en: Find the Roman, see what information he has. He patrols the border towers.

speaker: Bayek
en: For Egypt.

speaker: Gupta
en: For a free Egypt.

speaker: Bayek
en: There is another spy, Khati at the East Roman Fort. I should rescue him.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Centurion's list led me to you, and another of your comrades at the fort.

speaker: Gupta
en: Apollodorus will want to know that we are compromised, and a Roman invasion of the black lands is inevitable. Thank you, Medjay. For Egypt.

speaker: Gupta
en: For a free Egypt. May our victories multiply.

speaker: Child
en: There he is! The Man with the Eagle! I must tell the Scarab's Shadows! I want the bounty!

speaker: Child
en: Oh no, leave me alone! I didn't do anything!

speaker: Bayek
en: Quiet down boy, be calm. Why are you saying such things?

speaker: Child
en: There are bounty hunters looking for a man with an eagle. I will receive gold if I tell them.

speaker: Bayek
en: What bounty hunters?

speaker: Child
en: They call themselves the Shadows of the Scarab.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Scarab? Nek (Shit). Little boy: I am not the man you are looking for. That is no eagle. It is a pigeon.

speaker: Child
en: It is a very brave pigeon. Wait, are you lying? I'm telling the bounty hunters!

speaker: Bayek
en: I should find these Shadows of the Scarab.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier
en: There's the old medjay! Come here!

speaker: Bayek
en: They know a lot about me.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier
en: Is that really Bayek? The old medjay? I'll put his heart on a platter. (laughs) You still dress the part, medjay scum!

speaker: Bayek
en: Who do you hunt for? Tell me or face your final breath!

speaker: Egyptian Soldier
en: See there! The medjay of old. It's Bayek! I will draw and quarter him.

speaker: Bayek
en: How do they know me? What brings these men after me?

speaker: Egyptian Soldier
en: I will bring your head to my master!

speaker: Bayek
en: A scroll. Their leader is camped in the southern desert of the Sinai. Signed, the Shadows of the Scarab. Who are these desert hunters?

speaker: Bayek
en: Blood, hm. A bloody battle took place here.

speaker: Bayek
en: Bandits buried in the shimmering sands. Hm. Just like the Scarab.

speaker: Bayek
en: These bodies buried in the desert remind me of Taharqa. His influence still lingers?

speaker: Bayek
en: This is not a typical bandit camp.

speaker: Bayek
en: A statue of Sekhmet? Goddess of Vengeance? So this is where the Shadows nest? Show yourself!

speaker: Bayek
en: Hmm. There is no one here.

speaker: Bayek
en: A scroll dedicated to the Shadows of the Scarab... They were hunting me?

speaker: Bayek
en: The trail is fresh.

speaker: Bayek
en: Footprints. What is that further in the desert?

speaker: Bayek
en: Kawab.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am not your enemy, Kawab. We do not need to do this.

speaker: Kawab
en: For the great Taharqa! Forever the ruler of Letopolis!

speaker: Bayek
en: Taharqa's little boy has grown up.

speaker: Kawab
en: And you, medjay, have aged poorly.

speaker: Bayek
en: You have come to defend Taharqa's honor but you forget, he never had any!

speaker: Kawab
en: My father was the great steward of Letopolis.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is foolish! You are not the same as your father!

speaker: Kawab
en: For his honor.

speaker: Kawab
en: No! No!!! Cursed, my family is cursed to die at your hands, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your father did, but you don't have to. You are innocent.

speaker: Kawab
en: There is only darkness.

speaker: Bayek
en: You fight well, you have bred a fine group of warriors with your Shadows of the Scarab.

speaker: Bayek
en: Still winning?

speaker: Kawab
en: Just kill me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Kawab, do not make the same mistakes your father did.

speaker: Kawab
en: What other option do I have?

speaker: Kawab
en: I've tracked you as soon I could ride a horse and kill someone with a blade. Don't try to use your ideas to change my mind.

speaker: Bayek
en: I can tell you that killing me will bring you no redemption.

speaker: Kawab
en: Be done with me. Vanish me. My existence was a mistake anyways.

speaker: Bayek
en: I want to show you something. Come with me, Kawab.

speaker: Kawab
en: Where? Just allow me to join my father.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your father cut your grandfather's tongue out, he oppressed your people. Family is not always our chosen and true brotherhood.

speaker: Kawab
en: He was revered as a hero as well, and a leader.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do not be swayed by people's gossip.

speaker: Kawab
en: It is true that I never wanted to kill. I was driven to.

speaker: Bayek
en: I was driven that way once also, without sense though, doing misdeeds against the gods, yet Ma'at taught me a lesson.

speaker: Kawab
en: I am nothing if I do not honor my father!

speaker: Bayek
en: Then ask him why he supported child-killers? You ask him why he betrayed you!

speaker: Kawab
en: What am I suppose to do? I have nothing else.

speaker: Bayek
en: You could join us. The Hidden Ones.

speaker: Kawab
en: Your gang of killers in the shadows?

speaker: Bayek
en: We are more than this. We have a code. I had a family before I had this group. I gave it all up because I did not have a choice.

speaker: Kawab
en: And if I do not join?

speaker: Bayek
en: There is only one other option.

speaker: Kawab
en: This desert is my graveyard.

speaker: Bayek
en: Or your redemption.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is what I wanted to show you. Endless deserts and mountains. Do you hear the wind on the sands? The desert calls us at times. Now, will you answer back or be taken by it?

speaker: Kawab
en: All my life has been revenge and killing. But I believe what you are saying. Give me strength Ma'at to transcend who I am, to become a shadow of power and cause.

speaker: Bayek
en: Abandon yourself, and you become one of us.

speaker: Kawab
en: Then it is so. I will renounce my name, my family. I will find a new one, as a liberator, along side you Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: Now you are a Hidden One.

speaker: Kawab
en: This brotherhood is strong, Bayek. Thank you for giving me a chance. Soon I will be headed to Judea. King Herod is causing problems for the people.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hotephres? What is going on?

speaker: Hotephres
en: My friend, you came. I am glad.

speaker: Bayek
en: Who is this? Where is Khenut?

speaker: Hotephres
en: My wife is... wherever she goes. Withdrawn and cold. This is... yesterday. She was just leaving.

speaker: Woman
en: You are a pig. I was bored anyway. Thanks for the wine.

speaker: Hotephres
en: Khenut is probably down at the lake. I will take you to her. Let me know when you are ready to go.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hotephres, what is this? What are you doing? You will lose everything.

speaker: Hotephres
en: I know, I know. I am useless to anyone right now.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then stop being useless. Be angry. Pick up your sword and start fighting.

speaker: Hotephres
en: I hung up my sword years ago. I only got involved because Apollodorus practically demanded it. He thought us all threatened by some grave conspiracy. Now Shadya's dead.

speaker: Bayek
en: Something big is happening. You were right to try to help.

speaker: Hotephres
en: I was stupid! I did not want to do it. Khenut insisted, said it was our duty. If I had not listened to her Shadya would still live.

speaker: Hotephres
en: She will be up ahead. We built a shrine by the water. Shadya loves the water. We feed the fish before supper. I mean... she did... we used to...

speaker: Bayek
en: Khenut. It is good to see you... Khenut?

speaker: Hotephres
en: This is how she is now.

speaker: Bayek
en: There's something that might help. In Siwa, we have a ritual to mark a loved one's passing. Would you mind?

speaker: Hotephres
en: Go ahead.

speaker: Bayek
en: The ritual requires something. I will return shortly.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have what I need.

speaker: Greek soldier
en: You'll do what you're told, you lazy shit. If you need more grain, grow more. It's not my problem.

speaker: Khenut
en: Captain!

speaker: Hotephres
en: Khenut, no! We can't.

speaker: Khenut
en: I know you're not extorting grain from this farmer. Because you'd know that would be violating several Egyptian laws. As officals of Faiyum, we both know it. Don't we?

speaker: Greek soldier
en: I will see you soon, Official.

speaker: Khenut
en: My husband, we must shake off our grief. We cannot let others suffer too. Not when we can stop it. You were a fighter once. It is time to fight again. You see yourself the corruption. There is no-one to protect the people. This is not over.

speaker: Greek soldier 1
en: Why did we not just kill that Egyptian cow?

speaker: Greek soldier 2
en: Oh, don't worry. The commander has got something special planned for her. I know her type, proud and defiant. Thinks she's untouchable. See how proud she is when we remove her tongue. We'll come back tonight and gut her quietly. What do you think? (Laughs)

speaker: Bayek
en: He will not be missed, but he spoke of a commander. Someone else is giving the orders. This is not over.

speaker: Bayek
en: An insignia! I do not recognize this. Maybe Hotephres knows more.

speaker: Hotephres
en: You live.

speaker: Bayek
en: They'd marked Khenut for death. Death found them first.

speaker: Hotephres
en: I envy them. Well, it had to be done. These soldiers do not seem to understand anything else.

speaker: Bayek
en: There's more. The captain was under orders. I found this insignia on him. Do you know it?

speaker: Hotephres
en: Yes. This is not good. It is from Fort Boubastos, to the east. Run by another malakia who thinks himself untouchable. Khenut was right. People will continue to suffer unless we act. Bayek, I am sorry to ask this. We need your help.

speaker: Bayek
en: You have it. There's something I must do first, though. I will return soon.

speaker: Khenut
en: Shadya, my lotus. No other will suffer as you did, I swear it. Goodbye, my little tadpole. Swim forever free.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is this the storied Crystal of Thoth?

speaker: Bayek
en: This shows the Crystal of Thoth on the pinnacle of the obelisk.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah! The mirror reflects the light from the crystal!

speaker: Bayek
en: I see. If I move the mirrors, I can direct the light.

speaker: Bayek
en: There, beneath the Tree of Life, a path has been revealed!

speaker: Bayek
en: I have never seen such swords. Made of the strongest iron and have not rusted in all the ages spent under this tree.

speaker: Bayek
en: This must be the treasure Ptahmose is searching for.

speaker: Nena
en: You have come, champion of Thoth.

speaker: Nena
en: Can you feel it? A monstrous shade is at the gate. It threatens to devour us.

speaker: Bayek
en: I feel... nothing.

speaker: Nena
en: A heart. Blackened, fetid, so loathsome and heavy. It must have deceived the scales.

speaker: Bayek
en: No... but the weighting cannot be cheated. All must stand before the judgement of Osiris.

speaker: Nena
en: The corruption comes here, it will defile the world, blight the wheat that makes our bread. Poison the wine we drink. You must stop it, Bayek of Siwa.

speaker: Bayek
en: How do you know my name?

speaker: Nena
en: Your Ren was whispered by Thoth, the knowing one. He breathed it in my ear.

speaker: Bayek
en: What is the god's will?

speaker: Nena
en: There is a ritual, dark and heretical. Unearthed in the time of the Son of the Aten and locked away in the Hall of Knowing. You must bring it to me.

speaker: Bayek
en: A woman's prayer to Iset to make her unfaithful husband return to her.

speaker: Bayek
en: Healing rituals and spells.

speaker: Bayek
en: Harvest prayers. A farmer asking the Pharaoh for bountiful crops.

speaker: Bayek
en: The forbidden scripts are behind, there must be another way in.

speaker: Bayek
en: The hymn to the Aten, the heresy of the Pharaoh's father.

speaker: Bayek
en: These texts, they reek of forbidden scriptures.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nefertiti's letters to Akhenaten about the founding of their .

speaker: Bayek
en: This is it... A ritual that perverts the weighing ceremony? By the gods, no...

speaker: Bayek
en: This is dark heka indeed, I hope the Oracle understands the pact she makes.

speaker: Nena
en: It is a perversion of the Book of Breathing, intended to annihilate a man's Ka.

speaker: Bayek
en: This cannot be Thoth's wish? To defy Anubis the counter of hearts?

speaker: Nena
en: It is true this ritual is forbidden, sacrilege. But we must not let the poison seep through the veil.

speaker: Bayek
en: What would you have me do?

speaker: Nena
en: See with my eyes.

speaker: Nena
en: We must hurry, it may already be too late.

speaker: Nena
en: Return to me where the Duat begins.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have the things for the ritual. But... is there no other way? To destroy a man's ka is...

speaker: Nena
en: Do you know how this one tricked Osiris? How they avoided the devourer ? By using the heart of an innocent, a child. I do not have to tell you what that means, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then let us begin.

speaker: Nena
en: The warriors of the Jackal will try to stop us. Do not let them.

speaker: Nena
en: I invoke you, Lord of Silence. Give us your heka and your nekhakha. I invoke you, Devourer, soul-sucker, punisher. For we seek to banish an unclean soul from this realm. May your name die. May your body decay. You shall be turned back from heaven and earth, your soul will never stand before Osiris. Thy soul destroyed, thy body destroyed, thy ka destroyed. Am-k ari her em reth xesef neter. Am-k ari her em reth xesef neter. Am-k ari her em reth xesef neter!

speaker: Nena
en: Anubis is angry! Still they come.

speaker: Nena
en: The Jackal understands! His guardians will not oppose us much longer.

speaker: Nena
en: May you enter the afterlife with your enemy.

speaker: Bayek
en: Septimius! No, you will not corrupt the field of reeds as you corrupted me. Apep, devourer come!

speaker: Nena
en: These demons, the souls you take? They will not deny you passage. Be at peace. Your heart is heavy no more.

speaker: Nena
en: Thank you living one, you have stopped a great injustice. Anubis will welcome you when your time comes. May you live forever beneath the imperishable stars.

speaker: Kashta
en: I will honor you properly, great Tahira. Lay you to rest with your blades on a bed of heron feathers.

speaker: Amunet
en: Tahira's death sends a clear message, we must eliminate Rufio. The brotherhood in Sinai is on the brink of extinction.

speaker: Bayek
en: Did he land at the Quarry?

speaker: Amunet
en: No, at Arsinoe. He is most likely lingering on his octareme.

speaker: Amunet
en: He is a master at guarding himself, and cutting true fear into the heart of a people.

speaker: Rufio
en: Where my lieutenants have failed I will not. I won't set foot on that cursed peninsula of savages, but they will bow to me.

speaker: Bayek
en: So is Rome chaos, or is the bringing peace?

speaker: Amunet
en: Rome is a cracked wall, run by a drunk, a , and the leader of the Order. Octavian scares us all. Rufio left from under my watch, and I caught word of what happened at the bureau. But there are good souls too in Rome. What of Memphis?

speaker: Bayek
en: The Hidden Ones are fine. But with no clear pharaoh, we are lost. I worry our temples have been sold away. And then, there is Cleopatra.

speaker: Amunet
en: She has brought prosperity to Alexandria. This I cannot deny. It is her lover's army that bothers us now. Marc Antony bears the same stench of tyranny that Caesar did.

speaker: Bayek
en: Rufio carries this same odor.

speaker: Amunet
en: Yes, to the Sinai. Which is why we must be the welcoming party...

speaker: Bayek
en: ...of fire and blood.

speaker: Amunet
en: We did not choose this path. It chose us.

speaker: Woman
en: Bayek! Bayek! Quick you must help us, the village is being attacked!

speaker: Bayek
en: By Amun, how do they know my name?

speaker: Woman
en: Gamilat speaks of the hero from Siwa, the great warrior with the eagle.

speaker: Roman Soldier
en: Dirty Nabateans! Do not stand in Rome's way!

speaker: Amunet
en: This is a bloody massacre.

speaker: Bayek
en: Defend the Nabateans!

speaker: Amunet
en: This is madness! Why are they killing civilians?

speaker: Bayek
en: Something is not right.

speaker: Amunet
en: That should be all of them, I will survey the area to be sure.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will head to Rufio's nest. The battle is done. Now I should kill the man who sent these soldiers, Rufio.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nek! (Shit!) This Rufio is mad. I must stop him before the sea is full of the dead. By the gods! They have suffered like poor Shadya.

speaker: Rufio
en: Where is my wine? Don't forget to feed my lion, if he is hungry, I will make you his meal! I cannot believe Tacito and Ampelius failed me. In Ptahmose's case I expected it, that Egyptian piece of shit.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let death shine on you. Sekhmet guide my arrows. Let Sobek fly like the many. Oh great Mut, work within me. Anubis awaits.' By Amun I fire! By the rays of Ra! By the power of Horus.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is for Tahira!

speaker: Rufio
en: You will not break me down!

speaker: Bayek
en: Shut your mouth, Rufio.

speaker: Rufio
en: You are not a man at all! Less than a fly! The Hidden Ones are dead!

speaker: Bayek
en: Your Order will crumble!

speaker: Rufio
en: Why have you broken my plans?

speaker: Bayek
en: The Hidden Ones will never allow the Order of Ancients room to breathe.

speaker: Rufio
en: So it is true, the Hidden Ones exist.

speaker: Bayek
en: We thrive.

speaker: Rufio
en: Strange that you want the same things we want: peace, order. And, yet our ideas will survive. You could kill me but you cannot kill us.

speaker: Rufio
en: Caesar built a strong order before he was stabbed in the back by your cowardly wife.

speaker: Bayek
en: Our power burns in the shadows.

speaker: Rufio
en: And we create those shadows.

speaker: Bayek
en: May the Hidden Ones bury you. Anubis awaits.

speaker: Bayek
en: Rufio is dead, I should tell Amunet, she will be pleased.

speaker: Bayek
en: Amosis?

speaker: Amosis
en: Yes? Fresh cockles and mussels today!

speaker: Bayek
en: My name is Bayek. I come from Harkhuf. He needs your help, as a friend of Jeska.

speaker: Amosis
en: I'm listening.

speaker: Bayek
en: Since Jeska was killed, Harkhuf needs a trusted agent to shepherd people out from under Sefetu's watch.

speaker: Amosis
en: Dead? You and Harkhuf are out of touch! Jeska's too tough to be held by Sefetu. She escaped the Firebrand!

speaker: Bayek
en: What? Where is she?

speaker: Amosis
en: Back on the river. She took a felucca loaded with supplies to the people she sheltered. She's taken a dangerous route to the southwest past the hippopotamuses to avoid Sefetu's eyes. If you follow the coast, you'll find her.

speaker: Jeska
en: Hiyah! Away, you blasted river pigs! If I had a sharp knife, I would skin you for the leather! May Serapis curse you and your offspring! Go to the crows! These bloated lake cows! Help me drive them off!

speaker: Jeska
en: What are you called?

speaker: Bayek
en: Bayek.

speaker: Jeska
en: Good to meet you, Bayek. I am Jeska.

speaker: Bayek
en: How did you end up here?

speaker: Jeska
en: I got lost, sailed the wrong way.

speaker: Bayek
en: I would not call avoiding Sefetu's patrols "the wrong way."

speaker: Jeska
en: What do you know of Sefetu?

speaker: Bayek
en: Harkhuf believed you were dead. But you escaped. He needs you back.

speaker: Jeska
en: Help me get these supplies to my village. There are many depending on me. And we will talk.

speaker: Jeska
en: How do you know Harkhuf?

speaker: Bayek
en: I was sent to him by a man to whom I am pledged. I believe we are working towards the same end.

speaker: Jeska
en: Well, Harkhuf is a great man, though Sais is a region of self-proclaimed great men. But Harkhuf has a good heart. He cares for his people and his city.

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes, he protects them from cowards like the Scarab and Sefetu.

speaker: Jeska
en: I have smuggled many families, like poor Wenis and her son, out of Sais to keep them safe. Those have tried to refuse Sefetu, he has burned to death.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are courageous to protect families that are not your blood.

speaker: Jeska
en: If you say. I hide them in my village until we can arrange a caravan to get them beyond the desert. Hence the food and medicine I bring.

speaker: Bayek
en: How did you survive?

speaker: Jeska
en: Sefetu's soldiers brought me to Fort Nikiou, where they burned and tortured me. But I spat in their faces. When they thought me broken, I-by the gods! Sefetu has come!

speaker: Jeska
en: No! No! Pentu! Anen! Wenis! Sefetu's men are burning everything!

speaker: Bayek
en: Stay here. Let me take care of them.

speaker: Bayek
en: It is done.

speaker: Jeska
en: So many lives turned to ash... Is anyone left?

speaker: Bayek
en: We need to be quick. More will come.

speaker: Jeska
en: Did you hear that?

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes...

speaker: Jeska
en: Pentu! Oh, by the gods, you are still alive! I will not leave you here.

speaker: Jeska
en: My cousins have a farm nearby. It may be untouched. Please, help me bring Pentu!

speaker: Bayek
en: Of course. I will take him.

speaker: Jeska
en: Ipi! Abana! Are you there?

speaker: Woman
en: By Serapis! Is it you, Jeska? We saw what happened. We thought you'd died!

speaker: Jeska
en: Pentu survived! He needs help.

speaker: Woman
en: Of course! Bring him here.

speaker: Jeska
en: Thank you for Pentu's life.

speaker: Bayek
en: I did nothing that you would not have done. He owes his life to you. This is not the end of it, however.

speaker: Jeska
en: No. Those dogs still hunt for their prick master. I will go to Harkhuf. We must find a way to peel Sefetu out of his shell, and deal with him.

speaker: Bayek
en: I cannot bring your people back from Duat. But I will help you avenge your village.

speaker: Sobek Priest
en: This evil boy has profaned the gods. His punishment will be an example, and an atonement. His hands for thievery, his tongue for lying.

speaker: Novice
en: But I am telling the truth!

speaker: Sobek Priest
en: Silence, boy! You will not speak! Stealing from a god is the gravest of blasphemy! No punishment is too great for such transgression! Sobek is swift to judge the profaners! His many teeth will devour the unworthy. This worthless boy is an example. He's a caution to all those who would blaspheme. Beware! Oathbreakers will have their just reward! No man is above Sobek's law. No priest is beyond retribution. Justice will be done. Let this example instruct you in obedience and faithfulness. This boy's punishment will teach us all piety. Examine your hearts. Judge yourselves before the gods judge you. Sobek is a healer to those who trust him. But his judgement is swift to those who blaspheme! Be vigilant. Pay your offerings. Avoid the fate of this despicable boy!

speaker: Bayek
en: Priest, what has the boy done to deserve this?

speaker: Sobek Priest
en: This has nothing to do with you. Back away. The boy will get what he deserves.

speaker: Novice
en: I serve Sobek! I serve Sobek! I am his slave!

speaker: Bayek
en: Boy! What are you accused of?

speaker: Novice
en: I was charged with ferrying two gold Sobeks to Krokodilopolis. Just out of port, my ship sank by the lighthouse. I almost drowned. The statues were lost. I didn't steal them!

speaker: Sobek Priest
en: Silence! And you – step back, (peasant)!

speaker: Bayek
en: Eh, do not threaten me, Neb! I am a Medjay. If the boy speaks the truth, I will find your gold Sobeks. If he lies, he is yours to deal with. I should check the big Octareme ship.

speaker: Bayek
en: A recent shipwreck. This could be it.

speaker: Bayek
en: A golden statue of Sobek, beautifully made. Just as the boy said it would be.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: That last dive was a good haul. The gold Sobek will bring a small fortune. That shipwreck might be hiding more.

speaker: Bayek
en: A golden statue of Sobek. It is beautiful. The boy tells the truth. I should return these gold Sobeks to that odious priest.

speaker: Bayek
en: Priest, I have your precious golden Sobeks. Your novice spoke the truth.

speaker: Sobek Priest
en: This useless boy has been constant trouble. Many more punishments await him, for his carelessness.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your priest's clothing is just a mask for cowardice. By the gods I hate masks.

speaker: Sobek Priest
en: This has nothing to do with you, (peasant)! Crawl back into your desert hole.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am Medjay you dishonorable dog!

speaker: Sobek Priest
en: I have the authority here, Medjay. Guards!

speaker: Bayek
en: Your mask of authority is removed. May you walk in the land of the Duat.

speaker: Novice
en: What do I do now? The Temple will not accept me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Sobek has left the fate of this gold with you. You can return to the temple, or to your family. The choice is yours.

speaker: Novice
en: May Sobek be with you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Whatever you do, do it honorably. Egypt needs priests who do not wear masks.

speaker: Woman
en: Hey! A bad omen! Sobek is sick!

speaker: Man
en: Petsuchos is angry! The image of Sobek shows the god's will! What will we do?

speaker: Sehetep
en: I shall heal Sobek. Continue to worship!

speaker: Woman
en: Did you see his eyes? Something is wrong. We're cursed!

speaker: Man
en: That's a bad omen for certain! Something awful is going to happen! O Sobek! Forgive us!

speaker: Woman
en: What can we do? Are our offerings not enough?

speaker: Man
en: I already gave half my grain and a hundred flowers! Would gold be better?

speaker: Bayek
en: I thought the sacred crocodiles of Krokodilopolis were tame.

speaker: Guardian
en: I... do not know what happened! Petsuchos has never attacked anyone before. His eyes turned red! Did you see?! Is Sobek displeased with us?

speaker: Bayek
en: Nek! (Shit!) Even the gods turn their backs on the people. Where is Petsuchos now?

speaker: Guardian
en: Our priest, Sehetep, took the god back to the pool inside the temple. I have never seen him like this!

speaker: Bayek
en: Something about this isn't right. I should take a look at the crocodile's enclosure.

speaker: Bayek
en: No sign of the priest. Petsuchos looks agitated. I should try to stay unnoticed.

speaker: Bayek
en: A carcass. It has been chewed but not eaten.

speaker: Bayek
en: A foul-smelling liquid. Argh, the stench burns my eyes. Argh, nek! (shit!)

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone was injured in the enclosure. They went up the staircase.

speaker: Bayek
en: A discarded priest robe, and it's covered in blood. Whoever was wearing this was badly injured. The blood trail leads outside.

speaker: Bayek
en: Mauled by crocodiles. What was he doing back here?

speaker: Bayek
en: This was the man who poisoned the crocodiles. He was taking orders from "Melina the Hibiscus". A pretty name for a killer. She's at the Neorion Naval Arsenal, to the South. Who dares touch a god of Egypt? I'll hunt down this blasphemer.

speaker: Bayek
en: That has got to be her. A purple dress. Just like the Hibiscus flower.

speaker: Melina the Hibiscus
en: Hmm. These deteriorated much faster than previous test subjects. Dilated pupils. Vomiting. Could it be the higher dosage of hemlock? Or hellebore? Both? Ha-ha. Of course it's both! Hmm. Crocodiles aren't dogs, you know. (humming to herself) Killing them is easy; not killing them is much harder. The really tricky part is making their eyes bleed. Now that took skill, and years of research.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: I don't know what you've got against dogs.

speaker: Melina the Hibiscus
en: What? I love them! As long as you feed them they trust you. They're perfect for testing. Just don't feed them flowers. That's how I got my name you know.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: I know. You poisoned your own dog by feeding it hibiscus flowers.

speaker: Melina the Hibiscus
en: It was an accident, actually. They looked so pretty, I thought they'd taste good. My other dogs... ok. They were research.

speaker: Bayek
en: A poisonous little woman. Talented, but twisted. Sehetep. He was the priest at the temple. Gods, what is it with priests and money? Sehetep again! His sticky fingers are everywhere. He's becoming a serious problem. The poison was just for show. At least the temple crocodiles are not going to die. I should tell the guardian.

speaker: Bayek
en: Guardian of Sobek, the sickness was not an omen from the gods. Your crocodiles were poisoned, but they'll recover.

speaker: Guardian
en: Poisoned? Are you sure? By whom? They will pay with their lives!

speaker: Bayek
en: Your own priest Sehetep was responsible. He is trying to increase offerings from your followers.

speaker: Guardian
en: What!? Sehetep is Sobek's right hand! He would never do this! What you are saying is blasphemy!

speaker: Bayek
en: Argh, you priests! Forever holding to your superstitions. You've been told the truth. The gods themselves will judge what you do with it.

speaker: Bayek
en: I should let Padiaset know about Sehetep. He is not going to like it.

speaker: Reda
en: Thieves, Medjay, they're everywhere. A pestilence. The leader of these thieves stole from me. I asked him to stop – he didn't. So now, why don't you pay him a visit? He'll have something on him that'll make the visit worth it.

speaker: Reda
en: I... I do not admit this easily, Bayek. But someone attacked me and stole my wares. I know where this thief is. Help me, Bayek? Deal with this nek (shit) so he doesn't attack anyone else. You can keep whatever you find.

speaker: Reda
en: Medjay! A friend of mine was recently attacked in the desert for her goods. The thief ran off, but I know where he is. Deal with him, eh? You get whatever that fool has on him.

speaker: Reda
en: My informant was beaten and his goods, mine really, taken from him. The parasite who did this is near. Do me a favour, Bayek? Deal with them slowly. Then take whatever you find as your reward.

speaker: Benipe
en: Bayek! Our Medjay! You're back!

speaker: Bayek
en: What happened to your blacksmith shop?

speaker: Benipe
en: Those neket iadet (piece of shit) soldiers. Ptolemy's captain saw me making a sword and accused me of being a rebel.

speaker: Bayek
en: He was not wrong.

speaker: Benipe
en: They confiscated my tools!

speaker: Bayek
en: Bastards. All of Siwa needs a blacksmith. Even me.

speaker: Benipe
en: I cannot help you Bayek. Not until I get my hammer and tongs back. And I have to get that ugly-as-Apep captain off my ass!

speaker: Bayek
en: Is this captain with the tools somewhere I can find him?

speaker: Benipe
en: At the foot of the hills west of here. Camp Shetjeh.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will get those tools back, and I will take care of the captain.

speaker: Bayek
en: Benipe said the tools are in Camp Shetjeh. And the captain who is behind this. He is in Camp Shetjeh as well.

speaker: Urgent
en: Dear Muthis, It is important that we keep our foothold in Siwa, or else they will have our heads. I love you with all of my ka; however, no amount of offerings or prayer can replace the will of a warrior. Through a battle we speak to the gods.

speaker: Bayek
en: Benipe's tools.

speaker: Bayek
en: That's for my friend.

speaker: Bayek
en: That's everything. Benipe will be pleased to hear it.

speaker: Benipe
en: Bayek! How did it go?

speaker: Bayek
en: Here are your tools. That captain won't ever come back here.

speaker: Bayek
en: Camp Shetjeh? I think I have already solved your problem, Benipe. And I didn't even know it!

speaker: Benipe
en: At last, I can reopen my shop. Many thanks.

speaker: Bayek
en: My pleasure.

speaker: Benipe
en: I found these weapons I had hidden from the soldiers. Please, choose one for yourself. Go ahead, choose one. They are all of equal value.

speaker: Benipe
en: That bow uses a special twine. It does not strike deep, but you can shoot very quickly. The shield is made with bronze and leather. Good protection—some weapons bounce right off it! It is not large, but that mace can crack a skull with the best of them! That spear is sharp and long. You can keep back and still hurt your enemies.

speaker: Bayek
en: Thank you, my friend.

speaker: Benipe
en: Come by my shop anytime, Bayek.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Thanks again for your help, those metrokoites (motherfuckers) will think twice before attacking my poets again. We will be able to spread our word, and stomp out those filthy untruths, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: The regime will fear you, Phanos.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: They do already! Why do you think my poets are accosted in the street?

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Bayek, it is finally time to celebrate with my muses.

speaker: Bayek
en: Shouldn't you stay to oversee your actors?

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: We must find time to work on the next play. Bayek, you must come.

speaker: Bayek
en: This celebration better rival my own events in Siwa.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Come, Bayek! This will be an excellent night. Let us hurry! You will be our guest of honor! I remember the celebrations we would have in my house in the better years. Ah, memories.

speaker: Bayek
en: They have become less so of late?

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: These Phylakitai suffocate our celebrations. They know nothing of poets. They think they know truth...

speaker: Bayek
en: You know it better?

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Of course. Truth comes from Chaos. Not order.

speaker: Bayek
en: Senu sees something.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Bah! There is nothing but Dionysius that way. Come, you should loosen your robes in readiness!

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Bayek! Gennadios' phylakitai. I should have known those louts would follow us.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier
en: This! This is the fool who puts out that traitorous gibberish! Phanos the Fool!

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Ah, my home finally. Prepare yourself, Bayek. This is a night you will not forget.

speaker: Bayek
en: It had better live up to the tales that Aya told!

speaker: Bayek
en: This is grand, Phanos.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Bayek. Come! Enter our very own Elysian Fields!

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Welcome to the land of truth, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: I can see that, perhaps, Aya left out some details out of her stories.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Indeed! This is the perfect place for artist and muse to meet! Drakon! Remember that wine is not only for you. Artemis! Do not throw fruit. This is not the time for your target practice. Come, Bayek!

speaker: Woman
en: Phanos! Your plays are getting better in age. They are well improved from your previous works.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Ever the critic, thank you Leda. And this... is it. Where the poets of Alexandria find respite

speaker: Bayek
en: Wait. Do you hear that?

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Gennadios! His men must have come after us.

speaker: Bayek
en: We will deal with this, Phanos. Come, bring your blade.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: I will fill my ink wells with the blood of those metrokoites.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: They come, Bayek!

speaker: Bayek
en: Let the gods indulge!

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: Gennadios sends his regards, Phanos! Your treasonous filth is cause for death.

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: Gennadios knows of your ways! You are a plague on Alexandria. Phanos! We will wipe your treasonous ass out of here!

speaker: Bayek
en: Are your people safe, Phanos?

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Metrokoites! They have slayed some of my muses. Drakon, my favourite poet, will live, thankfully.

speaker: Bayek
en: There must be a way to stop them permanently.

speaker: Phanos the Yoounger
en: Bayek, we are blood poets now. This is our chance to bring people to our cause!

speaker: Bayek
en: Whatever it takes to defend freedom.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Give me some time, I will talk to my people, find their strongholds.

speaker: Taimhotep
en: (How loved you are in your house of life, Your inner shrine of being! You little seed, Sprouting with the absence of the flood That follows the moon. Your ka endures, My strength feeds your joy, Your heart's stir directs me on the path. I am she who wills the shape of your breath, Who sings your name into life.)

speaker: Bayek
en: Why do you weep? Your curse is lifted.

speaker: Taimhotep
en: You have lost a child, so you should understand that a mother's fear never ends.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nor does a father's rage.

speaker: Taimhotep
en: Fear and rage are fair replies to life's fragility. Please, leave me to my tears.

speaker: Mara
en: Neb, if you will follow me? We must give her privacy.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is there anything I can do to ease her?

speaker: Mara
en: Hmm. She has found a ritual of protection in an ancient scroll. Only a few ingredients remain to be

speaker: Bayek
en: I'll find them.

speaker: Mara
en: Wait, neb! An impatient soul is a troubled one. My lady needs parts from fresh-killed sacred birds. And would you kindly bring a fertility talisman in blue faience? There is a shop south of the temple basin where such items may be found.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will meet you on the road to the pyramids afterwards.

speaker: Maid
en: May you prosper.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will get the ritual item first, and then hunt down the birds.

speaker: Bayek
en: An abandoned tomb? The maidservant said there was a shop here. Strange place for a shop.

speaker: Owner
en: Ah, neb! Welcome to my humble shop. Seeking magical runes? Statuettes of uncommon value? A Medjay! How surprising. I have not seen your kind in some time, Medjay.

speaker: Bayek
en: We are a rare breed. As are merchants who set up shop in a tomb.

speaker: Owner
en: My customers appreciate privacy.

speaker: Bayek
en: They do not seem to appreciate variety.

speaker: Owner
en: My customers know I can provide what they seek.

speaker: Bayek
en: I hope you can do the same for me. May I have a look around?

speaker: Owner
en: But of course! I'll leave you to browse. Excuse me, but I have some business to attend to. I'll be back soon.

speaker: Bayek
en: An inventory. The talisman in blue faience is listed here.

speaker: Bayek
en: I should keep looking around.

speaker: Bayek
en: "And in the second chamber lie the worldly goods of Horapollo and Shesh, to protect them and provide them sustenance." The message is incomplete. I wonder what the rest of it says.

speaker: Owner
en: Seeking magical runes? Statuettes of uncommon value?

speaker: Bayek
en: Nothing of value in this room. Why would the merchant sell such cheap goods here? She is hiding something.

speaker: Bayek
en: The merchant did not want me to see this part of the shop. These goods must be stolen.

speaker: Bayek
en: A fertility talisman. Taimhotep will be pleased.

speaker: Bandits
en: You've browsed long enough, Medjay! You're scaring our customers!

speaker: Bayek
en: The maidservant said they want its tongue.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will take a few feathers for Taimhotep's ritual. That is all the items. Now to meet Taimhotep on the road to the pyramids.

speaker: Taimhotep
en: Bayek of Siwa! Come closer.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have found what you need, Taimhotep.

speaker: Taimhotep
en: The Seer spoke truth when he named you Deliverer. My ritual must be performed in the moon's shadow, at the base of the pyramid of Djoser. Will you guard me and my maid until it is done? There may be dangers on the road as well.

speaker: Bayek
en: Gladly.

speaker: Taimhotep
en: Then let us ride to the pyramid, and wait until the night unfurls in splendor.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is uncertain country. Why not bring more guards?

speaker: Taimhotep
en: My ritual must remain private.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is that also why we travel off the main road?

speaker: Taimhotep
en: Yes. It is less safe, but more secret. The lack of a son lowers my husband in the esteem of the people. And if they knew of the babes I have lost, his ability to compel the gods would be called into question. There are whispers against him already. My troubles bring shame to him, and to me.

speaker: Mara
en: Nebet, it is not your fault

speaker: Taimhotep
en: Hush, Mara. I know you mean to be kind, but the scrolls are clear. The woman is the carrier of the child's sex.

speaker: Mara
en: I do not believe that, nebet.

speaker: Taimhotep
en: Mara... we have had this conversation before. Let's be quiet now, in case our voices carry to unfriendly ears.

speaker: Bayek
en: Good idea.

speaker: Taimhotep
en: We are here.

speaker: Bayek
en: My sword stands between your ritual and any who threaten it.

speaker: Mara
en: Ptah's blessing on you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Every morning of my childhood, my father and I spoke the Prayer of the Medjay, a promise to those in need. "I am a Medjay. I am a feather in the eagle's wing... a living dagger, plunged from the sky into the heart of chaos. I am a truth unknown... a scabbard unfilled... a son of the Nile... and a defender of the people. You cannot kill me, for I walk among the dead. Come forth by day, and I will guide you home." My son should have learned this prayer from me.

speaker: Bayek
en: This messenger was tortured by the bandits.

speaker: Bayek
en: A touching letter. Hapti and Merope, lovers torn apart by oppression. Reminds me of Aya and myself. Poor Hapti, I should look into this, he could be in trouble. He should be easy to find with a tattoo.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is a massacre! What in the gods happened here?

speaker: Bayek
en: They killed them and then left them here to rot.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is the tattoo of Ankh. Poor Hapti... But there's no bracelet on him. His lover has no idea he is dead. This sickens me. I must put to rest his ka and return the bracelet.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hapti's wife will want this as a keepsake.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you Hapti's beloved?

speaker: Merope
en: I know why you're here, Medjay. He's dead isn't he? Hapti?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am sorry. There was a rebellion at the quarry, he...

speaker: Merope
en: No, I don't want to know. He was always so hotheaded. How could he leave us this way?

speaker: Bayek
en: I found his bracelet, he meant for you to have it.

speaker: Merope
en: What good is a bracelet? My child will grow up without a father. Thank you for telling me, you're a good man. But please, leave me alone to my grief. I'm just another woman the Romans have made a widow. This is the war no one speaks of.

speaker: Bayek
en: A scene of death. I should investigate.

speaker: Bayek
en: Scraps of a message. There's too much missing.

speaker: Bayek
en: Was this some terrible ceremony? There is so much blood, as if some butchery occurred here. But the elements have eroded many of the signs.

speaker: Bayek
en: Sekhmet, the goddess of hunters. But there are scratches here, above the statue's stomach. What does it represent?

speaker: Bayek
en: Scraps of blood and flesh. There was a body here, but crocodiles must have devoured it.

speaker: Bayek
en: The lid of a sarcophagus? There was a symbol here, but it is too damaged for me to make out. Troubling. If I had more information, I might understand this better. But as he was eaten by a crocodile... I'll keep an eye out for anything else so unusual.

speaker: Bayek
en: Indications of violence and bloodshed. I should investigate.

speaker: Bayek
en: Serapis, god of divine majesty and lord of the sun, someone has placed a mark upon you. The scorpion is the sign of Serqet.

speaker: Bayek
en: Curious, sinister writings.

speaker: Bayek
en: This poor man was half-eaten by crocodiles. But only after he died. Someone prepared him for burial, and cut out some of his sacred organs. His stomach at least, was removed.

speaker: Bayek
en: This symbol. A dedication to Serqet, the goddess of magic. The scorpion.

speaker: Bayek
en: Old blood stains this table. I think the body was prepared here. But crudely. This is no fine, skilled work.

speaker: Bayek
en: These deaths seem like some kind of perverse ritual against the gods. Who, or what, is driving it?

speaker: Bayek
en: What happened here? Omens of death.

speaker: Bayek
en: Looks like the pilot got away, but left embalming tools.

speaker: Bayek
en: A statue of Sobek, lord of the Nile. But he's contained within a symbol that invokes Serqet, the scorpion goddess of magic.

speaker: Bayek
en: They must have brought the sarcophagus by felucca. Pretty remote place for this. Some of those marks on the body look like the sacred organs were removed. At least the lungs are gone.

speaker: Bayek
en: Dark and foreboding invocations.

speaker: Bayek
en: These deaths are a harrowing journey into madness. What could the perpetrators hope to gain by invoking the goddess of magic?

speaker: Bayek
en: Blood on the water. Omens in the sky.

speaker: Bayek
en: This perverse poetry celebrates chaos. It inverts all that is divine and just.

speaker: Bayek
en: I suspect the sarcophagus was transported by cart. It is inscribed with the mark of Serqet, the scorpion goddess. But where is the body?

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone came here with a heavily laden cart. And left the same way, though the second track looks lighter.

speaker: Bayek
en: Poor man. You did not deserve to be dragged underwater by these hippos. And it appears you were prepared for the afterlife by a clumsy butcher with no thumbs. Where is your liver? This happened recently, and the cart may not have traveled far. There may be more to this mystery nearby. Those responsible should not be allowed to do this again.

speaker: Man
en: I wonder if olive trees can grow around here.

speaker: Woman
en: I don't know...

speaker: Man
en: Could be a great business. Plant an orchard across the river. Press the oil. Sell it up and down the Nile. Just like the olive trees back in Cyrene.

speaker: Woman
en: This is not Cyrene. Not everything from there is better. I like my sesame oil better. Besides, the area you are talking about? It's... not safe. Cursed maybe. My sister was gathering herbs near there last month and told me she heard weird singing in the middle of the night.

speaker: Bayek
en: Sarcophagi inscribed with the mark of Serqet. How much death does she require?

speaker: Bayek
en: What is that sound... voices? Ghosts? Demons?

speaker: Bayek
en: I need to find the source of the chanting.

speaker: Bayek
en: The mysterious killings have led here. This symbol is old. This place is from a long time lost.

speaker: Prophet of Serqet
en: What is this insolence? Who dares to intrude upon our most sacred work?

speaker: Bayek
en: Sacred? A trail of death led me here. This cavern reeks of the profane. Are you the bloody hand responsible?

speaker: Prophet of Serqet
en: The goddess Serqet is she who tightens the throat, and the one who lets us breathe. I do her will, I am her sting. All of the souls were chosen from lesser faiths. But we study their organs, and read the signs. Soon we will know Serqet's secrets, and become immortal.

speaker: Bayek
en: This was your last chance to win the goddess's favor. Let's test your immortality, shall we?

speaker: Bayek
en: I arrived too late to save this one. You will be the last victim of this cursed ritual.

speaker: Bayek
en: The ravings of a madman.

speaker: Bayek
en: Profane ravings to the gods.

speaker: Tjepu
en: Tefibi! Tefibi! When I get my hands on that boy he will pray that Osiris had taken him! Have you seen my idiot son? No? If you see him send him on my way. I will... buy whatever you have. Even if it is rancid. Tefibi!

speaker: Tjepu
en: Medjay! Thank the gods! I have not seen one of your kind in many moons.

speaker: Bayek
en: What troubles you, little mother?

speaker: Tjepu
en: My son, Tefibi. The boy is mad, always running off. He wishes to be some sort of thinker, Set take him! He has taken to searching for a cave near the beach, he should have been back by now.

speaker: Bayek
en: If he is lost, I will find him.

speaker: Tjepi
en: Thank you, Medjay

speaker: Bayek
en: This looks to be where she claimed Tefibi was.

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone's clothing. Torn.

speaker: Bayek
en: His wounds bled out in the water. He must have swam away.

speaker: Bayek
en: The blood leads around the lighthouse. I wonder...

speaker: Bayek
en: The blood trail leads to this door. I must prepare myself.

speaker: Tefibi
en: Ah!

speaker: Bayek
en: Tefibi? Your mother sent me to find you.

speaker: Tefibi
en: Well, that's good. I would have hurt you otherwise. With my mind.

speaker: Bayek
en: I doubt it little man.

speaker: Tefibi
en: Okay please help me up.

speaker: Tefibi
en: Whoa. Feeling a bit... dizzy. I think I lost a lot of blood.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then it is time we get you back to your mother.

speaker: Tefibi
en: She will be cross. Ah, fine. Lead on. I have enough strength to leave.

speaker: Tefibi
en: Mother sent a warrior to protect me. A philosopher does need a guard.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am not your guard. I am helping your mother.

speaker: Tefibi
en: Your badge. The eye of Horus?

speaker: Bayek
en: It is my Medjay badge.

speaker: Tefibi
en: Medjay? Ahhhhhh. . Weren't they killed by the Ptolemies?

speaker: Bayek
en: They forgot one.

speaker: Tefibi
en: Would you let me write your story? The last Medjay would be a fantastic tale.

speaker: Bayek
en: Well, what kind of story would you tell, Tefibi?

speaker: Tefibi
en: I know! A fable! One to put even Aesopica to shame! I will make you a camel, I think.

speaker: Bayek
en: I do not think I would like to be a camel.

speaker: Tefibi
en: A shame that. Maybe an eagle? How about a cow?

speaker: Bayek
en: Perhaps it is best to continue on from here in silence.

speaker: Tefibi
en: Ah. So be it.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: There! Get him. He robbed us!

speaker: Bayek
en: You stole from them?

speaker: Tefibi
en: Defend my free will warrior!

speaker: Bayek
en: I will deal with them.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: There! Get that map-thief!

speaker: Soldier 3
en: There's the rat that stole from us! Get that thief! Get back here, you gutless snake!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: The Phylakitai knows what you've done, thief! We will not let that pass!

speaker: Bayek
en: There. That should be all of them.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tefibi did you leave anything else out of your adventure? Say a crate of drachmas?

speaker: Tefibi
en: You wound me, Medjay! I am in search of knowledge. And a drachma or two, but never in theft!

speaker: Bayek
en: It looks like there are no others coming, Tefibi. Return to your mother and your studies.

speaker: Tefibi
en: Come and see me anytime in Alexandria, Medjay! I will be a great philosopher, just you wait.

speaker: Bayek
en: I... look forward to it, Tefibi.

speaker: Aya
en: So, you stand with Septimius now! And we are banned from the palace?!

speaker: Apollodorus
en: I do not begrudge the venom in your eyes. But listen for a moment.

speaker: Aya
en: Speak. Quickly. Or you will find yourself at the wrong end of my blade.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Your services are no longer needed. Cleopatra has granted you gold. I am sorry, Aya.

speaker: Bayek
en: Sorry? We gave her everything. We gave her the damned crown. And she stands next to him?

speaker: Aya
en: And where is justice for us? Septimius was supposed to be judged by Rome! Is Caesar protecting the Order?

speaker: Apollodorus
en: There are compromises to make a Queen of Cleopatra.

speaker: Bayek
en: The man who killed our son is now your ally! We are going to do whatever it takes to kill him, you realize?

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Caesar blamed you for the death of Ptolemy XIII. A Pharaoh, a God, Bayek, I cannot change this.

speaker: Aya
en: Be damned what Caesar thinks. It is with Cleopatra that I made the pact.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Give me time, Aya. I will ease this for us. Until then, I beg you, be careful. Not everything is as it seems.

speaker: Aya
en: Traitor.

speaker: Phanos
en: With all my words... I have nothing to say now.

speaker: Tahira
en: Cleopatra has been poisoned by Rome, and we by her treachery. We will burn with Egypt.

speaker: Pasherenpath
en: The Order is stronger now, they have Rome!

speaker: Bayek
en: Hold on! Hold on!

speaker: Bayek
en: I was wrong.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am responsible. When my boy died, I fought back, with rage and anger, but this only made them stronger.

speaker: Bayek
en: We are all different, but we fought together to put Cleopatra on the throne. This was a mistake, my friends, but at least it brought us together.

speaker: Bayek
en: Now our enemies are hidden behind crowns, working in the shadows of Kings and Queens. Who are the ones that work in the shadows for the people? We are. Something has come of all of this. And it starts right now. We must continue the fight, and defend the free will of the people. And no matter how small, our brotherhood is the only hope and our kingdom needs no crowns. What we believe in, our values, our creed, will unify us. And I promise that for all the sons of Egypt, I will be the father I was not that day in Siwa.

speaker: Bayek
en: To the brotherhood!

speaker: All
en: The brotherhood!

speaker: Aya
en: You were right. I trusted the wrong goddess. There is a question that yet lingers. Septimius. He took Alexander's Staff of Eden. Why?

speaker: Bayek
en: Indeed. He and Flavius had too much interest in Alexander's tomb. We start there.

speaker: Aya
en: I will destroy Cleopatra for what she has done.

speaker: Bayek
en: We must focus on the issue at hand.

speaker: Aya
en: What is left, Bayek? Tell me one thing left for us?

speaker: Bayek
en: Siwa. The rest of our land. We cannot stop now, Aya. We have yet to find Khemu's killer.

speaker: Aya
en: Yes. We will not falter there.

speaker: Bayek
en: Guards! Ahead!

speaker: Aya
en: Another pile of bodies will prove our point.

speaker: Bayek
en: It has been too long since we were together for longer than a few days.

speaker: Aya
en: Has it? It seems but moments.

speaker: Bayek
en: Aya, it is not easy, this path we walk.

speaker: Aya
en: Only if you look at it as days and not goals, Bayek. Come. We must hurry.

speaker: Aya
en: There are guards here...

speaker: Bayek
en: There is something amiss with all of this. Something foul.

speaker: Aya
en: These are all Romans. Caesar's men?

speaker: Aya
en: The guards will be looking for us here. We must be careful not to be seen.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: You think you can fell me with that? Ha!

speaker: Bayek
en: Apollodorus?

speaker: Aya
en: We must move quickly!

speaker: Soldier
en: You shouldn't have come here.

speaker: Bayek
en: At least we belong here.

speaker: Aya
en: Finally, someone we can kill.

speaker: Aya
en: Stop your flailing. You will live, fool.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Flavius was behind it all... I am sorry... Flavius killed your son. They were here. They took the orb from me. They... go to Siwa.

speaker: Bayek
en: Siwa?

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Bayek... Aya... Your people are in danger. Go... now.

speaker: Aya
en: Fare thee well, Apollodorus, to the house of Hades.

speaker: Teta
en: Feastday breads! Fresh feastday breads! Breads in all shapes and sizes! Bread in the shape of the ! (whispers) I curse Ahmes the fruit-seller, eater of his own shit. The finest bread in Memphis! Favorite bakery of Cleopatra, the Queen! (whispers) May the life and mind and memory of Ahmes the fruit-seller be forgotten. Coriander-seed bread! Date bread! Two loaves for the price of one on feastdays! (whispers) May the of Ahmes the fruit-seller putrefy into ash. Feastday breads! Buy a fresh loaf for your sweetheard! (whispers) May Ahmes the fruit-seller's be deprived of nourishment in the grave. Brighten your children's eyes with bread in the shape of a fish! (whispers) May Ahmes the fruit-seller's heart be eaten by

speaker: Teta
en: Hello, friend! Bread for your sweetheart?

speaker: Bayek
en: No, thank you. Why do you speak a curse under your breath?

speaker: Teta
en: The magician who sold it to me said I must recite it two hundred times a day. Since I cannot recite while I sleep, I do it while work. Though it is hard to get any baking done without my taster!

speaker: Bayek
en: What happened to your taster?

speaker: Teta
en: Gods blast the regime! They arrested him for not paying the tax on spices! And now I am out of cinnamon!

speaker: Bayek
en: Looks like you need more than a magician.

speaker: Bayek
en: The regime presses even a poor baker so hard? Helping her would be a strike against Ptolemy, however small. And her bread smells delicious.

speaker: Bayek
en: Could that be the man the baker is looking for?

speaker: Bayek
en: You are the taster?

speaker: Sasobek
en: Yes, I am he.

speaker: Bayek
en: Teta the baker asked me to bring you to her.

speaker: Sasobek
en: My beautiful Teta! Now I can see her face again before I die. I am weak with hunger and with love. Will you carry me to Teta?

speaker: Bayek
en: If I must.

speaker: Bayek
en: Can you walk?

speaker: Sasobek
en: I am too weak even to stand!

speaker: Bayek
en: Really?

speaker: Sasobek
en: My strength comes from the beautiful Teta!

speaker: Bayek
en: Does she know you feel this way about her?

speaker: Sasobek
en: I have not yet been brave enough to confess my love for her! Also, I am a wanted man.

speaker: Bayek
en: I can see that. You did not pay your taxes.

speaker: Sasobek
en: It has nothing to do with taxes! I'll tell you everything when we get back to Teta. Teta, beautiful Teta... Her face is like the sun! Teta, my love, I am coming to you!

speaker: Sasobek
en: Hurry! Not much further until I can see my love again!

speaker: Bayek
en: This man is heavy. Too good at his job, I suppose.

speaker: Sasobek
en: Teta!

speaker: Teta
en: You brought back my taster!

speaker: Bayek
en: This man has something to tell you.

speaker: Teta
en: Well?

speaker: Sasobek
en: Teta, I love you!

speaker: Teta
en: What?

speaker: Sasobek
en: And I uncovered a plot to poison the lady Taimhotep, beloved of the High Priest!

speaker: Teta
en: What?!

speaker: Bayek
en: What?

speaker: Sasobek
en: Lady Taimhotep loves our cakes and bread. For five years, we have delivered them to the Great Temple. But yesterday, I overheard a guard say that this week's cakes had been poisoned!

speaker: Bayek
en: Have they been delivered?

speaker: Sasobek
en: I... I don't know. They'd be in the garrison, if not.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then I will have to move quickly.

speaker: Teta
en: This... This is all too much for me.

speaker: Sasobek
en: Would you like to sit down?

speaker: Teta
en: No! I need to think.

speaker: Sasobek
en: Of course, love.

speaker: Teta
en: Hush!

speaker: Bayek
en: A basket of cakes. I got here in time. Now to make sure they will not poison anyone.

speaker: Bayek
en: Another basket of cakes. These need to be destroyed too. I should check to see if there are any others.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is the last of the cakes. Taimhotep is safe now.

speaker: Bayek
en: I found the cakes and destroyed them.

speaker: Teta
en: The lady Taimhotep is safe.

speaker: Bayek
en: And what about you?

speaker: Teta
en: We will go to the High Priest and tell him of this plot. He is a kind man. He will understand we meant his wife no harm.

speaker: Sasobek
en: Medjay... This terrible situation has brought about one good result.

speaker: Teta
en: In the , we will be married!

speaker: Bayek
en: Happy news! May you both prosper.

speaker: Man
en: She sells bread, I sell fruit. There is no reason for competition. I have heard Teta cursing me, but so far my liver seems fine. I do not know why Teta hates me so much.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Si-Mut
en: ... I remember, I remember, I can't remember! It's gone, lost, misplaced, hidden, sleeping, distraught, submerged. Gertha you have failed me.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Si-Mut
en: It's gone! Can you find it? It must be found, found, found... smiling like a hyena, great yellow teeth, then, snap! That's what I remember...

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Si-Mut
en: Nut, blue goddess of the sky and night, where is my treasure? Give it back, relinquish, unhand, bestow, bemoan, bemoan, bemoan...

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: I do not mean to bother you.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Si-Mut
en: Be off with you! It's none of your business! Gertha has it well in hand. And I never spoke of treasure! Certainly not! But can you find it for me? I left it, I'm almost certain, somewhere. It must be here in my writings. I discard my writings as I travel, leaving scrolls as a trail of woe wherever I go. Read this one!

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Si-Mut
en: It's gone. Gone, gone, gone, gone like the moon and the sun, alas. Don't bother me until you find the treasure, you ungrateful wretch! Did you read the scroll? Have you found the treasure? Despite all her efforts, Gertha never could. Oh, woe! Woe to us all!

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: Where is this place you lived?

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Si-Mut
en: Where I lived! Yes, I remember now. A marvelous place near the coast, just south of here. My collection of art and pottery I've found is housed there. How could I have forgotten? Gertha decorated the library!

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: I will go take a look there for your treasure.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: This must be where Si-Mut lived.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bandit 1
en: We've found a treasure trove here!

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bandit 2
en: The crazy coot collected all this!

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bandit 1
en: What if he comes back?

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bandit 2
en: He ran off like his pants were aflame. We've seen the last of him.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: Si-Mut collected all these treasures? What could he have lost that compares to this? Surely there must be a clue here somewhere.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: "Rabid dogs?" He must mean hyenas.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: I hate these cursed beasts.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Mountain Trade
en: We've established with a tribe up in the mountains. It's good trade, but risky. There are wild animals up there...

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: Many did not survive these hyenas.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: The goddess Nut. Goddess of sky and night.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: More writings of Si-Mut?

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: Si-Mut had quite an adventure. I will search for this bandit hideout.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: Ugh! What a foul odor! This must be the bog. He hid nearby.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bandit 1
en: You could not help but admire him!

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bandit 2
en: A knowledgeable man. His conversation jumped from topic to topic like a beautiful butterfly.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bandit 1
en: What was all that about a woman named Gertha?

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bandit 2
en: Some sort of goddess by my understanding.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bandit 1
en: Yes. Yes. I believe you are right.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bandit 2
en: And then he hid in the cave of the ancient creatures! Astounding.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bandit 1
en: An extraordinary nomad.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: Bones of the ancient creatures. I have heard of such things, but did not believe the tales.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: Of course. Si-Mut was here and left a scroll.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: The flooded quarry? I will soon have visited all of Sinai.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: Si-Mut? What is he doing there?

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Si-Mut
en: About time! Gertha and I were worried you got lost!

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: I have been scrambling across the desert following a trail of your writings.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Si-Mut
en: I know how to write?! That's wonderful, praise Amun! I remembered I clearly hid my treasure in a jar and sunk it here, in the Red Sea. In fact, I sank several, only one has the treasure. You'll have to find the right one.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: Very well.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Si-Mut
en: Gertha has been no help at all in this. Just swim around until you find it. It is a very clever hiding place, no? Have you found it? I'm very anxious to get it back.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: Empty!

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: What is this? The treasure?

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Si-Mut
en: You found it! My flamingo foot, it brings me good fortune!

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: A flamingo foot? This is your treasure?

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Si-Mut
en: Come along with me. You are due a reward!

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Si-Mut
en: I must show this to Gertha. She has been singularly unhelpful. I'm not certain she even believes in the power of the foot.

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Si-Mut
en: Gertha! This kind neb (sir) has found my lucky talisman! You have been such a disappointment to me! Pretending to care about my treasure and all the while worrying only about your hump! Our friendship is over! I award you to this man. Perhaps you can be a better friend to him!

scene: The Ballad of Si-Mut and Gertha
speaker: Bayek
en: Uh. Thank you.

speaker: Roman soldier
en: Ptolemy's men are breaking through our line!

speaker: Caesar
en: No, we wait until I see the signal. I can't believe you trusted a woman to do something of such importance. How are the fleet to receive their orders?

speaker: Bayek
en: Patience, Caesar.

speaker: Caesar
en: The die is cast. Come, we go to the battlefield! Medjay, cover the retreat.

speaker: Bayek
en: Many men have doubted Aya. All have found themselves dead by her blade.

speaker: Caesar
en: Ha! Hey! Hey!

speaker: Caesar
en: Out of the way! Brace yourself! Hard left! You better be as fast with your bow as they claim or we will be dead.

speaker: Bayek
en: You focus on driving. I will keep these fools at bay.

speaker: Caesar
en: Odd way to speak of your countrymen.

speaker: Bayek
en: Any who would give up on our people is no countryman of mine.

speaker: Caesar
en: To the back! Behind man! We're surrounded!

speaker: Bayek
en: I am working on it!

speaker: Caesar
en: Work more quickly! Behind us! The chariot gains! I hear more gaining on us!

speaker: Bayek
en: I am shooting as fast as I can, Roman.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is not good.

speaker: Caesar
en: What is it?

speaker: Bayek
en: Hope we don't find out, Caesar. Faster! Perhaps we can outrun it!

speaker: Bayek
en: We will face it. Ready yourself, Caesar. This is worse than any battle you've yet had.

speaker: Caesar
en: It can't be that bad.

speaker: Bayek
en: It is Osiris himself.

speaker: Bayek
en: The arrows are only making him angrier! Hold the chariot steady!

speaker: Caesar
en: My focus is on not being trampled, Egyptian.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have an idea.

speaker: Caesar
en: Just get rid of the damned thing!

speaker: Caesar
en: The lighthouse approaches quickly. We'll run out of land soon. Throw harder! There, it's the fleet!

speaker: Bayek
en: I have nothing left to throw!

speaker: Caesar
en: Anytime, Bayek.

speaker: Caesar
en: There will be songs of us, Bayek. Now we must join the ships... we will be heroes of sword and mind!

speaker: Roman soldier
en: The line runs three . According to our , Pothinus leads the charge.

speaker: Bayek
en: Keep the soldiers distracted, Caesar, I will handle Pothinus.

speaker: Caesar
en: Ad victoriam (For victory)!

speaker: Caesar
en: Flee while you still can! You lose ground, you heartless bastards! Keep on, men, we will defeat them. Not a one of you can stay my blade. Feel the blood rush, Bayek! And know that Mars himself drives your blade!

speaker: Pothinus
en: Meet Yugr Tn. She wishes to make your acquaintance!

speaker: Bayek
en: Pothinus! You will be in the Duat soon! Prepare yourself!

speaker: Pothinus
en: Come, Yugr Tn! Charge! The gods have entrusted me with your demise. You! You are but a gnat in our great plan! Oh, how I wish you could see yourself from such an angle, Bayek. You can still be done with this. Be free of this battle.

speaker: Bayek
