en: Your role in that insane order comes to an end, Pothinus. Face your judgement.

speaker: Pothinus
en: They went too far, in Siwa. I knew it then, but I just wanted peace for Egypt.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your peace leave many wanting.

speaker: Pothinus
en: This is inevitable. A good rule always does. My apologies, Bayek of Siwa. My fee is covered, it seems.

speaker: Pothinus
en: Now may I go to my glory.

speaker: Bayek
en: There is no glory left in Egypt.

speaker: Caesar
en: The damned eunuch is no more. Good. The speculatores found Septimius. He is in the village beyond. I will distract his men while you capture him. We must know what he plans.

speaker: Bayek
en: You'd think your spies would already know.

speaker: Caesar
en: They have their limits. But they claim Aya has a scent of that puppet King, so they also have their uses.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then Ptolemy is already caught. I will finish the rest.

speaker: Septimius
en: Ah! The fool finally comes. You will see your gods soon.

speaker: Septimius
en: Bayek of Siwa. We finally fight. Are you ready for your end?

speaker: Bayek
en: Prepare to face judgement, Septimius. You will find yourself in the Duat soon.

speaker: Septimius
en: Is that all your fury, Medjay? No wonder it was so easy to take your country.

speaker: Bayek
en: Keep talking, dog. You will find my fury soon. You will face judgement, Septimius. I will rip your heart out and feed it to the crocodiles, Septimius.

speaker: Septimius
en: Gods take you. Give up now! I will claim you died a hero, and not a traitor.

speaker: Bayek
en: You call this an attack?

speaker: Septimius
en: Did you miss me?

speaker: Caesar
en: Stop, Bayek. Septimius is a Roman. We will deal with him under our laws.

speaker: Bayek
en: He killed my son!

speaker: Soldier
en: The Pharaoh is dead!

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Everything for which we have worked for so long is now ours. We have defeated our enemies! Only I can lead Egypt into a new era of prosperity.

speaker: Beka
en: My Isesu... I will never see her again. Has anyone seen my Book of the Dead? Without it, my spirit cannot follow my wife's to the Field of Reeds. No one can help me! No one has seen my Book!

speaker: Beka
en: Have you seen my Book of the Dead in your travels, Medjay? I went all the way to Memphis to buy it!

speaker: Bayek
en: No. How was it lost?

speaker: Beka
en: Bandits. They came from the dunes nearby. When their leader saw how I cared for the Book, he wrenched it from me. I thought my heart would stop!

speaker: Bayek
en: I can help. I do not fear them.

speaker: Beka
en: I have been praying for someone like you. That Book will unite me with my wife's spirit!

speaker: Daughter
en: There you are, Father! We are going home.

speaker: Beka
en: But this Medjay is helping me!

speaker: Daughter
en: Oh yes, you are going to find his book? If by some miracle you do, thank you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Did you hear where the bandits meant to go?

speaker: Beka
en: Oh, I... The leader told the others to meet him at the Necropolis... I think.

speaker: Daughter
en: We live nearby.

speaker: Beka
en: I am not going home until I

speaker: Daughter
en: Father, the Book is gone. You will find Mother in the Field of Reeds without it. I promise.

speaker: Beka
en: That warrior will find the Book!

speaker: Daughter
en: Yes, yes. He will find it.

speaker: Beka
en: Thank you. You have given me hope that I will be reunited with Isesu.

speaker: Bayek
en: Here's the Book of the Dead. Beka will be pleased. Now to return the Book to the old man.

Mobare, I am sending a parcel your way. It contains dozens of books of the dead that we've stolen. You are to find their owners and demand a high price to have them returned, but do it discreetly. We don't want the Temple priests finding out about this.

speaker: Bandit
en: Thought you could steal from me?

speaker: Bayek
en: Is it stealing if you rob a thief?

speaker: Bandit
en: I took it for my father!

speaker: Bayek
en: Has your father left us?

speaker: Daughter
en: His good life is over. He was too weak to live 'til your return.

speaker: Bayek
en: May he be conducted in peace.

speaker: Daughter
en: He was in despair that his ka would not join my mother's.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where is his body? It is not too late.

speaker: Daughter
en: You are a blessing from the gods! He receives the rites in the small temple.

speaker: Bayek
en: Old man, your Book. May it guide you to your wife's side.

speaker: Bayek
en: That young woman is standing right on the edge of the cliff. I should check on her.

speaker: Tuaa
en: Who are you? What are you doing? Stay back or I'll jump! You aren't the first person to try and persuade me!

speaker: Bayek
en: Easy. That is a long way down, even for me.

speaker: Tuaa
en: It doesn't matter. Nothing matters anymore. A scorpion took my husband's life. There's nothing left for me now.

speaker: Bayek
en: You could find the scorpion that killed him, and kill it.

speaker: Tuaa
en: Are you mocking me or trying to be cruel?

speaker: Bayek
en: Even bitter laughter is better than death. Why don't you step away from the ledge? We can talk.

speaker: Tua
en: I don't know what to say.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tell me of your husband.

speaker: Tuaa
en: We used to come up here to watch the herons. Two of them built a nest together in that tree. We watched them bring fish for their young. We dreamed of our own children.

speaker: Bayek
en: And you're sad because you did not have any.

speaker: Tuaa
en: You're not very good at this, Medjay. You're not making me feel any better.

speaker: Bayek
en: There is no way to make you feel better. There is only tomorrow. And then the next day. One moment at a time.

speaker: Tuaa
en: What you say is true. I just don't think I can face it.

speaker: Bayek
en: I want to show you something. I'll return soon. Try not to jump.

speaker: Bayek
en: There were some herons nearby, down by that tree.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have got what I need. I should give the feather to the girl.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is for you.

speaker: Tuaa
en: A heron feather? Why?

speaker: Bayek
en: It is a Siwan ritual. Feathers mean a lot to us. Anubis will weigh all our hearts when we die against Ma'at's white feather. Yours. Mine. Our loved ones...

speaker: Tuaa
en: I know what you are doing. This feather is for my afterlife.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your husband will meet you in the Field of Reeds when it's time. But it's not a place to rush to. He would want you to live now, and be happy.

speaker: Tuaa
en: Yes, you're right. He would. I should thank you for this gift.

speaker: Bayek
en: You can thank me by showing me the way down.

speaker: Tuaa
en: Alright Medjay. You win. This way.

speaker: Tuaa
en: I'm sorry. I must seem childish to you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Believe me, no. I understand your grief..

speaker: Tuaa
en: That's why you knew what to say, isn't it? Did you lose someone too?

speaker: Bayek
en: Many have lost loved ones to the Ptolemies.

speaker: Tuaa
en: Does it get better?

speaker: Bayek
en: It gets better. But you will never be the same.

speaker: Tuaa
en: Yes. I already know that...

speaker: Bayek
en: What is your name?

speaker: Tuaa
en: I am Tuaa. I am not from here. I come from Krokodilopolis.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am Bayek, from Siwa. What are you doing in Soknopaiou Nesos?

speaker: Tuaa
en: You're from Siwa? I can tell. You're so nice. Your people are kind. I didn't want to waste my life sewing and weaving for my father. Then I met my husband and we eloped. We didn't have much, but we were happy here.

speaker: Bayek
en: You could return to your family. They will miss you. You could be happy again.

speaker: Tuaa
en: I can't go back to sewing carpets. Besides, my father will never look me in the face again.

speaker: Bayek
en: Few fathers would turn away the child they thought they had lost.

speaker: Tuaa
en: Leopards! Bayek!

speaker: Bayek
en: Stay back!

speaker: Tuaa
en: Dua Sobek! I thought we were dead!

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you hurt?

speaker: Tuaa
en: No, but that was terrifying! Death isn't so desirable when you really see it. I guess I do want to live.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ha! Now she wants to live! Ha, ha. Eh, that is good. But we should move before hyenas come for the carcasses.

speaker: Tuaa
en: Could you take me to the docks?

speaker: Bayek
en: You've decided where to go, then?

speaker: Tuaa
en: I'll find that scorpion that killed my husband! Haha! No, I think I know what to do. I'll head South, maybe even back to Krokodilopolis. I've always wanted to work at the theatre. This place has too many memories for me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Don't forget your family. Your father will miss you, whatever you think.

speaker: Bayek
en: Here we are. Will you be okay?

speaker: Tuaa
en: Thank you, Bayek. I will keep this feather, and weigh it against my heart. Go do your hero work!

speaker: Bayek
en: Be safe, Tuaa.

speaker: Bayek
en: The cat drowns... This ship sank carrying statues of the old gods.

speaker: Bayek
en: Aya kept a small charm of Bastet, the Invisible Paw when she had her morning sickness.

speaker: Man
en: Hilarus you old grain bag, your days are over!

speaker: Hilarus
en: Don't worry, I've got enough left for you!

speaker: Man
en: You are slow and weak! You can barely punch!

speaker: Man
en: Be done with it! Your bones will break next time!

speaker: Hilarus
en: Hello ground.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hey! Get off him. Leave him alone!

speaker: Man
en: Who are you? You want some too? Ok, come on then, hero!

speaker: Bayek
en: You are a little old for street brawling, aren't you?

speaker: Hilarus
en: You are going to lay into me with the insults, too? Youth is a state of mind, boy. The gods do not get old. But thanks for the help. It is good to have a brawling brother.

speaker: Bayek
en: You have an unusual fighting style. I like it.

speaker: Hilarus
en: I eat a lot of punches. A surprise strategy involving well-placed scars and internal bruising.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why were you fighting?

speaker: Hilarus
en: I have been fighting a long time. I was a champion when you were still on the tit! I have to fight.

speaker: Bayek
en: What do you mean? Are you in some kind of trouble?

speaker: Hilarus
en: Trouble? No! I make money from street fighting. Not everyone can afford the Gallic brothers in the arena. I give them a taste of it out here. It is a living if you can win some.

speaker: Bayek
en: But if I had not coming along...

speaker: Hilarus
en: It would have been another loss. It is cruel what age does to you. Hades! I miss the arena. I used to be good! I was Pompey's favourite for a time. Fighting out here feeds man. But there is no glory in it. Nothing beats the screams of thirty thousand bloodthirsty fans! One thing the arena gave me was an eye for talent. And you've got it. With some pointers, you would look the part. Why don't you take the next fight? I have had a few losses. I could use the rest.

speaker: Bayek
en: On one condition, old man. After this contract, you find another job.

speaker: Hilarus
en: Youth is a state of mind! It is up here. (whistles)

speaker: Hilarus
en: Alright, this is it. Do not underestimate him. Keep your hands up – you are dropping your right hand when you hook. Let me know when you are ready.

speaker: Man
en: It is the old melon, come to collect another beating.

speaker: Hilarus
en: Always the disrespect. It is going to bring you bad fate one day. Youth is a state of mind. Today I have got something special for you.

speaker: Man
en: Oh look! Grandpa brought a second. Come on then, pretty boy. Let us see what you've got.

speaker: Man
en: I did not agree to this! Cheating old man! I am done.

speaker: Hilarus
en: Who is the coward now, you little prick! Come back and finish the fight!

speaker: Hilarus
en: That was good work. A fine start! Almost worthy of the arena. What is your name, son?

speaker: Bayek
en: Bayek of Siwa.

speaker: Hilarus
en: Hmm, not really a fighter's name though, is it? We will want something more memorable like the Siwan Pretty Boy. We can talk about that later. Training first.

speaker: Bayek
en: Training? Listen old man...

speaker: Hilarius
en: The next fight is tonight. Let us meet at sundown. Say at the top of the lighthouse? Take some time to rest, analyze your performance. Fight with extreme ka, be a god, and do not forget! The top of the lighthouse at sundown!

speaker: Bayek
en: A beautiful night sky. It is nice up here. But where is that old fool? He is late.

speaker: Hilarus
en: Bayek! Down here!

speaker: Bayek
en: Why are you down there? You said to meet you up here!

speaker: Hilarus
en: Hurry. Come down. We have got a fight to get to!

speaker: Bayek
en: Why did you send me to the top of the lighthouse?

speaker: Hilarus
en: I have something to say to you. Hilarus is serious now. Students do not question their teachers.

speaker: Bayek
en: Old tomato, you are not my teacher...

speaker: Hilarus
en: I love that lighthouse, lost my virginity there. I wanted you to see it. That, and the climb is good for the lungs. Your reward was the view. It was worth it, don't you agree?

speaker: Bayek
en: It was actually. It is nice to take the time to realize how beautiful the world is...

speaker: Hilarus
en: You see! There is always method in my madness, Bayek. Remember that.

speaker: Bayek
en: What are you doing now!?

speaker: Hilarus
en: Racing you to the next fight!

speaker: Bayek
en: Rest easy grandpa.

speaker: Hilarus
en: Do not disrespect your teacher! I used to run circles in the arena for hours. Pompey called me The Camel of Hermes! I would never tire!

speaker: Bayek
en: By Amun! You're not my... Pompey compared you to a camel?

speaker: Hilarus
en: Hilarus Maximus, The Camel of Hermes.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hilarus... There must be something else you can do besides fighting.

speaker: Hilarus
en: What else is there! I once fought an entire garrison. You ever do that?

speaker: Bayek
en: I dabbled in it.

speaker: Hilarus
en: We have got another fight to finish. This way.

speaker: Woman
en: Ah... Haha! Help! Help! It's Hercules!

speaker: Man
en: You are mine, Helen of Troy! You cannot escape me!

speaker: Hilarus
en: Ha-ha! Yes, it is a brothel. This is your next lesson – do not allow yourself to be distracted. Our last fight is inside.

speaker: Woman
en: You are the challenger? I'm going to enjoy this. Come on, they are waiting.

speaker: Hilarus
en: Bayek, catch your breath. This one is going to be tough. When you are ready, let me know.

speaker: Man
en: The not-so-mighty Hilarus, come to claim lost glory. I see the rumors are true. You've got yourself a pet lion to hide behind. It will not matter. I will beat him for the money. Then I will beat you for the pleasure.

speaker: Man
en: Damn you! Cheating old man!

speaker: Hilarus
en: Oh that is how it is going to be? Then I am in too!

speaker: Woman
en: Well, that was a fetching display! How would you like something steady? Just look strong and take care of any trouble. You will be well looked after.

speaker: Bayek
en: Unfortunately, I am accounted for. Would you consider a genuine arena champion? Hilarus here was a favorite of Pompey's.

speaker: Woman
en: You are a little old, but you cut a good figure. Do you still have it in you?

speaker: Hilarus
en: Do I— Madam, I am Hilarus. Youth is a state of mind. You will be more than satisfied! If my charge releases me.

speaker: Woman
en: Come, then. We shall discuss the terms privately.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hilarus! How's the new... position?

speaker: Hilarus
en: Ah, the Siwan Pretty Boy is back! It is not so different from the arena, actually. What with the constant screams and groans. The owner keeps me... busy.

speaker: Bayek
en: You old dog...

speaker: Hilarus
en: Youth is a state of mind!

speaker: Bayek
en: The gladiatorial arena. So the Crocodile recruits from this place for his personal army. I need to find out more about it. Excuse me, what can you tell me about this place?

speaker: Woman
en: Can't you see? It's an arena for Roman blood sport. Barbaric, if you ask me. But it's found favour with those desperate to forget their troubles. It used to be a temple. It should have been left that way.

speaker: Bayek
en: Neb (Sir), what can you tell me about the men who fight here?

speaker: Man
en: Men? These are not men, they're gods! You've never seen such savage warriors. They could break you in half with one strike.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah. Do any of them have red hair?

speaker: Man
en: Gods among gods, have you never heard of the brothers from ? Can't you feel their eyes on you? Their statues are beside me!

speaker: Bayek
en: "Diovicos, the living embodiment of War. His fists are deadlier than any weapon. Viridovix, the loyal servant of Death. His scythe will ever reap the unworthy."

speaker: Man 2
en: Sir, we need more fighters. They're dying at an alarming rate.

speaker: Felix
en: Then find me fighters that can actually fight!

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you the owner here?

speaker: Felix
en: Yes I am the owner, Felix Martialis. Who are you? Another rough knuckle no-name seeking fame?

speaker: Bayek
en: I only want entry to the Arena. I heard you've got a fighter worth watching. With red hair.

speaker: Felix
en: You mean the Gallic brothers. You heard right. But let me save you some time, camel boy. You cannot afford it. Now piss off before you scare away someone who can.

speaker: Man 2
en: Sir, this man wears a Medjay badge!

speaker: Felix
en: A med what? I do not even care. Can you fight? You look the part, like a vicious... mangy dog. Nah, nah, I have already got an Egyptian. A huntress from Siwa who's worth three of you. She frequents the obelisk in the east end if you want an impromptu beating.

speaker: Man 2
en: It is the only way inside this arena. Fight in the streets and a gladiator can bring you in.

speaker: Bayek
en: So, the Gallic brothers are involved in Shadya's murder. But why are they doing the Crocodile's bidding? I need to get inside, and learn more. The Arena owner mentioned a Siwan gladiator to the east at an Obelisk. I wonder if I know her. Siwa is a small place. I should go and see.

speaker: Bayek
en: There's the Siwan. Wait. That looks like...

speaker: Kensa
en: Bayek? My friend! My brother! Oh! Shit, it's good to see you. What are you doing in Faiyum?

speaker: Bayek
en: I heard this was a good place to... to prosper. But I never expected to find you here, Kensa.

speaker: Kensa
en: What can I say? I heard the call of the arena. Can you believe it? I am a gladiator now! But come, come. Let us talk... and drink! Ha ha ha!

speaker: Kensa
en: I'm telling you, Bayek, I am so close to my dream. If only I was given the chance, I know I could become champion. I mean, wealth, luxury, fame! What more could a woman want?

speaker: Bayek
en: That's why I came to Faiyum. To make a new life for myself and bury the past. But I was turned away from the Arena doors.

speaker: Kensa
en: So you have finally given up on trying to put the world to rights? Good. Such things are impossible. Felix is slow to trust outsiders. But do not worry. With my backing, we'll soon be fighting side by side. First, we drink. And in the morning, we can go to the Arena for the proper introductions. It's good to have you here, old friend.

speaker: Kensa
en: I want this man to be my partner.

speaker: Felix
en: As it happens, the Iberian was torn apart by the lions yesterday. I may have an opening. And if Kensa vouches for you... You will need a title if you are going to team up, though. How about the Siwan warriors?

speaker: Kensa
en: I think "The Guardians of Siwa" would be more fitting.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is that memorable enough for you?

speaker: Felix
en: I have heard worse. Come inside.

speaker: Felix
en: This is where combatants wait their turn on the sand. What you smell is sweat, blood, and not a little offal. If you are predisposed to shitting your armor, this is where to do it. There is no Pharaoh or god in the arena to protect you, Medjay. This is where you will probably die. Try to do it with drama, it pleases the crowd. On the off-chance you live, you will be rewarded with glory and fame. And another chance to die. Such is the short but luminous life of a gladiator. All right... who do we have? Ah, there is Kallistos. Kallistos, a former soldier of Ptolemy who claims to know how to handle a sword. Horus. He was my best fighter once, but age ruins us all. He is not much more than a bedpan now. He trains the novices.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is that armor from Ptolemy's army?

speaker: Felix
en: Most of the fighters cannot afford their own armor. In any case, it is soon ruined. The army does not miss a few suits here and there. And it adds to the authenticity. Speaking of authenticity, in the arena you use the weapons I give you. There are no exceptions. You already know Kensa, whose glowing but suspect recommendation brought you here.

speaker: Kensa
en: Bayek! Krokodilopolis welcomes another champion!

speaker: Felix
en: Or another bag of blood and shit. I want to see if he can fight. And who better to test him than the one who recommended him?

speaker: Kensa
en: What do you say? Ready to draw sword old Medjay?

speaker: Bayek
en: Let's see if you have improved.

speaker: Kensa
en: Not bad, old man!

speaker: Bayek
en: How is that for old!

speaker: Kensa
en: Nek! (Shit!) I thought I had you.

speaker: Felix
en: You need more style and flash. But you have got a pleasing vicious streak for a sand dog. Okay, Kensa. You have got a new partner. We open the doors soon. Be ready.

speaker: Viridovix
en: These are the scraps that Felix wants to throw our way? Ha ha ha! They make a poor meal, my brother!

speaker: Kensa
en: I'm going to slice off your balls... and feed them to you.

speaker: Kensa
en: Our main obstacle to glory. The Gallic brothers.

speaker: Bayek
en: I know who they are.

speaker: Kallistos
en: Ah, the new Siwan fighter. I look forward to humiliating you in battle many times. Eh. I joke, of course. We might be pitted against each other out there, but that's all the more reason to stand together in here.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm glad to hear it. But why does one of Ptolemy's soldiers risk his life in the Arena?

speaker: Kallistos
en: I have trouble obeying orders, and the army frowns on that. But I have a family to support, so here I am.

speaker: Bayek
en: Have you ever challenged the brothers?

speaker: Kallistos
en: Viridovix and Diovicos? I haven't been thought worthy yet. In that, I consider myself fortunate.

speaker: Kensa
en: Are you well, my friend? You seem distracted. Don't worry, you will lose your nerves after the first fight.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm fine. But you have not yet told me how you came to be here.

speaker: Kensa
en: Now that is a story! I was taken as a slave during Ptolemy's time in Siwa. A sick beast named Septimius and his clan were going to use me. But I managed to get a sword and make my escape. I travelled here, where Felix took me in and trained me. But enough about the past! I can't tell you how happy I am to share this good fortune with you. Soon, the crowds will worship you almost as much as they worship me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes, yes. Let us split the sun in two with our swords.

speaker: Kensa
en: Ha ha! You are primed, indeed! Let Felix know when you are ready for our first match. The sooner we start, the sooner we're champions!

speaker: Bayek
en: You are Horus, are you not? Felix told me you're the trainer here.

speaker: Horus
en: Not by choice. Gallic brothers... hurt me. My head. Would have killed me if Felix did not stop them.

speaker: Bayek
en: What can you tell me about them?

speaker: Horus
en: You don't want to fight them. They are strong and fast, and they like killing. For them, it's fun... sport.

speaker: Bayek
en: We are ready.

speaker: Felix
en: Are you? Everyone thinks they are ready till they get a fist in the face. I am starting you against a few novices. If you survive, we will talk about more. Two warriors against the odds! The crowds love unfair fights. Do not disappoint them... or me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are they screaming for our blood or for theirs?

speaker: Kensa
en: Any blood will do! No such thing as innocent here. Do not stay your blade, brother. They certainly will not! Every man here knows the risks!

speaker: Bayek
en: You have taken to this new life easily.

speaker: Kensa
en: Can you see the look on their faces? They adore me, Bayek! The men. The women. I have everything I could want.

speaker: Felix
en: They are off to a good start! These two sand-bandits are tougher than they look!

speaker: Kensa
en: Keep fighting like this, old friend, and we'll catch the eye of a wealthy patron!

speaker: Bayek
en: And what then?

speaker: Kensa
en: Then a whole new world of opportunity, my friend. The best gladiators are sent on special missions, and earn more coin than you can imagine.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then let us make sure they notice us!

speaker: Felix
en: Victory for the Guardians of Siwa! The new darlings of the Arena! Who knows how far they can go?

speaker: Felix
en: Pairing you two toe stubbers was one of my best ideas. The crowd loves you!

speaker: Kensa
en: I told you we were destined for greatness, Felix.

speaker: Felix
en: Greatness? Easy easy, damsel dust mite. You have a long way to go. It is a good start, but you are not contenders. You do not get to the Gallic brothers by beating a few shit stain novices. Though to be honest, I hope you make it. I am weary of you nagging me.

speaker: Bayek
en: What do we need to do to face them?

speaker: Felix
en: Gods and piss, not you too! Just concentrate on the next round. For annoying me, I am adding lions this time. They have not eaten for days. You are their dinner. Find me when you are ready.

speaker: Bayek
en: If what Kensa says is true, any of the gladiators could be working for the Crocodile. There might be evidence here of jobs the Gallic brothers did. Maybe even the identity of their patron.

speaker: Horus
en: So, you are feeling good. Planning your ride to the top. Trust me, what we do... it's not noble. We are mercenaries, that's all.

speaker: Bayek
en: Mercenaries? Swords for hire by the wealthy?

speaker: Horus
en: Yes. So you heard. My advice – refuse the offers. It's a slippery dune. I have seen... good men die. Just fight and go home. Don't do the contracts.

speaker: Kallistos
en: An impressive first outing, Siwan. I'm a little jealous.

speaker: Bayek
en: I need a faster way to make coin. I've heard fighters are offered work outside the arena.

speaker: Kallistos
en: You're quick to learn secrets, my friend. We are not supposed to talk about it. But opportunities come along from time to time. I think I might have just proven myself worthy.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do you know who the contracts come from?

speaker: Kallistos
en: There is a reason these people operate in shadow. No one knows their identity. Take my advice. If you're lucky enough to be chosen, do what you're asked to, and be thankful for the money.

speaker: Kensa
en: We are on our way, old friend! After all this time! I might finally get my shot at the Gallic brothers. And it's thanks to you.

speaker: Bayek
en: I would like nothing more. What about these other contracts you mentioned earlier?

speaker: Kensa
en: Oh, the righteous Bayek is willing to dirty his hands? Times have changed, seni (friend). I suppose it is hard to be a Medjay, all the time. You will have to ask Felix about those... quietly.

speaker: Bayek
en: The best way to reach the Crocodile is to beat the Gallic brothers. As if I needed more reason to slit the throats of Shadya's killers.

speaker: Bayek
en: Felix, I've heard some gladiators are chosen for... extra work.

speaker: Felix
en: You heard wrong. And if there was an arrangement, you would have much more to do to earn your way in. Your job, you upstart dog nobble, is to fight. That is it. You earn your gold in the pit, or you do not earn it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then that is what I will do. We are ready.

speaker: Felix
en: Finally. They are asking about you two at the Arena in Cyrene. Put on a good show, and we all profit.

speaker: Bayek
en: How often do you fight lions?

speaker: Kensa
en: Only when Felix can get them! They are much more expensive than men volunteering for a beating!

speaker: Bayek
en: There seems little honor in killing animals.

speaker: Kensa
en: Kill or be eaten, Bayek! Besides, it's caged. We will be fine as long as we don't free it.

speaker: Felix
en: The Medjay and the slave girl are unstoppable! More ferocious than wild beasts!

speaker: Bayek
en: I thought the lions were caged?

speaker: Kensa
en: There are no rules in the Arena, seni! (friend!)

speaker: Felix
en: The Guardians of Siwa are victorious once again! Could the Gallic brothers be next?

speaker: Bayek
en: Is that Kallistos? What happened?

speaker: Horus
en: I warned him. He took a bad job. Just another blunt instrument for them to break against their enemies.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do you know who hired him?

speaker: Horus
en: No. And Felix won't tell you. That's how this works. Some die. Some get rich. And everyone keeps quiet.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where's Kensa?

speaker: Felix
en: Her talents were required elsewhere today. You are going to have to win this one alone. You will be fine.

speaker: Bayek
en: Another errand? Like the one that killed Kallistos?

speaker: Felix
en: Watch your tone, sword meat. What happened to Kallistos was... unfortunate. But he knew the risks. Fighters who ask too many questions do not survive. It is a dangerous job. Accidents happen.

speaker: Bayek
en: Another errand for the unknown patron?

speaker: Felix
en: Fighters who ask too many questions do not survive. It is a dangerous job. Accidents happen.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm only keen to prove myself.

speaker: Felix
en: Then win this match. You will get your chance against the brothers. Beat them, and you will be noticed.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is Kensa okay? Holy Anubis. I have to win this!

speaker: Felix
en: The Medjay is not missing his partner! What a warrior!

speaker: Felix
en: Are you watching, Krokodilopolis? Is this the rise of a new challenger? Will the Gallic brothers keep their crown?

speaker: Kensa
en: I am sorry I left you to fight alone, but I hear you did me proud?

speaker: Bayek
en: Felix sent you out on a job? Who was it for?

speaker: Kensa
en: I'll tell you everything in good time, brother. Just know that our future has never looked brighter!

speaker: Kensa
en: Bayek. This is the moment we've longed for. Our chance to seize the mantle of champions.

speaker: Kensa
en: Felix awaits!

speaker: Horus
en: So... you turn to fight the brothers. I won't say good luck. You won't get any. But listen to me. They are too strong together. That's how they beat me. Separate them. Fight one at a time and... maybe you live.

speaker: Bayek
en: Thank you, Horus. But don't worry. I am not dying today.

speaker: Horus
en: There are worse things than dying. Be careful.

speaker: Felix
en: You have done well for a country corn rat. Your time has come. The crowd is bored with Viridovix and Diovicos destroying opponents with ease. I am counting on you to make this entertaining. One more thing. Do not kill anyone! I want my top four fighters alive for rematches. I have given the Gauls the same order.

speaker: Kensa
en: All right. We will not kill them. But no promises about pain and humiliation. This is it, Bayek! Our big moment. They will build monuments and scrawl our names across temples after this. We will be adored! Rich! And champions.

speaker: Felix
en: Here are the contenders to the crown! The Guardians of Siwa! Undefeated! Unmatched! It's the Gallic Brothers!

speaker: Bayek
en: Crocodile!

speaker: Felix
en: The Gallic brothers are defeated!

speaker: Bayek
en: You killed a child called Shadya. Death is the least you deserve.

speaker: Diovicos
en: The girl by the lighthouse? We didn't kill her, I swear!

speaker: Viridovix
en: We have done many terrible things, Siwan. But the murder of the child is not one of them.

speaker: Felix
en: All hail the new champions! The Guardians of Siwa!

speaker: Diovicos
en: We were there, it's true. We saw the soldiers capture the girl and take her to Berenike. To... to the Crocodile.

speaker: Viridovix
en: It was she who drowned the child. Took a book from her, ordered a stone tied to her ankles and pushed her into the water. There was nothing we could do.

speaker: Kensa
en: This is the real reason you came to me, isn't it? To uncover this patron. This "Crocodile". Bayek, why didn't you confide in me, huh? I would have helped you.

speaker: Bayek
en: You're a mercenary, just like them. I couldn't take the chance!

speaker: Felix
en: What fate awaits the fallen? Will it be life... or death?

speaker: Kensa
en: No, Bayek. You know me better than...

speaker: Felix
en: Death.

speaker: Kensa
en: Bayek, you have to know!

speaker: Hotephres
en: So it was Berenike. She is the Crocodile. She is the one who killed Shadya. She is the one who has brought ruin to so many. She calls herself the sponsor of Faiyum's prosperity and culture, and her influence is felt throughout the region. Her wealth comes from her estate north of the city. Kerkesoucha granary, the largest in all of Egypt. She has arranged a symposium with others of influence in Faiyum. Every night, she retires to her villa, where she courts their favor with bribes and silvered words.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then that is where I will find her. Thank you for everything, my friend. What will you do now?

speaker: Hotephres
en: I will retire to our family villa. I need a drink. Khenut and I must mourn in peace. Farewell, Bayek. Once you have done what you must, we would be glad to see you again.

speaker: Bayek
en: Smoke. What has happened here?

speaker: Man
en: This is what happens when you refuse Berenike's orders. She demanded my land and when I refused, she had my home burned and then she bought it anyway.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do not worry. I will put an end to this.

speaker: Bayek
en: There is the granary Hotephres spoke of. The Crocodile must be inside.

speaker: Protester
en: Prosperity for all? Pah! It is prosperity only for the rich damned Greeks and their traitorous Egyptian pets. Did you hear about Aset? Her daughter was promised in marriage, but she could not afford the wedding. Now they are both begging for food in the slums! The damned slums! We cannot even trust the Phylakitai to help us! They eat from the corrupt Nomarch's hands! Food that belongs to our god damned families! They steal the grain from our own children's mouths! And what about Raho? His family lost their farm to the Greek friends of the Nomarch. Now they are forced to work like slaves on the land they once owned! Nek (Shit)!

speaker: Man
en: How many weeks have they been shouting at the gates? Still nothing changes. Nothing is done. Greeks just take and take. Most of my grain is taken by taxes and soldiers. I barely have enough left to eat. Is this shit what they mean by prosperity?

speaker: Orator
en: Faiyum is the happy recipient of the best in Greek culture. And it's thanks to our honorable Lady. We are all humble beneficiaries of her elegance, education and impeccable taste. Culture for all! Who is there to compare to our Lady of the villa? Who has done as much for the Faiyum? It is to her we owe our allegiance and our lasting thanks. Culture for all! Due to the unceasing efforts of our honorable Lady, the Faiyum is prospering again. There is more grain than there ever has been. Farms are producing at record rates, filling our storehouses. The Faiyum has never been safer! The increased security is a result of our Lady's selfless generosity. She has worked tirelessly to provide a safer community for all of us. The magnificent statues of Aphrodite you see around the villa hide a wonderful secret. These images of the goddess of beauty were all modeled after our honorable Lady of the villa.

speaker: Berenike
en: Are you enjoying your new station, my champion?

speaker: Kensa
en: Yes, my lady. It is everything I hoped it would be.

speaker: Berenike
en: You will want for nothing as long as you stay by my side. As long as you are loyal. As long as you never fail me.

speaker: Kensa
en: Yes, my lady.

speaker: Bayek
en: Kensa? Is this the luxury you sought? To be a slave to an enemy of Egypt?

speaker: Berenike
en: Anything to report?

speaker: Guard 1
en: Nothing, my lady. The rebels have been routed, and the Egyptians give us little cause for concern. Some have gathered outside in protest. A pointless gesture.

speaker: Berenike
en: Have the men take names.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Yes, my lady.

speaker: Berenike
en: Did he tell us anything of value?

speaker: Guard 2
en: No, my lady.

speaker: Berenike
en: A pity. Dispose of his body, along with the others. Tear his heart out. As instructed by the Order.

speaker: Kensa
en: I knew you'd come, old friend. Perhaps I was always meant to die at your hand.

speaker: Bayek
en: I do not want to kill you, Kensa. But look who you serve now.

speaker: Kensa
en: Who else did I have left?

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm sorry it had to end this way, old friend. May you find peace in Ma'at's embrace.

speaker: Berenike
en: You! How dare you come here?!

speaker: Bayek
en: Shadya!

speaker: Berenike
en: Murdered... by one of you...

speaker: Bayek
en: Shadya.

speaker: Berenike
en: Who?

speaker: Bayek
en: Shadya! She was the child you drowned.

speaker: Berenike
en: Like all of your kind, you fail to see what greatness lies in store for Egypt.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is that what you tell yourself? You do not remember those you killed. She was the child of Khenut and Hotephres.

speaker: Berenike
en: Khenut was a stubborn rock. That ledger would have meant the end to all our hopes.

speaker: Bayek
en: You destroyed families.

speaker: Berenike
en: I did what had to be done.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will destroy everything you stand for, Berenike! And I will destroy all others like you!

speaker: Bayek
en: But for now, all that matters is that you killed Shadya! And the last word you will remember will be her name! Shadya!

speaker: Bayek
en: I wonder how Hotephres and Khenut are. I should visit them.

speaker: Bayek
en: And here I am, at last, in the Faiyum. I will root out the agents of the Crocodile.

speaker: Crier
en: Culture for all! Greek and Egyptian knowledge joins in a new climate of restoration. The Faiyum is being raised above its humble beginnings. Guided by the principles of Greek civilization, Greece and Egypt live together in peace. Culture for all! Security for all! An increased military presence throughout the Faiyum has made life safer for everyone. Egyptian slums are being torn down, rebuilt, or segregated. Greek settlement is more secure than ever. Security for all! Trade activity has increased tremendously, creating substantial economic growth for Greek business throughout the Faiyum. Prosperity for all! Prosperity for all! Latest census figures show increased wealth for all in Faiyum. Thanks to the great Ptolemy's aid for Greek investors, profits have continued to multiply. Prosperity for all! With increased acquisition of Egyptian land and the use of Greek farming methods, farms in the Faiyum now have more success than ever! The new Faiyum promises peace and plenty. A new age of wealth under the guidance of Greek innovation! Prosperity for all!

speaker: Bayek
en: It seems I'm not the first visitor today. Hotephres! Nek (Shit), he's not here. I need to find out where my informant is.

speaker: Bayek
en: Who would have done such a thing! What were you protecting, boy?

speaker: Bayek
en: A lot of damage, but no blood or signs of a fight. Maybe he fled before this happened? Hmm. These scrolls tell me nothing useful. I should check upstairs.

speaker: Bayek
en: A child's doll. I'm going to kill this neket iadet (piece of shit) Crocodile.

speaker: Bayek
en: Scrolls and ink. Nothing that tells me where Hotephres has gone. Wait... feathers. From a messenger pigeon?

speaker: Bayek
en: A letter left behind by my informant. It looks like he fled, but the soldiers caught his servant. If the servant is still alive, he'll know where Hotephres is. They'll be holding him at the nearby military camp.

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: What's the story with the beat up Egyptian? By the Captain's tent. He looks half dead.

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: He's the servant of the Greek we're looking for. The Captain persuaded him to give up his master's location. He's not done yet, either. He'll eventually tell him everything else he knows.

speaker: Servant
en: Please... I've told you everything I know. Who are you?

speaker: Bayek
en: A friend. Hold still and stay quiet. I will get you out of here.

speaker: Servant
en: Gods. Thank you. Did Hotephres send you?

speaker: Bayek
en: No, but I must find him. I need his help to find the Crocodile. Will you help me?

speaker: Servant
en: Hotephres took a trader's ship to Lake Moeris. It has a large statue on board, and is marked by our symbol. The Crocodile has hired mercenaries to find him.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then I must hurry. Get somewhere safe. Be well.

speaker: Hotephres
en: So, now they send a son of Egypt against me? It has been a long time since I spilled so much blood.

speaker: Bayek
en: I was sent by Apollodorus. We share a common interest.

speaker: Hotephres
en: Who are you and what do you want, eh?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am Bayek of Siwa. And I seek information on the Crocodile.

speaker: Hotephres
en: The phantom that has brought Faiyum to its knees? What could you want with him?

speaker: Bayek
en: He belongs to a group that is destroying Egypt. I intend to hunt every last one of them down.

speaker: Hotephres
en: Bayek of Siwa, you don't know what you are up against. The Crocodile has transformed not only the land, but the people: those who do not cower in fear, are made to work for him.

speaker: Bayek
en: And you have no idea who the Crocodile is?

speaker: Hotephres
en: I stole a ledger from a Greek magistrate I suspect of corruption. It should reveal the identity of this "Crocodile". And if we get it to Apollodorus, we may be able to bring down the whole organization.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where's the ledger now?

speaker: Hotephres
en: I gave it to my wife Khenut to hide. As long as the Ptolemies think it's with me, my family is safe. That is why I have to stay on the move.

speaker: Hotephres
en: Here, this will tell Khenut you are a friend to be trusted. It is for my daughter Shadya. Once you have the ledger, find me at the docks, south of Euhemeria. Bayek, take a look around my ship before you go. I keep records of local problems which may have the Crocodile at their root. They may interest you, as a Medjay.

speaker: Egyptian Citizen
en: Greeks grow fatter and richer in Egypt while we go hungry. The poor are taxed more than the rich. Why is this happening? This is our home. Egypt belongs to us! Prosperity for all, they say. Well, where is it? Where are the benefits, the peace of mind? It is all with the Greeks! It is not for Egyptians! The new laws are made by Greeks for Greeks. Prosperity for all? There is no grain. They have burned our farms and driven us out. Where will we get our food? We know what Greek prosperity means! Famine for Egypt! Our Faiyum, our home, is now a place where there are Greek-only stalls. These neked iadet will not even serve Egyptians!

speaker: Khenut
en: We need to clean this place up and get it running again. Don't worry. I won't let them close down this kitchen.

speaker: Bayek
en: Khenut?

speaker: Khenut
en: Yes?

speaker: Bayek
en: Hotephres sent me. I am here to help. And I have your daughter's doll.

speaker: Khenut
en: Great. I was awaiting word from my man. Thank you, come, eat and we can talk.

speaker: Shadya
en: Oh, I love my new doll, Bayek! I will name her... Iset and she will be the protector of all Faiyum.

speaker: Khenut
en: Ever since Hotephres got a hold of that ledger, Faiyum has been on edge. Soldiers with torches patrol every night. And this alms kitchen was practically razed to the ground. They have left Shadya and me alone, at least. Hotephres has made sure of that.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where is the ledger now?

speaker: Khenut
en: I instructed our most loyal servant to hide it in our villa. They can search the place as many times as they want. They will never find it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Can you take me there?

speaker: Khenut
en: I have been summoned to the lighthouse for another of their "routine investigations".

speaker: Bayek
en: That may not be safe. The Ptolemaic authorities seem to be working with the Crocodile.

speaker: Khenut
en: It happens every few days. Don't worry. They wouldn't dare touch someone in an official position. Shadya, show Bayek the way to our home.

speaker: Shadya
en: Come on, uncle Bayek! You can see my house from that roof. Follow me! You are not afraid of heights, are you?

speaker: Bayek
en: Lead on, little one. I will follow.

speaker: Shadya
en: Haha! Where did you learn to climb like that? That looks like fun!

speaker: Shadya
en: I come up here a lot. Everything looks so beautiful. The people should be happy, but they are not.

speaker: Bayek
en: Don't worry. Your mother and father will look after them. Where is your house?

speaker: Shadya
en: On the hill over there! See it?

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes... and soldiers. Thank you, Shadya. You should go back to your mother now. It might get dangerous.

speaker: Shadya
en: Nothing bad will ever happen to me! Iset can fight, you know! She will protect me!

speaker: Bayek
en: Bye, Shadya! You and Iset enjoy your life!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Where is it? They said it would be here!

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Did we find the ledger?

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Not yet, but it won't be long. The captain is upstairs questioning the servant.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Stupid Egyptian vlakos (bumpkins). Khenut is a marked woman. Loyalty to her will get them killed.

speaker: Bayek
en: Maps of settlements in the Faiyum, part of Khenut's work. Interesting, but not what I'm looking for.

speaker: Bayek
en: Complaints to Alexandria about the administration's practices in Faiyum, from Khenut. She didn't have much success. No ledger.

speaker: Bayek
en: It won't open. There's something blocking it on the other side. There must be another way in.

speaker: Bayek
en: Another of Shadya's dolls. Did Hotephres make this one, too?

speaker: Bayek
en: An unfinished letter to the Sobek priests. Scathing. Khenut and the Cult don't see eye to eye. Nothing else here.

speaker: Bayek
en: Servants tried to barricade the doors. They weren't quick enough.

speaker: Bayek
en: Gods! Shadya wrote this. She has the ledger! And I sent her back to her mother! I have to find Khenut before the soldiers get to her! Oh, Shadya! What have you done, little one? You cannot play games with the Crocodile!

speaker: Bayek
en: Have you seen Khenut? Is she here?

speaker: Worker
en: The soldiers just came and took her to the Lighthouse. Young Shadya, too! Khenut argued with them but they would not listen. Something is wrong, isn't it? This has never happened before.

speaker: Bayek
en: Get word to Hotephres. Hurry! Damn all this! Khenut and Shadya are at the Lighthouse! I need to get there now! Nek (Shit)!... Nek (Shit)!

speaker: Soldier 3
en: What have we done? Gods! What have we done?!

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Easy, brother. The Crocodile did this, not you or me. Surely... it must have been necessary.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Say that when the nightmares come! We watched and did nothing. We are not innocent.

speaker: Khenut
en: Shadya... Shadya...

speaker: Hotephres
en: It is over. The Crocodile has won. The ledger, lost. My daughter... my Shadya... He has taken everything from us.

speaker: Bayek
en: He will pay for this. And all those who serve him.

speaker: Hotephres
en: None of that will bring Shadya back.

speaker: Bayek
en: No. But at least you'll have the comfort of revenge. We both will.

speaker: Hotephres
en: I hope so. I will do anything I can to help you, brother.

speaker: Bayek
en: Has Khenut been able to tell you anything?

speaker: Hotephres
en: Only that there were other men with the soldiers. Large, imposing warriors. One red-haired.

speaker: Bayek
en: Bandits? Soldiers?

speaker: Hotephres
en: I believe they were gladiators, from the arena in Krokodilopolis. It seems this... this monster uses fighters to do his bidding.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will find this monster, friend. He will die.

speaker: Caravan Lead
en: Headed to Thebes? It's a sand-scourged journey, but my caravan is fast!

speaker: Sutekh
en: Welcome, welcome to Thebes. You need a room? A bigger shield? A bodyguard?

speaker: Bayek
en: What is this?

speaker: Sutekh
en: The Pharaoh's Curse!

speaker: Bayek
en: As Ra lives! He landed a blow!

speaker: Bayek
en: You are nothing but a figment!

speaker: Scared Woman
en: I honor the gods! She comes for me! I stole nothing! Why do the Pharaohs' punish us?

speaker: Bayek
en: Return to the Duat! These people are innocent.

speaker: Scared Woman
en: Amun protect me, Amun protect us alL!

speaker: Terrified Woman
en: Sekhmet protect me. I only took a few drachma. There are worse than me. The abomination comes for us all. Amun has deserted us!

speaker: Bayek
en: Who summoned you?

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone has the artifact, is using it to summon the long dead. I must stop them before this curse murders all of Thebes. Amunet said her contact was near Luxor.

speaker: Sutekh
en: Merti, you know what this curse has cost Thebes, cost me! I have no one left.

speaker: Merti
en: Your uncle still lives, Sutekh. Perhaps he has work for you?

speaker: Sutekh
en: That scorpion? He wouldn't give me a fig his monkey spat out.

speaker: Sutekh
en: Ah, you survived the curse! They will speak of you throughout Thebes.

speaker: Bayek
en: Make sure no one speaks of me.

speaker: Merti
en: Enough, Sutekh.

speaker: Sutekh
en: Of course! No phylakitai (cops) will hear of the man with death in his eye!

speaker: Bayek
en: I was told you would help me. This is for you.

speaker: Merti
en: What is this? Who gave this to you?

speaker: Bayek
en: The woman you know as Aya.

speaker: Merti
en: Very well. What do you want?

speaker: Bayek
en: A rare artifact. I believe it's the cause of this curse.

speaker: Merti
en: Could it be?... Rumors, whispers. A relic was stolen from an unknown Pharaoh's tomb. Some say this desecration called the curse down upon us.

speaker: Bayek
en: I must find it.

speaker: Merti
en: There is quite a black market here in Thebes, secret auctions, rare trades. Talk to the merchants near the docks, they'll know more. Tell Aya our deal is done. I'm headed south. The curse comes too close for comfort.

speaker: Bayek
en: What if I have more questions?

speaker: Merti
en: Then find Isidora, the God's Wife of Amun. She will understand this curse in a way I cannot.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nefertiti and Akhenaten are no more. I defeated them in the Duat.

speaker: Isidora
en: You've seen the land of the dead, yet still live?

speaker: Bayek
en: No. It was a trick of the mind. I walked through the field of reeds, felt the breeze against my skin, but I was never there. I doubt I ever will be.

speaker: Isidora
en: Never doubt it. I do not need to know what you've done to know there is a way. I will help you find it.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Aten. Akhenaten passed it to his successors. It could've been stolen from any of their tombs.

speaker: Isidora
en: I hear Tychon's funeral is taking place soon. Did his ledger reveal anything else? He knew the tombs quite well.

speaker: Bayek
en: No. Irsu, the bile that robbed Nefertiti's tomb, did say he was working with others, but... well.

speaker: Isidora
en: What happened? Is he dead?

speaker: Isidora
en: Soldiers coming. Please, you should not be seen

speaker: Isidora
en: ... here.

speaker: Captain
en: Priestess, a question. We've been investigating a ring of unsanctioned tomb robbers. Imagine my surprise when our prime suspect turns up dead. I know you had your... differences. So tell me, priestess, who killed Tychon?

speaker: Isidora
en: Tychon? Was he not one of yours? A comrade of your Strategos? perhaps one of his allies grew tired of sharing the profits of the desecrated tombs. Did you find a dagger in his back? There are many who wished his death, how will you narrow your search?

speaker: Captain
en: Steer clear of Tychon's funeral.

speaker: Captain
en: Do a thorough search. See what she's hiding.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: You don't really think the God's Wife of Amun is involved do you?

speaker: Soldier 2
en: There's nothing here but prayer scrolls.

speaker: Captain
en: She's neck deep, I know it. Find the evidence.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Look sharp. We can't return empty handed.

speaker: Bayek
en: A brazen thief such as Tychon will live in the richer part of Thebes. I should pay my respects to the dead.

speaker: Bayek
en: Their slavish mourning leaves me time to search his villa.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Strategos' men have already been through here. What did they miss?

speaker: Bayek
en: Tychon made a fortune trading our history to Rome.

speaker: Bayek
en: No charm could save him in the end.

speaker: Bayek
en: Desecration and thievery paid for his expensive tastes.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Strategos ordered his men to apprehend Tychon.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tychon and Irsu were working together.

speaker: Bayek
en: Locked, I need another way in.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tychon's papers were undisturbed.

speaker: Bayek
en: Treasures from the Pharaohs, quite a hoard.

speaker: Bayek
en: What is this?

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone else is looking for the relic. So who are you, Lotus? The ship docked in Swenett. That's my next port of call. I should find the scribe's office, the manifest might tell who the ship belongs to.

speaker: Bayek
en: The relic corrupts absolutely. Isidora can not believe this is the will of the gods!

speaker: Bayek
en: The High Priestess has summoned the Army of Anubis to protect her!

speaker: Bayek
en: The relic, it's twisting what I see. I must find her.

speaker: Bayek
en: Locked. Whatever her reasons for doing this, they must be behind this door.

speaker: Bayek
en: As the wife of the Hidden One, she would keep her secrets close.

speaker: Bayek
en: She's trying to finish what her mother started. There is a note, "as he restored the god, so can he restore balance."

speaker: Bayek
en: Texts on the Ma'at ritual by Nitokris, God's Wife of Amun. Could this be Isidora's mother?

speaker: Bayek
en: After Akhenaten's reign, his son Tutankhamun restored the temples of Amun. He gave the orb to the priests!

speaker: Bayek
en: She always had the relic.

speaker: Bayek
en: A hidden tomb in the Valley of the Kings. The thieves never found it.

speaker: Bayek
en: She could kill countless in her misguided quest for 'balance' and 'truth'. Her mother would not want this.

speaker: Bayek
en: She means to finish what her mother started. A ritual to restore Ma'at in the hidden tomb of the long forgotten pharaoh.

speaker: Bayek
en: I know what it is like to lose someone you love, but this orb corrupts everything it touches.

speaker: Isidora
en: Ir nif di 'inh (it is done for him who has given life)... You stalk me like common prey now?

speaker: Isidora
en: Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: Give me the orb. I do not want to kill you.

speaker: Isidora
en: My mother told me this is our role. To restore Ma'at and put Amun back on his throne. This is why I was born. This is why I had to hide and watch while they slit her throat. So I would have the strength to do Amun's will.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is not strength. This is savagery.

speaker: Bayek
en: This must end, Isidora! You betrayed Amun, our people, your duty. I will not betray mine.

speaker: Bayek
en: His father Akhenaten passed down the orb.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tutankhamun wanted to restore balance, entrusted it to the priests of Amun.

speaker: Bayek
en: But Isidora distorted the ritual in the name of vengeance. She betrayed her own gods.

speaker: Isidora
en: Amun chose you. I do not understand. This was my birthright, my revenge. Why did he hear my cry? Why did he gave me the power to finish what she started, only for me to fail?

speaker: Bayek
en: Amun never gave you power. He gave you a choice.

speaker: Isidora
en: The feather of Ma'at. No... my heart is too heavy. Do you... believe Amun will protect me?

speaker: Bayek
en: As easy as it is to do wrong, it's easy for Amun to be merciful.

speaker: Isidora
en: His wrath passess in a moment. His breath comes back in mercy...

speaker: Bayek
en: May the Hidden One walks with you. The lord of the Duat awaits.

speaker: Sutekh
en: Put me down. Put me down.

speaker: Sutekh
en: I think I can manage on my own.

speaker: Bayek
en: Can you?

speaker: Sutekh
en: I once thought I had no one left in the world. Now I am a descendant of Ramesses the Great, and I have a family bigger than I could have imagined. Small price to pay. Thank you, neb. What will you do now with... that horror?

speaker: Sutekh
en: By Ra's light, I don't want it.

speaker: Bayek
en: All the more reason you should take it. You better than anyone knows what it can do. Bury it and all memory of it.

speaker: Sutekh
en: Alright, but not here. There are not secrets left in this valley.

speaker: Bayek
en: There must be one more, Sen.

speaker: Sutekh
en: You restore Ma'at, then leave. If that's what you want, then no one will hear of you from me. Hey, Bayek.

speaker: Sutekh
en: We'll meet again in the Field of Reeds. I'll see to it!

speaker: Sutekh
en: That is alright. We do not need any help. We'll close all this up. In a moment.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Lazy peasants! Make yourselves useful!

speaker: Villager
en: Thank the gods!

speaker: Medunamun
en: Find the names of any villagers who visit the temple regularly. I want to question them all.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Of course, my lord.

speaker: Medunamun
en: Round up the oldest villagers for me to question.

speaker: Guard 2
en: The oldest, my lord?

speaker: Medunamun
en: One may have heard an ancient story or know about the vault. Fatigue grips me like a python. No one works as hard as I.

speaker: Guard 2
en: You are a martyr, my lord.

speaker: Medunamun
en: Is this meat? You know I do not eat meat.

speaker: Guard 2
en: I believe it is a local root vegetable, my lord.

speaker: Medunamun
en: What has become of the priest I questioned?

speaker: Guard 2
en: He died, my lord.

speaker: Medunamun
en: Find more priests!

speaker: Medunamun
en: You! You have returned.

speaker: Bayek
en: To right your wrong.

speaker: Medunamun
en: I die, my work unfinished. So close, so very close to ushering in the perpetual rule of the strong and virtuous!

speaker: Bayek
en: Virtue?

speaker: Medunamun
en: The vault will give us the power of the gods. What is one boy?

speaker: Bayek
en: What is one boy?!

speaker: Khemu
en: Papo?

speaker: Bayek
en: Oh, so close. Hey, one more, one more.

speaker: Khemu
en: Ok.

speaker: Bayek
en: Eh.

speaker: Khemu
en: Well... I can try. This way, I'll get two!

speaker: Bayek
en: Hehehe, sure.

speaker: Khemu
en: Well.

speaker: Bayek
en: Up...strong...ready?

speaker: Khemu
en: Yes.

speaker: Khemu
en: Oh, you made me miss. You...

speaker: Chenzira
en: Khemu, come here! I found a hyena cave!

speaker: Khemu
en: A real one?

speaker: Chenzira
en: Yes!

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah, go ahead.

speaker: Chenzira
en: You're gonna love it, there's like sixteen hyenas, and they're so dark and scary.

speaker: Khemu
en: Sixteen? Well, you know what, er, I'd rather go hunt with my papo.

speaker: Chenzira
en: You always get too scared.

speaker: Bayek
en: Eh! Eh, eh, let's go on a real hunt, huh?

speaker: Khemu
en: Alright.

speaker: Bayek
en: Come, come.

speaker: Khemu
en: What are we hunting?

speaker: Bayek
en: The Oracle wants the pelt of an ibex stag for the ceremony.

speaker: Chenzira
en: You will stand next to the Pharaoh, won't you, Bayek? You're the Medjay!

speaker: Khemu
en: When I'm Medjay, I'll stand next to the pharaoh.

speaker: Chenzira
en: You'll never be Medjay. You're too scared.

speaker: Khemu
en: That's not true.

speaker: Chenzira
en: What about the hyena cave?

speaker: Khemu
en: Shut up!

speaker: Bayek
en: Enough, you two.

speaker: Khemu
en: The sand is so hot on my feet!

speaker: Bayek
en: Sometimes, they light on fire. It makes you faster.

speaker: Khemu
en: Heh heh. I want my feet to light on fire!

speaker: Bayek
en: It is up ahead.

speaker: Chenzira
en: Can I come?

speaker: Bayek
en: Heh heh, your mother's waiting for you.

speaker: Chenzira
en: All right. See you at the ceremony, Khemu!

speaker: Khemu
en: Bye, Chenzira!

speaker: Bayek
en: The herd is around here. We don't want just any stag. We want the pack leader.

speaker: Khemu
en: Which one is he?

speaker: Bayek
en: Big, with giant horns. Quiet now. Do what I do.

speaker: Khemu
en: Senu! Senu, come to me!

speaker: Bayek
en: Why are you calling Senu?

speaker: Khemu
en: Chenzira told me I should steal his feathers, so that my weighing ceremony gets me to the Field of Reeds.

speaker: Bayek
en: Anubis weighs your heart against a feather. You cannot tamper with this weighing ceremony. It is sacred.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is my favorite part, stay low! They will spot us unless we become like Amun, the god of Hiddenness.

speaker: Khemu
en: Yes Papo, we are the hidden ones.

speaker: Khemu
en: Ahhh! Oh no! I scared them!

speaker: Bayek
en: It's okay, more time for us to spend together! Enjoy the journey. Stay with me. We can do it together. See? My eyes and hand are in line with the arrow. That is the only way to shoot true.

speaker: Khemu
en: I wish I could put a hundred arrows on this bow.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hit!

speaker: Khemu
en: Did you hurt him?

speaker: Bayek
en: A clean shot to the heart hardly hurts at all. Let's get that pelt.

speaker: Bayek
en: We will take this to the Oracle before it gets dark.

speaker: Khemu
en: One day, I want to shoot an arrow through the sun.

speaker: Bayek
en: You can. Your arrow will have to become Senu.

speaker: Khemu
en: Imagine: all my arrows are Senus! Then I will be able to hunt anything!

speaker: Bayek
en: You said you'd like to see the Pharaoh up close?

speaker: Khemu
en: Yeah.

speaker: Bayek
en: What if you stand with me by his side?

speaker: Khemu
en: Can I do that?

speaker: Bayek
en: As my son and the future Medjay, yes.

speaker: Khemu
en: Papo, what is a Medjay, really?

speaker: Bayek
en: The first Medjay was a protector of the pharaoh. But now it means you must protect all the people of Egypt. Not just protect them, but work for their well-being.

speaker: Khemu
en: Oh, papo! I am so excited to be Medjay one day. You know all the secrets of Siwa. What if I never grow up to be a Medjay?

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah, of course you will! You are my son!

speaker: Khemu
en: But I get scared. I try to be brave, but sometimes it's hard.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hold on. Let's go this way.

speaker: Bayek
en: When I was about your age. Sometimes, I got scared, too. Your grandfather was a well-known Medjay, and he wanted me to bring honor to the family when I succeeded him.

speaker: Khemu
en: Yeah?

speaker: Bayek
en: One day, he took me up this way. At the top, he said something to me. A single word. It changed me.

speaker: Khemu
en: One word?

speaker: Bayek
en: I got over my fear. I knew I could do anything I needed to.

speaker: Khemu
en: What did he say?

speaker: Bayek
en: I will tell you once we're there.

speaker: Khemu
en: What word did your father say?

speaker: Bayek
en: "Jump". Don't think so long. Jump!

speaker: Khemu
en: Yes, papo.

speaker: Bayek
en: Trust me. You can.

speaker: Khemu
en: I do! I will!

speaker: Bayek
en: Jump, then!

speaker: Bayek
en: Come back, you're not ready.

speaker: Khemu
en: I can do it, papo! I can!

speaker: Chenzira
en: Aaaaaaah!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Shut up, you filthy, little shit!

speaker: Chenzira
en: Help! Help me!

speaker: Khemu
en: That's Chenzira!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: I said shut up!

speaker: Bayek
en: Run home to your mother. Chenzira will be fine. I will take care of it.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Medjay Bayek!

speaker: Bayek
en: Go! Now.

speaker: Khemu
en: I'm scared. I don't want to go home alone.

speaker: Bayek
en: Khemu, just do what I say, please! Go!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Medjay Bayek!

speaker: Bayek
en: I am indeed Medjay here. Who summons me?

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Sheathe your weapon and follow me.

speaker: Chenzira
en: You said you only wanted to talk to him! Ow!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Come.

speaker: Bayek
en: Who are you to give commands to me?

speaker: Soldier 1
en: You piece of shit, we don't have time to piss away.

speaker: Chenzira
en: Aaaaaaah!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Ha!

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Make a sound and you're dead.

speaker: Medunamun
en: What took you so long?

speaker: Man 4
en: Didn't want to be seen, sir. Kept to the shadows.

speaker: Medunamun
en: We are pleased you have joined us, Medjay. It is of great importance that we gain access to the vault. The temple priests stubbornly refuse to assist us. You are perhaps reluctant out of loyalty to the Oracle. We have someone to help convince you otherwise.

speaker: Rebecca
en: Bayek! I thought they just wanted to ask him a question! What have I done?!

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Quiet!

speaker: Medunamun
en: Come along!

speaker: Khemu
en: Papo!

speaker: Masked Man 1
en: See that no one comes in.

speaker: Bayek
en: Khemu! Are you hurt?

speaker: Masked Man 2
en: Go ahead. Try it your way.

speaker: Bayek
en: Leave my son out of this!

speaker: Masked Man 3
en: Your son has something to explain to you. Would the Ibis show him the orb?

speaker: Medunamun
en: We believe we need this to enter the vault.

speaker: Masked Man 1
en: This is a waste of time!

speaker: Masked Man 3
en: The boy is frightened! It's all right.

speaker: Khemu
en: Papo (Father). They need you to tell them about the vault. They need to know how to use this.

speaker: Rudjek
en: As Medjay, you must have some clue or key or legend that explains its use.

speaker: Bayek
en: I don't know anything about this vault! Please, leave my son out of this!

speaker: Soldier 4
en: My lords! The Pharaoh has been roused! He insists on coming here!

speaker: Medunamun
en: We will be discovered!

speaker: Masked Man 3
en: Quickly!

speaker: Masked Man 2
en: Talk to your son. If the vault isn't open when we return, you'll never see him again.

speaker: Khemu
en: Papo. I did what you said, but

speaker: Bayek
en: It's all right, son.

speaker: Bayek
en: No?

speaker: Khemu
en: Papo. I can get it to you.

speaker: Bayek
en: No. Khemu, don't.

speaker: Khemu
en: They're going to hurt us.

speaker: Bayek
en: Khemu, they'll... Khemu.

speaker: Masked Man 1
en: This foolish waste of time!

speaker: Bayek
en: No, Khemu, Khemu. No, come, come, come, come, come.

speaker: Masked Man 1
en: Out of time! Tell us!

speaker: Bayek
en: Oh, oh, I don't know!

speaker: Masked Man 2
en: We must go now!

speaker: Masked Man 1
en: I will cut the heart from the boy.

speaker: Bayek
en: Wait, wait, wait, wait, wait! Stop!

speaker: Masked Man 1
en: He will never know the afterlife.

speaker: Bayek
en: No, no, no, I will tell you, I will tell you, I will tell... no, no, no.

speaker: Masked Man 1
en: He's stalling for time.

speaker: Masked Man 3
en: What's this?

speaker: Masked Man 2
en: Stop! This is madness!

speaker: Masked Man 1
en: The Snake takes that as your answer.

speaker: Bayek
en: No! No! Khemu! Khemu... no, no, no.

speaker: Masked Man 1
en: Shut up!

speaker: Medunamun
en: We thought you were dead. You could not even save your own son! You are no one. Bayek of nothing. Father to nobody.

speaker: Bayek
en: Here! Here! And here is your "nobody"!

speaker: Bayek
en: May the Hidden One greet you. The lord of the Duat awaits.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Well done, my friend! Our hero returns! You've brought joy to Siwa.

speaker: Bayek
en: I should get to Alexandria. I need to see Aya.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Don't be in too much of a hurry. Siwa will always need its Medjay.

speaker: Bayek
en: But you are the protector here now. I'm always pleased to help.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Come see me when you're certain you're ready to go. We will drink a beer to our friendship!

speaker: Aya
en: Completely silent. The animals, too.

speaker: Bayek
en: Some sort of plague has hit the village.

speaker: Aya
en: That viper Flavius did this.

speaker: Bayek
en: We should have ripped out his entrails long before now. Let us get to the vault.

speaker: Aya
en: Roman soldiers.

speaker: Bayek
en: Must be Flavius' men.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Take those intruders down!

speaker: Aya
en: It was Flavius all along. He brought Caesar and the Romans here, hoping to take complete power.

speaker: Bayek
en: We trusted him. We were fools.

speaker: Bayek
en: Rabiah! What happened here?

speaker: Rabiah
en: Quickly... Hepzefa... The vault!

speaker: Bayek
en: Rabiah, we will come back to you when we can.

speaker: Aya
en: Heavily fortified. Behave my love.

speaker: Aya
en: We must be careful not to be seen.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Intruders! Attack!

speaker: Aya
en: Bayek, there is trouble ahead.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: The vault is opening! Run for cover!

speaker: Aya
en: Look! The vault!

speaker: Bayek
en: They're frightened of the opening door.

speaker: Aya
en: They're running! Careful. We don't know what's in there.

speaker: Bayek
en: We must find out what happened.

speaker: Aya
en: Bayek. Are we dreaming?

speaker: Bayek
en: We have entered the Duat.

speaker: Aya
en: Who could imagine such a land as this?

speaker: Bayek
en: No man should approach this close to the gods.

speaker: Aya
en: Who created this? The gods themselves? Ah! Here is the story of mankind... Bayek? Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: It is Hepzefa. Oh, my seni (friend). Your life is done here in the desert dust. They took my closest friend.

speaker: Aya
en: We must rush to stop Flavius.

speaker: Bayek
en: No! We cannot leave him here. He deserves a proper farewell.

speaker: Aya
en: Go ahead, Bayek. I am with you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hepzefa knew nothing of the Order. There was no cause for him to be killed. Flavius ripped out his heart as a message to me. It was he who killed Khemu.

speaker: Aya
en: My husband, we will end this.

speaker: Rabiah
en: Bayek. Ah, you found poor Hepzefa.

speaker: Bayek
en: Rabiah.

speaker: Rabiah
en: I saw what happened. It was horrible. The Roman leaders entered the temple vault.

speaker: Aya
en: Septimius and Flavius.

speaker: Rabiah
en: The objects they carried opened it as if by a god's hand. Hepzefa tried to stop them, but they rendered him helpless. They entered the vault, a blue fire seemed to emerge. I fled to no avail. The entire village lost its reason and fell to the ground like dolls.

speaker: Villager 1
en: They have destroyed Siwa.

speaker: Villager 2
en: They must die!

speaker: Villager 1
en: You must put an end to this!

speaker: Rabiah
en: Bayek. Aya. You have the prayers of the entire village to support you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let us bring Hepzefa to his rest. Then we will seek justice.

speaker: Officiant
en: Let the embalmers come. We pray Anubis accept this ornament in place of his heart, such that Hepzefa may walk free in the Field of Reeds.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hepzefa, old friend. I miss our talks, Hepzefa. And drinking beer! Siwa needs you, Hepzefa. Hepzefa. Where are you now, my friend? Walking in the Field of Reeds? Hepzefa. I could use your help now, seni (friend).

speaker: Bayek
en: Grandfather, I have missed you. I only wish you could've know Khemu.

speaker: Bayek
en: Animals. Using the necropolis as a den. No wonder it looks like this.

speaker: Rabiah
en: Bayek, Hepzefa would have wanted you to have this. The weapon he prized above all others.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am honored.

speaker: Aya
en: Some villagers captured a Roman soldier and questioned him. Flavius is headed for Cyrene and Septimius for Alexandria.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will kill Flavius.

speaker: Aya
en: There is a farm at the border of Cyrene. Someone there may have seen Flavius pass through. As for me, I will cut out the heart of Septimius.

speaker: Bayek
en: I feel as though wherever we go, tragedy follows. Perhaps we should come to terms...

speaker: Aya
en: It is hard. I don't want to let go, but...

speaker: Bayek
en: Every time I think of you, I think of Khemu and everything we lost.

speaker: Aya
en: Me too. So for now. We kill.

speaker: Bayek
en: Farewell, Aya.

speaker: Bayek
en: It has been too long, son. Oh, Khemu. Khemu. Your mother and I speak of you all the time. Much has happened, Khemu. It is peaceful here, son. I have come to visit, son. Just for a moment.

speaker: Bayek
en: Flavius will not escape me again. Flavius will not stop until he reaches Rome. I just don't give a nek (shit) anymore. Nothing will stop me. I cannot stop until Flavius's heart is in my fist.

speaker: Villagers
en: Oh, great and ferocious Flavius! All hail the mighty mane of Flavius. Do not anger him, Flavius the lusty, the indomitable!

speaker: Bayek
en: A lush land of pastures and fields. Trampled on by Roman occupation.

speaker: Bayek
en: This must be the farm Aya spoke of. Someone must have seen the Lion pass through.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Stop, Mereruka! I beg you.

speaker: Praxilla
en: By my . Forgive me!

speaker: Bayek
en: Peace, I am not your enemy.

speaker: Praxilla
en: I am sorry, it is just... He was such a gentle soul, once had me treat a wounded dog he had caught in a snare... Why would he do this?

speaker: Bayek
en: I have seen this before, in Siwa. I'm looking for the soul-eater responsible. Flavius.

speaker: Praxilla
en: The proconsul?

speaker: Bayek
en: That sack of rancid goat shit murdered my son, razed my village and now marches through your land with the light of Amun-Ra... Come, let us search the farm, look for survivors. I am Bayek of Siwa.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Praxilla, of this land gone mad.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Why would Flavius do this? They are just poor Siwan farmers.

speaker: Bayek
en: They stood in his path.

speaker: Bayek
en: Fresh cart tracks and footprints.

speaker: Praxilla
en: The Romans have threatened to take the farmers to the Citadel before.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why?

speaker: Praxilla
en: To work on weapons, fortifications, General Agrippa's orders.

speaker: Praxilla
en: The cruelty Flavius inflicted here, it sickens me.

speaker: Bayek
en: He will not stop till he reaches Rome. Then it too will fall before his godless ambition.

speaker: Praxilla
en: There must be someone left alive, women... children?

speaker: Bayek
en: Perhaps someone is hiding?

speaker: Praxilla
en: Nenet! Are you alright? What happened here?

speaker: Nenet
en: Redcloaks and that milksop with the Lion's head. Took anyone who could work, farmhands, my son Kade. Everyone. Then He came. Dark eyes, hooded as a raven. I wanted to throw stones to shoo him off. Something golden, bright in his claws. Held it up, crowing as they fell before him. Some by their own hands, others by those dearest to them. Against nature. Everyone crying, screaming, running, dying.

speaker: Bayek
en: How did you es

speaker: Nenet
en: No one sees poor Nenet, an old woman's husk with clouded eyes. But I saw them. Didn't cry out. Bit my tongue 'til I choked on the blood.

speaker: Praxilla
en: The men who did this... We will find them.

speaker: Nenet
en: Better hurry, girl. Raven flew north to the home of the huntress.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will try. Flavius also robbed me of my boy.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Let us bring Nenet to my cart.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Will you follow Flavius?

speaker: Bayek
en: I must.

speaker: Praxilla
en: For your son?

speaker: Bayek
en: For every son.

speaker: Praxilla
en: You must miss him very much?

speaker: Bayek
en: All my waking and sleeping hours.

speaker: Praxilla
en: You will see him again in The Field of Reeds.

speaker: Bayek
en: I hope so. Nenet spoke of the home of the huntress?

speaker: Praxilla
en: Yes, Cyrene, the shining porticos of Roman conquest. It is north of here.

speaker: Bayek
en: If Flavius is there, I will find him and destroy every fiber of his ka.

speaker: Praxilla
en: When you arrive in Cyrene, look for my friend Diocles. I would trust him with my life, and yours. As a magistrate, he hears petitioners in the Agora... Give him this.

speaker: Bayek
en: I hope this heals the madness in this land.

speaker: Praxilla
en: I pray you get the justice you seek, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why would they take Nenet's son Kade?

speaker: Praxilla
en: The Citadel casts a long shadow over Cyrenaica. There are rumors that General Agrippa and Flavius are preparing for war.

speaker: Bayek
en: Against Egypt?

speaker: Praxilla
en: Do you doubt their ambition?

speaker: Bayek
en: No. They won't stop until I stop them.

speaker: Praxilla
en: I will bring Nenet to my clinic in Balagrae, south of the Temple of Aesclepius. Though that place has troubles enough.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will find you if I can.

speaker: Man 1
en: Worship him, worship him. Mars incarnate. Flavius of Cyrene!

speaker: Bayek
en: Flavius has taken their wits. This is not good or natural. Will they dance till their feet bleed?

speaker: Woman 1
en: Do you hear the beautiful music?

speaker: Man 2
en: Dance, dance, dance for Flavius!

speaker: Woman 2
en: We will have a Bacchanal!

speaker: Man 3
en: The Lord Flavius is our Muse.

speaker: Man 1
en: We offer you our true expression, God who walks among us.

speaker: Woman 1
en: I will dance till I can dance no more.

speaker: Man 2
en: Flavius has made us his Maenads.

speaker: Woman 2
en: He has given me ivy leaves to wear.

speaker: Man 3
en: I give my feet in service to Flavius, the god of war.

speaker: Man 1
en: Oh great and beauteous Flavius.

speaker: Man 2
en: Unconquered, heroic, furious Mars, rejoice in strife, and in the blood wars.

speaker: Man 3
en: Fierce you are, your mighty power can make the strongest peaks and deepest rivers shake.

speaker: Man 1
en: Walk, walk, into the flames. Flavius will burn away your crimes.

speaker: Man 2
en: Flavius makes our farms prosper, our children fat.

speaker: Bayek
en: They think Flavius is their god! What madness is this?

speaker: Man 1
en: The Lion's fire will cleanse you!

speaker: Man 3
en: Flavius our God. I was found wanting in his sight.

speaker: Man 1
en: Feel the searing heat of forgiveness.

speaker: Man 4
en: For Flavius! His Order is God.

speaker: Greek soldier
en: None shall take the healing weed. Stay away, these silphium fields are the property of the Republic.

speaker: Bayek
en: Flavius has made this man his mouthpiece.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Keep off the silphium plants! Flavius has decreed, all silphium is Roman silphium. By order of Flavius, Silphium belongs to the Republic. Taking silphium is punishable with death. Anyone stealing silphium will be executed! Silphium shall only fall to Roman scythes. Do not touch! Do not touch!

speaker: Bayek
en: So this is the shining city of Cyrene? Let's see how Romans have brought so-called civilization to the Greeks here.

speaker: Orator 1
en: An Ode to the Lion of Rome. Slender arrows are lodged in my heart. Love vexes the chest that it has seized. Shall I surrender or stir up the sudden flame by fighting it? Oh Flavius! I will surrender!

speaker: Bayek
