en: A Love poem? There's no end to Flavius' sick games.

speaker: Orator 1
en: A burden becomes light when it is carried willingly. And I am so willing. Your shining eyes, your raven hair, your manly gait, your skin so fair!

speaker: Woman
en: He's gone mad!

speaker: Orator 1
en: O Moon, you cannot share the same night as Flavius. Sun your light dims next to his radiance. Stars blink out, tides hold back. For you are nothing next to the Lion of Rome. I will drown myself in the pools of your eyes. I will sacrifice myself on the altar of your brow.

speaker: Man 1
en: An ode to Flavius? He's lost his wits.

speaker: Orator 1
en: Flavius, you stride in splendor, like a lion. You stride, with vital breath, while mountains watch in awe. Death has no dominion over the God who walks among us. But if you slept eternal, I would lie down and beg the ferryman to take me. My tears would fall like a silent scream. Dew on the petals of the radiant rose.

speaker: Man 2
en: And throw him in throw him in the sacred pool to cool off.

speaker: Orator 1
en: There is no purer love than mine. I'll follow you through all divine. My heart doth sigh with thought of you. I sit and yearn beneath the yew. Its branches shield me from your sun. O' shining and exalted one.

speaker: Citizen
en: Came back from Balagrae with a crook up his arse. Demanded my taxes for the year! They burned my farm when I refused!

speaker: Diocles
en: And you are sure it was Leander's men?

speaker: Citizen
en: My wife said no good would come of defying him. I hate it when she's right.

speaker: Diocles
en: Leander will pay. You have my word.

speaker: Citizen
en: Your word, Diocles? Will that sow my scorched fields? Bring my goats back to life? I am done with you, and this land. Your word... pah!

speaker: Diocles
en: And how has our most "venerated" magistrate extorted you, Egyptian?

speaker: Bayek
en: Praxilla said you could help me. I am Bayek.

speaker: Diocles
en: Is she alright?

speaker: Bayek
en: As well as anyone can be with Flavius desecrating your land. I've followed that fucker's murderous trail all the way from Siwa.

speaker: Diocles
en: So the rumors?

speaker: Bayek
en: True. As are his preparations for war.

speaker: Diocles
en: One more oppressor. Egypt will never be stable again. Invasions upon invasions. Flavius will make of Egypt one giant tomb. He rules from the Acropolis, but it's crawling with Romans. I pray the dice fall in your favour, Bayek. I must deal with his lapdog, the magistrate Leander. Seek me out again, if you would be a friend to Cyrene.

speaker: Bayek
en: Thank you, Diocles. It is time for my son to enter The Field of Reeds.

speaker: Orator 2
en: Even when your kind appears to triumph, still shall we rise again. The Order of Ancients is born of a realization. We need no creed, no indoctrination. We do not lurk in the shadows. We stride in the light.

speaker: Bayek
en: It is just Order of Ancients propaganda. Flavius has turned you into enemies of freedom.

speaker: Orator 2
en: Sons of Prometheus, you will follow us. Only by serving the Order can you be saved. Our only desire is that the world be as it is. A place of order, symmetry, harmony. The gods crave them. Out of the yawning veil of nothingness, the stygian void of chaos, Gaia emerged.

speaker: Orator 3
en: The free will advocated by these tricksters does not exist. Do not listen to them. They claim the people should be free to make their own choices. That we live without any form of laws and restraints. We say, "should the thief be free to steal your cattle? Should the murderer be free to extinguish the life of your son?"

speaker: Orator 4
en: You cannot stop us. We will have our new world. Pay no heed to the enemies of knowledge. Nothing happens randomly. All events we witness, we experience, happen for a reason and by necessity. They think they can break the shallow chains of determinism? They do not understand that the fabric of the universe is not woven from the threads of chaos, but of order. May the Father of Understanding guide us all.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: The Temple of Mars. Good to see our Roman Gods outside of Rome.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Proconsul Flavius scares the shit from my bowels.

speaker: Flavius
en: Do you think I can't feel you skulking in the shadows, Bayek of Siwa?

speaker: Bayek
en: I have followed your path of murder and madness all the way from my homeland. And now, you will answer for my son's death, Roman!

speaker: Flavius
en: No, Egyptian. Now, you will bow before your god!

speaker: Bayek
en: You murdered my son, my friends... Why didn't you kill me when you had the chance in Alexandria?

speaker: Flavius
en: You should have joined the Order! You need us. But you chose slavery.

speaker: Bayek
en: The man who killed my son. Cowering in another temple.

speaker: Flavius
en: Your Medjay friend Hepzefa also had a stubborn streak. Like your son.

speaker: Bayek
en: These are nothing but tricks. Your time on this sand has ended!

speaker: Flavius
en: Your mind will break eventually, just like all the others. My power, my potential, can you not feel it? You're nothing but a farmer. Camel-herders and shit-shovellers, that is all Egypt is.

speaker: Bayek
en: You robbed my son of his afterlife! I will cut your heart out!

speaker: Flavius
en: I am the Lion! None will mourn you, Medjay. I will rip your ka from your body.

speaker: Bayek
en: He was a child, Flavius. My child!

speaker: Flavius
en: That's the one thing I do not regret in my life.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will never give you peace!

speaker: Flavius
en: Your son's death made the Order bow to me. Caesar, even. I had Rome. It gave me an empire of a thousand sons, each one greater than the last.

speaker: Flavius
en: Come on, finish me, you coward! The waste of time!

speaker: Bayek
en: I can't do, I can't, I can't do it!

speaker: Khemu
en: It's all right, papo (father)...

speaker: Bayek
en: No... I will... I will lose you forever.

speaker: Khemu
en: Not forever. I will be waiting for you in the Field of Reeds.

speaker: Bayek
en: This relic should never be found again. Aya must know our son's ka has been put to rest.

speaker: Esiocles
en: Whoah! What's that man doing up there?

speaker: Esiocles
en: Mister, mister! Over here!

speaker: Esiocles
en: That was the greatest thing I ever witnessed and I once saw a snake swallow a cat whole!

speaker: Bayek
en: A cat really? And who are you?

speaker: Esiocles
en: Esiocles, but all my friends call me Esio.

speaker: Bayek
en: Well Esio, I am Bayek.

speaker: Esiocles
en: How did you do that? Are you magic? Will you leap some more for me and my friends? I can tell you about my home, the most amazing city of Cyrene as we go?

speaker: Bayek
en: How can I refuse such a gracious offer? Lead the way, Esio.

speaker: Esiocles
en: Me and my gang will give you the grand tour, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: You have a gang?

speaker: Esiocles
en: Yes, I'm the most important child in Cyrene.

speaker: Bayek
en: I can see that, Esio.

speaker: Esiocles
en: Let's go to the baths. It's where people walk around naked being scraped and scratched and rubbed with oils. I hate getting my hair wet, don't you Bayek?

speaker: Bayek
en: It is why I shaved it off, Esio. And washing behind the ears I bet?

speaker: Esiocles
en: Ha! yes! Some fancy Roman from the Citadel built it... Vi... Vitru... well anyway he spent ten thousand drachma on a floor made of little squares. All that for somewhere you wash! When I grow up, I am going to have a wife who'll never make me wash.

speaker: Bayek
en: Wives like that are hard to find, Esio.

speaker: Esiocles
en: Could you jump from up there?

speaker: Child
en: The top of the Baths?! That's a death sentence!

speaker: Bayek
en: Sure, Esio, I could do that with my eyes closed.

speaker: Esiocles
en: Come on everyone, come see Bayek fly!

speaker: Child 1
en: No-one can climb that high... can they?

speaker: Esiocles
en: See! Didn't I tell you he was brave?

speaker: Child 2
en: Oh my days, what if he falls?

speaker: Esiocles
en: He's stickier than a lizard on a rock.

speaker: Child 3
en: Yay, yeah! Whoohoo! Look at him go.

speaker: Child 2
en: Jump! Jump, Bayek. We're watching! Go!

speaker: Child 1
en: Go on! Anytime now! Jump!

speaker: Esiocles
en: Some of those scaredy cats thought you would miss the cart, but I never doubted you.

speaker: Bayek
en: I was not sure myself, Esio. So where's next?

speaker: Esiocles
en: You're Egyptian right? My father says you don't worship the same gods as we Greeks.

speaker: Bayek
en: We have some in common. Like Serapis.

speaker: Esiocles
en: Oh yes, Serapis. I've heard of him. Apollo is all Greek and my favorite. He likes poetry, music, wine and all that kind of stuff. But I like him because he has a bow and arrow and likes to hunt. Do you like to hunt, Bayek?

speaker: Bayek
en: I do, I used to hunt with my boy, Esio.

speaker: Esiocles
en: If you jump from his Temple there, then maybe he will be watching from Mount Olympus and reward me with my own bow and arrow so I can hunt rabbits in the woods!

speaker: Bayek
en: I would like to see that.

speaker: Esiocles
en: This is it! Isn't Apollo marvelous?

speaker: Child 1
en: It's impossible, right?

speaker: Child 2
en: He swoops through the air, like an eagle.

speaker: Esiocles
en: We are all watching.

speaker: Child 1
en: I can't watch! Tell me when it's over.

speaker: Child 2
en: He's so brave! Have you ever seen someone so brave?

speaker: Esiocles
en: And I am the one who found him.

speaker: Child 3
en: I know, Esio. This is the best of days.

speaker: Esiocles
en: Make Apollo proud, Bayek!

speaker: Esiocles
en: Apollo is sure to reward me now!

speaker: Child 1
en: You did it, you did it!

speaker: Child 2
en: Our friend Bayek does the impossible!

speaker: Esiocles
en: Let's go to the next jump! I have one last leap in mind for you, Bayek. Are you ready for your greatest challenge?

speaker: Bayek
en: Well that depends! Do you think I can do it?

speaker: Esiocles
en: I believe you can do anything, Bayek.

speaker: Child 1
en: I'm glad we joined Esio's gang, this is unbelievable.

speaker: Esiocles
en: Wait until I tell my sister about today! She used to play with me all the time, but now all she does is moon over that magistrate Diocles. And his stupid, floppy hair.

speaker: Bayek
en: Well, you did promise a challenge, Esio!

speaker: Esiocles
en: Nobody is allowed up there except the Romans. But you look like you can handle a few measly bucket heads. Are you ready, Bayek? I present the Acropolis. Don't let the Romans see you!

speaker: Child 1
en: Hera mother of gods! It's too high!

speaker: Child 2
en: Go on jump Bayek, jump from the tower!

speaker: Esiocles
en: I know you can do it! Don't think about the watery depths!

speaker: Child 3
en: No! No! I heard the Romans keep a in there!

speaker: Esiocles
en: Bayek can take on a kraken, can't you, Bayek?

speaker: Child 1
en: Can't you jump some more, Bayek? Please? It's my birthday!

speaker: Child 2
en: Liar! That was last month!

speaker: Esiocles
en: Stop crowding him. Stop crowding. He's not your slave. He is an important man with important things to do.

speaker: Child 1
en: Farewell Bayek. Come back when I'm older and we'll get married.

speaker: Child 2
en: Do you think with practice we could leap like that?

speaker: Esiocles
en: I won't forget this day Bayek. We should honor it. I officially name you the flea of Cyrene.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will treasure it. Goodbye Esio, stay out of trouble.

speaker: Esiocles
en: I can't promise, but I will try, for you, Great Flea. I hope you get to hunt with your son again soon!

speaker: Bayek
en: So do I, Esio.

speaker: Esiocles
en: Flea! I told my sister about you and she forgot all about Diocles! Look everyone! It's the Flea of Cyrene.

speaker: Nena
en: Warriors of Anubis. He breathed his divinity into them, made them the guardians of balance. The strongest among them. You must take his potent spark.

speaker: Essence of God
en: The potent spark of a warrior of the Jackal.

speaker: Bayek
en: Great wanderer of the endless fields, forgive me.

speaker: Man 1
en: Stop pissing off the foreman! Last thing we need is to get shipped off to the aqueduct!

speaker: Man 2
en: That place is the bowels of Hades. I saw cousin Houi yesterday he said the Romans will start making examples of people soon, cut a few threads.

speaker: Man 1
en: Romans! Ha! Sometimes I wonder if we made the right decision coming here... Faiyum was not so bad.

speaker: Man 2
en: The foreman sent a guard to check on us? We were not complaining! We were working hard!

speaker: Bayek
en: I am not a guard, I am a Medjay from Siwa. Does he treat you badly? The work here looks back-breaking.

speaker: Man 1
en: No! Compared to the Siwans up at the aqueduct we are revered like pharaohs!

speaker: Man 2
en: I would not go that far.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are there problems at the aqueduct?

speaker: Man 1
en: Some snooty engineer, Vitruvius. He is working our countrymen to death. And now the Roman army is involved. Which is never good...

speaker: Bayek
en: I will see what is going on, seni (friend).

speaker: Roman soldier
en: Maybe the lash will loosen your tongue.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: Enough! My workers are not to blame. Send me some soldiers with half a brain, or we'll never find my .

speaker: Roman Soldier
en: General Agrippa will hear of this! A Roman standing up for Egyptians! Pathetic!

speaker: Vitruvius
en: Tell Agrippa I need real soldiers who will help me find these thieves! Now scuttle back to your wine you sacks of uselessness.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you the one responsible for working my people to death?

speaker: Vitruvius
en: Your people? They are my people, I'm keeping them alive in the face of increasingly bad odds. But who are you, my Egyptian friend?

speaker: Bayek
en: Bayek of Siwa. Protector of these people.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: Well Bayek of Siwa, I am Vitruvius and contrary to popular belief not all Roman are your enemy. If you would help your people, then help me. Our tools have been stolen. My surveying tool, the dioptra specifically. Without it construction has stalled on the aqueduct. The General's idiots believe my workers are to blame.

speaker: Bayek
en: Maybe I can look for this... dioptra?

speaker: Vitruvius
en: With it, this elevated river would flow into the farms of Cyrenaica. Talk to Dedi up at the construction site. He used it last. Fortuna go with you, Bayek of Siwa.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you Dedi?

speaker: Dedi
en: Hades' fiery crotch! I did not take it, please do not kill me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Dedi, wait!

speaker: Bayek
en: Calm down, I won't hurt you, just tell me where the dioptra is.

speaker: Dedi
en: It was lunchtime and my wife brought me a fresh roasted chicken leg for lunch which was nice as it has been an eon since I had...

speaker: Bayek
en: Sounds delicious but get to the part about the master's tool? Your lunch won't solve this crime...

speaker: Dedi
en: Oh I see. Well I left the dioptra in the cave and when I came back it was gone. Scrobbled away by wolves, spirits or worse!

speaker: Bayek
en: What does this dioptra look like?

speaker: Dedi
en: Like a brazier, made of three parts. A bit you see through, a bit you measure with...

speaker: Bayek
en: I will find it, just try not to die of fright before then.

speaker: Dedi
en: Please find the dioptra. My head looks so much better attached to my shoulders!

speaker: Bayek
en: A bandit den. Well at least we know it was not spirits that stole the tool.

speaker: Bayek
en: Looks like a piece of the dioptra.

speaker: Bayek
en: Part of the missing surveying tool.

speaker: Bayek
en: Another piece of the tool.

speaker: Bayek
en: I should return to Vitruvius, before the Romans make an example of Dedi.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: You have it? You have my dioptra?

speaker: Bayek
en: I found it in a bandit camp above the aqueduct.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: Really? Some of my workers complained of hearing whispers from there, believed it was haunted. I was sure it was just superstitious nonsense.

speaker: Bayek
en: I dealt with it. Nothing will haunt you now, living or dead.

speaker: Vitruvius
en: Excellent and now General Agrippa has no more reason to bully my workers. He's become more ambitious since Flavius returned from Siwa and it is not a welcome change. Thank you Bayek, you saved my... our people's lives. I am in your debt.

speaker: Bayek
en: Fortuna smile on you, Vitruvius. Your work will help a lot of people in Cyrenaica.

speaker: Bayek
en: They'll have peace until the Romans send another general. It is endless! We must make the Hidden Ones as enduring as the Order.

speaker: Amunet
en: There is a more immediate problem. Gamilat. The people look on him as if upon a god. They glorify his every action.

speaker: Bayek
en: He fights for the people's freedom.

speaker: Amunet
en: You and I just witnessed a massacre. I have spoken to the villagers. There have been many such massacres. Gamilat witnessed a man and a woman being killed by the soldiers, but stopped his men from interfering.

speaker: Amunet
en: In each, Gamilat sends his rebels to provoke the Romans. The rebels hide among the villagers, inviting the Roman backlash to fall upon the most vulnerable. Many villagers are slaughtered in the fight.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are saying he does this knowingly?

speaker: Aya
en: This tactic creates martyrs for the cause, and families eager to take vengeance upon the Romans.

speaker: Bayek
en: His plan was to cause a slaughter to recruit more rebels?

speaker: Amunet
en: He's done this again and again. He is building a rebellion at a terrible price.

speaker: Bayek
en: He is a friend.

speaker: Amunet
en: Recall, that Cleopatra was more than a friend, yet I trusted her too well. You helped me see my mistake.

speaker: Bayek
en: He and I must talk.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am astonished by Gamilat's actions. Is he leading the rebellion for personal power?

speaker: Amunet
en: I don't think so. I believe he wants the rebellion to succeed so badly, that he is blind to the cost. He genuinely sees the villagers as martyrs. He does not consider that they had no choice. And the tactic has been successful! He will certainly use it when the Romans send another general.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tell me of your life in Rome.

speaker: Amunet
en: It's a marvelous place. Full of intrigue, deceit and corruption. The perfect city for a Hidden One!

speaker: Bayek
en: Ha! I expected you to talk about the wine!

speaker: Amunet
en: The wine is very good. You should come visit sometime. We'll have a taste.

speaker: Bayek
en: I might do that.

speaker: Bayek
en: It is ahead.

speaker: Amunet
en: He will be surrounded by his rebels.

speaker: Bayek
en: They see him as a god. We cannot challenge him in front of them.

speaker: Haganu
en: Now that Rufio has fallen, so shall Rome! All hail the Hidden Ones, who have freed us from Roman rule. Rufio thrashes in the Duat, drowning in the river of Jackals, clasped in the grip of the Lady of Slaughter. I will never tire of telling the legends, for they write themselves, they burn inside the sands of the Sinai.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 1
en: Awful young, aren't you? Come here, play soldier. Have a laugh.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 2
en: I have no reason to laugh.

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 1
en: Sure, it is all very serious. Why are you here, then?

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 2
en: To honor my father, killed by the Romans.

speaker: Bayek
en: Neb! (Sir!) Where is your leader?

speaker: Egyptian Soldier 3
en: Gamilat is on a hunt near the oasis.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'll go speak to Gamilat. You stay here. Keep the rebels away.

speaker: Amunet
en: Fight well.

speaker: Bayek
en: Gamilat. The great hope of the Nabateans. I'm about to disappoint them all.

speaker: Gamilat
en: Bayek. What is this about?

speaker: Bayek
en: You have been provoking massacres. Many innocent villagers have died.

speaker: Gamilat
en: I have exposed the vile cruelty of the Romans. The martyrs have inspired countless warriors to continue the fight.

speaker: Bayek
en: "Martyrs"?

speaker: Gamilat
en: What are the lives of a few villagers in light of freedom for all?

speaker: Bayek
en: The "lives of a few villagers"? They had no choice in the matter.

speaker: Gamilat
en: Bayek, don't be absurd. We fight on the same side!

speaker: Bayek
en: No. Here, we simply fight.

speaker: Gamilat
en: So be it.

speaker: Gamilat
en: You will be the ultimate martyr. You cannot harm me now. You fight well, Hidden One. But my shield is the strongest in all the Sinai.

speaker: Gamilat
en: It's over, Bayek. I have the high ground.

speaker: Gamilat
en: Raaaah! This gives me no pleasure. Let's end this once and for all! Burn, Bayek! Let your accusations turn to ashes. Your blows will glance off this shield. You have become a torch for the cause! Now, you are done for!

speaker: Bayek
en: There is freedom, and there is the life of innocents. Both must be balanced on the scale.

speaker: Gamilat
en: It is now my heart that will lie upon the scale of Anubis.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your heart beat too strongly in favor of its cause. The innocent must always be protected.

speaker: Gamilat
en: My ardor shone like sun in my eyes, blinding me. You have done right by me. I accept this death.

speaker: Bayek
en: From this day, no Hidden One will raise a sword against an innocent. So it shall be written.

speaker: Bayek
en: May you find peace in the Duat.

speaker: Gamilat
en: And may the Hidden Ones last until the end of time.

speaker: Haganu
en: The greatest of leaders, Gamilat, is now dead, and his story lives on in the warriors of the Sinai. He could kill a million tyrants with one breath, a divine arrow, the great Gamilat is no longer! (Humming)

speaker: Amunet
en: Should we kill their dreams?

speaker: Bayek
en: Let them have their heroes. For now the Hidden Ones are forgotten, this is in our favor. Gamilat's death serves a higher cause.

speaker: Amunet
en: No more senseless martyrs.

speaker: Bayek
en: Have we done good?

speaker: Amunet
en: Our tenets need to be passed on to those who have taken our oath, so they have a true creed to study.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Hidden Ones will pass onto Petra and towards Judea. And forever. The Creed must live beyond any one.

speaker: Amunet
en: No one shall be bigger than the greater group. When I return to Rome I will not speak of heroes, I will speak of discipline and perseverance.

speaker: Bayek
en: Amunet is a Mentor to this brotherhood. Our will never rests...

speaker: Amunet
en: ... and our blades shall never tire.

speaker: Amunet
en: We have done good.

speaker: Bayek
en: Khemu would often speak of Senu as my 'Horus'. "Pappo, her keen eye protects you".

speaker: Bayek
en: Rabiah!

speaker: Rabiah
en: Bayek! It does my heart good to have you again in Siwa.

speaker: Bayek
en: You nursed Senu back to health. I never expected to see her again.

speaker: Rabiah
en: She is a tough old bird.

speaker: Bayek
en: Like you!

speaker: Rabiah
en: Ah, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hepzefa' tells me you are healing the villagers as best you can. It would give me much pleasure to help you.

speaker: Rabiah
en: That is kind of you. May your ka(soul) be blessed. I can always use help. The soldiers are brutes. Almost every villager has cuts, bruises, broken bones. To help them, I put together a makeshift ("house of life") in the old ruined temple. Friends bring me medicines from Yamu, but now the soldiers stop everyone entering the village and steal their goods. So we tried to bring medicine on a boat instead.

speaker: Bayek
en: And the soldiers stopped that also.

speaker: Rabiah
en: They sank the last shipment. The medicine jars are scattered across the bottom of the lake.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will get them for you.

speaker: Rabiah
en: Thank you Bayek. Bring it to the old temple. I must go there now.

speaker: Bayek
en: The medicine could be anywhere in this lake. Senu can help me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Rabiah is waiting for these jars.

speaker: Rabiah
en: Ah Bayek, Amun be praised.

speaker: Bayek
en: What has happened? Why aren't the patients in the temple ruins?

speaker: Rabiah
en: The soldiers threw us out. Even though I pay the nomarch to allow me to use the temple, every few weeks soldiers come to take our medicine and food stocks. Always the same soldiers. They call it a "tribute", a tax for the Pharaoh's Royal Army. We barely have what's needed to take care of the poor souls that need our help.

speaker: Bayek
en: Vultures. Don't worry Rabiah, I will make certain they don't bother you anymore.

speaker: Rabiah
en: Be careful, Bayek.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: It's hardly worth raiding this camp.

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: I don't like raiding this place. Full of diseases. What if the nomarch finds out about our raids?

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: He doesn't give a fig about this smelly bog.

speaker: Greek Soldier 3
en: Damn. Not much here this time.

speaker: Rabiah
en: Bayek! Did you succeed?

speaker: Bayek
en: The temple is yours now. Those soldiers won't bother you again.

speaker: Rabiah
en: All my patients thank you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah, I almost forgot to give you your medicines from the sunken boat.

speaker: Rabiah
en: Ha, ha. In all the excitement, I forgot about them myself!

speaker: Bayek
en: The oasis of Siwa is lucky to have you, Rabiah.

speaker: Rabiah
en: Ha, ha. Promise me you will not become consumed with your vengeance, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: I think of nothing else. By the grace of Amun, one day I will be free of it.

speaker: Isidora
en: Tychon conducts his business around Hatshepsut's Temple area.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let's hope this thief keeps a records of his spoils.

speaker: Prayer of Amun
en: The prayer that Isidora gave Bayek to protect him from the heretic Akhenaten.

speaker: Tychon
en: Curse be damned, that fool will get us all killed.

speaker: Bodyguard
en: Didn't you and he work together?

speaker: Tychon
en: Not for years. Irsu's a loathsome maggot who's murder his own mother.

speaker: Bodyguard
en: And how's your mother these days?

speaker: Tychon
en: That's different, she started it.

speaker: Tychon
en: Who sent you? That bastard Irsu? Or one of the others?

speaker: Bayek
en: Some kind of code, about the artifacts they took from the Pharaoh's tombs. And this...

speaker: Bayek
en: Tychon hides all his stolen treasures at the Temple of Hatshepsut.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hail to thee, maker of all, creator of existence, chief of the gods. Hail to thee, Amun-Ra, lord of all the thrones in the world.

speaker: Dust of Amun
en: At Isidora's behest Bayek scraped this dust from the golden statue of Amun. He must use it to consecrate Akhenaten's tomb to the true gods.

speaker: Bayek
en: All the signs lead to Akhenaten being buried with the great Pharaohs'.

speaker: Bayek
en: Empty. I need to scatter the dust from Amun's statue somewhere else. I need to find more clues to the Aten.

speaker: Anubis Warrior
en: You do not belong here. There is nothing here for one such as you.

speaker: Bayek
en: I promised to consecrate this tomb to Amun. I can start by defiling this vision of Akhenaten.

speaker: Bayek
en: The ceremony in the farmlands. Djehuty believed the statues contained Akhenaten's spirit. Maybe destroying them will release it?

speaker: Bayek
en: The rays of the Aten, they are pointing to the statues of the Heretic Pharaoh.

speaker: Bayek
en: The false idols need to be destroyed.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is where it ends, at the temple.

speaker: Bayek
en: By Ra's light!

speaker: Bayek
en: The great god dies.

speaker: Bayek
en: And the Aten is taken up by his successor.

speaker: Bayek
en: Was he ever a god, or only a mortal? I banish you to the radiant planes.

speaker: Rudjek
en: You are the Medjay from Siwa? I thought Medjays were supposed to protect the pharaoh?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am Medjay to no pharaoh. You see this?

speaker: Rudjek
en: I can read my own name, nek! (Shit!) We will find you. We will find you, in your sleep!

speaker: Bayek
en: Sleep? I never sleep. I just wait. In the shadows. And I will kill you all. Everyone who sniffed the air that day in Siwa.

speaker: Man
en: Excuse me! I'm looking for a man named Bayek. I'm here to give you passage to the Sinai.

speaker: Haganu
en: In blackest night, the Sinai sleeps, exhausted with grief. Our mouths filled with ashes, we weep tears of blood. Who will deliver us from despair? (Humming)

speaker: Haganu
en: Our hero moves with the mist, as silent as the sea, delivering death. Unknown, unseen, ever forgiving. (Humming) Listen. Let me tell you of him. The Legend of Siwa. The shadow who is Bayek. Bayek... (Humming)

speaker: Bayek
en: Sounds like quite a man.

speaker: Jarha
en: Hush your racket, auntie. You will just make the Hippos excited. Or call the bandits back.

speaker: Woman
en: Is-is that him?

speaker: Jarha
en: No, not Meketre.

speaker: Woman
en: But where is Meketre? What will we do without my cherished Meketre?

speaker: Jarha
en: I cannot worry about that now. If things do not change, the crops will rot and we will starve!

speaker: Jarha
en: Neb, you look strong, and carry yourself without fear. Can you help a poor farmer?

speaker: Bayek
en: Your friend was killed by a hippo.

speaker: Jarha
en: Yes! The beasts' rampage slaughtered many! Yesterday, we were attacked by bandits. In their wake, they disturbed these hippos, and drove them into our fields. The gods seem content to piss on us. We cannot harvest the crops, nor can we put the dead to rest with the hippos in our fields.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let me help you collect the dead.

speaker: Jarha
en: Hmm. Poor cousin.

speaker: Woman
en: Is it him?

speaker: Jarha
en: No, not Meketre.

speaker: Jarha
en: No, not him. I would help you, but I am no match for those beasts.

speaker: Jarha
en: Hmm.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is this Meketre?

speaker: Jarha
en: Not this. This is my wife's brother's son. He was a fool. A brave fool. But a fool.

speaker: Woman
en: My poor Meketre is-is gone!

speaker: Bayek
en: The last one, I think.

speaker: Jarha
en: And Meketre not among them.

speaker: Woman
en: What will I do now?

speaker: Jarha
en: Thank you, neb. Their souls will now rest in peace.

speaker: Bayek
en: Who is this Meketre your aunt mourns?

speaker: Jarha
en: Our protector. Brave and strong, like you! He would chase away fierce animals, or the bandits who plague us. I guess there is no one left who can keep us safe...

speaker: Bayek
en: Such are a curse upon all of Egypt, it seems. Where do these bandits roost?

speaker: Jarha
en: There is a canyon. I would take you there, but it is far too dangerous... also, someone must deal with the dead.

speaker: Bayek
en: Of course... I will find it.

speaker: Jarha
en: The bandits are known as the Hungry Great Ones. May the gods protect you!

speaker: Woman
en: Will I ever see my dear Meketre again?

speaker: Bayek
en: Hush, nebet. We do not know he has crossed over yet.

speaker: Woman
en: Without him, no one will help me tend the field. Or keep me safe. Or sing to me under the stars.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will see what I can find.

speaker: Meketre
en: Psst! Will you free me?

speaker: Bayek
en: Let me get you out of here.

speaker: Meketre
en: Hurry. These bandits breed like rats.

speaker: Meketre
en: Thank you. But why did you save me?

speaker: Bayek
en: Your aunt spoke of your desperate straits. I would free any unjust captive, but the plight of a protector is something I cannot ignore.

speaker: Meketre
en: You are a Medjay!

speaker: Bayek
en: We are of the same brotherhood.

speaker: Meketre
en: Yes! I must hurry home. The war chief, Fat Homer, took the Hungry Great Ones on a raid! You move like a lion! Would you help me stop them?

speaker: Villagers
en: No! The Hungry Great Ones are going to kill us all! Where is our protector!? Why have the gods abandoned us!? Run! Run or else you'll be taken by the Hungry Great ones!

speaker: Bayek
en: Meketre, I think we are done. You fought like a lion, yourself.

speaker: Meketre
en: I have learned much from you! You've made me a better protector. Egypt needs more people like you.

speaker: Bayek
en: The land needs more people like us.

speaker: Meketre
en: I will sing songs of our battle to my aunt to remember this day.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ha.

speaker: Bayek
en: If I am to find the Hyena, I must first speak to Mered, Apollodorus' contact. He's a merchant somewhere in this marketplace.

speaker: Mered
en: Welcome to Mered's Wares, traveler. Well? What do you think?

speaker: Bayek
en: Junk.

speaker: Mered
en: Be off, then.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah, I haven't finished.

speaker: Mered
en: Are you blind? I've nothing left to show you.

speaker: Bayek
en: But you've much to tell me. About the Hyena.

speaker: Mered
en: Ah, funny. As it turns out, that happens to be the most expensive thing I'm offering.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hm, funny indeed.

speaker: Mered
en: Delivery upon payment. Do you have enough to barter with me?

speaker: Bayek
en: Here, your absurd fee. Now what can you tell me?

speaker: Mered
en: The Hyena... is not her real name.

speaker: Mered
en: Hahahaha! Easy, easy! A poor attempt at humor, I'm afraid. Her name is Khaliset.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where can I find her?

speaker: Mered
en: A favor. Some customers of mine took my horse after a dispute. Their camp lies in a quarry just south of here. Take my men, retrieve my horse, and I'll give you what you came for.

speaker: Bayek
en: Agh, how you found yourself in Apollodorus' company escapes me.

speaker: Mered
en: You'll get it for me... if Apollodorus wants my continued service... A favor for a favor. My mount, for the Hyena's location. Give my men a hand. They'll know exactly what to look for. It'll be easy. Get going, before those bastards do something stupid with my mount.

speaker: Warrior
en: You are friends with Mered?

speaker: Bayek
en: Argh, barely. He is a necessary ally.

speaker: Warrior
en: Mered rarely keeps protectors as allies. He doesn't trust authorities. But he pays well. And very few pay at all here in Giza. Cannot trust the sand in your hand.

speaker: Bayek
en: What can you tell me of the Hyena? This Khaliset girl?

speaker: Warrior
en: Ha ha! We speak one word, and we are Hyena food. Nice try. Come on! Be on guard, we have a horse to retrieve.

speaker: Bayek
en: This must be Mered's horse. He neglected to tell me his "customers" were bandits.

speaker: Mered
en: You're back! Well, look at this!

speaker: Bayek
en: You failed to mention it was in the possession of bandits.

speaker: Mered
en: Slipped my mind! Hmm... good. Stronger than mine.

speaker: Bayek
en: I thought you said it was yours...

speaker: Mered
en: Ahem, yes! Yes, of course it is! You've done good by me, my friend.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then you'll deliver as promised.

speaker: Mered
en: My word is my word... but I've one more thing to ask of you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ack, I'm done with your games.

speaker: Mered
en: All right... the Hyena lives in a cavern just over those hills. Day and night, she roams the desert, collecting silica. Precious tear drops of the gods. What has happened to those who have interfered is best left unsaid.

speaker: Bayek
en: If I find you've led me on another futile chase, it won't be my words that hit your ears.

speaker: Mered
en: A thousand promises. I have no reason to defy you. Don't die out there. (laughs) Khaliset takes shelter in a cave in the hills behind Menkaure.

speaker: Mered
en: Hey! That's my horse!

speaker: Bayek
en: You can't steal something already stolen, Mered.

speaker: Bayek
en: So this is the Hyena's lair. No sign of Khaliset, though. Mered was telling the truth. I need to figure out where she went.

speaker: Prisoner
en: I do not want to die! Help! Help me! Please! Do not... do not let her take me! Please! Get me out!

speaker: Prisoner
en: Mercy. Thank you, Medjay.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Hyena. Where is she?

speaker: Prisoner
en: I do not know. I am... I'm the only one left! She took the others away hours ago!

speaker: Bayek
en: Took them where?

speaker: Prisoner
en: She kills them! I know it! She... she... her hands. Oh, gods! Her hands are so bloody.

speaker: Bayek
en: Peace, friend. You are free. I will deal with Khaliset.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where is Khaliset taking captives? And why?

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone has made this their home.

speaker: Bayek
en: A letter. The symbol of the Snake is on it. Khaliset is clearly working with the Order. And they don't know she took some of this silica for herself. What was worth the danger of crossing the Order?

speaker: Bayek
en: This is where Khaliset slept, protected from sandstorms. The lotus flower of rebirth. She must have picked these for a reason.

speaker: Bayek
en: Now why would one of her loyal beasts be caged?

speaker: Bayek
en: Khufu's tomb. She has detailed every crevice. Ah, she has not finished. That is where I will find her. I will head to the pyramids.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hyenas... Khaliset must be inside.

speaker: Khaliset
en: You! Who dares enter here, where silence has befallen her?

speaker: Bayek
en: A Medjay who has treaded many dunes to find you. Hide if you must, Hyena, but this tomb will not protect you.

speaker: Khaliset
en: I demand that you stop here. Turn back now, and I will excuse this intrusion.

speaker: Bayek
en: Siwa was an intrusion.

speaker: Khaliset
en: Foolish man, I am Iset, possessor of magic, the gods live here, not you!

speaker: Bayek
en: What sort of mischief is she entertaining?

speaker: Khaliset
en: Be gone! Osiris cannot be disturbed!

speaker: Bayek
en: This trap door, what is it protecting?

speaker: Khaliset
en: Heathen! The wakeful one is asleep. Go no further, or I will drench these arid plains with your blood!

speaker: Bayek
en: What is this place? A tomb beneath a tomb... Is this where you hide, Hyena?

speaker: Bayek
en: What gruesome madness happened here!? A dark place with a window to the gods. What kind of ritual is she performing?

speaker: Bayek
en: Still warm. And this ceremonial knife. This was a sacrifice.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hrm... Khaliset drew these symbols here. Was she trying to figure out their meaning?

speaker: Bayek
en: Offerings to Osiris. Protector of the dead.

speaker: Bayek
en: This sarcophagus is decorated with goddesses of the mother. Strange symbols are marked all over it. I think I know what dark deeds Khaliset was after here.

speaker: Bayek
en: Khaliset was doing a ritual. She began by calling to Osiris with these offerings. She used a knife to sacrifice her captives. She collected their blood for some dark purpose. She was attempting to learn these strange symbols. She must have found them in this room. Once she knew the symbols, she carved them here. And ended the ritual with a final prayer over the sarcophagus. Khaliset must be trying to bring someone back to life. But just who is buried down here?

speaker: Bayek
en: Child...

speaker: Khaliset
en: My child!

speaker: Bayek
en: You lost your child?

speaker: Khaliset
en: I haven't. Her rest is temporary. You have intervened in her reawakening.

speaker: Bayek
en: And yet, you aligned yourself to the Order. Ravaged this tomb. Khaliset

speaker: Khaliset
en: Don't you dare say my name! My name does not merit your lips, you who have dishonored her! I am a good mother! Hiyaah!

speaker: Khaliset
en: You are no match for me, desert scum!

speaker: Khaliset
en: You are no different than any of the others who have come before you! Come! Fight me if you must. Then your blood will be part of my daughter's resurrection. I will bury you in the sand, fool.

speaker: Khaliset
en: Now, I will show you what happens to those who desecrate my daughter's tomb! Hiyaah!

speaker: Khaliset
en: Hathor, protect me from this defiler.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have come only for you, Hyena. The gods need not be involved.

speaker: Khaliset
en: You have infringed upon Eshe's place of rest, trespasser. The gods are already involved. And so you will find the same fate as all other trespassers. Death by my hand.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are in pursuit of the impossible, Khaliset. No measure of magic can bring our children back.

speaker: Khaliset
en: My child will come back through the powers of Those Who Came Before.

speaker: Bayek
en: Only the gods came before.

speaker: Khaliset
en: Some came between the gods and us. It is their gift. You cannot defeat me, Medjay! Come and face me! My heart bleeds without my Eshe by my side. Be thankful. Your blood will help bring her back.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your daughter is dead, Khaliset. Nothing will return her. Nothing can.

speaker: Khaliset
en: I will save my daughter no matter the cost. Enough of your pointless words!

speaker: Bayek
en: Then heed my weapon instead, Hyena.

speaker: Khaliset
en: Hahahahaha! This is who they send after me? The bugs on my beasts are fiercer!

speaker: Bayek
en: You would be best to give yourself up, Khaliset. I know your pain.

speaker: Khaliset
en: You know nothing of my pain!

speaker: Bayek
en: No child would want this from their parent, Hyena!

speaker: Khaliset
en: Do not speak of what my child wants! You fight like a man without passion! Lay down your weapon. It will be faster that way. Are you ready to be part of something greater than yourself, Medjay?

speaker: Khaliset
en: Do I walk among the dead now?

speaker: Bayek
en: A just end. You defiled the dead and enabled the people who killed my son. All on a selfish whim.

speaker: Khaliset
en: No! I gathered the silica for them—it powered the magic stone of Those Who Came Before. You saw it, didn't you? The symbols only needed to be learned.

speaker: Bayek
en: It is not meant for us.

speaker: Khaliset
en: It makes no difference now. I wanted to protect my daughter in life and death. I have done neither...

speaker: Khaliset
en: Osiris! Please grant me a reunion. She walks alone in the Field of Reeds! Am I to remain in the Duat forever?!

speaker: Khaliset
en: I just want my daughter back... please!?

speaker: Bayek
en: May you find your daughter in the afterlife, Khaliset. May the Lord of the Duat guide you.

speaker: Mered
en: You have returned... alive.

speaker: Bayek
en: You have your horse, and the desert is free of the Hyena. Why so disappointed, Mered?

speaker: Mered
en: Ah it is nothing. I bet that you would die within those walls, Medjay. You come out, I lose money. Ah! I know. Maybe you can throw a corpse in there for me? We both win!

speaker: Bayek
en: I pray this be the last time we meet, Mered.

speaker: Mered
en: Did I tell you of the time I ate a scorpion? I have no feeling in my mouth whatsoever. Thanks again for that horse, friend. But... had to sell him on. One time, long ago, I chased the Hyena down myself. But you're not interested in that! You're interested in Mered's wares! I had an unbreakable sword! I thought of you, but, another buyer came around. Business. I bet you wish you could work for ol' Mered, eh Bayek? Think of the life! But, no, he's already got his men.

speaker: Bayek
en: The bloodless titan! Forgive me Sobek, I must slay your son.

speaker: Bayek
en: Thoth bade Iset fear not. "I have come from heaven to heal the child for his mother." That was not our truth.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is blood pooling beneath this door!

speaker: Bayek
en: Butchered Sobeks in Krokodilopolis! Gods, this is an illegal tannery.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hung out to dry like rags. No wonder the place is locked tight. Hiding the murder of gods!

speaker: Bayek
en: These mummies are sloppy work. This is the foulest blasphemy!

speaker: Bayek
en: The mummies are stuffed with gold and valuables. Where are they taking them? There are shipping consignment markings on them.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is a lot of gold. Someone is making a big profit from this sacrilege.

speaker: Bayek
en: Crocodiles are being slaughtered and mummified. The work is sloppy and careless. This is sacrilege beyond imagining. The mummies are used as coin sacks, then stacked like packages. They are using the bodies of murdered gods for smuggling! Amun! The smell alone turns my stomach. Those who do this deserve death. How can this be happening in Egypt? By the gods, it must be stopped! I need to find where the mummies are being shipped. This tannery must have a dock nearby.

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone is in trouble!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: I don't want to do this. But you put your nose where it doesn't belong, priest.

speaker: Padiaset
en: You know this is wrong. Wrong! Killing Sobek's children? Filling their bodies with unclean gold? Who orders such bloodshed and sacrilege?

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Sobek has chosen his right hand, and we must obey him. I'm sorry. I will make this quick.

speaker: Padiaset
en: You cannot shed innocent blood! You are meant to protect the temple and the people!

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Damn you priest! I have no choice. Nek!

speaker: Padiaset
en: Thank you Medjay! My life is spared, but it seems much that is good is already dead.

speaker: Bayek
en: I saw the tannery and the mummies. I know what they are doing to Sobek's children.

speaker: Padiaset
en: So you have seen it? Dua Sobek! It is unthinkable. I am Padiaset. I serve in the temple South of the city. Forgive me. I must return. I need to pray for guidance.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is going to take more than prayer, priest. We need to act. The mummies had markings on them. I think they are being moved by ship.

speaker: Padiaset
en: Ship? The cult has a trireme. It follows trade routes South of the city. Do what you must, Medjay. I will pray for you. But please, risk no more bloodshed.

speaker: Bayek
en: Bloodshed comes, whether we risk it or not. I should search for the ship's manifest. It will tell me where the mummies are headed.

speaker: Bayek
en: The ship's manifest. The cargo is bound for the Trireme Stranding Camp to the West. Why would Sobek priests be dealing with soldiers?/More evidence the cult is working with Ptolemy's soldiers. Money, power, and corruption. It is always the same. I need to go to that camp and find out more.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is the Trireme Stranding Camp. The information I need is probably in the Captain's tent.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: I just don't understand why we're dealing with those scale huggers!

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Have you seen the coffers of gold in the Captain's tent? That's a damned good reason right there.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: What? Those are coming from the Sobek priests? Well the, never mind. I'll guard their temple anytime!

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Ha-ha! You whore. Their requests for help keep increasing though. I don't think the Captain's happy about it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Sobek's children butchered and turned into money sacks! Those godless neks!

speaker: Bayek
en: Chests full of treasure. This corrupt scheme has been going on for some time.

speaker: Bayek
en: Correspondence between the Captain and a priest named Sehetep. The cult and Ptolemy's soldiers are conspiring together. What else are they doing?/Correspondence between the Captain and Sehetep. Sehetep again! That poisonous priest from the northern temple is becoming a big problem.

speaker: Bayek
en: I should let Padiaset know about Sehetep. He is not going to like it.

speaker: Roman Soldier 1
en: Harwa knows how to pick his workers.

speaker: Roman Soldier 2
en: It is a wonder these children didn't build Amenmesse's pyramid.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ahhh, so this is the secret quarry the rebels spoke of.

speaker: Child
en: I heard Aretas killed himself instead of coming here.

speaker: Khety
en: Please, Osiris come and take me. I hate it here. I prefer death to slavery.

speaker: Khety
en: Ahh, you must be the killer shadow Haganu sings of.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is no place for a child.

speaker: Khety
en: Yes neb (sir). You see the hungry eyes on the children here? All bought off a slave merchant on the Way of Horus, where he rides his shiny mount.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will kill this sick soul and you will see the sun again.

speaker: Khety
en: Thank you killer shadow. You are living up to your good name.

speaker: Child
en: He will free us, thank Amun!

speaker: Bayek
en: That horse is draped in finery. Must be the slave merchant.

speaker: Bayek
en: That mount could come in handy.

speaker: Child
en: Yes! Fill him with arrows! By the gods, is it true? We will taste freedom again! Amun-Ra has sent a liberator!

speaker: Harwa
en: Damn you! Ruining my work!

speaker: Child
en: I am free! Long live the killer shadow!

speaker: Bayek
en: Go now!

speaker: Tahemet
en: Look at this, tell me what do you see?

speaker: Bayek
en: I see you. Exactly where I left you pouring over dusty papyrus and losing more than you win on dice.

speaker: Tahemet
en: Knowledge is not necessarily wisdom, Bayek. You have heard of Ramesses the II, yes? The Great Pharaoh, father to a hundred children? He is the Pharaoh who walks.

speaker: Bayek
en: How do you know?

speaker: Tahemet
en: This speaks of it, strange because it must be a thousand years old.

speaker: Tahemet
en: A great king, his soul fragmented. Doesn't say why he is here. For revenge? Or, he has unfinished business?

speaker: Bayek
en: As do we all.

speaker: Tahemet
en: Wait, Bayek. Let me see, before you get yourself killed!

speaker: Tahemet
en: The pharaoh's name, the pharaoh's shadow, an ancient ritual it's all here... fascinating.

speaker: Bayek
en: If he is like the others, I know what needs to be done. But I will need the parchment.

speaker: Tahemet
en: Of course... So about my finders fee?

speaker: Bayek
en: Or you could give it to me from the goddness of your heart? Unless you already lost that on another bad roll of the dice?

speaker: Tahemet
en: Take it with my blessing. Ra protect you, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Pharaoh's Jb, his Sheut, his Ren? This is how I will quieten the great Ramesses.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ramesses' temple. Built so his memory would not wither. Does it keep the secret of his tomb?

speaker: Bayek
en: Bandits have made camp here. If something remained they probably took it.

speaker: Bayek
en: An unmarked tomb with the same cartouche from the hymns and songs.

speaker: Bayek
en: What will I find in the Pharaoh's tomb? More desecration?

speaker: Bayek
en: What path should I follow now?

speaker: Nefertari
en: Bayek of Siwa, you have come. Will you help my husband Ramesses find the peace he deserves?

speaker: Anubis Warrior 1
en: The living are not welcome.

speaker: Anubis Warrior 2
en: Leave! Leave this place.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ramesses the great is your husband?

speaker: Nefertari
en: In life I was his most beloved consort. The favourite queen of a great man.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why does he walk the black land?

speaker: Nefertari
en: He lived a glorious life, vanquished our enemies, gave us prosperity, but in death his ka finds no peace. Once the medjay were servants of the Pharaohs...

speaker: Bayek
en: I am medjay no longer.

speaker: Nefertari
en: But you know what it is to sacrifice for something greater than yourself. Ramesses served Egypt like no other. Has he not earned an ageless slumber?

speaker: Bayek
en: What will you have me do?

speaker: Nefertari
en: I will whisper the ritual in your ear.

speaker: Nefertari
en: You are the cup bearer of the Keeper of Harmony. Set free the spoils of war and return his Hemset. The Ka of Ozymandias. Be furious in wrath, take it from those who hide it. It must stride on the sands. Side by side they must ascend into the deathless feathers. And summon the ba, the traverser of worlds.

speaker: Nefertari
en: The bones of the earth-god quake. The two doors of the horizon are open; its bolt slide, revealing him upon his firm throne.

speaker: Nefertari
en: The face of the god is open, revealed.

speaker: Bayek
en: Bringer of peace. Champion of Kadesh. Face me, I bring you rest.

speaker: Nefertari
en: Ra grant you eternity with your beloved, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: Such greatness.

speaker: Bayek
en: But did he achieve this alone?

speaker: Bayek
en: The relic replaced with a... half-eaten apple? The thief has a sense of humor.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hired thugs. So where are the merchants they were paid to protect?

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone ran away from the auction.

speaker: Bayek
en: They took prisoners. This one died before they could get him on the boat.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where did they come from? Maybe from that wharf across the river?

speaker: Bayek
en: The auction was underway... when the soldiers arrived. In the chaos, someone saw an opportunity to take the relic. But was it soldiers, or someone else? They killed the bodyguards, but captured the merchants. And took them across the water to Hatshepsut's sanctuary. One way or another the path to the relic leads there.

speaker: Irsu
en: I shed blood for that relic. It was mine by right. That damn boy cost me everything.

speaker: Irsu
en: The trinket's gone! Leave me be.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where's the artifact?

speaker: Irsu
en: Up my ass.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do not test me.

speaker: Irsu
en: Neket (fucking) nephew stole it. But he doesn't know where the tomb is.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then tell me.

speaker: Irsu
en: Ask the others. They... knew where to look.

speaker: Bayek
en: What others? Who were you working with?

speaker: Irsu
en: Wash my heart and kill me. I'm gone anyway.

speaker: Bayek
en: No, no, no... Where did your newphew go, ugh?

speaker: Irsu
en: My boys chased his west from the auction. Should've killed him with his parents. Were going to turn me in.

speaker: Thug Leader
en: Come out, thief. We're not going anywhere. Give us the relic and we won't feed your guts to the vultures.

speaker: Sutekh
en: Shoo! Get away!

speaker: Bayek
en: Who's in there?

speaker: Sutekh
en: No one, nothing. Only the dead.

speaker: Bayek
en: You're a little noisy for a spirit. You're the auction thief everyone's looking for.

speaker: Sutekh
en: No, not me? What auction! The burning desert sun has made you delusional, neb (sir).

speaker: Bayek
en: It is night. I'll find a way in and we'll talk.

speaker: Sutekh
en: No! Go away!

speaker: Bayek
en: The same footprints from the auction. Irsu's nephew?

speaker: Bayek
en: You're the boy from the docks... Sutekh?

speaker: Sutekh
en: No, yes, I mean nothing, no one... who are you?

speaker: Bayek
en: Bayek, and I need the artifact you stole.

speaker: Sutekh
en: Are you with my uncle, neb (sir)?

speaker: Bayek
en: No, but I am the man with death in his eyes remember?

speaker: Sutekh
en: If you are looking for treasure from the Pharaohs, I can get better. Golden statues, collars of lapis and carnelian? This is just a worthless trinket.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then give it to me.

speaker: Sutekh
en: I can't let you have it.

speaker: Bayek
en: You have nowhere to go, Sutekh.

speaker: Sutekh
en: I must return what my uncle stole!

speaker: Sutekh
en: Please, leave me this one thing. It's my mother, she's

speaker: Bayek
en: Your parents are gone.

speaker: Sutekh
en: Because of this! And Nefertiti will never harm another, if I can only bring it back to her tomb.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then why haven't you?

speaker: Sutekh
en: ... My neket (fucking) uncle never told me where it was.

speaker: Bayek
en: He's dead.

speaker: Sutekh
en: May Ra light his passing!

speaker: Bayek
en: Give it to me. I will return it.

speaker: Sutekh
en: Why? You've lost nothing.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nothing, I was a medjay, a husband, a father. I painted half of Egypt with the blood of those who took that from me. All of it over a relic like this one.

speaker: Sutekh
en: Take it. Take it. I believe you.

speaker: Sutekh
en: What is wrong?

speaker: Bayek
en: I was expecting... something else.

speaker: Sutekh
en: You promised. Nefertiti's tomb lies west of the main path in the valley.

speaker: Bayek
en: I thought you didn't know where it was.

speaker: Sutekh
en: This is the tomb of her architect. I've been stuck in here for ages. I figured it out.

speaker: Sutekh
en: There might be more of my uncle's men. But I know another way out. You will remember your promise?

speaker: Bayek
en: I will. What will you do now?

speaker: Sutekh
en: Find work and stay out of trouble.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why do I find that hard to believe?

speaker: Bayek
en: The tomb of Queen Nefertiti. Will anything be left inside?

speaker: Bayek
en: Queen Nefertiti's sarcophagus. Is she still within?

speaker: Anubis Warrior
en: You ka is living, this land is for the dead. You should not have come.

speaker: Bayek
en: What is this? Can this be... Aaru? If I return the relic to the temple, Nefertiti's spirit may rest again.

speaker: Bayek
en: What is this? A truly wondrous beast! Such a mount is worthy of the Guardian of Soul himself. The Stallion of Death! Can the living even ride this beast?

speaker: Bayek
en: Something was stolen from the Pharaoh, I would return it.

speaker: Priest
en: You do not belong here. Your flesh is unclean, drenched in blood and consuming grief. You cannot make Nefertiti whole.

speaker: Bayek
en: I must try.

speaker: Priest
en: Then plunge deep into the holy waters.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Pharaoh you honor is not at peace.

speaker: Priest
en: You come to offer a relic of Nefertiti on a plate filled with impure offerings. You mock the gods!

speaker: Bayek
en: This vision is the mockery. I would set it right.

speaker: Priest
en: Then purify the sacrifice. That which would feed the gods on their sacred ship.

speaker: Praying Man
en: You stand before us, Great of Praises, Lady of Grace. Sweet of love. Beloved of the living Aten. The celestial ruler, the sole god. Mistress of and . Mother of the Black Land. Lady of all women. I honor you, I delight in the knowledge that you brought me to serve at your side in the fields of Aaru.

speaker: Bayek
en: This relic, it was stolen from Nefertiti.

speaker: Priest
en: You cannot bring that to the temple, not when the offerings are sour, they will offend Hathor.

speaker: Bayek
en: What is soured?

speaker: Priest
en: The libations must be pure. In water you see your own face, but in wine the heart of its garden.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have done what was asked. A symbol of her power and authority as a Pharaoh.

speaker: Bayek
en: Enough! This ends here.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nefertiti. Was she a Pharaoh, or a god?

speaker: Bayek
en: Is that the relic I seek? If so, who holds it now?

speaker: Bayek
en: I need to find the hideout. It should be visible from a height.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah, there it is.

speaker: Bayek
en: The entrance is closed. There must be another way in.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is it. Ah. The Hidden Ones' bureau.

speaker: Kashta
en: My name is Kashta. It is an honor to meet you, Mentor.

speaker: Bayek
en: No formalities, Kashta. We are both equally Hidden Ones.

speaker: Paanchi
en: Bayek! Greatest of them all. I have heard the songs.

speaker: Gamilat
en: Such loss of life!

speaker: Bayek
en: Tahira?

speaker: Tahira
en: Ah, Bayek. Thank the gods you have come.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your message was urgent.

speaker: Tahira
en: These are the swords of two Hidden Ones I recruited. Killed in a massacre.

speaker: Gamilat
en: They will be remembered as martyrs to the cause.

speaker: Tahira
en: This is Gamilat. Leader of the Nabatean rebels.

speaker: Bayek
en: What happened?

speaker: Gamilat
en: We retreated through the village. The Romans pursued us in a furry and took their anger out on the villagers.

speaker: Tahira
en: It was a pure butchery! Innocent men and women. The Hidden Ones tried to stop it and were killed.

speaker: Bayek
en: They understood the risks.

speaker: Tahira
en: I assigned them to help the rebels.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tahira, what has been done cannot be undone. The Hidden Ones have no place in battles. But we can help the rebellion by eliminating the Roman leader.

speaker: Gamilat
en: General Rufio. But he is in Rome.

speaker: Tahira
en: Rufio has three lieutenants here in the Sinai.

speaker: Bayek
en: These three men will die.

speaker: Tahira
en: Let's get to it.

speaker: Gamilat
en: I am indebted to you.

speaker: Bayek
en: We do this for the people, Gamilat.

speaker: Gamilat
en: Yes, the people! The people and I are one and the same.

speaker: Kashta
en: We have Hidden Ones watching each of Rufio's lieutenants. They'll tell you anything you need to know.

speaker: Phidias
en: You! Get over here. Er, no. Not you. You will not do, either. This must be dealt with quickly. Is there no one up to my task? I need someone for one quick job. It's good coin. No, not you, you, keep going. Do not stop here. No , not that one. He is too... handsome. How I wish those bandits had not killed my man Arikonos. Poor fool. At least the jackals had a good meal.

speaker: Phidias
en: You! That insignia... You are a man of honor? There are so few remaining.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am a Medjay. I solve problems.

speaker: Phidias
en: Good! I have one. A most precious treasure, which must be delivered today. You will be well compensated for your work. Here are some drachmas to start.

speaker: Bayek
en: This city is much more expensive than I'm used to.

speaker: Phidias
en: Good! It is settled. Follow me.

speaker: Phidias
en: The thing I ask you to do is of the utmost importance.

speaker: Bayek
en: Of course it is.

speaker: Phidias
en: Being a merchant is no simple matter, sir. I assure you, moving tiger skins or even statues is not easy work. Ah, these workers! Never where you tell them to be. As I was saying, you must be quick. Oh. And do not stray for your task. At all. I will know if you have. This is all I have since the flood.

speaker: Bayek
en: Seems you care a lot for your... cargo.

speaker: Phidias
en: I swear on her mother's grave, she was sent from the Gods to make Alexandria better.

speaker: Bayek
en: She?

speaker: Phidias
en: I have your bodyguard, Kara. Do not let this be a repeat of the last time, daughter.

speaker: Bayek
en: Wait, this hardly seems to be what you ask

speaker: Phidias
en: Medjay, I will pour drachmas down your throat as long as she is safe. And Kara, remember the reception tonight. You will be ready.

speaker: Kara
en: Of course father! I would not miss it!

speaker: Kara
en: I am so happy you have come to assist me, sir.

speaker: Bayek
en: We will get you home fast. Do not worry.

speaker: Kara
en: Oh, of course. Thank you, my bull. You look just like Heracles. Perhaps I'll call you my Heracles.

speaker: Kara
en: Finally! Change of plans, Heracles.

speaker: Bayek
en: Who? No matter, child, it's time to return you home.

speaker: Kara
en: I will not go. Have you met the priests here? Dull. No! I must go to the central market. I heard of new Persian linens. I need them.

speaker: Bayek
en: Or what?

speaker: Kara
en: I will scream. Which will call the soldiers. Then, well, even if you survive, Father will be quite angry.

speaker: Bayek
en: Anubis take this city. Are you Sekhmet in disguise? Sent to test me?

speaker: Kara
en: What was that?

speaker: Bayek
en: Nothing.

speaker: Kara
en: Good! First we must get my horse. She's been treated absolutely terribly without me around. You'd think someone would clean this water, eugh. You guide the boats well. Much better than any of my other bodyguards. You know if you want to go fast... it would be alright. Look at the city, Medjay. Must be so intimidating for someone like you.

speaker: Kara
en: I simply adore this part of the city. So rustic. You can smell it in the air! They live a truly simple life here. Pegasus simply can't wait to be reunited with me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Of course you named your horse Pegasus.

speaker: Man
en: Young miss, it's so nice to see you again. As you asked, she has been given new shoes.

speaker: Kara
en: There now, was that so difficult?

speaker: Man
en: Now, what of my pay?

speaker: Bayek
en: The deal was only to get you home, not to pay for your horse.

speaker: Kara
en: I'm sure my father would not be pleased with you discussing this in front of him, horseman.

speaker: Man
en: Of course. Uh, I'll discuss it with your father.

speaker: Kara
en: Oh, Pegasus. I know you missed me. Yes, you did, you beautiful creature. If only you had wings! Time to go, bodyguard!

speaker: Bayek
en: That is it. I am taking you home, Princess Kara.

speaker: Kara
en: Oh, all you big, broody types are the same. Never let me have any fun.

speaker: Bayek
en: I should just leave you here.

speaker: Kara
en: You're duty bound to deliver me, are you not?

speaker: Bayek
en: Who would know if I left?

speaker: Bayek
en: Your conscience would, of course.

speaker: Kara
en: Look there, bodyguard. That is where I had my first... discussion with a soldier.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am sure he was very grateful.

speaker: Kara
en: We must stop at the market for more linens.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will take you to your house as your father bade, and nowhere else. Now, lead on.

speaker: Kara
en: You know you are absolutely destroying my chances at getting the perfect linens.

speaker: Bayek
en: There are different kinds of linen?

speaker: Kara
en: You are much... more serious than my usual bodyguards. You could move faster, bodyguard.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have a name.

speaker: Kara
en: Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah, you do know my name.

speaker: Kara
en: I remember all their names, you know.

speaker: Bayek
en: Whose names?

speaker: Kara
en: The bodyguards. I send gifts to their families when I can.

speaker: Bayek
en: Kara. Kara

speaker: Kara
en: ... Yes?

speaker: Bayek
en: If we go find you your linens, would you be happy?

speaker: Kara
en: Really? Of... course! Thank you, Bayek. You have an interesting stare.

speaker: Bayek
en: Thank you.

speaker: Bayek
en: We are close. Finally.

speaker: Kara
en: Aha! Finally, these linens show some promise. Ugh! It's so heavy. Would you help me?

speaker: Kara
en: Bayek! Pegasus! They stole my horse!

speaker: Bayek
en: Stay here. Do not leave!

speaker: Bayek
en: It is done.

speaker: Bayek
en: Whoa, there, girl. Time to get home. Your troublesome mistress will have missed you. Pegasus. Huh. I like it. It suits a horse. Aya would like your spirit.

speaker: Kara
en: Over here, Bayek! ...Papa, since Pegasus was limping, Bayek went to deal with her shoe. He was only gone a moment!

speaker: Phidias
en: Ah. I heard of some commotion, but according to my little princess, you're the hero of the day.

speaker: Kara
en: Can he always be my bodyguard? Please, Father?

speaker: Phidias
en: How much does it cost to hire a Medjay permanently?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am here only a short while.

speaker: Phidias
en: Alas. Then allow me to grant you a hero's pay for a hero's service.

speaker: Aya
en: What are you waiting for, my love? Shall we race, like we did in Siwa?

speaker: Bayek
en: Only if you're ready to lose.

speaker: Aya
en: Bold words. I will see you back them up. Eat my dust!

speaker: Aya
en: Eat my dust!

speaker: Bayek
en: What is the prize for winning?

speaker: Aya
en: You'll never find out! You're slower than Ramses, and he's been dead a few years now!

speaker: Bayek
en: You can't keep that pace.

speaker: Aya
en: Try me! Faster, beast, faster! I need to prove a point!

speaker: Bayek
en: Seems I have come out on top.

speaker: Aya
en: Seems you have.

speaker: Bayek
en: We all have weaknesses.

speaker: Aya
en: Yes, and yours is winning graciously.

speaker: Aya
en: The expected result.

speaker: Bayek
en: If you are that confident, let's race again.

speaker: Aya
en: No time!

speaker: Bayek
en: What is this about?

speaker: Aya
en: The Queen is about to speak. Let's go and listen.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: As they rule, the gods curse our land, withholding the river's floods. But as the living goddess ascends the throne, the waters will rise again! Through me, Memphis shines as rubies set in gold! Through me, Egypt triumphs!

speaker: Cleopatra
en: I cannot lose them. They must know my voice as that of the goddess.

speaker: Aya
en: My Queen...

speaker: Cleopatra
en: The Apis Bull persists in ailing?

speaker: Aya
en: We have found the cause of his sickness. He was poisoned.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Who did this?

speaker: Aya
en: The Twin Priestesses.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Have them boiled to death inside a .

speaker: Aya
en: Goddess, no.

speaker: Bayek
en: They were coerced. Their brother was kidnapped by a priest of Anubis with a blue scarf and a cough.

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: Hetepi! But he is amongst my closest advisors.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Those living in one's shadow are the least worthy of trust.

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: If even Hetepi is against me...

speaker: Bayek
en: Your wife and child were threatened by him, but now they are safe. We can overcome this.

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: The priests of Anubis will be conducting rites in the Great Temple. Look for their masks.

speaker: Aya
en: My blade will serve as well as his.

speaker: Bayek
en: No, Aya. Let me.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: I care not who kills the priest. Let it be done before we head to Herakleion in the north.

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: Wait!

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: Ptah-Nun the father breathe strength into your arm.

speaker: Aya
en: So you go to kill again. Tell me, how do you make sense of it?

speaker: Bayek
en: Sometimes, ritual is all that stands between a man and madness. Each time I feel my body locked in combat, my wounds crushed against those I have inflicted, each time I feel the tearing free. I pay it tribute with a prayer. This prayer is not for the dead, or for the gods. It is for me. My creed gives the meaningless meaning and shapes the formless. Without it, I could not kill.

speaker: Aya
en: Hm. You would not want to hear the words that make me capable of killing. Now go.

speaker: Bayek
en: Only one of these priests has to die. I must strike carefully.

speaker: Bayek
en: A priest of Anubis... but is it Hetepi?

speaker: Bayek
en: Another priest of Anubis.

speaker: Bayek
en: How many priests does one city need?

speaker: Bayek
en: Is that the man I seek?

speaker: Bayek
en: Hetepi hides among his brothers.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Lizard. The priest who cursed Memphis.

speaker: Hetepi
en: I serve the ways of old Egypt. (coughing)

speaker: Bayek
en: Old Egypt asks a heavy price!

speaker: Bayek
en: Innocents mutilated, children ripped from the womb, the High Priest's name abused

speaker: Hetepi
en: His name was muck before you arrived. The masses are the cattle of the gods, driven by the herdsman's whip. You are one of them, Bayek.

speaker: Hetepi
en: You are a cow.

speaker: Bayek
en: It is will that drives me, not fear.

speaker: Hetepi
en: Oh, yes? And who passes the whip over your back? Who demands that you stain your ka with my death?

speaker: Bayek
en: I have my gods. Now face yours.

speaker: Bayek
en: By your death, the curses of Memphis are lifted. I should report to the others.

speaker: Aya
en: My Queen, they acted only to lift the threat on their brother's life.

speaker: Bayek
en: Curses will trouble you no more.

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: Hetepi. What could have driven him to such madness?

speaker: Bayek
en: Memphis is yours again.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Ours.

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: With these dark matters settled, we can finally prepare for the Festival of Apis.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: May demons feast on Hetepi's ka. And may those guilty of Khemu's death soon follow.

speaker: Aya
en: It is agony to leave you, but... I must go on alone.

speaker: Bayek
en: Aya

speaker: Aya
en: I will stand by my duty!

speaker: Bayek
en: Where will your duty take you?

speaker: Aya
en: North. To set the sea aflame.

speaker: Bayek
en: I walk on your water.

speaker: Aya
en: I hope we will hunt together again soon. Until then, let us take this night as ours.

speaker: Bayek
en: I should speak to Pasherenptah right away. He's likely at the Great Temple.

speaker: Man
en: Forgive me, neb (sir), but access to the inner sanctum is restricted at this time.

speaker: Bayek
en: I can wait a little.

speaker: Man
en: What is your name?

speaker: Bayek
en: Bayek of Siwa.

speaker: Man
en: Ah, we were told to expect you. You may enter, so long as you do not disturb the rites.

speaker: Taimhotep
en: You dare accuse me, you coward? You, who spent the past three days cringing behind the doors of our home? It is your spinelessness that dooms us, not my neglect!

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: I am blamed for the whole city's troubles, and when I suggest we might share the blame, you deny all

speaker: Taimhotep
en: I deny blame when I am free of it! Ask your little priestlings to see if they have neglected

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: Taimhotep, I visited them before I came to you! I have spoken to all the priests. Each one swears to handling your meals with the utmost care!

speaker: Taimhotep
en: And you trust their word over mine? How could you think that I would take the smallest risk with our child? Do you doubt my love for him? For you?

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: No! But you are very agitated right now.

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: Perhaps we forgot some part of the ritual...

speaker: Taimhotep
en: I will vomit if I hear more. Have no doubt of this. If our child dies, I die.

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: No, my lotus, do not speak like that!

speaker: Taimhotep
en: I must go to the Seer's house. Just leave me be.

speaker: Bayek
en: High Priest.

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: Uh... ah, Bayek. I'm sorry. I'm, ah...

speaker: Bayek
en: I have come to seek the Lizard.

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: Oh, the Lizard... One more affliction for Memphis.

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: The city withers in the darkness of a curse. Disease, pestilence... the poisoned stink of the air.

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: The Apis Bull sickened nearly unto death.

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: The gods have abandoned us. The people look to me for guidance, but I am as lost as they.

speaker: Bayek
en: Pash!

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: Apis, how have we wronged you?

speaker: Bayek
en: Pash...

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: The curse touches even my own house. My wife, Taimhotep, has miscarried three times this year. She is with child again, but if... If she loses a fourth...

speaker: Bayek
en: I will look into this curse.

speaker: Pasherenptah
en: My wife's Seer can help. His house is to the southwest.

speaker: Bayek
en: If the gods are responsible, I will kneel beside you as they strike us down.

speaker: Seer
en: Grow, O light; come forth, O light...

speaker: Taimhotep
en: My child!

speaker: Seer
en: You have come at last!

speaker: Mara
en: Who is this man?

speaker: Seer
en: He is the Deliverer. Many years I have waited for him.

speaker: Bayek
en: What?

speaker: Taimhotep
en: Quick, help me dream my child away from death!

speaker: Seer
en: Let us proceed with the ritual.

speaker: Seer
en: Bring me the cauldron. I am the Master of Secret Things, the form of the soul that rests in the heavens. I am servant to the Great God, who gives light exceedingly. I am the Companion of the Flame, in whose mouth the fire is not quenced.

speaker: Seer
en: Sothis, reveal yourself here today, and answer me without falsehood.

speaker: Seer
en: Let your eyes be opened. Devoid of moisture, come forth from the stream! Sothis, let their eyes be opened!

speaker: Taimhotep
en: Let your eyes be opened.

speaker: Bayek
en: What is this gods forsaken place? Is someone there?

speaker: Bayek
en: What is that? Some kind of tomb? I must keep moving or be swallowed by the desert.

speaker: Bayek
en: That shadow, that is the soul eater!

speaker: Bayek
en: O you door-keepers who guard your portals, who swallow souls and who gulp down the corpses of the dead. What a journey I have made, the things I have seen. I am but one of you.

speaker: Bayek
en: No!

speaker: Bayek
en: Anubis, Lord of the dead! Did that crazy old fool poison me?

speaker: Bayek
en: So Apep can be hurt! You will not devour my heart! He is weakening! I am he who drives off the destructive one.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ra protect me! Arg! Nek (Shit)! Poison. I take the bow, I sweep the sky with it. Hurts, doesn't it?! I am he who knots the chord and lashes the shrine together. You will not devour my heart!

speaker: Bayek
en: I am the great one within his eye! You will not claim me, Destructive one! Return to the chaos sea. Apep will tear the Duat apart. You will feel the sun god's wrath. I will not go into the valley of darkness! It is not my time yet! I will destroy you! Die, soul-eater!

speaker: Bayek
en: Be gone, swim to the pool of Nu.

speaker: Khemu
en: What's that, papo (father)? Papo (Father)?

speaker: Khemu
en: Will you teach me to hunt? Look, papo (father)! I am the Great Hunter Orion. Father! Senu! What do you see?

speaker: Seer
en: They are returned, safe from him who would close their eyes in darkness.

speaker: Taimhotep
en: My child lives!

speaker: Seer
en: Praise to the gods.

speaker: Taimhotep
en: What do you see?

speaker: Seer
en: Your enemy and hers are the same.

speaker: Seer
en: Refuse... the temple food. He who prepares it poisons your womb with flesh of the dead. Go and slay the poisoner, and lift Memphis out of evil.

speaker: Taimhotep
en: Praise to he who will deliver us all.

speaker: Seer
en: If you wish to speak of your own true seeing, come to me in the fullness of the moment.

speaker: Bayek
en: Thank you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Aya!

speaker: Aya
en: My love! Are you well?

speaker: Bayek
en: Better for seeing your face.

speaker: Aya
en: There's a strangeness in your eyes. What afflicts you?

speaker: Bayek
en: Dreams. Of our son.

speaker: Aya
en: Bayek...

speaker: Bayek
en: The High Priest's wife has been poisoned. Her Seer claims that her poisoner is our enemy.

speaker: Aya
en: The Lizard?

speaker: Bayek
en: I believe so.

speaker: Aya
en: The Apis Bull is also at the point of death. Let's go to the temple – we can speak more of your dreams on the way. Come, we'll take a boat for speed.

speaker: Aya
en: So, how does it feel to be Medjay to the whole of Egypt?

speaker: Bayek
en: Like trailing after an ant colony, sometimes. But I'm proud to serve those in need.

speaker: Aya
en: As am I – and proud to serve the Queen.

speaker: Bayek
en: Have you spoken to the High Priest?

speaker: Aya
en: Yes, in advance of the Queen's arrival.

speaker: Bayek
en: She's coming to Memphis?

speaker: Aya
en: Yes.

speaker: Bayek
en: The exiled ruler appears in the heart of Old Egypt. That will set the young Ptolemy on notice.

speaker: Aya
en: It lifts my heart to see you, Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: Aya, you are the one joy left in my life. I want you at my side again.

speaker: Aya
en: I am bound to the Queen's service.

speaker: Bayek
en: And our bond?

speaker: Aya
en: It means as much as ever! But we have seen the Order's evil now.

speaker: Bayek
en: We can fight it shoulder to shoulder.

speaker: Aya
en: I've promised the Queen...

speaker: Bayek
en: What has she done for you that I have not?

speaker: Aya
en: She lifts my gaze to the horizon.

speaker: Aya
en: I will never stop mourning what we lost. Never. But I must make a world that is larger than our griefs, so that no mother ever again lives what I have lived.

speaker: Bayek
en: After I kill the Lizard

speaker: Aya
en: After you kill the Lizard, I will leave Memphis.

speaker: Bayek
en: Then I will follow. Let us hunt together, as we did before.

speaker: Aya
en: You said dreams troubled your mind. Do you want to tell me of them?

speaker: Bayek
en: No. I would rather not burden you.

speaker: Aya
