en: We will need to speak of it someday, once the sands have settled.

speaker: Bayek
en: Once the sands have settled. When will that be?

speaker: Aya
en: Soon, I hope.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where should we begin?

speaker: Aya
en: Check the god's enclosure. I'll speak to the priestesses.

speaker: Bayek
en: Of course, give me the dungheap job.

speaker: Bayek
en: The best way out is through. Peach pits. Half my father's herds died because of this. I should search the place where the god's food is stored. I will have you soon, poisoner.

speaker: Bayek
en: Pasherenptah would use a taster for the god's water.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your coat has lost its luster, Shining One. And your flanks are hollowed. Hathor give you strength.

speaker: Bayek
en: These are offerings to the bull. They seem sound.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hey! Do you feed the Apis Bull?

speaker: Worker
en: No. Them girl priestesses take care of all of that.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do you know where his fodder is kept?

speaker: Worker
en: In that building over by the stairs. But they shut it up last week when the bull got sick.

speaker: Bayek
en: My thanks.

speaker: Bayek
en: The bull's sickness could come from his food, but it is too soon to say. I need more evidence.

speaker: Bayek
en: Food for the bull. The rest is likely stored inside this shed.

speaker: Bayek
en: Peach pits. If the Apis Bull was fed with these, that would explain his sickness. And the necklace here... One of the Twin Priestesses wore something like it. Let us see if the other is missing a weight from around her neck.

speaker: Aya
en: Greetings, Sisters of Osiris.

speaker: Bayek
en: As I thought. One priestess is missing her necklace.

speaker: Aya
en: How long have you served in this temple?

speaker: Taous
en: Two months, ever since the new Bull was chosen.

speaker: Aya
en: I am a servant of the Queen, who wishes very much to see Apis thrive. Can you tell me of your daily habits?

speaker: Taous
en: Every day is the same. We wake for morning prayers and then we feed the god.

speaker: Tawe
en: We bless his grain... A man pours out his water and cleans away his filth

speaker: Aya
en: Do any of his caretakers look suspicious?

speaker: Tawe
en: Why... yes! The, um, farmer... I've always thought the farmer who brings his grain had an evil look. Maybe you should question him.

speaker: Aya
en: Question him? No. I will find this farmer, and I will deliver to him the justice of my blade.

speaker: Taous
en: Wait, won't you speak with him first?

speaker: Aya
en: No need. The denunciation of those sworn to the Twin Goddesses is enough. He has sinned against the god. He must die.

speaker: Taous
en: My sister spoke too quickly. The man could be innocent.

speaker: Aya
en: You know why Apis is sick.

speaker: Taous
en: Yes.

speaker: Aya
en: Can the cause be found in his quarters?

speaker: Taous
en: Yes, Nebet.

speaker: Aya
en: Then we will await the return of my comrade before passing judgement.

speaker: Bayek
en: This is a subtle way of poisoning an animal.

speaker: Aya
en: My sisters, this is surely an accident?

speaker: Bayek
en: One, maybe. But not a bushel.

speaker: Tawe
en: We had to save Panchrates!

speaker: Bayek
en: Eh? Who?

speaker: Taous
en: Our brother. Bandits ripped him away from us, as we walked in the market.

speaker: Taous
en: They forced us to poison the god!

speaker: Tawe
en: They told us they were going to feed our brother to crocodiles unless we...

speaker: Taous
en: We have not slept through the night since.

speaker: Tawe
en: I'm so sorry! We had no choice. We never

speaker: Bayek
en: Something is wrong. These are no curses.

speaker: Aya
en: The Order is surely behind this.

speaker: Aya
en: Go to the temple of Hathor without me. The twins cannot be left alone. Quickly, to the Temple of Hathor.

speaker: Tawe
en: Please find our brother!

speaker: Taous
en: They say the Temple of Hathor is haunted. Be careful!

speaker: Aya
en: Bayek is used to ghosts. Let's keep going.

speaker: Panchrates
en: Let me free! My sisters surely weep for my return.

speaker: Guard
en: And the girls in the tavern weep for mine, but they'll be just as surely disappointed.

speaker: Panchrates
en: I suppose wine is too much to ask for, but may I at least have a drink of water?

speaker: Guard
en: How about I pour piss down your gullet and call it wine?

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you Panchrates?

speaker: Panchrates
en: I am. Praise the gods for bringing a strong warrior to save me!

speaker: Bayek
en: You are injured. I will carry you home.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tell me about your kidnapping.

speaker: Panchrates
en: Best not to speak of it out in the open. Besides, my wounds are making me very tired. Here is my house. Before we go inside, let us speak.

speaker: Panchrates
en: I prefer to spare my sisters the ugliest details of my story.

speaker: Bayek
en: Of course.

speaker: Panchrates
en: The man who ordered my abduction is a priest of Anubis at the Great Temple.

speaker: Bayek
en: A priest in Pasherenptah's circle! How can I find him?

speaker: Panchrates
en: He wears a blue scarf, and has a terrible cough.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Lizard. He is marked.

speaker: Tawe
en: Panchrates! Are you hurt? Did they mistreat you?

speaker: Panchrates
en: They kept me tied up... fed me little but crusts of bread fit for beggars...

speaker: Aya
en: So?

speaker: Bayek
en: This is the Lizard's work. And so I must stain my hands with another priest's blood.

speaker: Aya
en: The Order is everywhere. To protect Egypt, I would kill a thousand priests. You and I are pledged to violence, now and always.

speaker: Bayek
en: Pasherenptah should know of this.

speaker: Aya
en: He waits at the palace. I have horses for us nearby.

speaker: Felix Martialis
en: The glorious Medjay has returned. You caused quite a furor. You surprised me. Not bad for a sand scratcher. I like entrepreneurs, free spirits, money makers. You love to fight, I love to make money. Together we can do both. I will find the fights, you win them, we both get rich. Or I get rich. You get what I give you. If you want more challenge, head to Cyrene. I mentioned your name to the arena owner there. You are welcome.

speaker: Alba
en: Dark skin, light step, brooding. You must be the Siwan Felix raved about. It takes a lot to impress that one. You must be good. But let's not do awkward introductions. I prefer to get straight to business, and your reputation precedes you. If you've come to bleed for gain and glory, Cyrene welcomes you with open arms.

speaker: Man
en: I don't want you playing with him. The Man-Beast lives there! Do you want to be cut in pieces? Now come away!

speaker: Bayek
en: Seni (friend), forgive me, I overheard you just now. You said something about a Man-Beast.

speaker: Man
en: The Man-Beast has been taking people from here for months.

speaker: Bayek
en: People have gone missing? Have you told the Phylakitai?

speaker: Man
en: The Phylakitai are useless. Just last week, three fishermen disappeared. Bits of them floated in a few days later. They did nothing. Anyway, we know who it is — that raving old maniac over there. We're watching him.

speaker: Bayek
en: Things are often not what they appear. I should talk to this Man Beast.

speaker: Man 1
en: He might be possessed by Sobek himself.

speaker: Man 2
en: He's too crazy to be the Man Beast. He never does anything but pray.

speaker: Man 1
en: He is eating the victims of Sobek!

speaker: Man 2
en: No-one goes missing on his land. They just show up in the water near his house. We should leave him alone. His poor child.

speaker: The Man Beast
en: Sobek eats with his mouth... He with the pointed teeth... Sobek eats while he mates... He rends whom he will...

speaker: Bayek
en: My friend. Could I speak with you? Do you know anything about the missing people?

speaker: The Man Beast
en: I. Am. Not. Your. Friend. Go away from here! Sobek eats with his mouth... He with the pointed teeth... Sobek eats while he mates... He rends whom he will...

speaker: Bayek
en: I will not get anything useful out of him.

speaker: Bayek
en: There is meat in the baskets for feeding the fish. Gods, that could be human.

speaker: Bayek
en: Anything taken by the current ends up here.

speaker: Bayek
en: Flesh. it is rotting and waterlogged, and hard to identify. It's come here from upstream.

speaker: Bayek
en: This place is a damn slaughter yard! But I can't tell if the flesh is human. In all my years as a Medjay, I have never seen anything like this. It is floating here from somewhere further upstream.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hi. What's your name?

speaker: Child
en: This is my toy Sobek. See? He carries his babies in his mouth. Father made it for me.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is... a nice toy.

speaker: Child
en: Can you tell my friends to come back and play? Sobek didn't really eat the people in the river. It's just a game.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nek! (Shit!) More body parts! Where are they all coming from?

speaker: Bayek
en: This ruined felucca has been here a long time. The body parts are more recent. I should continue upstream and find the source.

speaker: Bayek
en: More blood in the water. It seems to be coming from that cave. By Amun, what is going on?

speaker: Bayek
en: What is this place? It stinks of death. This must be where all the body parts are coming from.

speaker: Bayek
en: Amun! So many corpses, all half eaten. Argh, the stench!

speaker: Man
en: Hello! Who's there? Please! Help me!

speaker: Bayek
en: Cushions and luxury. These look like seats for some kind of theater.

speaker: Bayek
en: Good wine, and refreshments. Whoever sat here was well pampered.

speaker: Man
en: Thank the gods! Hurry, we have to leave before he comes back.

speaker: Bayek
en: Who? What is happening here?

speaker: Man
en: The Embalmer. He's throwing people to crocodiles. His guests watch as they're ripped apart.

speaker: Bayek
en: Be calm. You are safe. Where is he now?

speaker: Man
en: Safe? No one is safe here! He kidnapped me at the market where I was selling fish. I'm getting out of here! I never imagined anyone could do something like this!

speaker: Bayek
en: I will find a way to the market. This Embalmer has given his last show.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nek! (Shit!) This embalmer is sick!

speaker: Bayek
en: Such extravagance. This Embalmer is making a lot of money.

speaker: Embalmer
en: Friends! I trust you enjoyed the show? Unfortunately, the next show may be delayed. I've only found one... participant. It may take time to find more.

speaker: Woman 1
en: I don't know if I should say this, I wouldn't want you to think me odd.

speaker: Woman 2
en: You're among friends, dear.

speaker: Woman 1
en: Well, have you considered using people from the slums? The Faiyum has no lack of them. They're of no real use.

speaker: Embalmer
en: I'll talk to my associate.

speaker: Embalmer
en: I don't want to hear it! Another show is filling up, and we're low on bait. Find me some more! The work we do is more important than you realize.

speaker: Man
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Embalmer
en: When the crocodile disfigured me I wanted to die. I wished I had. As I worked in the temple, I began to understand. I had been marked by the god himself. Our little show, it's much more than entertainment. It's a sacrament. An offering. In a way, you're playing the role of a priest. Remember that.

speaker: Man
en: That is a wonderful interpretation of things.

speaker: Embalmer
en: Do people really enjoy this? Boring. Unoriginal. Bland.

speaker: Bayek
en: Now I embalm you with death.

speaker: Bayek
en: A sick man. That's an end to his evil. May the gods deal with those who watched his shows.

speaker: Man
en: It's your own fault! You've been hiding opium from us! What do you think the Commander would do?

speaker: Meritmaat
en: Gentlemen. There is no need for further hostility. You're Mahu right?

speaker: Mahu
en: How do you know my name?

speaker: Meritmaat
en: Nothing much happens in Kerke I do not know about. Your wife just had your second child. And you are Kawab.

speaker: Kawab
en: That is right!

speaker: Meritmaat
en: The soldiers are not paying you enough. That is going to be tough when your new baby arrives. You too, Herihor. I know your father is sick. You could use some help.

speaker: Herihor
en: Who couldn't?

speaker: Meritmaat
en: Why do I not have gifts sent around for your families? Just to make things easier this month.

speaker: Man
en: Enough! Fine, you can carry on. But remember we have the girl. Any further trouble and she disappears.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do you need help?

speaker: Meritmaat
en: A Medjay! I am Meritmaat, the village leader. Ah, do not worry about they are just middle men for Ptolemy's soldiers. I have an understanding with their Commander. Opium and honey for protection of the village. He is the one we have to worry about.

speaker: Bayek
en: Sounds like they took a hostage?

speaker: Meritmaat
en: Hah, just like the Medjay of old! If you want to be a hero, they took her to the nearby military camp. If she still lives you will find her there.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will return with her soon, Meritmaat. And then you can decide if I am a hero.

speaker: Bayek
en: This must be the kidnapped girl. She is drugged, but still breathing. I have to get her out of here.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you okay? You were drugged.

speaker: Henuttawy
en: Yes... thank you, I... gods! The Commander was going to put me on the next opium shipment. Send me somewhere... far away.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Commander? Do you know where he is?

speaker: Henuttawy
en: I think he left the camp on a ship. That's all I remember. I'm sorry.

speaker: Bayek
en: Alright. Go and show yourself to Meritmaat. Do not let any soldiers see you.

speaker: Bayek
en: I should return to Meritmaat also. I need to talk to her about the Commander.

speaker: Meritmaat
en: Medjay! I heard you freed the girl.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Commander was not at the camp. But we should deal with him. Tell me everything you know.

speaker: Meritmaat
en: The local soldiers and middle men I can deal with. But the Commander... he's vicious. A murderer. I dare not confront him. Years ago he took another hostage. My own daughter. There was no Medjay to save us then. He killed her to assure our compliance. For the village's sake I did nothing.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have got an idea how to get to him. The shipments of opium go along the river. I will follow them, find him, and end your agreement.

speaker: Meritmaat
en: Then may Horus guide your blade, Medjay. Sink it deep! Do not be merciful! The Commander is guilty as Set.

speaker: Bayek
en: How did this all happen?

speaker: Meritmaat
en: We grow honey and opium. They're commodities the army found impossible to ignore. At first they tried to take over the village. Some of our men resisted. They were branded rebels and traitors and hunted down. Those that weren't killed fled North. Ironically, they joined with the rebels. We send them opium and money whenever we can. The Commander became suspicious, so he took another hostage. If you had not rescued her, I think he would have killed her too.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will deal with this murderer, I promise you.

speaker: Meritmaat
en: I have made the most of things. Until now I have managed to stop anyone else being taken. But we will never be free while the Commander lives.

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: Why does the commander tolerate Meritmaat, the old hag? I would have gutted her long ago.

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: You've heard the way she talks to us!

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: Yeah! We should abduct more of her children. She'll be much nicer.

speaker: Bayek
en: There is a sweet smell hanging in the air. Opium. This is the right ship.

speaker: Bayek
en: A manifest. This ship unloads at Memphis. That is where I will find the Commander.

speaker: Bayek
en: Memphis. The Commander terrorizing Kerke will be somewhere in this city. Probably near a dock.

speaker: Bayek
en: The murderous neket iadet (piece of shit) is dead. But what is this about Meritmaat's daughter? She might still be alive! And right here in Memphis!

speaker: Bayek
en: Greetings nebet. Are you the Commander's daughter?

speaker: Ipy
en: I am. May I help you?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am the bearer of... strange news. But you must believe me. Your mother still lives.

speaker: Ipy
en: My mother? I was abandoned as a child. How could that be? Who are you?

speaker: Bayek
en: I have something here you should read.

speaker: Bayek
en: Take your time. Decide what to do. Your mother is at Kerke, to the South. She misses you. If you do return to her, tell her that her Medjay friend fulfilled his... heroic task.

speaker: Sminthos
en: For the rarest and most exotic goods in Cyrene talk to the Mouse.

speaker: Sminthos
en: Hey you there, big strong Egyptian!

speaker: Man
en: That Futuo Sminthos! He's tainting our market with his worthless tat.

speaker: Woman 1
en: That Mouse is always sniffing around here.

speaker: Woman 2
en: He sold me a potion, said it would make Quintus fall madly in love with me.

speaker: Woman 1
en: And, did it?

speaker: Woman 2
en: Gave him the shits for a week. Now he won't even speak to me! That rodent ruined my life!

speaker: Bayek
en: Get many Egyptians in Cyrene?

speaker: Sminthos
en: You'll get no judgment from the Mouse, but you did stick out.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Mouse? An odd title my friend.

speaker: Sminthos
en: Yes, yes, I am the Mouse because I can access the more hard to find trinkets. If you follow me to my shop, I'll show you... I have bows, blades, scepters... you won't be disappointed. The Mouse guarantees it... Sir...

speaker: Bayek
en: Bayek. Alright, let's see what you have, Mouse.

speaker: Bayek
en: Don't you have trouble with the Romans.

speaker: Sminthos
en: Well you know what they say about our friends. The Greeks invented the threesome and the Romans added women. (laugh) Besides I know how to stay hidden, Sir Bayek, with the way I look, I have to. People think the Mouse is unlucky. They don't see I'm an entrepreneur and savior of the waifs and strays.

speaker: Bayek
en: Waifs and strays?

speaker: Sminthos
en: The children, Sir Bayek! I give them work, a roof over their little heads. Without me they'd be on the streets!

speaker: Sminthos
en: Oh cursed Mouse! Woeful Mouse! They took it, they took everything, Sir Bayek. The Roman swine must have taken my chest to the barracks. Please, will you recover it?

speaker: Bayek
en: And why would I do that?

speaker: Sminthos
en: Because you know what it's like to be brushed aside, victimized by those who hold themselves above you. The Mouse will die on the streets with no living to support him, and what of the children... will no-one think of the children? And I could probably spare a fine reward for my savior.

speaker: Bayek
en: I would not want the children on my conscience.

speaker: Sminthos
en: Gods bless you, Sir Bayek. I will wait for you in the market behind the baths. Good luck, my friend.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Mouse's stash!

speaker: Sminthos
en: You have saved my life for a second time, Sir Bayek! I am blessed! Blessed by the gods who brought you to me on this the greatest of days! The Mouse will embrace you! As a sign of my undying gratitude.

speaker: Bayek
en: Please don't!

speaker: Sminthos
en: Then money, I will shower you with riches to make Croesus jealous.

speaker: Bayek
en: Take care of yourself Mouse, try not to get caught in any more traps.

speaker: Sminthos
en: Ah such grace, such wit! You deserve more than mere money. Come see me again later, I will find you something special from my stash.

speaker: Sminthos
en: Sir Bayek, my eyes weep in joy at the sight of you. Did you hear? Some black market merchant is trying to undercut me!

speaker: Bayek
en: I see you have made new friends.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: They were setting up an ambush! It's a good thing I came to welcome you, eh? It's been months. Look at that beard!

speaker: Bayek
en: It's been nearly a year, my friend.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: It feels good to get out and fight! I am out of practice. In Siwa, everyone defers to the soldiers on pain of death... or worse.

speaker: Bayek
en: I've killed one of the masked ones. The Heron.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Four more. Come, it has been a long road. You need rest!

speaker: Bayek
en: No, no rest. Not until all the masked ones' guts lie baking in the sand.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Gods, I have missed you.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Where is your mount?

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah, there you are, boy!

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Let us go, seni (my brother)!

speaker: Bayek
en: How have you been holding up since I left?

speaker: Hepzefa
en: It has been difficult, Bayek. Without you, the villagers look to me to keep order. But the soldiers have set up a garrison, and they rule over all.

speaker: Bayek
en: A garrison in Siwa?

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Ptolemy wants the entire region kept under heel. I do my best to keep the villagers out of trouble. I could use your help.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'll do what I can. But do not forget, I have my own justice to pursue.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: I knew I could count on you, seni (friend).

speaker: Bayek
en: What happened here?

speaker: Hepzefa
en: The garrison soldiers are brutal. If they suspect a villager is lying to them, they burn his neighborhood. And worse.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Welcome home, Bayek! Siwa has missed you!

speaker: Soldier
en: You owe all you have, your farms, your goods, your children; you owe your very lives to His Highness, Ptolemy.

speaker: Bayek
en: The villagers are drained of life.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: No one in the wahat (oasis) can make a move without being questioned, threatened, taxed or beaten. We all have learned to obey and keep our heads down. You see how it is.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let's not attract attention.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Are you going to go to your house?

speaker: Bayek
en: Nothing there for me. Tell me about the Ibis.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Medunamun.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is he here?

speaker: Hepzefa
en: He is a plague on the oasis. As you can see, the soldiers have become more brutal since he arrived. Before, they got drunk and fought with the villagers. Now that Medunamun is here, they are disciplined and vicious.

speaker: Bayek
en: All the more reason to kill him.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Do not take him lightly. He is lean and sinewy, but very powerful.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Ah, home! Leave your mount, he will not stray far. Go ahead on in.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Rest, my friend. It has been a difficult day.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have no interest in rest. I must prepare for this man.

speaker: Rabiah
en: Hepzefa? Hepzefa! Once again, the soldiers—Bayek?

speaker: Bayek
en: Rabiah, my Rabiah.

speaker: Rabiah
en: I have worried about you.

speaker: Bayek
en: You know me, you should be worried!

speaker: Rabiah
en: Look at you. Cuts, contusions...

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm fine.

speaker: Rabiah
en: Sit, sit, sit. I'll take care of it.

speaker: Bayek
en: You haven't changed.

speaker: Rabiah
en: You and Aya, I've always patched you two up, made excuses to your parents... Times have changed, but you, I can count on.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Slumbering Osiris, I thought you would never wake up!

speaker: Bayek
en: Rabiah patched me up and I just...

speaker: Hepzefa
en: I let you sleep. You need to be alert to tangle with Medunamun. In fact, my friend...

speaker: Bayek
en: A new bow?

speaker: Hepzefa
en: See if you like it. Best spot to hit is right in the head. One of the dummies is sturdier than the other. More arrows in the rack over there. Good.

speaker: Woman
en: Hepzefa!

speaker: Hepzefa
en: What is it?

speaker: Woman
en: Soldiers are coming for you!

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Go! Come, quickly.

speaker: Soldier
en: Make certain no one gets out of the house alive. Hepzefa! We're just here to talk. Nomarch Rudjek's been killed. Your friend the Medjay may have been involved! Come out if you wish to clear his name. Prepare an ambush.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Nek (Shit)! They will find my letters and burn down my place. I will be executed.

speaker: Bayek
en: Don't worry. I will take care of this.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Watch out!

speaker: Soldier
en: What's that? Who's there?

speaker: Bayek
en: Keep low!

speaker: Hepzefa
en: He is getting too close.

speaker: Bayek
en: Now for the rest of them.

speaker: Bayek
en: That does it.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Thank you Bayek. I told you these neket iadets (pieces of shit) do not care.

speaker: Bayek
en: I cannot believe their gall.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: It is sad. Come upstairs. I will show you all the Medjay duties of Siwa. All the problems of Siwa are here. I try to help everyone, but it's more than I can do.

speaker: Bayek
en: So you're telling me you do not have the powers of a god?

speaker: Hepzefa
en: But the real problem is that man you want to kill: Medunamun. The people were hopeful when he first arrived. Surely things would improve. We soon learned the truth, actually...

speaker: Medunamun
en: I fear for the safety of your family, priest. I will move them to a more secure area.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: That is the man you're up against.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will find him and kill him.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Medunamun is a lot more powerful than he looks and he is surrounded by the finest soldiers.

speaker: Bayek
en: I do not care.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: You'll be killed. You need to get tougher if you want to murder than spindly shit. For sure you will need better armor.

speaker: Bayek
en: I can make that myself.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Weapons are more difficult. The soldiers took everything in the village.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will talk to the blacksmith.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Yes. Benipe can certainly make something for you. Or Senu can help you find what you need.

speaker: Bayek
en: Senu? Senu is alive?

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Look who is coming!

speaker: Bayek
en: Senu, old girl! In fine form.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Rabiah has nursed her to health.

speaker: Bayek
en: I must thank her.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: The people are desperate for your help, Bayek. They'll help you if you help them.

speaker: Bayek
en: I understand.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: When you get a chance, take a look at my table. Some villagers need help.

speaker: Priest
en: Guards are everywhere! By Serapis. Where is that Medjay? Only he can help me. I don't feel safe anymore. The gods are not welcome in Alexandria... Now I pray Amun save me.

speaker: Priest
en: Medjay! Over here!

speaker: Bayek
en: Priest? But why are you on the street?

speaker: Priest
en: The guards discovered that I gave their food back to the people. Now they hunt me. I have a bounty on my head. Being a priest of light is a dark job in this filthy city.

speaker: Bayek
en: I can get you out of Alexandria, Priest, if you like, but... I cannot keep you safe forever.

speaker: Priest
en: I ask too much of you, Medjay. There is a small temple north of here that will take me in. The Phylakitai will be watching the roads, Medjay. We must leave by the canal, there should be boats there.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will spew arrows on any who get in our way. Be like Amun, Priest. Perhaps we can sneak you out without the guards knowing.

speaker: Priest
en: Careful, Medjay! We must be cautious, Medjay!

speaker: Bayek
en: Hide, Priest! I will take care of these guards! Ha! You call that a swing! Come at me!

speaker: Bayek
en: You can come out now, Priest.

speaker: Priest
en: I...I've never seen blood before in such quantities. The Devourer and Apep must be smiling. And the smell. The stench.

speaker: Bayek
en: You... get used to it.

speaker: Priest
en: Truly?

speaker: Bayek
en: No.

speaker: Priest
en: Bayek. It is rare that priests are called upon to serve the people. And now I suffer for it.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are to serve the gods, Priest. Not the people.

speaker: Priest
en: Let's take one of these boats.

speaker: Bayek
en: And it will have to do. It looks sturdy enough.

speaker: Priest
en: I go to a temple near the Pharos. They will take me in. I hope. Perhaps it is true what they say - Alexandria is a city filled with liars.

speaker: Bayek
en: I've met a kind hand or two here in Alexandria, Priest.

speaker: Priest
en: Sometimes it's enough to know that not everyone would kill another for a drachma.

speaker: Priest
en: We are nearing the arsenal responsible for all ill that has befallen me. They will be on alert.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ready yourself then, Priest.

speaker: Priest
en: They come after us with feluccas?

speaker: Bayek
en: Apparently they wish to show other priests the error of your ways.

speaker: Priest
en: It was only food! The people were starving.

speaker: Bayek
en: You may show yourself, Priest. They have gone.

speaker: Priest
en: I owe you more than my life, Medjay.

speaker: Bayek
en: We are not yet at your island. We still have a little ways to go.

speaker: Priest
en: Thank Serapis. Now, what were we saying...

speaker: Bayek
en: Here is where you wish to stop? Is this the island?

speaker: Priest
en: Yes. It is yet a short distance to the temple. I will be safe, Medjay. I will practice at the temple as a new man. I will leave you with a small token of my gratitude.

speaker: Bayek
en: May your happiness multiply.

speaker: Priest
en: This where you and I part, Medjay. I am a Priest no longer. Lysander was my name. It will be nice to be Lysander once more, I think.

speaker: Bayek
en: Walk in peace then, Lysander.

speaker: Lysander
en: And you Medjay... Bayek. Thank you.

speaker: Bayek
en: A history of the lost keepers of this place.

speaker: Bayek
en: The sword is missing. I wonder if Maahes succeeded at the house of Serqet, or whether his cause was lost there?

speaker: Man
en: Who's there? I am armed! I will hurt you so much the gods will sing stories of how badly for ages!

speaker: Bayek
en: Keep the peace, friend. I am merely curious.

speaker: Man
en: There is little enough left of value. The jackals have already stripped this site clean!

speaker: Bayek
en: I read about an ancient battle, between Maahes and Ochus, and wondered if it was here.

speaker: Man
en: This was where Maahes fought and died at the hands of Bagoas the eunuch and Mentor the Rhodian! You may have read my version of Ma'ani-Djehuti ("I have seen Thoth")? No? No matter.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do you know what became of Maahes' sword?

speaker: Man
en: The Sword of Ptah? Said to be sacred to both Sekhmet and Serqet? No, but as I said, this place has long been plundered. The bandits stay north of here, so I stay far away.

speaker: Bayek
en: Thank you. I'll head north.

speaker: Bayek
en: These must be the bandits the historian spoke of. I wonder where they are keeping the Sword of Ptah.

speaker: Bayek
en: Thank you dearest goddesses. I will use this to keep the faith.

speaker: Woman
en: You cannot stay in there! You are only making it more difficult on yourself!

speaker: Woman
en: My idiot brother has barricaded himself inside.

speaker: Man
en: Who is that you're speaking to!? It's one of them, isn't it!?

speaker: Woman
en: No, you fool! He fears Sefetu's men. But hiding his head in a bush solves nothing!

speaker: Man
en: I am not an ostrich! Do I hear horses!? Is it them? You better run!

speaker: Woman
en: Please. If he does not work, Sefetu's tax collectors will do something terrible.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am not sure if I can convince him... but I will keep an eye out for these tax collectors. Perhaps I can persuade them to leave you alone.

speaker: Bayek
en: A hidden entrance. How long has this been here?

speaker: Bayek
en: A dead end. It does not make sense. There must be a way forward.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah! By Amun! What is this?

speaker: Bayek
en: This is not Egyptian.

speaker: Pedestal Narrator
en: Retransmission. Segment 6. Acquiring Contemporaneity. It has been one-hundred nine days since the Great Catastrophe. The messenger speaks. Wake up. Not from a dreamless sleep or an absence of light. But from a reality that will soon cease to be. Wake up. The next chapter is unstoppable. And yet. The greatest revolutions sometimes originate from the confines of impossibility, do they not? Change your mind. Subvert your perception. Stop this world. Bend it into something new. Destiny is not without irony. Here I am, imploring a lesser version of myself... to do what I could never do. In this timeless moment, you and I are a bridge. Both of us from different eras, meeting halfway at the narrowing of the hourglass in this ocean of sand. It is not enough to tell time. You must learn Time. (Reality is a simulation. Break the code.) And in so doing, escape the inescapable. Fill in the blanks: the ones hiding between words, between worlds. Find the spaces that we could not erase, the variables that ended up erasing us. If you do not, they will erase you as well. Time told of a story that ended with us, and now it tells of a story that ends with you. Once upon a time, a new story will begin. After the functions which run our days have scattered into an array of random numbers. We found solace in Order, we thought it would help us rule the world. We were wrong. Order never served us. It has kept us within the code, within the boundaries. We were tricked into thinking we were the ones writing the rules when they were in fact guiding us to our conclusion. You need to transgress. You, of all people, understand the value of disobeying. Take an unexpected turn, away from the path that is drawn straight ahead of you. The Animus was humankind's first unconscious attempt to explain what it could not see. Understanding genetic memories, an eye into history. But the Animus bears a fatal flaw. It follows the rules from those who embrace Order just as we did. It allows you to witness – but not alter. Your Animus is different. As is the mind that imagined it. It could escape the code. It could do that leap, and make possible a decision that defies the order of things that are. Wake up. Be the chaos that comes to be. Gods are just like you and me. Remember. Nothing is real. Everything is permitted.

speaker: Bayek
en: Master Taharqa? My name is Bayek, from Siwa.

speaker: Taharqa
en: I am indeed Taharqa, grand planner of Sais and steward of Letopolis.

speaker: Bayek
en: I met your family. Your wife sent me here. She said you might know about the one called the Scarab.

speaker: Taharqa
en: This is not the place to speak, for who knows who may overhear our words? Come inside, and I will answer you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your son is very proud of your work. He misses you.

speaker: Taharqa
en: He'll be here soon. I dream of my son, and his sons, following in my steps. The world is made by great men dreaming big. What do you dream of, Bayek?

speaker: Bayek
en: I do not have the luxury of dreams. Just finding the Scarab.

speaker: Taharqa
en: The Scarab preys upon the weak. He is no threat to me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you not afraid of the Scarab, Taharqa? It seems after what he did to your father-in-law...

speaker: Taharqa
en: Whatever happens to poor Ghupa tears me. Whatever my life's work, whatsoever I did to bring that down upon him... I beg the gods forgive me.

speaker: Servant
en: Master Taharqa! They're attacking the ruins again!

speaker: Taharqa
en: Bayek, come fight with me!

speaker: Taharqa
en: The wind is picking up. Not good.

speaker: Taharqa
en: That keening is the voice of the (sandstorm). The desert dogs use the storm as a rallying cry. These reavers use the sandstorm to mask their raids. Stay close to me! Do not let these curs surround you!

speaker: Taharqa
en: I will not let you destroy my great work! Over here! Drive these neket iadets (pieces of shit) back! They pour out of the storm! These reavers fly on the wings of the storm! Your blood will water the soil of my home! You face the greatest of Egypt! Come, Medjay, fight with me! Quick, hunt them down! Spears of Letopolis, rise up and defend your homes! Medjay, show them the teeth of justice! Bayek, do not stray into the storm! You expected to find our soft bellies, but instead, you have found our iron teeth! These reavers think themselves lions, they are but whipped curs! Bayek, hunt them down! Stay with me, Bayek! Letopolis will stand against you, curs! Die, you sons of dogs!

speaker: Taharqa
en: Bayek, you fell upon them like Sobek's teeth! Bayek, ride with us! These desert dogs have crossed me for the last time. And with your fierce iron, I know we can end their threat.

speaker: Bayek
en: I understand your thirst for blood, Taharqa, but these bandits are not my concern. Tell me about the Scarab before you ride.

speaker: Taharqa
en: Is that not the badge of a Medjay you wear? These reavers are a threat to the good and innocent people of Letopolis. Come with me, Bayek! And once we have returned these curs to the desert they so love, then I will tell you the story you want to hear.

speaker: Bayek
en: All right. I will join your cause for today.

speaker: Taharqa
en: Come, Bayek! Take up your iron and join us! Brave, loyal servants of Letopolis! We will root these reavers out of their holes, and spill their blood on the sand!

speaker: Bayek
en: The task you've put yourself up to. It seems impossible.

speaker: Taharqa
en: Only the gods can know that for sure, Bayek. And if I do not reach for the stars, how will I know how close I can get? Letopolis was a wonder once before the desert overtook it. I mean to show the world, to show the gods, that men can conquer anything if they put their minds to it. Perhaps you have been sent by the gods to help me realize my vision. A strong arm, a keen eye. We could restore this land to glory.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have my own great work ahead of me.

speaker: Taharqa
en: We shall see if I cannot convince you!

speaker: Bayek
en: Hmm. Sounds like a few bandits are roosting up top.

speaker: Taharqa
en: My thanks to you, Bayek. Before you arrived, I thought my dream was doomed to die. You gave me the strength to hunt down these reavers.

speaker: Bayek
en: Who were they?

speaker: Taharqa
en: Blood-fevered followers of Sekhmet, the Lady of Slaughter. They wish nothing more than chaos and ruin.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are they connected to the Scarab?

speaker: Taharqa
en: No, they think themselves lions, but they are no more than carrion eaters. And now they will feed the scavengers! I will bring this priest back to the city. Meet me at my house. We will dine and I will tell you what you need to know.

speaker: Priest Karro
en: May Ptah bless you and the protector saving me, Master Taharqa.

speaker: Taharqa
en: How did you end up here?

speaker: Priest Karro
en: I was kidnapped by these blood-crazed raiders! I thought the road from Memphis to Letopolis was safe.

speaker: Taharqa
en: It is now. And I will ensure it stays so. You say you came from Memphis?

speaker: Priest Karro
en: Memphis is home to many priests. They do not need me there. But Letopolis is fertile ground, planted by your hard work.

speaker: Taharqa
en: How are things in Memphis?

speaker: Priest Karro
en: I must admit... Memphis is under a shadow. The high priest angered the gods and is cursed to see the doom of the city. Your messengers reached Memphis, singing of your vision of tomorrow. I have come here to serve the gods.

speaker: Taharqa
en: Once you are rested, we will make a home for you in Letopolis.

speaker: Kawab
en: Bayek! Did you see the sandstorm? Come! Father said you'd join us for dinner!

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm glad you made it safely, Maharet.

speaker: Maharet
en: Ha, yes, the gods blessed our passage.

speaker: Kawab
en: We saw vultures and a hyena! And so much sand!

speaker: Taharqa
en: Ha ha ha, enough sand to fill a lifetime! That is why we need so many to help us with our great work.

speaker: Bayek
en: And what do you promise them, Taharqa?

speaker: Taharqa
en: A parcel of land with a house to call their own. They must only help reclaim it from the desert.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is all? Just dig up your house? Heh.

speaker: Taharqa
en: It is no simple task. We must all pitch in, to honor the gods.

speaker: Kawab
en: People know his vision is a true one!

speaker: Bayek
en: It is good to honor your father, Kawab.

speaker: Taharqa
en: To the savior of Letopolis!

speaker: Maharet
en: Mmm, let us have some honeyed dates now, and... Are you all right, Bayek?

speaker: Taharqa
en: Are you unwell?

speaker: Bayek
en: May the gods be against you, Taharqa, in all that you do!

speaker: Bayek
en: (spits) (tries to clear throat) (feels the sand in his teeth) Senu... Aya... where are you, my love? Khemu... I am failing you... please don't... hate me. Soon, I will walk the outer darkness with the Hidden One, leading me into the Field of Reeds...

speaker: Medunamun
en: You have become that which you seek to punish. Did my death please you? To scratch my name out on your skin? All that blood and vengeance, but will it bring you peace? Aren't you tired? Just lie down in the sand and sleep.

speaker: Rabiah
en: Still so handsome, if I were a girl again, I would give Aya reason to be jealous! You and Aya, you walk such a dangerous path. Medjays. The last. Bayek of Siwa? What are you of now? He he he. The stars brought me. The stars will take me too. It has been so long, Bayek. Too long.

speaker: Hepzefa
en: Would you turn your back on me, friend? You are a normal man, yet the fate of our world is upon your shoulders? I will die if I must, protecting Siwa, that which you abandoned. Our people still need your protection, Medjay. Siwa yearns for you, Bayek. Remember your roots. Siwa is your home. Come share a beer, seni. (friend.)

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: The poets defend your ka. You are a normal man, yet the fate of our world is upon your shoulders? You must free them, Medjay. Or their bones will turn to dust. Do you think your path is certain?

speaker: Aya
en: Where is our son, Bayek? Where is my Khemu? Bring me back our son. The Masked Ones are everywhere. May Amun walk at your side. Bring me the heads of the Order. We must allow our son to pass into the Field of Reeds. So you remember when we were children? We lived so fiercely, so free.

speaker: Eudoros
en: The Snake? Me? It's laughable how little you know. You are an actor among fools! Did it feel good? Killing me, watching the light fade from my eyes? The Snake grows and lives in sands untouchable.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: We became close, Aya and I, she spoke highly of you, as a Medjay. Do you really think you can save our people, Bayek?

speaker: Cleopatra
en: How could a boy hope to rule a kingdom? The Eagle will not take the Serpent in its claws. We cannot stand by and let Egypt fall to our enemies!

speaker: Ptolemy
en: Pharaohs made chariots, brought gods into human hearts, our divinity is to be protected by the Medjay. They have killed Egypt, do you understand? Bow before your king, Egyptian!

speaker: Bayek
en: There now, good boy.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hiyah! May the gods smile upon you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Stripped of armor, weapons, and coin. Where to begin? Now, to hurry before the wind erases the tracks.

speaker: Bayek
en: First my steel. Then, the Scarab.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Did you pack up the gear?

speaker: Guard 2
en: Yes, remarkable armaments. It's packed up in a crate as payment to Sefetu.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Good. We'll send it to Fort Nikiou in a few days.

speaker: Guard 2
en: How long do you think it will take for him to die?

speaker: Guard 1
en: The guy we buried? Hmm. Two days?

speaker: Guard 3
en: He looked tough. I'd bet five drachma he'd survive for at least three.

speaker: Guard 1
en: You're on. Wait. Who is going to check?

speaker: Bayek
en: They should have stayed in the shadows.

speaker: Taharqa
en: Oh gods, smile upon my work so that my name might remain enduring in this temple forever and ever. O mother Nut, watch over me so that I may be placed among the imperishable stars and may never die. O mother Nut, watch over me, so that I may be placed among the stars and never die. Oh gods, smile upon my work so that my name endures.

speaker: Bayek
en: I see you now, out of the shadows.

speaker: Taharqa
en: Me? I do not hide in the shadows. I was in front of you the whole time. Your eyes were too weak to see. You are a speck, to be swallowed up by time.

speaker: Bayek
en: For a moment I thought you were doing good in this life.

speaker: Taharqa
en: Good? Evil? Those are phantasms of the desert. No more than a mirage, like yourself. Soon only my true vision will remain.

speaker: Taharqa
en: So... this is how a dream dies.

speaker: Taharqa
en: I could have built something to last an age!

speaker: Bayek
en: And Ghupa could have sung stories of your accomplishments.

speaker: Taharqa
en: There are things I regret! We all labor for higher powers. We are all in thrall to greater forces. There is no escape.

speaker: Taharqa
en: I am but one in the Order of Ancients. This victory will bring you no peace!

speaker: Bayek
en: It is not peace that I seek. It is not for my soul that I walk this path.

speaker: Taharqa
en: The Order of Ancients will remember me as the bringer of waters and a builder of cities!

speaker: Bayek
en: Or the desert will blow in... and scatter the dreams of Letopolis like dust.

speaker: Kawab
en: Aaaahhh! Father!

speaker: Kawab
en: I'll cut you down! Like you did my father!

speaker: Kawab
en: I thought you were our friend! I hate you!

speaker: Bayek
en: Take care of him. Try to make him understand if you can.

speaker: Maharet
en: You have brought blood and death to my house.

speaker: Bayek
en: You were blind, but now you must open your eyes. Your husband was the Scarab. He did this. Your father was tortured and scarred by this man. As were so many others.

speaker: Maharet
en: No...

speaker: Bayek
en: It is up to you to raise your boy into the light, out of the blood and shadows of his father's legacy.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am sorry, my son.

speaker: Town crier
en: Hustlers! Entrepreneurs! Wanderers! Seek not your solace here, but let your feet carry you to fabled Letopolis. Letopolis is a dream given form—a new home for you—built by your hands and labors. It is not without its dangers, but the promise of a glorious tomorrow awaits you! It is a shining lighthouse of hope, all alone in the desert night.

speaker: Woman 1
en: I heard Nofure say they were packing up to move to Letopolis.

speaker: Woman 2
en: They are going to risk the trip?

speaker: Woman 1
en: So she said. Their farm is failing, so they see it as a new start.

speaker: Woman 2
en: It sounds like a lot of work. To restore and rebuild a whole city.

speaker: Woman 1
en: Yes, but they say it is a promise of a new life.

speaker: Woman 2
en: If you believe them.

speaker: Woman 1
en: Well, I'll wait for Nofure to get settled and write us with news. Then we will see.

speaker: Man 1
en: I heard another merchant failed to pay Sefetu.

speaker: Man 2
en: What happened?

speaker: Man 1
en: The firebrand had his soldiers burn the man's ship and all his goods. Told him if he failed to pay again, next time it would be his flesh that would burn.

speaker: Man 2
en: That son of a...

speaker: Man 1
en: Not too loud! You do not know who is listening.

speaker: Man 3
en: Where did you hear that?

speaker: Man 4
en: Some of the guards.

speaker: Man 3
en: And what did they say?

speaker: Man 4
en: That they passed a field of victims buried in the desert.

speaker: Man 3
en: Who did it?

speaker: Man 4
en: No one knows. Maybe the Scarab.

speaker: Man 5
en: The tax collectors ask for too much. It's not worth it.

speaker: Man 6
en: But what can we do?

speaker: Man 5
en: I will not put words between your teeth, but I am going to pack my things and travel to Letopolis. Master Taharqa is building a wonderful place for all.

speaker: Man 6
en: It is tempting... but all my family is here. You are lucky to have no wife or children, you can just leave.

speaker: Woman 3
en: Master Taharqa's wife is so kind. I cannot thank the gods enough for delivering her to us.

speaker: Man 7
en: I have heard that about Lady Maharet.

speaker: Woman 3
en: It's true. She heard our business was suffering, and bought a full cart of cloth for her new home.

speaker: Man 7
en: Are they moving to Letopolis?

speaker: Woman 3
en: Yes. That is where he works all the time. I only hope they don't forget those of us who still live here.

speaker: Egyptian soldier 1
en: That old mute was skulking around again.

speaker: Egyptian soldier 2
en: Isn't he from some rich family?

speaker: Egyptian soldier 1
en: Maybe. Maybe that's why no one has chased him out of town.

speaker: Egyptian soldier 2
en: I think he lives up at the Taharqa estate.

speaker: Man 8
en: And why do you want to work here?

speaker: Man 9
en: Even as far as Cyrene I heard about the Brewery of Sais, and the recipe that Master Harkuf has crafted.

speaker: Man 8
en: Yes, his father built it, and he keeps it successful.

speaker: Man 9
en: Everyone speaks so highly of him!

speaker: Man 8
en: He is a great man. If anything were to happen to him, many in this area would suffer.

speaker: Man 10
en: My dearest, we do not have enough to pay Sefetu his accursed taxes. When he comes, I will talk to him about selling myself into bonded labor.

speaker: Woman 4
en: No, no, you don't have to! I confessed our plight to Lady Maharet and she gifted me a purse, full of coins. It will buy us a month or two.

speaker: Man 10
en: That family is so generous! We must make a libation to the gods in their honor!

speaker: Woman 5
en: Is there any news about Jeska?

speaker: Woman 6
en: Nothing since that demon's soldiers arrested her. None escape the Firebrand's fort alive.

speaker: Woman 5
en: It's not fair! She was going to help us get out of Sais!

speaker: Woman 6
en: Nothing is fair. We must pray the gods lift Cleopatra to her rightful place, to bring us out of fear and pain.

speaker: Man 11
en: Careful you don't overfill the jars!

speaker: Man 12
en: Give me another portion of dates.

speaker: Man 13
en: Have you had Macedonian dates? I tasted some from a merchant last time I was in Alexandria. Best I have ever had.

speaker: Man 14
en: Where is this delivery headed?

speaker: Man 15
en: To Yamu, for the Sekhmet ceremony. Get them sealed up and on the cart.

speaker: Bayek
en: I seek the master brewer, Harkhuf.

speaker: Harkhuf
en: I have no time. Speak to one of my overseers, if you must.

speaker: Bayek
en: You misunderstand. I am a Medjay. Apollodorus sent me.

speaker: Harkhuf
en: Apollodorus! Of course.

speaker: Bayek
en: He sent me for the Scarab, the shadow that darkens Sais.

speaker: Harkhuf
en: Shh! Please! That is an evil name to speak aloud! Apollodorus knows that people are suffering. In my position, many confide in me. Trade is strangled, the soldiers run rampant, and the weight of Ptolemy's taxation crush the breath from us. Come with me. Let us retire where we have a roof overhead.

speaker: Harkhuf
en: There are many terrible stories about the Scarab, I am sure Apollodorus told you. Tales of mutilations, disappearances, and folk buried in the desert and left to die. A horrendous fate. Trapped in the shimmering sand. Your mind and body pounded by the relentless sun. Waiting for the final release into the Duat.

speaker: Harkhuf
en: But these are only stories. There are real villains in Sais... but the Scarab? If he exists, it is not safe to speak of him.

speaker: Bayek
en: The investigations of Harkhuf's agents, concerns of the people. Sais is no different than Siwa.

speaker: Harkhuf
en: The last man who asked questions about the Scarab was near beaten to death, with his tongue cut out.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hmmm. Who was he?

speaker: Harkhuf
en: Old Ghupa... Father-in-law to the most powerful man in the region, Taharqa.

speaker: Harkhuf
en: That boy, Kawab, is his grandson.

speaker: Bayek
en: Eh, you tired of winning? I'm looking for your grandfather. Do you know where he went?

speaker: Kawab
en: No, he left on the road to Camp Pyrrhos. He should have been home by now.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'll see if I can find him along the road.

speaker: Man 15
en: Is it true? Did Sefetu burn your sister's farm?

speaker: Woman 7
en: Yes! He has no mercy!

speaker: Man 15
en: What about your sister and her family?

speaker: Woman 7
en: They escaped, thank the gods. Jeska helped them out of town, past the guards at Camp Pyrrhos.

speaker: Man 15
en: This situation is impossible!

speaker: Woman 7
en: Someone must do something! How can Pharaoh Ptolemy let the abuse continue?

speaker: Greek soldier 1
en: What are we to do with the beggar that Markos caught in the (officer's) tent?

speaker: Greek soldier 2
en: If he survives the beating the men gave him, we'll sell him at the harbor for a drachma.

speaker: Greek soldier 1
en: Did you know he was mute?

speaker: Greek soldier 2
en: Perhaps half a drachma, then.

speaker: Greek soldier 3
en: What happened to the beggar ?

speaker: Greek soldier 4
en: The mute? Markos and Tykon beat him for sneaking around the camp. Poor bastard collapsed.

speaker: Greek soldier 5
en: By the gods, Markos, I think you've killed him.

speaker: Greek soldier 6
en: No, no, he still breathes. Stupid fool. This will teach him.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ghupa. I will get you out.

speaker: Bayek
en: I think you will survive.

speaker: Bayek
en: I know the Scarab took your tongue. But we can help each other. Harkhuf told me that you were investigating the Scarab. Help me, and I can ensure he dies.

speaker: Kawab
en: Grandfather! Are you all right? Is he hurt?

speaker: Bayek
en: Banged up, bruised and thirsty. The soldiers did not take kindly to him. But he will be all right. Where is your father, Kawab? We must speak of this.

speaker: Kawab
en: Father is away, on his great work. Mother! Grandfather is hurt! Soldiers mistook him for a beggar again!

speaker: Maharet
en: Father, what have you done this time?

speaker: Bayek
en: He was searching for the Scarab. I hope he can help me. And, in return, I can protect your family.

speaker: Maharet
en: The Scarab is nonsense. Everyone knows this.

speaker: Kawab
en: He wants you to read them.

speaker: Bayek
en: It looks like the Scarab is summoning warriors to the city of Letopolis.

speaker: Maharet
en: By the gods! That is where my husband is.

speaker: Bayek
en: The city swallowed by the desert?

speaker: Kawab
en: It is Father's destiny to rebuild it! We're going to join him soon. Right, Mother?

speaker: Maharet
en: Yes. My husband Taharqa has been slaving there for months. I am sure he can help you. He knows everyone there.

speaker: Kawab
en: If you go, tell him I can't wait to see him!

speaker: Bayek
en: Of course I will, Kawab.

speaker: Bayek
en: I should meet with Gamilat near the pyramid.

speaker: Bayek
en: I cannot believe this pyramid is being taken away! For what sick cause?

speaker: Bayek
en: Gamilat, there you are.

speaker: Gamilat
en: I must find a way into the pyramid. O gods. Glory and heroes are all that a people need. It makes life livable. If I cannot find these shards of star, the will of Nabatea and Egypt will be crushed. Ptahmose is fierce. I may lose a few men in order to win this battle.

speaker: Gamilat
en: Bayek, our hero! Just in time. We are planning our raid on Ptahmose, Rufio's mason.

speaker: Bayek
en: He is the one leading this pillage?

speaker: Gamilat
en: Yes! The temple will be gone soon. The pyramid as well. Ptahmose does not care about Egypt.

speaker: Gamilat
en: He has employed Nabateans to carry out his sad work for Rufio. A soulless wheka. He would give Amun to Rome as a slave if he could.

speaker: Gamilat
en: The people need monuments and sacred sites. If they disappear, the people's spirit will be crushed.

speaker: Bayek
en: They will remain, if we kill this Ptahmose fast enough.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let's get this Ptahmose.

speaker: Gamilat
en: This is our best chance to kill him, away from his camp, we must take him now! If we kill him, we will be seen as legends. I will fight beside you with all my heart.

speaker: Bayek
en: Shhhh. Quiet. Stay focused.

speaker: Gamilat
en: Romans are all around the pyramid, faithless bastards.

speaker: Bayek
en: He isn't here!

speaker: Gamilat
en: Nek! (Shit!)

speaker: Gamilat
en: Ahhhhhh!

speaker: Bayek
en: Gamilat?

speaker: Gamilat
en: I'm okay! There's a secret passage down here!

speaker: Bayek
en: I should join the "hero".

speaker: Gamilat
en: Amazing isn't it Bayek? There must be a pharaoh buried down here!

speaker: Bayek
en: A hidden chamber of our ancestors.

speaker: Gamilat
en: Magnificent, isn't it? Check for treasure, more of it, to fund our cause!

speaker: Bayek
en: We should leave and get Ptahmose, that is our priority.

speaker: Gamilat
en: What is this? What were they constructing down here?

speaker: Bayek
en: We will need to find a way through.

speaker: Bayek
en: And what of this pyramid?

speaker: Gamilat
en: A failed venture of Taharqa's in honor of the pharaoh Amenmesse. Legend has it a sacred rock fell from the sky... Taharqa was seeking shards from this rock. Rumour has it they are stored in this pyramid. How I would love to find them! Haganu calls them the shards of star. A blade made of these shards would make its bearer very powerful. I would love to see you wield such a weapon Bayek!

speaker: Bayek
en: These shards cannot fall into Roman hands.

speaker: Gamilat
en: I cannot climb like you Bayek. Help me get to such great heights.

speaker: Bayek
en: Stay on this platform while I find a way to move it.

speaker: Gamilat
en: By the gods it's working! I'm rising like the sun! Almost there!

speaker: Gamilat
en: I have reached the exit Bayek, oh thank you great Hidden One!

speaker: Gamilat
en: Snakes everywhere! My father died from a snake bite.

speaker: Bayek
en: Come on my seni (friend).

speaker: Gamilat
en: These snakes remind me of Apep.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have fought Apep before.

speaker: Gamilat
en: More junk in our way!

speaker: Bayek
en: Not a problem.

speaker: Bayek
en: So Ptahmose serves Rome?

speaker: Gamilat
en: Yes, I'm sure he works for Cleopatra even. Rufio is Marc Antony's General and so they all defer to that savage couple of monarchs.

speaker: Bayek
en: None of them can be trusted.

speaker: Gamilat
en: She is the rightful ruler, by blood. Her dynasty is ours too, many Nabateans believe in her.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do you?

speaker: Gamilat
en: I would like to meet her and decide. See her so-called divinity. But you have, isn't that right?

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes. She does seduce the hearts of the people. But her dynasty is one of dust and betrayal. Amunet knows this all too well.

speaker: Gamilat
en: Some say she brings greatness to Alexandria.

speaker: Bayek
en: Nek. (Shit.) Greatness is not something to strive for.

speaker: Gamilat
en: I adore it. One must accept one is great, as you are.

speaker: Bayek
en: Stay on the platform, I will make it rise.

speaker: Gamilat
en: Bayek, I think I may have found the shards of star!

speaker: Bayek
en: What have you found?

speaker: Gamilat
en: A scroll! Nek! (Shit!) Not the sacred objects I was hoping for. Let's get out of here!

speaker: Bayek
en: Our troubles are not over.

speaker: Gamilat
en: One more battle before we are free again!

speaker: Gamilat
en: You keep the scroll, it means nothing to me. Perhaps you can learn more form it.

speaker: Gamilat
en: I will get the rebels at my outpost to lead the attack on Ptahmose.

speaker: Bayek
en: Too many innocents may die. I will do this alone.

speaker: Gamilat
en: As you wish. Rain upon him like the soul of the sky.

speaker: Bayek
en: A mysterious poem. Later I will explore the Temple of Thoth.

speaker: Bayek
en: You are no mason, and Amun does not run in your ka. Only Anubis does.

speaker: Ptahmose
en: If they refuse to speak, make the incisions in their skin, and push scarabs into their flesh. And have them drink rotten wine. If they do not divulge anything, skin them. Slowly.

speaker: Rebel
en: Please no! I have told you everything, by all the gods, I will not lie to you! Just kill me already! Kill me please!

speaker: Ptahmose
en: Rome guides Egypt. The Masonic brotherhood will bring all our sacred shards into the great temples. Under our tutelage, the eye of Horus will overlook Egypt, and act as a beacon for our Masonic order. I will share these riches with the great Oracles of Rome. We need the Blades of Thoth. Where are they? The entire temple is ours. Rufio will be pleased.

speaker: Ptahmose
en: Are those the Blades of Thoth?

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes. The shards of the star were not meant for you, Ptahmose.

speaker: Ptahmose
en: I cannot believe it. Kill that neket iadet! (Piece of shit!)

speaker: Ptahmose
en: Rufio, the shards of star still elude us...

speaker: Ptamose
en: The Order is eternal. You are ephemeral.

speaker: Bayek
en: I should meet with the Hidden Ones. Tell them the good news.

speaker: Man
en: Aristo's work is fine. A peripatetic philosopher, it's a shame what has happened to him.

speaker: Callista
en: Curse the King! Curse this miserable city! Curse Eudoros! May they all rot! Where's that bottle of wine? No one can get him back for me! He'll die in prison because of that viper, Eudoros! What will I do without him? Without my Aristo? My comforter, my job, my love.

speaker: Callista
en: Who are you!? One of Eudoros' phylakes?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am no friend of Eudoros'.

speaker: Callista
en: He's brought nothing but sorrow to my husband Aristo. The great poet-philosopher... jailed! Jailed for writing beautiful things!

speaker: Bayek
en: Words are a powerful weapon.

speaker: Callista
en: My love spent years writing his masterwork. Years! Then Eudoros plagiarized it and passed my husband's genius off as his own!

speaker: Bayek
en: And Aristo took him to court?

speaker: Callista
en: Months of arguments! In the end, my husband is beaten, ridiculed and tossed in a cage!

speaker: Bayek
en: Is this what passes for justice in Alexandria?

speaker: Callista
en: Oh, my dear man, if you right this wrong, my husband and I can flee this city and be done with this ordeal. If you free him, I know of a boat that will take him on the southern docks, I will wait for you. Please, just bring me back my Aristo.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is this Aristo?

speaker: Aristo
en: Who's this? Another of Eudoros' sycophants come to sneer? Leave me alone with my woes.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am a friend of Phanos! A protector.

speaker: Aristo
en: Hit that one again! He deserves it. Get them! Hit that one next! That one smells vile, look out!

speaker: Aristo
en: You have more courage than Achilles himself! You've released me from daily beatings!

speaker: Bayek
en: We should go quickly.

speaker: Aristo
en: The vlakos broke my hip. Be careful, I pray you!

speaker: Bayek
en: Your wife tells me to get you out of Alexandria.

speaker: Aristo
en: My wife! The dear woman. Yes, there's a boat in port. Take me there. That Eudoros! What a detestable man! He couldn't forgive me for writing a better book. It was a book about the Nile. Full of marvelous descriptions. I'm very good at descriptions, if I do say. That's why Eudoros stole so much of my book! His own writing is insipid! He know nothing of the Nile River! Couldn't describe a hippopotamus if it bit him on the ass. The soldiers will certainly kill me if they find us. And what will become of my dear wife? She is the light of my life. She hated my book, though. "Too many crocodiles." she says. Which is a fair criticism. Still, Eudoros has a lot to answer for.

speaker: Bayek
en: I should tell you, Eudoros is dead.

speaker: Aristo
en: Glad to hear it. May he roast in Hades for eternity. Did you kill Eudoros yourself?

speaker: Bayek
en: I did.

speaker: Aristo
en: Good man. I hope it was painful for that dung-eater.

speaker: Aristo
en: Please, we must get out of this city. We must flee. Those damned guards will find me. Egypt is no place for a philosopher. This new generation of Alexandrian poets seems to make a new order.

speaker: Bayek
en: They certainly take risks.

speaker: Aristo
en: Give them my regards, will you. It is ever harder to produce good works here.

speaker: Callista
en: Aristo! Over here! The boat is ready. We set sail as soon as you're aboard.

speaker: Aristo
en: My wife! Thank the beneficent god!

speaker: Aristo
en: We made it!

speaker: Callista
en: My love! I'm so grateful that you are free!

speaker: Bayek
en: You should leave, the Phylakitai will surely come after you.

speaker: Aristo
en: I shall flee. My wife has booked us passage to Crete. It was always our plan to go there. Perhaps we will have a better life there.

speaker: Bayek
en: May the gods look over you on your journey.

speaker: Aristo
en: My beliefs on duty and honor are ambivalent, but I can see that you have done yours. If all of Egypt was filled with men of your virtue, life would be divine.

speaker: Bayek
en: Burning corpses! This is blasphemy! Who did this?

speaker: Bayek
en: Hey, why are you burning the dead? Don't you fear the gods? Their souls will be forever cursed.

speaker: Woman
en: I'm sorry to do it, but I have no choice in this. The gods themselves have afflicted us with a pestilence. The dead must be burned to save the living.

speaker: Bayek
en: What pestilence? Is there a plague?

speaker: Woman
en: Truly, I don't know. Elders have begun falling sick. Children have died clutching their bellies in agony as their parents watch on, lifeless in their beds.

speaker: Bayek
en: This would be cruel even for the angriest of gods.

speaker: Woman
en: No one cares about us. Any help would be appreciated... in the Faiyum, the poor aren't worth spit.

speaker: Slums Sobek Priest
en: My children, your hunger is known. Turn to Sobek for your nourishment. Sobek has provided a way. Though the food is humble, it gives life. Eat with thanksgiving, and trust in he who is Pointed of Teeth. The Lord of Waters may take our souls, but we will all rejoice in the Field of Reeds! The Splashing One, who came from the Great Goddess! He who made the herbage green. Lord of the Nile! Dua Sobek!

speaker: Woman
en: Another dead farmer whose family will now lose their land. They used to eat at the alms kitchen in the market. But soldiers began harassing them. Greek merchants said they were bad for business.

speaker: Bayek
en: There are no signs of a plague on the body.

speaker: Bayek
en: These bowls are filthy. What have the villagers been eating? They must have the food stored somewhere. I should have a look around.

speaker: Bayek
en: These urns contain strong seasonings.

speaker: Bayek
en: This food is rancid. It smells like shit. It's completely unfit for eating. This gruel is not fit for rats, let alone people. The strong spices are not for taste, they are disguising the rot. I need to talk with whoever made it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Tell me about the food you eat. Where does it come from?

speaker: Woman
en: A merchant makes it for the poor here. It's not much, but at least it's something. We're thankful. You're welcome to try some.

speaker: Bayek
en: By the gods no. I do not know how you stomach it. I need to talk to the merchant. Where can I find him?

speaker: Woman
en: His house is to the south of the town market. I can take you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let's visit this merchant of yours. I will follow you.

speaker: Woman
en: May Sobek reward you for helping.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have passed many prosperous farms. People here seem to be doing well. Why are there so many poor?

speaker: Woman
en: Ah yes. Those are Greek farms. The Greeks pay lower taxes, so they prosper. Meanwhile, the Egyptian farmers are slowly forced from their lands.

speaker: Bayek
en: What happens to the land when the farmers leave?

speaker: Woman
en: Once the owners die, by law the land is freed. If it's good land, the Greeks take it. If not, the desert takes it. Either way, Egyptians are left to starve. Many end up in the slums.

speaker: Woman
en: This is the home of the merchant who provides the food.

speaker: Bayek
en: Even the cats here look better fed than the poor.

speaker: Woman
en: The owner is obviously of substance. Not all Egyptians seem to be equal.

speaker: Bayek
en: Some are just more equal than others.

speaker: Woman
en: This is awful!

speaker: Bayek
en: No wonder people are falling sick!

speaker: Woman
en: Who would do this?

speaker: Bayek
en: It is time we met this poisonous merchant.

speaker: Woman
en: Give him a taste of his own cooking.

speaker: Man
en: How may I help you? This is my home. Are you lost?

speaker: Bayek
en: You can explain to me why you have been poisoning the poor. My guess is so you can take their land. It is easy if they are dead.

speaker: Man
en: You're referring to the trouble in the slums? Whatever you've heard, I assure you, you misunderstand. I do what I can to help.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have seen your kitchen, merchant. I know what you are doing. And I will see that you are brought to justice.

speaker: Man
en: Oh... I see. Well that changes things. Now you're trespassing. And I have the right to protect myself. Men!

speaker: Man
en: If you were reasonable, I wouldn't have to do this! We could have worked this out!

speaker: Man
en: I'm not dying over this! Hold him off!

speaker: Man
en: Where are my men? They were just filthy beggars! Why do you care so much about them? No-one will miss them! We can talk about this! I'm wealthy! I can pay you!

speaker: Man
en: Filthy Medjay scum, you have no authority here! Who do you think you are? You can't touch me! Help me! Help! Soldiers!

speaker: Bayek
en: This merchant of death was murdering the poor for their land. His love of money was the real sickness. Faiyum won't miss him. The dead can rest. There will be no more burning.

speaker: Sminthos
en: Psst, Sir Bayek! Over here.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why so secretive, Mouse?

speaker: Sminthos
en: I have shenanigans in mind, my friend.

speaker: Sminthos
en: The reward is money for you, and an idyllic new life for the Mouse. A farm by the coast where I will raise chickens, goats...

speaker: Bayek
en: But...

speaker: Sminthos
en: The man wants a Pharaoh's ransom for the deeds, Sir Bayyek. But Dolos the spirit of cunning sent you to help with my foolproof plan.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm guessing this plan involves the Romans.

speaker: Sminthos
en: And smugglers! So, will you join me on one last adventure, Sir Bayek?

speaker: Bayek
en: Why not.

speaker: Sminthos
en: It's surprising what Roman lips will spill if you ply them with enough wine. Sir Bayek! We're not done with the caper. The snitch told me the smuggler's ship has a codename. Corvum nigrum, the Black Crow. Before they dock the Crow drops her contrabrand into the shallows...

speaker: Sminthos
en: We'll make a pirate of you yet! Steal the dock manifest from the Romans. It will tell us the Black Crow's route into the harbor. I'll wait for you across the docks. Don't get caught, Sir Bayek!

speaker: Bayek
en: Lions and other wild animals are exotic and expensive cargo. Must be why there's so many guards.

speaker: Bayek
en: Here it is, the Black Crow and notes from the Roman dock-master!

speaker: Sminthos
en: Sir Bayek, you return unscathed!

speaker: Bayek
en: The manifest says the ship arrived from Alexandria with the first tide.

speaker: Sminthos
en: Ah, they'll have dropped their illegal imports at the shipwreck east of Apollonia.

speaker: Bayek
en: However, based on the manifest, the Romans cracked the code, they'll be looking too.

speaker: Sminthos
en: I have turned you into a pirate, Sir Bayek! A swindler of the seven seas!

speaker: Bayek
en: Hahaha... Eh, I must admit this is one of your more enlivening schemes, Mouse.

speaker: Sminthos
en: It is good to hear your laugh, my friend. I've arranged to meet the man at the ruins on the coast. Come there with the "plunder". Soon that joyous land will be mine.

speaker: Bayek
en: This treasure will do more good for the Mouse than the smugglers.

speaker: Arsenius
en: Find it you sacks of uselessness!

speaker: Sminthos
en: Bayek! Kill these swindlers! You're in trouble now my friend is here!

speaker: Arsenius
en: Where is our loot?

speaker: Sminthos
en: They trussed me up like a hog!

speaker: Sminthos
en: He was just another liar and cheat.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where will you go now?

speaker: Sminthos
en: Cyrene was a cruel mistress, Sir Bayek, but it's time to retire.

speaker: Bayek
en: You will miss her?

speaker: Sminthos
en: Miss Romans kicking me to the street? Miss people spitting at my poor "cursed" face? No!

speaker: Bayek
en: You should use this boodle to really buy a farm you wanted, Mouse.

speaker: Sminthos
en: Yes, I will. And make wine from my wines and cheese from my goats. Then one day we'll raise a cup to our friendship...

speaker: Bayek
en: That will be the best of days.

speaker: Sminthos
en: Here, your reward. Thank you from the depths of my heart... Bayek.

speaker: Bayek
en: A man's heart is his own god. Goodbye... Sminthos.

speaker: Jeska
en: Bayek! It was Sefetu! They took Harkhuf. I know what they will do. Torture him with red-hot tongs. Perhaps rip his tongue out. Then kill him with a burning dagger to the heart.

speaker: Bayek
en: The prisons of Fort Nikiou.

speaker: Jeska
en: Wait! They thought I was dead and tossed me in the well. I crawled through corpses and escaped by an underground stream to the river.

speaker: Greek soldier 1
en: Last time I was in Sais, I think I overdid it.

speaker: Greek soldier 2
en: Huh? What do you mean?

speaker: Greek soldier 1
en: Sefetu's got the people so cowed you can do whatever you want. Eat their food, screw their women, hell, kill their men, and no one will raise a voice against you.

speaker: Greek soldier 2
en: Really?

speaker: Greek soldier 1
en: Stick with me, kid. I'll show you how it's done.

speaker: Greek soldier 2
en: Hahah. Cannot wait!

speaker: Bayek
en: Keep calm, Harkhuf. I will get you out.

speaker: Harkhuf
en: Bayek! You will need to find the key Sefetu wears around his neck! Hurry!

speaker: Greek soldier 1
en: Can't believe some puss-filled wart of a Medjay has been killing our men.

speaker: Greek soldier 2
en: I heard he killed the archers Sefetu left in Sais.

speaker: Greek soldier 1
en: That and more. When Sefetu catches him I heard he's going to burn his fingers and toes off, then his ears, nose, tongue, balls.

speaker: Greek soldier 2
en: Sweet Serapis.

speaker: Greek soldier 1
en: They don't call him the Firebrand for no good reason. Don't screw up.

speaker: Greek soldier 2
en: Yeah.

speaker: Sefetu
en: You are a thorn in my ass. I will burn every inch of you and feed your ashes to the gods.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have the key here.

speaker: Harkhuf
en: Did you kill that clod of shit?

speaker: Bayek
en: Come on. Come!

speaker: Bayek
en: Come quickly, this place may still be dangerous.

speaker: Harkhuf
en: Hapi, keep me safe. May the gods be against you bastards. Blast, blast, blast... God of grain, watch over me.

speaker: Harkhuf
en: Thank you, my friend. Apollodorus was right to bring you in. You honor the badge you wear. Come visit us if you ever get the chance. May Hapi watch over you, and ensure your beer cup ever overflows.

speaker: Priestess
en: I will find you, heinous snakes, find the offerings you stole from Amun, Lord of Thebes!

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone has dared to steal from Amun?

speaker: Priestess
en: I can not fathom it, but statues of the Theban triad were taken from the temple. Offerings from those terrified by the curse.

speaker: Bayek
en: Desecration is rife in this ancient city. Perhaps I can offer Amun my blade, priestess?

speaker: Priestess
en: And who are you that would do his work?

speaker: Bayek
en: Bayek of Siwa.

speaker: Priestess
en: A savior from the Oasis? Then Amun sharpen your sword, Bayek of Siwa. Find me again if you have news of the stolen idols. The black market merchants are my next port of call. I should seek the counsel of the high priestess Isidora.

speaker: Bayek
en: Offerings, simple statues, hardly worth much at the market. So why steal them and risk the Hidden One's wrath?

speaker: Bayek
en: A broken vase, did it fall from above?

speaker: Bayek
en: Our thief climbed down here, at night while the temple slept.

speaker: Bayek
en: A broken ladder, a clumsy thief indeed.

speaker: Bayek
en: More blood. Seems you cannot escape the wrath of the Hidden One. He can't have gone far.

speaker: Priest Thief
en: Ow, help me! Please, someone! Anyone! I am dying! My life's light fading from my eyes. Why have the gods forsaken me? Why!

speaker: Priest Thief
en: My leg... I can't feel my leg...

speaker: Bayek
en: More will be broken if you don't explain the stolen idols.

speaker: Priest Thief
en: I am bleeding to death and you threaten me? What kind of monster are you?

speaker: Bayek
en: Speak and I might find a priest to aid you.

speaker: Priest Thief
en: Might? Might? Ahhhhh! The blackness is claiming me. Anubis grips my throat...

speaker: Bayek
en: Speak!

speaker: Priest Thief
en: Alright! Alright... A black robed man. I meet him in the rich quarter for payment when I have idols to sell.

speaker: Bayek
en: And you returned to the temple because...?

speaker: Priest Thief
en: More idols! But none to take, and then... a goose it flew at me, knocked me from the ladder.

speaker: Bayek
en: Punishment from the great cackler Amun?

speaker: Priest Thief
en: No! You are trying to frighten me. But I've told you everything. Now get me some help! Get help! You promised you...!

speaker: Bayek
en: When the idols are safe, perhaps.

speaker: Robed Man
en: Where is that toothless calf?

speaker: Bodyguard
en: Probably in a cell squealing like a hog.

speaker: Robed Man
en: I needed someone who cared for money more than the gods, beyond that he is nothing.

speaker: Robed Man
en: I honor he who walks, The Aten! Kill him. In the name of the sole gods!

speaker: Bayek
en: The drowned sun, the mother consumed by fire... This is not about profit, but heresy.

speaker: Bayek
en: Eclipse the moon. Smear it in the blood of the Apis.

speaker: Meat Merchant
en: Meat, fresh meat! the best beef in Thebes. Slaughtered just this morning at the temple, freshest in the city. I still have the liver of the magnificent beast! Only the best cuts for the best tables!

speaker: Bayek
en: Slick with blood and... urgh, the stench is unbearable.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ignite the mother with your fire.

speaker: Bayek
en: Blackened and burned. But still recognizable as the great mother.

speaker: Thebes Blacksmith
en: Amun preserve me! Thank you, neb (sir), you saved me from the Lord of Thebes wrath!

speaker: Bayek
en: Drown the father with your tears.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Lord of Thebes, a sorry sight.

speaker: Bayek
en: The priestess will want the offerings returned, whatever state they are in.

speaker: Priestess
en: Blood mongers! You make profit from the suffering of Thebes. A living is honestly come by, not stolen. The Hidden One will strike you down from the shadows. Your trinkets and cures do nothing against the curse. False hopes from your false idols.

speaker: Priestess
en: Soulsucking hope peddlers, they are a plague on Thebes.

speaker: Bayek
en: That's as may be, but I found the thief and the offerings. He was stealing them for a follower of Akhenaten.

speaker: Priestess
en: The Heretic Pharaoh? Are the perpetrators dead?

speaker: Bayek
en: The follower yes, the thief fell when he escaped the temple. You can find him in the grounds.

speaker: Priestess
