en: This sickness infects all it touches. But thank you, Bayek of Siwa. May radiance ignite your darkness. Go with Hidden One's blessing.

speaker: Rebel 1
en: I detest that fort! They rob every Nabatean who enters, and all must enter!

speaker: Rebel 2
en: Gamilat tells me a Hidden One may attempt to enter it.

speaker: Rebel 1
en: That would be suicide!

speaker: Rebel 2
en: Not for a Hidden One. Gamilat ordered us to help him if he gets into trouble.

speaker: Rebel 1
en: What Gamilat orders, I will do. He is the chosen of the gods.

speaker: Maqwat
en: Bayek! Over here!

speaker: Maqwat
en: Tahira said you would come.

speaker: Bayek
en: Who is my target?

speaker: Maqwat
en: Ampelius. He oversees all commerce on the peninsula. You will find him below.

speaker: Maqwat
en: He squeezes bloody juice from every coin that passes along the Way of Horus and through those walls.

speaker: Bayek
en: How will I know him?

speaker: Maqwat
en: There you have a problem. He dresses exactly like his captains. From afar, he is impossible to identify.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you certain he is in the fort?

speaker: Maqwat
en: I am certain. My partner went in there earlier and never came back.

speaker: Bayek
en: Wait for me at the Praying Hands. If I find your partner, I will bring him there.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah, Senu, dear girl. He cannot be found. He is dressed like all the others.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where is this cursed Ampelius?

speaker: Ampelius
en: ... ten, eleven... mm-mm.

speaker: Ampelius
en: The Order is eternal. (laughs)

speaker: Pelias
en: Told her to hurry back... Ruia, where have you got to? Where is that damn girl!?

speaker: Pelias
en: You, neb, are young and your legs are strong. Perfect for my needs. A pigeon arrived not long ago. I sent Ruia to fetch it, but she is so unreliable. Probably batting her eyes at the master of arms.

speaker: Bayek
en: If I see her...

speaker: Pelias
en: Never mind her. I want my letter. Run up to the Pigeon Tower and fetch it. All news is important to us these days.

speaker: Bayek
en: All right, steward. I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Bayek
en: The pigeons are in a ruckus. What has upset them?

speaker: Bayek
en: An ill omen. How did that charcoal get spilled?

speaker: Bayek
en: Such a mess.

speaker: Bayek
en: Blood. Still fresh.

speaker: Bayek
en: The railing broke... when someone went over it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Lot of blood. Where's the body?

speaker: Bayek
en: I cannot leave you here. I will take you back to Pelias for the proper rites.

speaker: Bayek
en: Poor Ruia. If you had only known how to make such a leap... What did you get yourself into? Beasts with the faces of men prey on the weak and powerless. We cannot simply show our bellies to the jackals that plague our land.

speaker: Pelias
en: By the gods... Ruia! What happened?

speaker: Bayek
en: She was thrown to her death from the Pigeon Tower.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your letter.

speaker: Pelias
en: Why was she killed?

speaker: Pelias
en: That is the badge worn by Dymnos, our Master of Arms. Why did she have it?

speaker: Bayek
en: I will find out soon enough.

speaker: Pelias
en: You, poor, poor girl. May you walk in the Field of Reeds.

speaker: Bayek
en: Dymnos? I'm looking for Ruia.

speaker: Dymnos
en: Why would I know where that peasant is?

speaker: Bayek
en: Perhaps because she has your badge.

speaker: Dymnos
en: Shit. Well... She was just an Egyptian dog. No matter.

speaker: Bayek
en: Why did you do it?

speaker: Dymnos
en: Truth, I didn't mean to kill her. Only teach her a lesson for her insolence. She refused to read a letter for me.

speaker: Bayek
en: You must confess to Pelias.

speaker: Dymnos
en: I suppose you want the same fate as Ruia, you stupid Egyptian. I'll teach you the same lesson she learned!

speaker: Bayek
en: Come. Try.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hm. The letter he mentioned.

speaker: Pelias
en: Was it Dymnos?

speaker: Bayek
en: Yes. He killed Ruia out of base cruelty. And he died because he thought I was also less than a person.

speaker: Pelias
en: What a senseless tragedy. She was a smart girl, with a good heart. The letter you recovered, it is information for Apollodorus. I will make sure he gets it.

speaker: Bayek
en: A strong musk clouds the air... a tanner lives nearby.

speaker: Woman 1
en: How are you keeping today?

speaker: Man 1
en: Most well, thank you nebet. Life is certainly not easy here, but at least we work for ourselves. Not in fear of the lash and only to fill Sefetu's coffers.

speaker: Woman 1
en: Yes! Our hard work supports our families and friends.

speaker: Man 1
en: The Firebrand has hurt so many people in this world that I am sure his heart will be eaten by the Devourer upon his death.

speaker: Woman 1
en: So it will be.

speaker: Man 2
en: How was the hunt?

speaker: Man 3
en: Tough. We had to range far to find any good prey.

speaker: Man 2
en: Oh?

speaker: Man 3
en: Yeah. Best hunting was up to the north west of the village.

speaker: Man 2
en: Up near the large rock at the tip of the coast?

speaker: Man 3
en: Right. Careful, though. Hyenas tend to den around there.

speaker: Man 4
en: How is the house coming?

speaker: Man 5
en: Slow, to be honest. It's hard to get all the materials I need to properly fix it up.

speaker: Man 4
en: Yes, I know how it goes. It took me months to gather everything I needed for our home.

speaker: Man 5
en: Have you heard the stories of Letopolis?

speaker: Man 4
en: In passing. But I would rather scrounge for materials here than have to shovel for weeks under the hot sun for my house.

speaker: Man 5
en: You are right! Leave the desert for the gods!

speaker: Woman 2
en: Could you stand to be married to him?

speaker: Woman 3
en: Well, yes it's true he does stink, but he's well known for his work. And people pay well for it.

speaker: Woman 2
en: I suppose that's fair.

speaker: Woman 3
en: You should be nicer to her. Sau village is better for having a tanner here.

speaker: Woman 2
en: Good points. I'll try.

speaker: Woman 3
en: Oh, the gods shame me, neb. The tanner is my husband. He carries that stench home whenever he returns from camp.

speaker: Bayek
en: Is he here now?

speaker: Woman 3
en: By the smell, you would think so! But it's worse when he's around.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do not let it trouble you. We all must do work we do not relish.

speaker: Woman 3
en: You are right. My husband works hard, but cannot keep up with demand for his services. The Medjay are said to be legendary hunters. If you would like to earn some good coin, go and see him. I'm sure he could use your help.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hmm. I will consider it. Where would I find him?

speaker: Woman 3
en: His hunting camp is north and west of Sau. He will be tanning hides for days. If only there were some way for him to deal with the stink.

speaker: Bayek
en: What's this? Scented oils. Might take the edge of the tanner's stench.

speaker: Sau Tanner
en: No! Keep your jaws away! Back beast! Anyone! Help! Please! Sweet Serapis, where did you come from? Back! Back you beast! I will turn you into leather armor.

speaker: Sau Tanner
en: My thanks, traveler. I did not expect the gods to send help my way this day. I was afraid that beast wanted to eat me in revenge for my craft. What brings you this way?

speaker: Bayek
en: Your wife in Sau told me you might need a hunter.

speaker: Sau Tanner
en: Yes, yes. Too much demand and not enough supply. I would be more than happy to pay you good coin for the hides I need. And for you to risk their teeth.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am listening.

speaker: Sau Tanner
en: I need hyena ears, crocodile eggs, and vulture skulls.

speaker: Bayek
en: What do you do with vulture skulls?

speaker: Sau Tanner
en: Many priestesses of Iset use them for headdresses. They pay well.

speaker: Sau Tanner
en: Well now, what do you have for me?

speaker: Bayek
en: All that you asked for.

speaker: Sau Tanner
en: Ah yes! Good, good! And in fine condition. They will do nicely. Your pay.

speaker: Bayek
en: And there's this... Do not think me rude, but I found these scented oils. I thought you could use them.

speaker: Sau Tanner
en: I should not refuse I suppose, if only to give my wife some relief! Take this as a token of good faith.

speaker: Menehet
en: Thank the gods that this festival will soon be over. I hope you will find some answers in the market. The merchants have short tempers and may refuse to speak. That was the fourth tourist this week to shout at me.

speaker: Customers
en: This looks like a child made it! These cat mummies are false! I won't pay one drachma for this! Why, there's nothing but straw in here! You filthy neket iadet! How dare you try to trick me into paying for this junk? My sister told me she bought a statuette from you, and it broke. You sold me an amulet of Hathor, and my wife got sick anyway!

speaker: Bayek
en: Greetings, I am

speaker: Merchant 1
en: You have come to the right place, neb! We have everything you could possibly want!

speaker: Bayek
en: What I want is to ask about false idols sold at the market.

speaker: Merchant 1
en: I have heard rumors of such, but there is nothing to them. Now leave, if you want to avoid trouble.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do you know anything of flawed mummies sold to tourists?

speaker: Merchant 2
en: If you are not here to buy, I have no time for your questions.

speaker: Bayek
en: Menehet, the priest is concerned about the

speaker: Merchant 2
en: And I am concerned about my business, so keep your distance!

speaker: Bayek
en: Tell me of the fake mummies being sold here.

speaker: Baqet
en: I have no desire to be dragged into this.

speaker: Bayek
en: Menehet sends me. Your silence is an insult to his holy office.

speaker: Baqet
en: Er, I wish to anger neither him nor the gods. We are forced to sell items of lesser quality, or see our stalls destroyed.

speaker: Bayek
en: Who is behind this?

speaker: Baqet
en: I can say no more now. Let us meet tonight, where the village turns to farmland.

speaker: Baqet
en: My friend! I am glad to see you have kept our appointment. Come, sit with me and share a drink of wine.

speaker: Bayek
en: I do not have time for that.

speaker: Baqet
en: It is a beautiful night. Let us enjoy the coolness of the air for a moment before turning to business.

speaker: Bayek
en: Merchant, I am not here to take in the air. Who is behind the traffic of false icons?

speaker: Baqet
en: Well, you see, it is no simple story. There are many involved in this terrible affair, but they would all tell you the same thing... "Pity the trusting man, for he suffers great pain."

speaker: Baqet
en: Seek evil, and you will always find it! Sailing unknown waters always brings the risk of shipwreck! The path to knowledge is perilous!

speaker: Bandit 1
en: No one will find your body once we feed it to the crocodiles!

speaker: Bandit 2
en: I can't wait to see what guts look like. Eat shit, Medjay scum!

speaker: Bandit 3
en: This one's a worthy fighter. A shame his curiosity will be fatal.

speaker: Baqet
en: A man who fights as well as you can perhaps afford to be trusting.

speaker: Bayek
en: Talk, or you will meet the same fate as your friends.

speaker: Baqet
en: That will not be necessary. Among the dunes southeast of here is the bandit camp where the fake mummies are made. I suppose you will go and destroy it now.

speaker: Bayek
en: Better I smash the camp than your head.

speaker: Bayek
en: Destroying these forgeries will earn the favor of the gods. As Ra lives! What a disgrace.

speaker: Bandit 1
en: Can you believe how stupid these Greeks are? They wouldn't be able to tell a live cat from a dead one, never mind a cat from a straw one!

speaker: Bandit 2
en: Watch your tone. My father's a Greek.

speaker: Bandit 1
en: Oh, really? Then I have some cats to sell him.

speaker: Bandit 2
en: Shut up and get back to work.

speaker: Bayek
en: Menehet will rest easy, now that this is done.

speaker: Menehet
en: Ah, here you are!

speaker: Bayek
en: I have dealt with the trafficking of false mummies.

speaker: Menehet
en: Thank you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Heh, how can I ease the burdens of an old friend.

speaker: Bayek
en: A child! Their desecration is boundless. This Strategos of Yebu must answer to Osiris.

speaker: Bayek
en: When did such oppression become Egypt's legacy?

speaker: Bayek
en: You will steal Egypt's past no longer.

speaker: Galenos
en: Spare a moment for a poor old sot? Will none of you help me? A stole my eyes!

speaker: Bayek
en: What is this madness, old man? Your eyes have been ravaged?

speaker: Galenos
en: Yes, a manticore devoured them!

speaker: Bayek
en: A mythical beast stole your sight?

speaker: Galenos
en: With the face of a woman and the body of a lion.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is one ferocious lion.

speaker: Galenos
en: Quick! Before she returns. Take me to my friend Theramenes at the clinic. He will know what to do.

speaker: Bayek
en: Madness is your bedfellow. But I can't leave you here to be eaten by beasts.

speaker: Galenos
en: I only went berry picking.

speaker: Bayek
en: There are many wild animals about, do you not have a bow?

speaker: Galenos
en: A bow against a manticore?

speaker: Bayek
en: My bow has killed a thousand beasts.

speaker: Galenos
en: Argg! Are you the griffin? Spiriting me off!

speaker: Bayek
en: Be still Galenos, it is me Bayek, your savior.

speaker: Galenos
en: Are we near. Near the clinic, Bayek?

speaker: Bayek
en: I hope so.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you the healer Theramenes?

speaker: Theramenes
en: Yes, yes. Is that Galenos? By the Fates, what happened to him?

speaker: Bayek
en: I found him by the road, crying that the Manticore took his eyes.

speaker: Theramenes
en: And his wits along with them. I have honey and euphrasia... but the temple purloined my more exotic supplies.

speaker: Bayek
en: I've brought him this far, so what do you need?

speaker: Theramenes
en: You'll help? Wonder of wonders. I will give you a list.

speaker: Bayek
en: Let's see what Theramenes can do with these.

speaker: Bayek
en: How is our patient?

speaker: Theramenes
en: A babbling fool. We'll get no sense from him til I can relieve his pain. Silphium extract will do it.

speaker: Bayek
en: That Roman weed?

speaker: Theramenes
en: Silphium is our weed and because of the Romans it's almost extinct. They process it at the depot north of here.

speaker: Bayek
en: Which is heavily guarded I bet?

speaker: Theramenes
en: Should be no problem for one as resourceful as you. Haha.

speaker: Bayek
en: I should return this wonder cure to Theramenes.

speaker: Theramenes
en: You are a marvel. I will bring our friend back to his senses, not that he had that many to begin with.

speaker: Bayek
en: If I stumble across a manticore stalking the woods of Balagrae, I will bring you its head.

speaker: Theramenes
en: Now that I would welcome my boy, they say that its venomous sting will paralyze a man instantly. I could have some use for that! Medicinally speaking of course!

speaker: Bayek
en: Of course. Farewell, Theramenes.

speaker: Galenos
en: Farewell Bayek! And watch out for manticores!

speaker: Bayek
en: The fresh-water spring in the Amanai Cave. I know that cave. Better look into it.

speaker: Bayek
en: The Amanai cave. Aya and I used to come her as kids. Bandits must be inside.

speaker: Man
en: I must get them! There are so many of them! Dear Amun, help me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Kett? Is that you? What are you doing?

speaker: Kett
en: Bayek! I heard you were back. Keep quiet, they'll hear you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Who will hear me?

speaker: Kett
en: Bandits! The bastards took over the spring. Almost everyone on this side of Siwa gets their water from here.

speaker: Bandit 1
en: If you see that farmer again, bring him to me. I want to question him.

speaker: Bandit 2
en: Beat any passing farmers to a pulp, men. Let them know we mean business.

speaker: Bayek
en: That's it. Bandits will think twice before coming back here.

speaker: Kett
en: Bayek, the spring, you got it back?! Thank the gods. The farmers need this desperately. I'm very grateful, Bayek. It's like having our Medjay back again.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm glad I could help.

speaker: Kett
en: May Amun walk with you, seni (friend).

speaker: Bayek
en: I have killed all these neket iadet (pieces of shit). Apollodorus must be told. To Herakleion.

speaker: Egyptian soldier 1
en: Ah, look it is the Medjay.

speaker: Egyptian soldier 2
en: One more warrior to add to our ranks.

speaker: Egyptian soldier 1
en: I hope Amun works among us.

speaker: Woman
en: I have been praying so often, my priest said I should relax.

speaker: Man
en: We will get through this. Apollodorus is coming with our wine. All is not lost, Cleopatra is still the goddess.

speaker: Woman
en: I hope these tough times do not kill her aura.

speaker: Man
en: Her aura is as strong as ever. Her temple will be redesigned in her name.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: I'm coming with your wine!

speaker: Apollodorus
en: May your days be filled with the light of Ra.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Ah! Look who was returned! Bayek of Siwa! Perfect that you have met us in Herakleion, a city of wine, women, whatever a Medjay like you desires... and deserves.

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah, to the Queen.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Bayek. You arrive at an opportune time.

speaker: Bayek
en: Cleopatra. I am still looking for the men who killed my son. The Order is neutralized. Was my hunt for me or for you?

speaker: Cleopatra
en: I have two more names. The Order can't be

speaker: Bayek
en: And how many more names after that?

speaker: Cleopatra
en: As many as it takes.

speaker: Bayek
en: I wish to bring my son to the afterlife where he belongs, not—I like you, Cleopatra, but the royal matters that seduced my wife do not sway me so.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: What does the badge mean to you? Have you forgotten?

speaker: Bayek
en: This badge means more to you than it does to me.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: This is not one man we are fighting. Nothing ends simply. Aya has understood that you have a new reality: I am your Pharaoh, you are Medjay to all of Egypt. Follow me, we have a gift.

speaker: Bayek
en: Speaking of Medjay, any news of Aya?

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Aya is still defending the seas. We are expecting Pompey and his fleet anyday now, to unite against the Order and change the land.

speaker: Bayek
en: I did see a lot on my hunt that sickened me. Our land is being oppressed greatly. I realized we cannot let the Order rise again.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Yes, Bayek, the two new names, the Jackal and the Scorpion, are within my brother's inner circle. We believe they are the ones behind the attempt on my life.

speaker: Bayek
en: An attempt on your life? By your brother's phylakes?

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Hard to tell. A Gabiniani. One of Septimius' warriors. They form a militia two thousand strong. I had hoped to ally with them.

speaker: Bayek
en: With Septimius? The Roman lug? He leads them?

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Yes, the dreamer who posits himself as truly Egyptian, and yet sends a man to murder me. Not very Egyptian if you ask me. Aya feels he is working for the Order and has a proxy here named Venator.

speaker: Bayek
en: Perhaps he is the masked one that forced my son's death upon me.

speaker: Livius
en: Futuo (Fuck)! Just kill me already, you cowards.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Here is your gift. He is in the Order of Ancients like Septimius. We found him snooping around the villa. We think he knows who killed your son.

speaker: Livius
en: My brother Septimius killed your son, and I don't give a shit.

speaker: Bayek
en: Shit-giving is my job.

speaker: Livius
en: I just fucked those twins... Venator...

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Enough for you? I will press him for more information. I suggest you visit the brothel in town.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Yes, go dig through this Dionysian town and unearth the plot against us.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Septimius is in town, his main Phylakes is a man named Venator. We heard rumors he is lurking around the brothel.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will clean this town up. And ensure our safety.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: My plan is to rename this temple in my name. Is the town safe yet?

speaker: Bayek
en: I got busy and distracted. It is a beautiful region.

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Any luck? Enjoy the brothel? Time is of the essence, if we want to catch Septimius.

speaker: Bayek
en: I am working on it.

speaker: Helen
en: Ah, a true warrior. I have a discount for—wait, you are not with the Gabinianis, are you?

speaker: Bayek
en: No, I am not. I am a Medjay.

speaker: Helen
en: Wow, Medjays used to come here all the time, but not recently. Who do you work for, then?

speaker: Bayek
en: Cleopatra.

speaker: Helen
en: I heard she was in town. Well, a Medjay working for his pharaoh, you must have gold to burn.

speaker: Bayek
en: I would like to speak with your legendary twins.

speaker: Helen
en: "Speaking" is what you call it? I suppose we all have our thing. The twins are going to cost you, if you want to speak or anything else with them, Medjay.

speaker: Helen
en: Make yourself comfortable upstairs, the twins will come for you. They had a rough night yesterday, so don't "speak" too hard with them, hm?

speaker: Brother
en: You wanted to speak to us?

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm looking for a Gabiniani named Venator.

speaker: Brother
en: Shhh. Do not say that name!

speaker: Sister
en: He is a neket iadet (piece of shit)! I won't hold my tongue for that monster! Everyone is scared of him, but you should kill him! He's staying at the top of the square.

speaker: Bayek
en: He won't be staying anywhere, ever again.

speaker: Bayek
en: By Anubis. This place has been busy. Venator does not work alone.

speaker: Bayek
en: Blood on the walls. This Venator is sick. What have you and your men been up to?

speaker: Bayek
en: This place smells like a swamp. Broken dishes, it reeks of foul play.

speaker: Bayek
en: Target practice on Cleopatra? Venator is training his Gabinianis for an assassination.

speaker: Bayek
en: Lutes, lipstick, and scented oils. Were women of the street here? And Roman regalia. Odd. Seems Venator wants his men to mix well.

speaker: Bayek
en: Wine casks. This doesn't smell like wine, though. Oil in wine casks? Enough oil to burn down the whole city. I fear the Queen was right, Venator is plotting. Hm... but I need more information. Something is missing.

speaker: Bayek
en: My gods. A crafty plan. One of the men is posing as a woman. Must be to infiltrate the palace. Posing as wine merchants, they will dock and set a fire to cause a panic. With an archer ready to pick off the Queen in the confusion. Somewhere high. Venator, more than just one of Septimius' dogs. You have your own puppets within the Order. I have to find them before they strike.

speaker: Alexus
en: How do I look? Later on, I plan on playing the lute for the Queen.

speaker: Woman
en: You look great. You are with the musicians who will play for Cleopatra? You are so lucky.

speaker: Alexus
en: Yes, I am looking for the other musicians, have you seen them?

speaker: Woman
en: No, I have not. Are you planning on coming to the orgy?

speaker: Alexus
en: Well... when in Rome...

speaker: Woman
en: We're in Egypt, idiot.

speaker: Woman
en: Alexus!

speaker: Bayek
en: He was an imposter! A Roman man who wants to kill the Queen. I am doing you a favour!

speaker: Woman
en: Never a dull moment in this town.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Can we return to the brothel? Let's leave Cleopatra and enjoy life.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: No way, futuo (fuck)! I can't wait to burn Cleopatra.

speaker: Lamplighter
en: I talked with Venator, and he even paid me to light the braziers. Apparently, Cleopatra's defenses are weak. This will be the easiest assassination in the world.

speaker: Archer
en: Cleopatra...

speaker: Bayek
en: Aya! My love!

speaker: Aya
en: Bayek!

speaker: Bayek
en: Ah! You smell of the sea!

speaker: Aya
en: The high seas have taken me for some time. But now I am yours.

speaker: Aya
en: Ahh! Move!

speaker: Apollodorus
en: I am wounded, Aya! Protect the Queen! Aya! I am wounded! You must protect the Queen!

speaker: Aya
en: I am coming!

speaker: Bayek
en: I got this my love!

speaker: Soldier 3
en: The so-called Queen. Your throne shall resemble a tomb.

speaker: Bayek
en: Which one of you claims to be Venator?

speaker: Soldier 3
en: He is our leader, and you will not get to him!

speaker: Bayek
en: Oh, please!

speaker: Bayek
en: That takes care of these thugs. Yet not Venator.

speaker: Venator
en: Your Queen is an unworthy bitch.

speaker: Bayek
en: That is no way to talk of a goddess.

speaker: Venator
en: If you are a guardian of Egypt, the country will surely be dead in moments.

speaker: Bayek
en: Keep talking, you'll soon find yourself without a head.

speaker: Venator
en: Did you stop by the brothel and see my handiwork?

speaker: Bayek
en: Your intimidation is sad. Come, let me give your ka a break.

speaker: Venator
en: You futuo (fuck)! You think you can change any of our plans?

speaker: Bayek
en: You will soon be dead. That is change enough for me.

speaker: Venator
en: Death to Cleo! We are the Gabinianis and Egypt is ours! OUUURAH!!! My warriors were thwarted, but I shall not be.

speaker: Bayek
en: Two axes isn't enough axes.

speaker: Venator
en: Let this queen die. The only dignity she has left, is death.

speaker: Bayek
en: If death requires dignity then allow me to decorate you, for you are the most decorated official.

speaker: Bayek
en: Save a place in the Duat for your brother Septimius.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hey, Old Man. Oh, are you injured?

speaker: Apollodorus
en: Just a flesh wound.

speaker: Bayek
en: Aya.

speaker: Aya
en: I am fine. Nothing hurts anymore.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: My mind is a riot. All I have is that I am pushed further, one more attempt to snuff me out.

speaker: Apollodorous
en: My Queen, rest and remember

speaker: Cleopatra
en: I do not need rest. This civil war is no closer to ending. I need a fucking throne. My throne rots in the hands of my brother. Instruct Phoxidas to prepare my ship. We head to meet Pompey. My last resort.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: You two go ahead and tell him we are coming.

speaker: Aya
en: Yes, my Queen.

speaker: Aya
en: Bayek, if we don't get to Pompey first, Septimius might.

speaker: Aya
en: Appears those Gabinianis left us a felucca, kind of them.

speaker: Aya
en: Septimius is the shit-eater. He is the man we must escort to the Devourer.

speaker: Bayek
en: And of Pothinus?

speaker: Aya
en: He will be more fodder for the Devourer.

speaker: Bayek
en: And then we return home.

speaker: Aya
en: We will only return home with Cleopatra in our company, to show Siwans what has changed. What we have changed.

speaker: Bayek
en: How are things on your trireme?

speaker: Aya
en: Great. Phoxidas has entrusted me with

speaker: Bayek
en: Why don't we take each other here?

speaker: Aya
en: In this reed boat?

speaker: Bayek
en: Take advantage of these rare moments between us, before your new job steals you away as savior of all of Egypt.

speaker: Aya
en: You make jokes but it is not funny. It is greatness I am after. This country is at civil war. One simply cannot deny it. Everywhere is misery.

speaker: Bayek
en: I love you, Aya. And we are Medjay. We do serve and protect, but we work alone. I share your hatred for Ptolemy. But remember: Cleopatra is a Ptolemy. She is the better of two evils.

speaker: Aya
en: We must serve greatness. What greatness do we serve now?

speaker: Bayek
en: We are parents.

speaker: Aya
en: We were parents. I love you, Bayek of Siwa. But what are you of now?

speaker: Bayek
en: Death hangs in the air.

speaker: Aya
en: The stench is great. Getting familiar with rotten flesh.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are those bodies?

speaker: Aya
en: Gods! The Nile will run red for many moons.

speaker: Bayek
en: Osiris will be busy. These are Romans.

speaker: Aya
en: None of Ptolemy's neket iadets (pieces of shit)?

speaker: Bayek
en: No.

speaker: Aya
en: An unceremonious removal.

speaker: Bayek
en: Looks like we missed the boat.

speaker: Bayek
en: Septimius has beat us.

speaker: Aya
en: Funny how all great men are reduced to food for maggots. This is a cemetery for our ambitions.

speaker: Cleopatra
en: No, no, it can't be... Where is Caesar?

speaker: Aya
en: He has arrived in Alexandria. He is guarded heavily so there's

speaker: Cleopatra
en: Bring me to him. I will get to Caesar if I have to drag myself through the sewers of the palace.

speaker: Bayek
en: What fool would set up camp out here? I should have a look. Greek garb...

speaker: Corteseos
en: Wake up! Wake up! Oh, what luck! You're all right! Here, stand up!

speaker: Corteseos
en: Damn, I thought you were lying on it.

speaker: Bayek
en: Lying on what? What happened?

speaker: Corteseos
en: My notes. I'm a geographer – Corteseos. Nice to meet you. Looks like we were attacked. They emptied my pockets. Took my notes, too! You might want to check your pouch.

speaker: Corteseos
en: You too... I should have known better than to travel the desert on my own. I am going to find those thieves! They ought to pray to all their gods that my notes are undamaged!

speaker: Bayek
en: We're lucky enough to be alive. What do you remember?

speaker: Corteseos
en: Remember? I was clubbed in the head! I only recall the sound of a horse galloping away.

speaker: Bayek
en: There might be tracks. Stay here.

speaker: Corteseos
en: Tracks? You cannot be serious.

speaker: Corteseos
en: Those notes are my life's work! Years and years of work. I am lost without them. I was mapping this pyramid one moment, and the next I'm spitting up sand. If you are thinking of chasing these thieves down, just, be careful! If something happened to you, I could not forgive myself.

speaker: Bayek
en: These tracks are fresh and lead southward. If I am lucky, they have not yet disappeared beneath the sand.

speaker: Bayek
en: The thieves fled towards those ruins.

speaker: Bayek
en: What's a child doing out here? It's dangerous.

speaker: Ngozi
en: I'm just finding things for Anta! What are you doing here?

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm a Medjay – looking for some thieves who came this way. Did you see anyone?

speaker: Ngozi
en: Oh! No. No one!

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you here alone?

speaker: Ngozi
en: No, ermh...I mean yes, alone.

speaker: Bayek
en: That boy is hiding something.

speaker: Bayek
en: Someone has dug their way through here. Too small for me. There must be another way around.

speaker: Bayek
en: It is odd for a child to be playing here, no?

speaker: Neema
en: Oh! Wha-what do you mean?

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm looking for some stolen items – looks like you could help me...

speaker: Neema
en: I don't know what you're talking about!

speaker: Bayek
en: My child. You are not at fault, I am here to help.

speaker: Neema
en: We hid it in Menkaure's pyramid! I'm sorry! We had to do it for Anta!

speaker: Bayek
en: I am sure Anta is a good friend, but Giza is no place for such foolishness.

speaker: Apheru
en: This is our pyramid!

speaker: Bayek
en: You've got quite the swing.

speaker: Bayek
en: Just how many of you are there?

speaker: Apheru
en: Only my brother, sister and I. Don't harm them! I'm the one responsible.

speaker: Bayek
en: I want the notes you stole from the Greek geographer you knocked out. And I want my money back.

speaker: Apheru
en: We've given everything to the bandits from the hills west of Hemon Tombs. They have Anta too and won't give her back unless we steal for them.

speaker: Bayek
en: Who's Anta?

speaker: Apheru
en: Our protector! We were going back to Memphis when they took her. If we don't do as they say, they will kill her!

speaker: Bayek
en: Bandits who profit from children. Neket iadets. Get your siblings and stay out of sight. You have my word, I will return Anta to you.

speaker: Apheru
en: Do you really think you can get Anta out safely?

speaker: Bayek
en: This is the camp where Anta is being held. The children gave everything to these bandits, so I should keep an eye out for Corteseos' notes. Hmmm. No trace of Anta or the notes. The bandit's stash is likely to be guarded deep inside their hideout.

speaker: Bayek
en: Anta? Anta.

speaker: Bayek
en: Of course... You're Anta, their protector?

speaker: Bayek
en: This should cover what the bandits took from me.

speaker: Bayek
en: Corteseos's notes must be elsewhere.

speaker: Bayek
en: You know your way back... Come on, girl.

speaker: Bayek
en: So Anta, you are a protector too? Excited, aren't you? You will see them soon enough. I'm right behind you, Anta

speaker: Bayek
en: I told you to stay out of sight.

speaker: Apheru
en: I know, but this was our fault and we thought you could use some help. The horseman is much, much bigger than you.

speaker: Bayek
en: Horseman?

speaker: Apheru
en: You haven't seen him? He's the most harrowing of them all. Big and strong! He's the one who took Anta.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hmm... He might have Corteseos' notes. Probably using them to locate treasures.

speaker: Apheru
en: I have seen him in the ruins around Khufu's pyramid!

speaker: Bayek
en: I will take care of this Horseman. You should leave. Now!

speaker: Bayek
en: I should have a look around the pyramids. I can finally find those notes. Hmm. Do I wait for this horseman to come back to his cave at night... or seek him out as he roams and terrorizes Giza?

speaker: Bayek
en: Corteseos' notes. He will be happy to see these.

speaker: Bayek
en: Eh! I bring good news.

speaker: Corteseos
en: My notes! By Zeus! I can't believe it! I owe you my life!

speaker: Apheru
en: Is it over!? Are the bandits gone?

speaker: Bayek
en: They won't bother you anymore. So you can stop bludgeoning people over the head now.

speaker: Corteseos
en: Are these the thieves!?

speaker: Bayek
en: Oh, easy, friend. There was a misunderstanding. Their hands were forced. These kids need a safe passage back to Memphis. Right?

speaker: Apheru
en: Yes, to the house of Nef, with all the other children.

speaker: Corteseos
en: I have not yet mapped out Memphis! It was supposed to be my next stop. Do you know the way?

speaker: Bayek
en: Oh, no. They know their way around.

speaker: Corteseos
en: What luck! Come along, then!

speaker: Apheru
en: Eh... Memphis?

speaker: Courteseos
en: Oh, of course! Thank you.

speaker: Neema
en: Come visit us!

speaker: Suphia
en: Good to see you, Namrut!

speaker: Namrut
en: Nefertari sent reinforcements I see?

speaker: Suphia
en: His name is Bayek, a dear friend of Nefertari's. I've asked him to come along and he graciously accepted.

speaker: Namrut
en: I suppose we all do.

speaker: Bayek
en: I hear you are in some trouble. I owe a favor to Nefertari.

speaker: Namrut
en: If it's as you say...Follow me, and stay close – we've got quite a journey ahead.

speaker: Namrut
en: The path to the mine was clear, but that doesn't mean it will be on the way back. Be ready for anything.

speaker: Bayek
en: You seem uneasy, Namrut. Why the hesitance?

speaker: Namrut
en: I don't like straying from the plan. These lands are teeming with dangers. Bandits. Soldiers. The wild. It's why we make the trips at night – helps avoid trouble.

speaker: Bayek
en: Where are you camped?

speaker: Namrut
en: In an abandoned fort to the West, our point of retreat.

speaker: Bayek
en: Retreat from what?

speaker: Namrut
en: An attack on a nearby encampment. There were more soldiers than we thought. Lost a lot of good men.

speaker: Bayek
en: How many wounded?

speaker: Namrut
en: Enough. That's why being close to the mine is so important. The healers work wonders. We are lucky Nefertari allows these deals. She has a pure heart. Risks her neck. The mine belongs to the regime after all. We should be out of harm's way once we cross that bridge.

speaker: Namrut
en: This is it. When we get inside, I will need your help to tend to the wounded while Suphia prepares the natron. I pray we have not lost more men.

speaker: Suphia
en: I will set up. Bayek, follow Namrut. He will show you what to do.

speaker: Namrut
en: These men – move them to the rear, by the kilns. This way. We will line them up. It will be easier for Suphia.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your band is much smaller than I imagined.

speaker: Namrut
en: Small but united. We fight for one another. I am merely one of them, spared by the gods this time.

speaker: Egyptian Rebel 1
en: Careful! Aghh!

speaker: Egyptian Rebel 2
en: Cold... I am so cold...

speaker: Bayek
en: Their wounds are severe, but they'll live if Suphia is anything like Nefertari.

speaker: Namrut
en: You and Nefertari are old friends?

speaker: Bayek
en: Something like that. She saved my life after I killed Rudjek.

speaker: Namrut
en: You are the one that killed Rudjek, eh? I cannot believe it – by the gods! The brazier!

speaker: Namrut
en: The fire will alert the regime!

speaker: Namrut
en: They have found us!

speaker: Soldier
en: Rebels! Move in, leave none alive! Archers! Ready your arrows!

speaker: Namrut
en: Look out! Protect the healer.

speaker: Soldier
en: Kill the wounded last. It is useless to fight! You are outmatched! Lay down your weapons, and we will make it quick.

speaker: Namrut
en: I would rather stick my sword down your throat.

speaker: Soldier
en: Those who oppose Ptolemy's reign die!

speaker: Namrut
en: Those who fight me die.

speaker: Soldier
en: This one fights alongside these rebels. A fool's choice!

speaker: Namrut
en: It's Suphia! She lit the brazier! Why would she draw the soldiers to us!? I will go check on the others. Go do something about Suphia.

speaker: Suphia
en: Back off! You are a murderer! No! Stay away from me!

speaker: Bayek
en: Talk!

speaker: Bayek
en: The omens... It was you. Why?

speaker: Suphia
en: Rudjek... I loved him. He promised me a better life! You took him from me!

speaker: Bayek
en: Now I see. You're Rudjek's mistress. Well, your fucking lover killed my son. I feel nothing for you.

speaker: Suphia
en: You're meant to die!

speaker: Bayek
en: Come!

speaker: Namrut
en: What a shame. Such a pretty girl. There's no room for pretty in our war.

speaker: Bayek
en: Death drives us to do things we regret.

speaker: Namrut
en: She tricked us both.

speaker: Bayek
en: Your men?

speaker: Namrut
en: The pile of dead gets bigger. We will treat the survivors. No time to fetch another healer.

speaker: Namrut
en: Your past follows you, Bayek. We have the natron, at least. We will do what we can. You best be on your way.

speaker: Bayek
en: I should go meet Tahira above the Quarry.

speaker: Tahira
en: Ah Bayek, it is time to dispose of Rufio's lieutenant.

speaker: Tahira
en: Tacito often comes out to roost atop the quarry.

speaker: Tahira
en: He is a brutal overseer. He makes an example of his workers everyday.

speaker: Tahira
en: I will stay close by and get a view of this (fool) before we pounce on him like Senu. But are you sure it is wise to kill him in the open?

speaker: Bayek
en: Tahira, this sends a message. The Hidden Ones will not settle for any oppressor.

speaker: Tahira
en: To kill him in front of his army or the workers will cause riot!

speaker: Bayek
en: At times, the public effect of our actions is secondary to the good they will bring.

speaker: Tahira
en: I trust you old friend. I ran across the Nile with you, and I will run across the Sinai. I am waiting for the perfect chance. He should be somewhere in this area.

speaker: Tacito
en: This quarry is your only hope. And you have spat on hope. Our work ensures the Walls-of-the-Ruler are solid to prevent Nabatean raids. The gods will not shine on you. Nor will your pharaoh, Cleopatra. Rome and Egypt share an alliance, you must see it this way. Egypt is a Roman and you will be punished by the alliance, not one country or another, you are punished by one greatness. We provide a fine, strong brew, and yet still some of you pull a sour face and try to stand against us.

speaker: Man
en: Why are you doing this? You sick man!

speaker: Tacio
en: shall punish you! Before you are many insubordinates, thieves, women of the night and other sad citizens. Lady Justice rules the Sinai as well as all lands under Roman rule. The crime of lethargy is as severe as treason and desertion. This quarry is run by rule of law. If work slows our villages suffer, our military weakens. That is enough for today with these insubordinate pigs. Let them rot in the sun. The stench of flesh will be a solemn reminder to others thinking of rebelling. That's taken care of. What was I saying? Oh, yes! Eventually I will require you to carry out the torture. The spectacle is what drives true fear into a populace. It also keeps them entertained. The Sinai will one day be like my native Cyrene, a productive and loyal colony. I could use some pomegranate wine. I wonder what Marc Antony and Cleopatra are plotting. The spectacle must commence now. Let my voice echo throughout Klysma! I want you all to know, this is the theatre of death for those who try to stand against us.

speaker: Tacito
en: Ahhhhh, bloody pathetic guards! Jupiter save me. Someone defend me against this savage! Why are you ruining my spectacle! Rebel in our midst!

speaker: Man 1
en: Death to Tacito!

speaker: Man 2
en: Kill him! He deserves it!

speaker: Bayek
en: Let Osiris maul your ka in eternity.

speaker: Tacito
en: Egyptians all! Rome will be your wise master.

speaker: Tacito
en: The Order is eternal.

speaker: Bayek
en: I need to regroup with Tahira.

speaker: Tahira
en: Ready. I fear more Romans are on the horizon. Tacito has a larger force than this, I am certain of it. If we cut down the entire operation, we may cause a rebellion, which will bring more good to Sinai. This could get messy. Freeing those prisoners could help our battle. A quiet approach could prove effective.

speaker: Tahira
en: Woe to the wicked! You neket iadets! (pieces of shit!) It is a liberation! May hyenas feast on these Romans!

speaker: Bayek
en: Reinforcements. I will add them to the offering for Anubis.

speaker: Roman Soldier 1
en: There they are! Cut them down!

speaker: Roman Soldier 2
en: You may never rebel against the Great Rome!

speaker: Roman Soldier 4
en: Who is rousing the people?

speaker: Rebel 1
en: Rejoice brothers and sisters!

speaker: Roman Soldier 5
en: Ahhh!

speaker: Rebel 2
en: Tacito is dead, let us retake the Quarry!

speaker: Rebel 3
en: Return the land of the Turquoise to the Nabateans! Gamilat works fast! Our rebellion grows!

speaker: Tahira
en: Yes Bayek! You are still the fine warrior I knew.

speaker: Bayek
en: As are you Tahira, you still fight with Sobek.

speaker: Rebel Captain
en: A great victory for the Nabateans! Gamilat led us to another triumph!

speaker: Bayek
en: Ensure this quarry remains in good hands.

speaker: Rebel Captain
en: That will be hard. Rufio will send more centurions. And there are still slaves inside the quarry who need to be liberated.

speaker: Bayek
en: Resilience is your greatest weapon.

speaker: Rebel Captain
en: You work for Gamilat? He told us of the Hidden Ones, great shadowy heroes.

speaker: Bayek
en: No one works for the Hidden Ones.

speaker: Rebel Soldier
en: Well thank you for defending us. If I see your sigil in the future, I will respect it.

speaker: Nikias
en: Bayek? I did not expect to see you here!

speaker: Bayek
en: Quite the estate.

speaker: Nikias
en: Yes, we've been lucky. Father breeds horses, and his horses have often won in the games. I told him about meeting you.

speaker: Bayek
en: You told him what?

speaker: Nikias
en: Not much. That you are a rider. That you know Claridas well.

speaker: Bayek
en: Too well, by half.

speaker: Nikias
en: Come! He would love to meet you.

speaker: Philocrates
en: Beautiful, isn't she?

speaker: Bayek
en: Bright eyes, flawless gait. She wants to win.

speaker: Philocrates
en: You know a thing or two about horses. Nikias, who is your friend?

speaker: Nikias
en: Father, this is Bayek. He once raced with Claridas. My father, Philocrates of Kanopos, son of Themistocles of Kanopos.

speaker: Philocrates
en: Grew up with Claridas? Let's see you drive, Barek. Nikias, keep close. Maybe you'll learn something.

speaker: Bayek
en: It's Ba—Fine.

speaker: Nikias
en: Does Siwa have a great course for racing?

speaker: Bayek
en: No, we are a small village. We did have chariots. The old kingdom and its Pharaohs brought them.

speaker: Nikias
en: I envy that freedom.

speaker: Nikias
en: When was the last time you raced Claridas?

speaker: Bayek
en: A long while. I barely know the name.

speaker: Nikas
en: Careful! Tighter on the reins! Watch the statuary! Icarus was the true master of the races. Something Claridas hopes to aspire to. My father loved Icarus. He was his favourite ch- his favorite rider. Let's show my father your natural skill! You have a light touch! You are a natural! With you riding for the Green, I'm sure we can win in the Hippodrome! Faster, Bayek, faster! Such speed!

speaker: Nikias
en: What's going on? Something's wrong!

speaker: Nikias
en: Father! Hurry, Bayek!

speaker: Philocrates
en: You fools! You let them steal Saganaki!

speaker: Man
en: Sorry, sir!

speaker: Philocrates
en: Where is my son? Nikias! Horse thieves! Here! The balls on them! She's my winningest horse! You have to get her back!

speaker: Nikias
en: We won't let you down, father!

speaker: Nikias
en: Hurry, men! We can't let these brazen raiders get away with this! The honor of Prasina Green depends on it!

speaker: Green 1
en: For Prasina Green!

speaker: Nikias
en: Keep a sharp eye out! Father loves that horse more than me— More than all the others we've raced!

speaker: Green 2
en: For Philocrates! For Saganaki!

speaker: Nikias
en: We must be getting close.

speaker: Green 3
en: For Icarus! For Prasina Green!

speaker: Green 4
en: For the Green!

speaker: Green 1
en: How many bandits do you think there are?

speaker: Green 4
en: Do not worry. We have the Medjay with us. We will be fine.

speaker: Green 3
en: Who are these bandits?

speaker: Green 1
en: Scum who are working for the blues, I'm sure.

speaker: Green 3
en: Have you heard about the Great Hungry Ones?

speaker: Green 1
en: Who are they?

speaker: Green 3
en: Bandits down south. I think they ride war hippos.

speaker: Green 1
en: What? Are you serious?

speaker: Green 3
en: So I've heard.

speaker: Philocrates
en: By Serapis, you did it! I cannot believe it! I was convinced we'd never see Saganaki, or my son, again.

speaker: Bayek
en: I dealt with the bandits who stole her. I suspect they stole Saganaki on behalf of your blue rivals.

speaker: Philocrates
en: Gods blast them! We'll have to beat the Blues in the races, to teach them shame and humiliation. I hope you race wearing the green, Baret.

speaker: Bayek
en: I... I will do my best.

speaker: Bayek
en: Here, let me help you with that.

speaker: Nito
en: What, you think me helpless?

speaker: Bayek
en: I am surprised to see a woman in your condition working so hard. The arrival of a child is a blessed event.

speaker: Nito
en: I am no delicate lily.

speaker: Bayek
en: Oh, are you in pain?

speaker: Nito
en: Bah, my little bean is just making herself known. My workers are so slow! I need to run over and check on them.

speaker: Bayek
en: Allow me, nebet.

speaker: Man
en: Baba! Ipuy! Can you hear me? Baba! Ipuy!

speaker: Ipuy
en: I am here!

speaker: Man
en: Are you okay?

speaker: Ipuy
en: My leg is hurt. I don't know how bad.

speaker: Man
en: And Baba?

speaker: Ipuy
en: I don't know. I can't see him. Get help!

speaker: Man
en: Please! Help! Quickly!

speaker: Bayek
en: What happened?

speaker: Man
en: The tunnel collapsed! Baba and Ipuy are trapped inside!

speaker: Bayek
en: How can I help?

speaker: Man
en: Are you strong enough to clear the way? See if you can bring them out. Please, neb, they are my brothers.

speaker: Bayek
en: Stay here. I will do what I can.

speaker: Bayek
en: I'm going to have to force a way through.

speaker: Bayek
en: Hey there, are you hurt?

speaker: Ipuy
en: Argh! I twisted my ankle! my brother Baba was working further in. The tunnel collapsed. I don't know if he's alive.

speaker: Bayek
en: I will get you out first, then find him.

speaker: Ipuy
en: Careful! I think I heard a hissing sound nearby!

speaker: Man
en: Ipuy! I will help him from here!

speaker: Ipuy
en: You need to go back and find Baba! hurry! He might be hurt, or worse!

speaker: Bayek
en: Take care of him. I will find your last brother.

speaker: Man
en: Thank you, neb!

speaker: Bayek
en: Peace, Wadjet. Forgive me for killing your green ones. There is no other way through.

speaker: Bayek
en: Are you hurt?

speaker: Baba
en: No, I managed to squeeze in here just before it collapsed. I had no idea this was here. We were digging to reach the river...

speaker: Bayek
en: That place was probably part of the old temple... Do you need help getting out of here?

speaker: Baba
en: I am fine. I am going to meet with my brothers and take a break.

speaker: Bayek
en: What is this place?

speaker: Bayek
en: Chief Nito, the well tunnel partially collapsed, but I was able to help the workers.

speaker: Nito
en: My little bean and I are so fortunate you passed by when you did, Medjay. May the bless you a thousand times for your efforts!

speaker: Bayek
en: Take care of yourself. May the gods bless your little one.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Would not know truth if it hit them in the head! Alexandrians! We must stand up against this sickness that spreads in silence! Pah! This Gennadios! He seeks to stifle the Alexandrian Poets! He knows not what kind of enemy we are. They may jail me, but I will not sell my blood to the death merchants of this regime!

speaker: Woman
en: I'm worried about Phanos. Did you see his latest play? It was very dark.

speaker: Man
en: He is a poet. They have other passions.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Bayek! Finally, someone who appreciates my genius. My play has been confiscated!

speaker: Bayek
en: You are attracting trouble.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Worse yet, they jailed my actors – all among the finest poets of Alexandria. They say if I attempt to put on the play, I will be put to death.

speaker: Bayek
en: Be careful, Phanos. You are frail and brittle. You stick to writing, and I will help you find your play and actors.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: They threw my actors into the garrison, you believe that Bayek? If the Phylakitai want a fight, I will fight. I did not start this war, but I will finish it. The Ptolemies have opprested poets before! They banished us all to Nubian mines.

speaker: Bayek
en: Perhaps if your play was performed at the temples, it would reach more people.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Woah, wait... I did not realize you Siwans knew so much about the theatre.

speaker: Bayek
en: In Siwa we had many great satires performed at the temple. I remember watching one in which Anubis gets engaged to a jackal.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: How, fascinating. I have yet to see the Egyptian satires.

speaker: Bayek
en: What is your play about?

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: It is called "Phah-roar Enough", a rousing comedy about oppression and the ignorance of the Pharaoh. Oh, and lions.

speaker: Bayek
en: Sounds... interesting.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: Is this theatre not magnificent? And empty because of the regime. Please Bayek, fly like Senu and bring life back to this amphitheater. I miss my poets.

speaker: Man
en: Anyone have any food? Water? Anything? Could do with a bit of food though. Can't even look an actor in the face. Psstt. I'll immortalize you in poetry... if you get me out of here.

speaker: Man
en: Ah, carried to safety. An experience like no other.

speaker: Bayek
en: Will you be still. I pray you, be quiet.

speaker: Man
en: Hey! Careful there, big guy. Faster, big man. We have a revolution to make happen. Ah, this reminds me of my youth on stage. I was an excellent sack of grain in my premiere appearance.

speaker: Man
en: Thank you! But, there are two more of us. They escaped. Gennadios' Phylakitai seek to kill them. They also took the play and headed toward the palace. If it lands in the wrong hands, Phanos will be in danger.

speaker: Bayek
en: Do you know where the actors hide?

speaker: Man
en: Their home, not far from here. Don't worry about me. I'll find my way back to the theatre.

speaker: Egyptian soldier
en: Where is that treasonous fool?

speaker: Greek soldier
en: You will find that filthy beggar. Now.

speaker: Egyptian soldier
en: Sir! I believe he is an actor.

speaker: Greek soldier
en: I don't care what he is. We must find him or I'll be stuck mucking stables for weeks.

speaker: Egyptian soldier
en: I'm sure the damned fool is around here somewhere.

speaker: Greek soldier
en: Maybe if we speak some lines he could be fooled into coming after us.

speaker: Bayek
en: Time to go, young poet. Wait, Isn't there supposed to be two of you?

speaker: Man 2
en: Kapaneus? He fled... and accidentally brought the guards to me. They hunt me like a dog. If you could deal with them, I can return to Phanos, and our masterpiece will go on!

speaker: Bayek
en: Be calm. We will be out of here quickly.

speaker: Man 2
en: Of course! I will be silent as

speaker: Bayek
en: Be still. I think I hear them.

speaker: Man 2
en: You know, you are perfectly Phanos' type.

speaker: Bayek
en: I have no idea what you speak of.

speaker: Man 2
en: You are a perfect brooding hero! A grand story, until the Gods smack him down mightily for his temerity!

speaker: Bayek
en: That is not helpful.

speaker: Man 2
en: But such a tragedy this will be. All will be pushed to tears!

speaker: Bayek
en: Phanos awaits you.

speaker: Man 2
en: Now there is nothing that will stop us from exposing this regime! Thank you, friend. I'm sure Kapaneus will find us eventually... he always does. ...When the danger is past, of course.

speaker: Man 3
en: You dare! No, not quite. You... dare! That's it! That's it! Carve your eyes! Carve your eyes! Carve. Your. Eyes. At you, gall. No. At their gall! No it's at gall. At gall. Got it.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: You did it, Bayek. Thank you. I never doubted you. Aya is a lucky woman.

speaker: Bayek
en: Aya always spoke highly of your plays.

speaker: Phanos the Younger
en: She enjoyed my pro-Cleopatra work, "My Pharaoh Lady." Now we can perform this play like true poets. The guards may kill us, but it is an artist's duty to see his vision fulfilled! I will write a play for you someday, Bayek... "The Last of the Medjay." No, no...

speaker: Man 2
en: Don't worry, we'll change the names of the main villain, Ptolemy, and the title. We won't die, and the play will go on.
